objets.notes: Ayyubid forces commanded by Turan-Shah invade Banu Kanz lands in Nubia, seizing the strategic frontier fortress of Qasr Ibrim.

objets.notes: Growth of Azanian and Zanj settlements in the Swahili coast. Local industry and international trade flourish.

objets.notes: Starting with the first Hijrah (migration) of Prophet Muhammad's followers to Ethiopia, Islam spreads across Eastern, Northern and Western Africa.

objets.notes: Archaeological evidence indicates that crucible steel is manufactured at Galu, south of Mombasa. Metallurgical analysis of iron artefacts indicates that the techniques used by the inhabitants of the Swahili coast combined techniques used in other African sites as well as those in West and South Asian sites.

objets.nom: Emergence of the Swahili City States.
The oldest Swahili texts in existence date to this period
objets.notes: The oldest Swahili texts in existence date to this period. They are written in old Swahili script (Swahili-Arabic alphabet) based on Arabic letters.

objets.notes: The ancestors of the Iraqw are credited as the builders of the Iron Age settlement at Engaruka in Northern Tanzania. Complex irrigation systems supporting intensive agriculture supported an estimated peak population of 40,000. It is recognised as the largest abandoned system of irrigated agricultural fields and terraces in sub-Saharan Africa.

objets.nom: Kilwa's ruler makes a recorded pilgrimage to Mecca.
The Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama is the first known European to reach the East African coast,…
objets.notes: The Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama is the first known European to reach the East African coast, landing at Kilimane, where he stayed for 32 days.

objets.nom: Captain John Homere, part of Francisco de Almeida's fleet, captures the archipelago of Zanzibar, making…
objets.notes: Captain John Homere, part of Francisco de Almeida's fleet, captures the archipelago of Zanzibar, making it part of the Portuguese Empire.

Oman's conquest of Kilwa leds the Yao to flee to Mozambique island.

Over 100,000 slaves pass through Zanzibar as part of the Arab slave trade.
The founding of the Chagga states of Kilimanjaro.
Kilwa was reviving and becomes East Africa's largest slave port with the Yao returning from Mozambique…
objets.notes: Kilwa was reviving and becomes East Africa's largest slave port with the Yao returning from Mozambique as slave taders. The enslaved were sold to the French colonies of the Mascarene islands.

objets.nom: Smallpox plagues southern Tanzania.
The Shambaa Kingdom enters a golden age under Kimweri ye Nyambai's reign.
Famine in Ukerewe.

Omani Sultan Seyyid Said moves his capital to Zanzibar City.

objets.notes: German missionary Johannes Rebmann, accompanied by Johann Ludwig Krapf, become the first Europeans to report seeing Mount Kilimanjaro.

King Muyigumba conqueres the northern and central Hehe chiefdoms into a unified Hehe state.

objets.notes: Sultan Seyyid Said dies at sea and is succeeded by his sons Thuwaini bin Said, in Muscat and Oman and Majid bin Said, in Zanzibar.

objets.nom: British explorers Richard Burton and John Speke travel from Zanzibar to the East African coast and begin…
objets.notes: British explorers Richard Burton and John Speke travel from Zanzibar to the East African coast and begin their exploration of continental East Africa.

objets.nom: Maize is grown in the Pangani Valley.
Burton and Speke reach Lake Tanganyika, the first known Europeans to do so.
King Mirambo of the Nyamwezi rises to power.

objets.notes: Zanzibar and Oman are split into two separate principalities with Majid bin Said becoming the first Sultan of Zanzibar.

objets.notes: Songea's king Mputa Maseko is killed by dissident Ndendeuli who flees east to the Kilombero valley and recreates Ngoni style military state forming the Mbunga people, forcing the Pogoro to flee eat to the Mahenge plateau.

objets.nom: The Kiva rebellion, where Bondei rebel against the Shambaa Kingdom's rule.
Islam becomes the major religion among the Zigua and Bondei.
Zanzibari Sultan Barghash bin Said stops the export of slaves over the sea.

Bagamoyo pays tribute to the Zaramo fearing attack.

Kilwa's biggest export switches from slaves to wild rubber.
Fipa King Kapufi of Nkasi hires an Arab Prime minister in his court.
The Pare at Mbaga attack a slave trader settlement of Kisiwani.
King Songea Mbano of the Ngoni raids the eastern stateless peoples like the Ngindo, Makonde and Mwera…
objets.notes: King Songea Mbano of the Ngoni raids the eastern stateless peoples like the Ngindo, Makonde and Mwera forcing them to flee further eastwards leaving empty land.

objets.nom: The Ngoni and Hehe end their war with Bena partitioned amongst them as a buffer.

objets.notes: The Germans led by Peters land at Saadani and start the invasion reaching the Ngulu mountains and signing a sham treaty with Chief Mafungu Biniani of Ngulu .

objets.notes: The Society for German Colonization is formed by Karl Peters in order to acquire German colonial territories in overseas countries. Peters signs treaties with several native chieftains on the mainland opposite Zanzibar.

objets.nom: The German East Africa Company is formed by Karl Peters to govern German East Africa.
The German government announces its intention to establish a protectorate in East Africa.
An agreement is reached between Britain and Germany designating a wide strip of land along the coast as…
objets.notes: An agreement is reached between Britain and Germany designating a wide strip of land along the coast as being controlled by Sultan Barghash bin Said, along with Zanzibar, Pemba, and Mafia. The area that is to become Tanganyika is assigned to Germany while the area to become Kenya is assigned to Britain.

objets.nom: The Germans occupy Dar es Salaam.
The Zaramo attack two German stations in Dar es Salaam .
Tanga is bombed by German warships.
The German East Africa Company leases the coastal strip opposite Zanzibar from Sultan Khalifah bin Said…
objets.notes: The German East Africa Company leases the coastal strip opposite Zanzibar from Sultan Khalifah bin Said for 50 years.

objets.nom: The Zigua boycott a station in Old Korogwe.
Germans hang Abushiri .

The Battle of Kibosho.

objets.notes: The Anglo-Zanzibar War is fought between Zanzibar and the United Kingdom. It lasted approximately 38 minutes and is the shortest war in history.

objets.notes: The Zanzibar Revolution by local Africans overthrows the Sultan of Zanzibar and his primarily Arab government. Sheikh Abeid Karume becomes the first President of Zanzibar.

objets.notes: Archaeologist Mary Leakey and her team discover homoinid fossil footprints at Laetoli, south of the Olduvai Gorge.

objets.nom: Premier recours à l'emprunt étranger : le grand vizir Mustapha Khaznadar contracte auprès de la banque…

objets.notes: premier recours à l'emprunt étranger : le grand vizir Mustapha Khaznadar contracte auprès de la banque parisienne Erlanger un emprunt de 35 millions de francs gagé sur la mejba, dont cinq millions seulement parviennent dans les caisses de l'État. Dilapidé aux trois quarts en moins d'un an, il rend impossible le paiement de la première annuité.

objets.nom: Incapable d'honorer l'emprunt de 1863, le gouvernement étend d'abord la mejba aux villes jusque-là…
objets.fr: Incapable d'honorer l'emprunt de 1863, le gouvernement étend d'abord la mejba aux villes jusque-là…
objets.notes: incapable d'honorer l'emprunt de 1863, le gouvernement étend d'abord la mejba aux villes jusque-là exemptées, puis en double le montant, de 36 à 72 piastres. Cette mesure déclenche l'insurrection conduite par Ali Ben Ghedhahem (1814-1867), férocement réprimée. Les conséquences de cette révolte furent dramatiques puisque le déséquilibre des…

objets.nom: La contestation gagne l'aristocratie beylicale : le prince El Adel Bey, demi-frère de Sadok Bey, quitte…
objets.fr: La contestation gagne l'aristocratie beylicale : le prince El Adel Bey, demi-frère de Sadok Bey, quitte…
objets.notes: la contestation gagne l'aristocratie beylicale : le prince El Adel Bey, demi-frère de Sadok Bey, quitte secrètement son palais de La Marsa pour se réfugier chez les montagnards khroumirs insurgés, par hostilité au grand vizir Mustapha Khaznadar. La rébellion échoue — son compagnon Mahmoud Djellouli est décapité, deux dignitaires mamelouks sont…

objets.nom: Lors du congrès de Berlin, le Royaume-Uni et l'Allemagne donnent carte blanche à la France en Tunisie.
objets.fr: Lors du congrès de Berlin, le Royaume-Uni et l'Allemagne donnent carte blanche à la France en Tunisie.

objets.nom: La flotte française déployée le long du littoral bombarde Sfax et prend la ville après dix jours de siège.
objets.fr: La flotte française déployée le long du littoral bombarde Sfax et prend la ville après dix jours de siège.

objets.nom: Le Bey doit accepter le 12 mai 1881 le Traité du Bardo, (Traité de garantie) qui établit le protectorat…
objets.fr: Le Bey doit accepter le 12 mai 1881 le Traité du Bardo, (Traité de garantie) qui établit le protectorat…
objets.notes: Le Bey doit accepter le 12 mai 1881 le Traité du Bardo, (Traité de garantie) qui établit le protectorat français. Il est signé par le général Bréart, le consul Théodore Roustan, Sadok Bey et le grand vizir Mustapha Ben Ismaïl. Il place le gouvernement beylical sous protectorat français. La France devient responsable de la défense et des relations…

objets.nom: Le consul de France Théodore Roustan annonce à Sadok Bey que la France va intervenir en réaction aux…
objets.fr: Le consul de France Théodore Roustan annonce à Sadok Bey que la France va intervenir en réaction aux…
objets.notes: le consul de France Théodore Roustan annonce à Sadok Bey que la France va intervenir en réaction aux incursions de tribus de Kroumirie en territoire algérien.

objets.nom: Le Conseil d'État français rend l'arrêt Couitéas, né du refus des autorités d'exécuter par la force un…
objets.fr: Le Conseil d'État français rend l'arrêt Couitéas, né du refus des autorités d'exécuter par la force un…
objets.notes: le Conseil d'État français rend l'arrêt Couitéas, né du refus des autorités d'exécuter par la force un jugement d'expulsion de tribus installées sur un domaine du Sud tunisien ; il consacre la responsabilité sans faute de l'État pour rupture de l'égalité devant les charges publiques, principe toujours en vigueur.

objets.nom: Bourguiba rompt avec la direction du Destour et fonde le parti nationaliste du Néo-Destour dans la ville…
objets.fr: Bourguiba rompt avec la direction du Destour et fonde le parti nationaliste du Néo-Destour dans la ville…
objets.notes: Bourguiba rompt avec la direction du Destour et fonde le parti nationaliste du Néo-Destour dans la ville de Ksar Hellal (Sahel tunisien).

objets.nom: Alors que Ali Belhouane est convoqué par le juge d'instruction, une foule se rassemble devant le Palais…
objets.fr: Alors que Ali Belhouane est convoqué par le juge d'instruction, une foule se rassemble devant le Palais…
objets.notes: alors que Ali Belhouane est convoqué par le juge d'instruction, une foule se rassemble devant le Palais de justice. Des coups de feu éclatent. Des heurts sanglants se produisent et se soldent par 22 morts et près de 150 blessés. L'état de siège est proclamé à Tunis, Sousse et dans le cap Bon.

objets.nom: Le Néo-Destour appelle à une grève générale : une grande manifestation conduite par Mongi Slim et Ali…
objets.fr: Le Néo-Destour appelle à une grève générale : une grande manifestation conduite par Mongi Slim et Ali…
objets.notes: le Néo-Destour appelle à une grève générale : une grande manifestation conduite par Mongi Slim et Ali Belhouane se dirige vers le siège de la résidence générale. Devant une foule de 10000 personnes, Belhouane harangue les manifestants : « Nous sommes venus aujourd'hui démontrer notre force [...] celle de la jeunesse qui ébranlera le colonialisme…

objets.nom: Des soldats allemands se livrent à une rafle dans la Grande synagogue de Tunis : les hommes sont retenus…
objets.fr: Des soldats allemands se livrent à une rafle dans la Grande synagogue de Tunis : les hommes sont retenus…
objets.notes: des soldats allemands se livrent à une rafle dans la Grande synagogue de Tunis : les hommes sont retenus pour le travail forcé alors que beaucoup de femmes et d'enfants sont maltraités par les soldats.

objets.nom: Des bombes sont lancées sur les édifices représentant le protectorat à Sousse, Sfax, Djerba, Tunis,…
objets.fr: Des bombes sont lancées sur les édifices représentant le protectorat à Sousse, Sfax, Djerba, Tunis,…
objets.notes: des bombes sont lancées sur les édifices représentant le protectorat à Sousse, Sfax, Djerba, Tunis, Matmata et Gafsa. Des écoliers manifestant pour l'indépendance sont arrêtés à Soliman et Nefta.

objets.nom: Chedly Kastalli, vice-président de la municipalité de Tunis et cofondateur en 1921 du Parti réformiste,…
objets.fr: Chedly Kastalli, vice-président de la municipalité de Tunis et cofondateur en 1921 du Parti réformiste,…
objets.notes: Chedly Kastalli, vice-président de la municipalité de Tunis et cofondateur en 1921 du Parti réformiste, est abattu à l'entrée de la médina, à la veille des élections municipales auxquelles il s'était porté candidat. Le même jour, un second attentat vise sans l'atteindre le ministre du Commerce, le docteur Ben Raïs. L'assassinat est attribué aux…

objets.nom: L'assemblée constituante vote l'abolition de la monarchie beylicale, au pouvoir depuis 1705, et proclame…
objets.fr: L'assemblée constituante vote l'abolition de la monarchie beylicale, au pouvoir depuis 1705, et proclame…
objets.notes: l'assemblée constituante vote l'abolition de la monarchie beylicale, au pouvoir depuis 1705, et proclame la république. Elle élit Habib Bourguiba, Premier ministre sortant, aux fonctions de président de la République. Une délégation de l'assemblée constituante, composée de Jallouli Farès, Ali Belhouane et Driss Guiga vient signifier à Lamine Bey…

objets.nom: Lors d'une rencontre à Rambouillet, Habib Bourguiba presse le président Charles de Gaulle de restituer…
objets.fr: Lors d'une rencontre à Rambouillet, Habib Bourguiba presse le président Charles de Gaulle de restituer…
objets.notes: lors d'une rencontre à Rambouillet, Habib Bourguiba presse le président Charles de Gaulle de restituer la base de Bizerte. Ce dernier le tempère en évoquant des négociations.

objets.nom: Salah Ben Youssef, principal opposant à Habib Bourguiba, est assassiné à Francfort (Allemagne).
objets.fr: Salah Ben Youssef, principal opposant à Habib Bourguiba, est assassiné à Francfort (Allemagne).

objets.nom: Le du Néo-Destour s'ouvre à Bizerte
objets.fr: Le du Néo-Destour s'ouvre à Bizerte
objets.notes: Le du Néo-Destour s'ouvre à Bizerte. Il adopte alors le socialisme comme doctrine et prend le nom de Parti socialiste destourien le 22 octobre.

objets.nom: D'importantes inondations font plus de 400 morts et occasionnent d'importants dégâts matériels
objets.fr: D'importantes inondations font plus de 400 morts et occasionnent d'importants dégâts matériels
objets.notes: d'importantes inondations font plus de 400 morts et occasionnent d'importants dégâts matériels. Les villages de Chebika, Tamerza et Midès, dans le sud-ouest du pays, sont ravagés et définitivement évacués par leur population.

objets.nom: Habib Bourguiba refuse de signer le décret-loi généralisant les coopératives
objets.fr: Habib Bourguiba refuse de signer le décret-loi généralisant les coopératives
objets.notes: Habib Bourguiba refuse de signer le décret-loi généralisant les coopératives. Émeutes dans le Sahel tunisien contre la politique de collectivisation des terres, contribuant à la fin de l’expérience socialiste.

objets.nom: Lors de la deuxième visite du leader libyen Mouammar Kadhafi à Tunis se produit l'incident du Palmarium
objets.fr: Lors de la deuxième visite du leader libyen Mouammar Kadhafi à Tunis se produit l'incident du Palmarium
objets.notes: lors de la deuxième visite du leader libyen Mouammar Kadhafi à Tunis se produit l'incident du Palmarium. Face aux pressions de Kadhafi en faveur de l'unité arabe, Habib Bourguiba lui répond par l'exaltation de la nation tunisienne.

objets.nom: Lors d'un sommet organisé au Kef, le président algérien Houari Boumédiène propose la constitution d'une…
objets.fr: Lors d'un sommet organisé au Kef, le président algérien Houari Boumédiène propose la constitution d'une…
objets.notes: lors d'un sommet organisé au Kef, le président algérien Houari Boumédiène propose la constitution d'une union tuniso-algérienne. Habib Bourguiba décline cette proposition et avance le développement de la coopération économique entre les deux pays.

objets.nom: Des émeutes, connues sous le nom de Jeudi noir, ont lieu à Tunis à la suite d'une grève générale lancée…
objets.fr: Des émeutes, connues sous le nom de Jeudi noir, ont lieu à Tunis à la suite d'une grève générale lancée…
objets.notes: des émeutes, connues sous le nom de Jeudi noir, ont lieu à Tunis à la suite d'une grève générale lancée par l'Union générale tunisienne du travail. Elles font officiellement 52 morts et 365 blessés (200 selon d'autres sources). L'état d'urgence est instauré.

objets.nom: À la suite des accords de Camp David entre Israël et l'Égypte, la Ligue arabe installe son siège à Tunis.
objets.fr: À la suite des accords de Camp David entre Israël et l'Égypte, la Ligue arabe installe son siège à Tunis.

objets.nom: Environ combattants palestiniens débarquent à Bizerte, en provenance de Beyrouth, après un voyage de six…
objets.fr: Environ combattants palestiniens débarquent à Bizerte, en provenance de Beyrouth, après un voyage de six…
objets.notes: environ combattants palestiniens débarquent à Bizerte, en provenance de Beyrouth, après un voyage de six jours à bord du vaisseau chypriote Sol Phryne. Ils reçoivent un accueil enthousiaste de la population locale.

objets.nom: Des émeutes, provoquées par le doublement des prix du pain et des produits céréaliers, éclatent à…
objets.fr: Des émeutes, provoquées par le doublement des prix du pain et des produits céréaliers, éclatent à…
objets.notes: Des émeutes, provoquées par le doublement des prix du pain et des produits céréaliers, éclatent à travers le pays. Le gouvernement déclare l'état d'urgence le 3 janvier, impose un couvre-feu alors que les émeutes touchent Tunis et Sfax, ferme les écoles, interdit tout rassemblement de plus de trois personnes puis positionne des tanks dans les rues…

objets.nom: Un raid de l'armée de l'air israélienne, connu sous le nom de code Opération Jambe de bois, a lieu…
objets.fr: Un raid de l'armée de l'air israélienne, connu sous le nom de code Opération Jambe de bois, a lieu…
objets.notes: un raid de l'armée de l'air israélienne, connu sous le nom de code Opération Jambe de bois, a lieu contre le quartier-général de l'Organisation de libération de la Palestine à Hammam Chott (au sud de Tunis).

objets.nom: Des explosions ont lieu dans quatre hôtels de Monastir et de la région de Sousse
objets.fr: Des explosions ont lieu dans quatre hôtels de Monastir et de la région de Sousse
objets.notes: des explosions ont lieu dans quatre hôtels de Monastir et de la région de Sousse. Ils font 13 blessés dont sept Italiens, quatre Britanniques et deux Allemands. L'Organisation du Jihad islamique revendique, le 10 août, la responsabilité des attentats.

objets.nom: Le président Zine el-Abidine Ben Ali décide de gracier l'ancien ministre de l'économie nationale Ahmed…
objets.fr: Le président Zine el-Abidine Ben Ali décide de gracier l'ancien ministre de l'économie nationale Ahmed…
objets.notes: le président Zine el-Abidine Ben Ali décide de gracier l'ancien ministre de l'économie nationale Ahmed Ben Salah. Il gracie également, le 14 mai, le président du Mouvement de la tendance islamique, Rached Ghannouchi, que la Cour de sûreté de l'État avait condamné le 27 septembre 1987 aux travaux forcés à perpétuité.

objets.nom: Le siège de la Ligue arabe, situé à Tunis depuis 1979, est officiellement ramené au Caire.
objets.fr: Le siège de la Ligue arabe, situé à Tunis depuis 1979, est officiellement ramené au Caire.

objets.nom: Deux pirates de l'air tunisiens tentent de détourner sur Alger un DC-9 d'Alitalia assurant la liaison…
objets.fr: Deux pirates de l'air tunisiens tentent de détourner sur Alger un DC-9 d'Alitalia assurant la liaison…
objets.notes: deux pirates de l'air tunisiens tentent de détourner sur Alger un DC-9 d'Alitalia assurant la liaison entre Rome et Tunis. L'avion, qui transporte 130 passagers et 7 membres d'équipage, se pose finalement à Tunis comme prévu.

objets.nom: L'accord d'association avec l'Union européenne, signé le 17 juillet 1995 et qui doit mener la Tunisie à…
objets.fr: L'accord d'association avec l'Union européenne, signé le 17 juillet 1995 et qui doit mener la Tunisie à…
objets.notes: l'accord d'association avec l'Union européenne, signé le 17 juillet 1995 et qui doit mener la Tunisie à une complète libéralisation économique d'ici 2008, entre en vigueur après sa ratification par la Belgique (dernier pays européen à parapher le texte).

objets.nom: Le président Zine el-Abidine Ben Ali et pour la première fois deux autres candidats, Mohamed Belhaj Amor…
objets.fr: Le président Zine el-Abidine Ben Ali et pour la première fois deux autres candidats, Mohamed Belhaj Amor…
objets.notes: le président Zine el-Abidine Ben Ali et pour la première fois deux autres candidats, Mohamed Belhaj Amor et Abderrahmane Tlili, se présentent à la présidentielle. Le président sortant est réélu avec 99,44 % et le Rassemblement constitutionnel démocratique remporte 91,6 % aux législatives.

objets.nom: L'ancien président Habib Bourguiba meurt à son domicile de Monastir à l'âge de 96 ans
objets.fr: L'ancien président Habib Bourguiba meurt à son domicile de Monastir à l'âge de 96 ans
objets.notes: l'ancien président Habib Bourguiba meurt à son domicile de Monastir à l'âge de 96 ans. Le président Zine el-Abidine Ben Ali proclame un deuil national de 7 jours. Ses funérailles ont lieu le 8 avril à Monastir.

objets.nom: Plusieurs centaines de personnes rendent hommage, à la cathédrale de Tunis et en présence de…
objets.fr: Plusieurs centaines de personnes rendent hommage, à la cathédrale de Tunis et en présence de…
objets.notes: plusieurs centaines de personnes rendent hommage, à la cathédrale de Tunis et en présence de représentants du gouvernement et de personnalités politiques italiennes, à l'ancien chef du gouvernement italien Bettino Craxi décédé le 19 janvier. Il est enterré dans le petit cimetière chrétien d'Hammamet où il vivait en exil depuis 1994 car mis en…

objets.nom: Un Boeing 737 de la compagnie EgyptAir en provenance du Caire s'écrase près de l'aéroport international…
objets.fr: Un Boeing 737 de la compagnie EgyptAir en provenance du Caire s'écrase près de l'aéroport international…
objets.notes: un Boeing 737 de la compagnie EgyptAir en provenance du Caire s'écrase près de l'aéroport international de Tunis-Carthage. 15 des 64 personnes qui se trouvent à bord meurent.

objets.nom: Un camion-citerne de gaz naturel bourré d'explosifs saute devant de la synagogue de la Ghriba et tue 21…
objets.fr: Un camion-citerne de gaz naturel bourré d'explosifs saute devant de la synagogue de la Ghriba et tue 21…
objets.notes: un camion-citerne de gaz naturel bourré d'explosifs saute devant de la synagogue de la Ghriba et tue 21 personnes (14 Allemands, 5 Tunisiens et 2 Français). 30 personnes sont blessées.

objets.nom: Trois opposants, Mohamed Bouchiha, Mohamed Ali Halouani et Mounir Béji, se présentent à l'élection…
objets.fr: Trois opposants, Mohamed Bouchiha, Mohamed Ali Halouani et Mounir Béji, se présentent à l'élection…
objets.notes: trois opposants, Mohamed Bouchiha, Mohamed Ali Halouani et Mounir Béji, se présentent à l'élection présidentielle boycottée par les autres partis de l'opposition. Le président Zine el-Abidine Ben Ali est officiellement réélu pour un quatrième mandat avec 94,49 % des voix. La Chambre des députés est désormais composée de 189 députés au lieu de 182.

objets.nom: Un ATR 72 de la société Tuninter, filiale de Tunisair, avec 39 personnes à bord est contraint d'amerrir…
objets.fr: Un ATR 72 de la société Tuninter, filiale de Tunisair, avec 39 personnes à bord est contraint d'amerrir…
objets.notes: un ATR 72 de la société Tuninter, filiale de Tunisair, avec 39 personnes à bord est contraint d'amerrir au large de Palerme. L'accident fait 16 morts et 3 disparus. L'appareil assurait un vol entre Bari (Italie) et Djerba.

objets.nom: Le gouvernement annonce la fermeture de son ambassade au Qatar « à la suite de la campagne hostile à la…
objets.fr: Le gouvernement annonce la fermeture de son ambassade au Qatar « à la suite de la campagne hostile à la…
objets.notes: le gouvernement annonce la fermeture de son ambassade au Qatar « à la suite de la campagne hostile à la Tunisie menée par la chaîne qatarie Al Jazeera ».

objets.nom: Le président de la Chambre des députés Fouad Mebazaa devient officiellement le président intérimaire à…
objets.fr: Le président de la Chambre des députés Fouad Mebazaa devient officiellement le président intérimaire à…
objets.notes: le président de la Chambre des députés Fouad Mebazaa devient officiellement le président intérimaire à la suite d'une décision du Conseil constitutionnel. Il demande au Premier ministre Mohamed Ghannouchi de former un gouvernement d'union nationale.

objets.nom: Le gouvernement abroge la circulaire du 5 novembre 1973 qui interdisait le mariage d'une Tunisienne…
objets.fr: Le gouvernement abroge la circulaire du 5 novembre 1973 qui interdisait le mariage d'une Tunisienne…
objets.notes: le gouvernement abroge la circulaire du 5 novembre 1973 qui interdisait le mariage d'une Tunisienne musulmane avec un non-musulman (sauf conversion de l'époux à l'islam). L'annonce, faite par la porte-parole de la présidence Saïda Garrach, fait suite à un appel de Béji Caïd Essebsi lors de la fête de la Femme du 13 août.

objets.nom: L'Assemblée des représentants du peuple adopte la loi organique (promulguée le 23 octobre) relative à…
objets.fr: L'Assemblée des représentants du peuple adopte la loi organique (promulguée le 23 octobre) relative à…
objets.notes: l'Assemblée des représentants du peuple adopte la loi organique (promulguée le 23 octobre) relative à l'élimination de toutes les formes de discrimination raciale, qui pénalise pour la première fois les actes et propos racistes — une première dans le monde arabe et en Afrique du Nord.

objets.nom: Lancement, depuis le cosmodrome de Baïkonour à bord d'une fusée Soyouz, de Challenge One, premier…
objets.fr: Lancement, depuis le cosmodrome de Baïkonour à bord d'une fusée Soyouz, de Challenge One, premier…
objets.notes: lancement, depuis le cosmodrome de Baïkonour à bord d'une fusée Soyouz, de Challenge One, premier satellite tunisien — un nanosatellite conçu par le groupe Telnet. La Tunisie devient le premier pays du Maghreb et le sixième d'Afrique à fabriquer son propre satellite.

objets.nom: Hittite Empire established in the region of Anatolia with capital in Hattusa near present-day Boğazkale,…
objets.notes: Hittite Empire established in the region of Anatolia with capital in Hattusa near present-day Boğazkale, Turkey.

objets.nom: Battle of Kadesh between the Hittite Empire and the New Kingdom of Egypt.
Collapse of the Hittite Empire, splinters into several independent Syro-Hittite states.
Ionian Revolt, military rebellion by the Greek regions of Anatolia against Persian Empire rule
objets.notes: Ionian Revolt, military rebellion by the Greek regions of Anatolia against Persian Empire rule. Revolt is crushed.

objets.nom: Alexander III of Macedon crosses the Hellespont into Asia, making his landing in present-day Turkey.
Alexander III of Macedon defeats the armies of the Achaemenid Empire in the Battle of the Granicus river…
objets.notes: Alexander III of Macedon defeats the armies of the Achaemenid Empire in the Battle of the Granicus river (modern-day Biga Çayı).

objets.nom: The Roman invasion of Anatolia begins with the annexation of Attalid Pergamon by the Roman Republic
objets.notes: The Roman invasion of Anatolia begins with the annexation of Attalid Pergamon by the Roman Republic. The entire region is later brought under Roman rule. For the next few centuries, under Roman rule, the region becomes prosperous, roads and infrastructure are built and improved and coastal communities flourish.

objets.nom: Exécution de Çandarlı Halil Hayreddin Pacha
objets.fr: Exécution de Çandarlı Halil Hayreddin Pacha

objets.nom: Fin du siège et prise de Nicée par le bey Orhan; début du siège de Nicomédie.
objets.fr: Fin du siège et prise de Nicée par le bey Orhan; début du siège de Nicomédie.

objets.nom: Mourad II remonte sur le trône pour la deuxième fois à la suite des actions d'Halil Pacha qui fomenta…
objets.fr: Mourad II remonte sur le trône pour la deuxième fois à la suite des actions d'Halil Pacha qui fomenta…
objets.notes: Mourad II remonte sur le trône pour la deuxième fois à la suite des actions d'Halil Pacha qui fomenta une révolte des janissaires, son fils Mehmet II étant jugé trop immature et incompétent pour diriger l'Empire face aux hongrois, serbes et byzantins qui y voyaient une occasion de mener à bien une nouvelle croisade contre les Ottomans.

objets.nom: L'empereur romain d'orient Jean VI Cantacuzène est élevé sur le trône de Constantinople avec le soutien…
objets.fr: L'empereur romain d'orient Jean VI Cantacuzène est élevé sur le trône de Constantinople avec le soutien…
objets.notes: l'empereur romain d'orient Jean VI Cantacuzène est élevé sur le trône de Constantinople avec le soutien des Ottomans.

objets.nom: Mort du sultan Mehmet II le Conquérant, son fils aîné Bayezid II monte au trône; néanmoins il se dispute…
objets.fr: Mort du sultan Mehmet II le Conquérant, son fils aîné Bayezid II monte au trône; néanmoins il se dispute…
objets.notes: mort du sultan Mehmet II le Conquérant, son fils aîné Bayezid II monte au trône; néanmoins il se dispute le pouvoir avec son frère Cem (dit Zizim), l'autre fils de Mehmet.

objets.nom: Fin de l'interrègne, Mehmet Ier unifie le pays.
objets.fr: Fin de l'interrègne, Mehmet Ier unifie le pays.

objets.nom: Exécution de Sehzade Mustafa qui était le principal prétendant au trône, à cause d'une fausse lettre.
objets.fr: Exécution de Sehzade Mustafa qui était le principal prétendant au trône, à cause d'une fausse lettre.

objets.nom: Le grand vizir Gedik Ahmed Pacha s'empare de Caffa sous le commandement du sultan pour sauver le khanat…
objets.fr: Le grand vizir Gedik Ahmed Pacha s'empare de Caffa sous le commandement du sultan pour sauver le khanat…
objets.notes: le grand vizir Gedik Ahmed Pacha s'empare de Caffa sous le commandement du sultan pour sauver le khanat de Crimée des forces génoises. objets.notes: Most of Hungary under Turkish control. Hungary is divided, by agreement between the Ottoman sultan Suleiman I and Ferdinand I of Austria.

objets.nom: Capture of Muscat
objets.notes: Capture of Muscat. Muscat in the management of the Portuguese Empire, Seized by the Ottomans.

objets.nom: Peace of Amasya signed with the Safavid Empire
objets.notes: Peace of Amasya signed with the Safavid Empire. Western Armenia (Eastern Anatolia), western Georgia (incl. western Samtskhe), and western Kurdistan fall in Ottoman hands. The latter also gained control over most of Mesopotamia (Iraq). Eastern Armenia, Eastern Georgia (incl. eastern Samtskhe), Dagestan, and Shirvan (present-day Azerbaijan Republic)…

objets.nom: The reign of Suleiman the Magnificent (Suleiman I) ends
objets.notes: The reign of Suleiman the Magnificent (Suleiman I) ends. Siege of Szigetvár. Selim II accession to throne.

objets.nom: Ottoman–Venetian War (1570–73)
objets.notes: Ottoman–Venetian War (1570–73). Conquest of Cyprus.

objets.nom: Battle of Lepanto
objets.notes: Battle of Lepanto. The Holy League defeated the Ottomans.

objets.nom: Fire of Moscow (1571)
objets.notes: Fire of Moscow (1571). Crimean khan Devlet I Giray raided the city of Moscow.

objets.nom: Conquest of Tunis
objets.notes: Conquest of Tunis. Selim II death. Murad III accession to the throne.

objets.nom: Selimiye Mosque was built by architect Mimar Sinan between 1569 and 1575.
Treaty of İstanbul between Ottoman Empire and Safavid Persia; Georgia, Azerbaijan and Armenia as well as…
objets.notes: Treaty of İstanbul between Ottoman Empire and Safavid Persia; Georgia, Azerbaijan and Armenia as well as west Iran under Ottoman rule.

objets.nom: Treaty of İstanbul between Ottoman Empire and the Safavids; Georgia, Azerbaijan and Armenia as well as…
objets.notes: Treaty of İstanbul between Ottoman Empire and the Safavids; Georgia, Azerbaijan and Armenia as well as western Iran under Ottoman rule. Reaching the widest border in the east of the Ottomans.

objets.nom: Long Turkish War
objets.notes: Long Turkish War. The series of wars that lasted 13 years, ended with the Peace of Zsitvatorok.

objets.nom: Ottoman–Safavid War
objets.notes: Ottoman–Safavid War. The Ottomans lost all the lands they won with the Ferhat Pasha Treaty.

objets.nom: Kuyucu Murad Pasha suppresses the Jelali revolts.
Kuyucu Murat Pasha suppresses Jelali revolts
objets.notes: Kuyucu Murat Pasha suppresses Jelali revolts. Turkmens suffer heavily.

objets.nom: Treaty of Nasuh Pasha between Ottoman Empire and Safavid Persia
objets.notes: Treaty of Nasuh Pasha between Ottoman Empire and Safavid Persia. Ottoman Empire gives up all gains made by Treaty of Istanbul of 1590.

objets.nom: Treaty of Serav signed with the Safavid Empire after further losses in the Ottoman–Safavid War (1603–18).
Treaty of Zuhab signed with the Safavid Empire
objets.notes: Treaty of Zuhab signed with the Safavid Empire. Roughly restored the borders as agreed per the Peace of Amasya (1555). Decisive partition of the Caucasus, recognition of Ottoman control of Mesopotamia (Iraq). Western Georgia (incl. all of Samtskhe this time) and Western Armenia decisively fall in Turkish hands. Eastern Georgia, Eastern Armenia,…

objets.nom: Deposition of Sultan Ibrahim, enthronement of Mehmed IV.
Köprülü Mehmed Pasha is appointed Grand Vizier, inaugurating the Köprülü political dynasty, a family of…
objets.notes: Köprülü Mehmed Pasha is appointed Grand Vizier, inaugurating the Köprülü political dynasty, a family of viziers, warriors, and statesmen who dominated the administration of the empire during the last half of the 17th century, an era known as the Köprülü era (c. 1656–1703).

objets.nom: Death of Köprülü Mehmed Pasha
objets.notes: Death of Köprülü Mehmed Pasha. His son Fazıl Ahmed Pasha becomes Grand Vizier.

objets.nom: Austro-Turkish War
objets.notes: Austro-Turkish War. War ended with the Peace of Vasvár.

objets.nom: Polish–Ottoman War
objets.notes: Polish–Ottoman War. Ottoman conquest of Kamianets-Podilskyi (Kamaniçe). The war end of the Ottoman Empire reached its maximum size in europe.

objets.nom: Death of Fazıl Ahmed Pasha
objets.notes: Death of Fazıl Ahmed Pasha. His brother-in-law Merzifonlu Kara Mustafa Pasha becomes Grand Vizier.

objets.nom: Buda lost to the Austrian Habsburgs.
Battle of Zenta
objets.notes: Battle of Zenta. Ottoman defeat. Grand Vizier was killed.

objets.nom: Ottomans cede Hungary to Austria in the Treaty of Karlowitz.
Ottomans cede most of Hungary to Austria in the Treaty of Karlowitz.
Revolt of Patrona Halil
objets.notes: Revolt of Patrona Halil. End of Tulip era. Ahmet III is dethroned.

objets.nom: Battle of Çeşme, the first of a number of disastrous fleet battles for the Ottomans against Russia.
First Serbian Uprising
objets.notes: The Serbian Revolution begins.

objets.nom: Kabakçı Mustafa rebellion
objets.notes: Reformist sultan Selim III dethroned. New sultan is Mustafa IV

objets.nom: Alemdar Mustafa Pasha suppresses the rebellion
objets.notes: Alemdar Mustafa Pasha suppresses the rebellion. But Selim III is dead and Mahmut II becomes the new sultan.

objets.nom: Second Serbian Uprising
objets.notes: The Serbs revolt.

objets.nom: Greek War of Independence
objets.notes: The Greek War of Independence begins.

objets.nom: Auspicious Incident
objets.notes: Auspicious Incident. Massacre of the Janissary corps by Sultan Mahmud II: Foundation of a modern western style army.

objets.nom: Algeria is conquered by the French.
Greek War of Independence
objets.notes: Greek sovereignty is formalized.

objets.nom: Crimean War
objets.notes: The Crimean War with Russia began which, though won with British, French and Sardinian aid, would further demonstrate how backward the Ottoman military had become.

objets.nom: Ottomans default on their public debt, having first entered into loan contracts with its European…
objets.notes: Ottomans default on their public debt, having first entered into loan contracts with its European creditors shortly after the beginning of the Crimean War.

objets.nom: Opened the 1876–1877 Constantinople Conference, which ends the Tanzimat reforms after they bankrupt the…
objets.notes: Opened the 1876–1877 Constantinople Conference, which ends the Tanzimat reforms after they bankrupt the Empire.

objets.nom: Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878)
objets.notes: Another war with Russia begins.

objets.nom: Cyprus is occupied by Britain.
Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878): The Treaty of San Stefano recognizes Romanian and Serbian independence,…
objets.notes: Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878): The Treaty of San Stefano recognizes Romanian and Serbian independence, as well as the establishment of an autonomous Bulgarian principality under nominal Ottoman protection. Austria-Hungary occupies Bosnia by default.

objets.nom: Egypt goes under British protection.
The province of Eastern Rumelia is transferred to Bulgarian jurisdiction.
Hamidian massacres, where the Ottoman Empire under Sultan Abdul Hamid II kills between 200,000 and…
objets.notes: Hamidian massacres, where the Ottoman Empire under Sultan Abdul Hamid II kills between 200,000 and 400,000 Armenians in order to reassert Pan-Islamism as a state ideology.

objets.nom: Italo-Turkish War
objets.notes: The Ottomans are defeated by Italy in a short war, with the Italians gaining Libya and ending the 340-year Ottoman presence in North Africa.

objets.nom: First Balkan War
objets.notes: Albania declares independence

objets.nom: The Empire enters into World War I on the side of the Central Powers
objets.notes: The Empire enters into World War I on the side of the Central Powers. Cyprus is annexed outright by Britain.

objets.nom: The Gallipoli Campaign: Under the command of Mustafa Kemal, the Ottoman army successfully repels Britain…
objets.notes: The Gallipoli Campaign: Under the command of Mustafa Kemal, the Ottoman army successfully repels Britain invasion of the Dardanelles in Turkey.

objets.nom: Russian Revolution occurs, ceasing hostilities in the Caucasus, allowing Enver Pasha to establish the…
objets.notes: Russian Revolution occurs, ceasing hostilities in the Caucasus, allowing Enver Pasha to establish the Army of Islam and retake lands in eastern Anatolia from Russia, ultimately to pre-war borders.

objets.nom: Armistice of Mudros, ending hostilities in the Middle Eastern theater of World War I, including Clause…
objets.notes: Armistice of Mudros, ending hostilities in the Middle Eastern theater of World War I, including Clause VII, stating that "The Allies to have the right to occupy any strategic points in the event of any situation arising which threatens the security of the Allies." This clause was subsequently used by the Greeks, Italians, French, and British to…

objets.nom: Treaty of Sèvres, marking the beginning of the partitioning of the Ottoman Empire
objets.notes: Treaty of Sèvres, marking the beginning of the partitioning of the Ottoman Empire. Rejected by Turkish nationalists and eventually leads to the abolition of the monarchy by the Government of the Grand National Assembly based in Ankara.

objets.nom: A Turkish civil code based on the Swiss Civil Code was accepted
objets.notes: A Turkish civil code based on the Swiss Civil Code was accepted. The code granted expanded civil rights to women and prohibited polygamy.

objets.nom: The Surname Law was accepted, abolishing the former titles of Bey, Effendi, Pasha, Sultan, and Hanım as…
objets.notes: The Surname Law was accepted, abolishing the former titles of Bey, Effendi, Pasha, Sultan, and Hanım as of 26 November.

objets.nom: First Democratic Elections in Turkish Republic
objets.notes: First Democratic Elections in Turkish Republic. General İsmet İnönü and his Republican People's Party, which had ruled the country since 1923, loses election to newly formed Democratic Party of Celâl Bayar and Adnan Menderes.

objets.nom: Korean War
objets.notes: The Korean War began. Turkey was a part of the joint UN operation.

objets.nom: Turkey began to host the United States Air Force at the Incirlik Air Base as a deterrent to the Soviet Union.
Istanbul Pogrom
objets.notes: The Istanbul Pogrom started the process of driving many Greeks and Christians from Turkey.

objets.nom: 38 officers of Army form a junta and organize the 1960 Turkish coup d'état
objets.notes: 38 officers of Army form a junta and organize the 1960 Turkish coup d'état. They claim the Islamists had gained influence in the government. After this clash over the "separation of religion and state/government" between İnönü's Republican People's Party and his opponents, democratically elected President Celâl Bayar and Prime Minister Adnan…

objets.nom: After the ending of the 1991 Persian Gulf War, the Incirlik Air Base enforced the northern no-fly zones…
objets.notes: After the ending of the 1991 Persian Gulf War, the Incirlik Air Base enforced the northern no-fly zones in Iraq.

objets.nom: Kosovo War
objets.notes: NATO interceded in the Balkans to end a civil war in the region. Turkey was part of the mission.

objets.nom: Turkey gave NATO the green light and allowed İzmir to become the command center of the operation to oust…
objets.notes: Turkey gave NATO the green light and allowed İzmir to become the command center of the operation to oust Muammar Gaddafi's regime in Libya.

objets.nom: A corruption scandal to topple the ruling AKP failed.
Local elections held with the ruling AK Party displaying an overwhelming victory, especially in the…
objets.notes: Local elections held with the ruling AK Party displaying an overwhelming victory, especially in the motherland of Anatolia.

objets.nom: Turkey starts designing and manufacturing its own national tank Altay, helicopter Atak and drone Anka…
objets.notes: Turkey starts designing and manufacturing its own national tank Altay, helicopter Atak and drone Anka for the first time.

objets.nom: Alleged attempted coup and subsequent crackdowns and purge
objets.notes: Alleged attempted coup and subsequent crackdowns and purge. Over 80,000 arrested or detained, 150,000 dismissed (nearing 10% of public employees).

objets.nom: Istanbul nightclub shooting – At least 39 people were killed and 69 people were wounded in the Reina…
objets.notes: Istanbul nightclub shooting – At least 39 people were killed and 69 people were wounded in the Reina nightclub in Beşiktaş Istanbul.

objets.nom: Presidents of Azerbaijan, Turkey, Georgia inaugurated Trans-Anatolian gas pipeline in the central city…
objets.notes: Presidents of Azerbaijan, Turkey, Georgia inaugurated Trans-Anatolian gas pipeline in the central city of Eskisehir, Turkey with the participation of Petro Poroshenko, and Aleksandar Vucic.

objets.nom: The Turkish Armed Forces launched its Olive Branch land and air operation in north-western Syria,…
objets.notes: The Turkish Armed Forces launched its Olive Branch land and air operation in north-western Syria, capturing large areas which was under Kurdish control.

objets.nom: Turkey confirmed its first COVID-19 case, caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus
objets.notes: Turkey confirmed its first COVID-19 case, caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus. This was quickly followed by the rapid emergence of the COVID-19 outbreak in the country.

objets.nom: To the East of Qahtan A'ad settles Oman.
The Qahtanis began to move to the Tihama coasts and the lowlands
objets.notes: The Qahtanis began to move to the Tihama coasts and the lowlands. A tradeline began to flourish along the red Sea Tihama coasts. During this period the Qahtanis began to settle in small trading colonies in neighboring East Africa.

objets.nom: The Sabaean Kingdom came into existence.
The Qahtanis began using a variant of the Phoenician script; this will lead to the recording of South…
objets.notes: The Qahtanis began using a variant of the Phoenician script; this will lead to the recording of South Arabian history from this point onwards.

objets.nom: Awsan appears as independent nation in a region that will partly controlled by the Qatabanians.
Hadhramawt rise as Sabean vassal kingdom in the region known now (AD 1990) as eastern Yemen.
Ma'een kingdom builds its capital in Baraqish.
The Qatabanians rise as Sabean vassals in the region known now (AD 1990) as central and east Yemen.
The Sabeans build their capital on the edge of the mountains regions in Sirwah.
The temple of Marib is finished.
War between Ma'een and the Sabeans.
After securing their borders with Ma'een the Sabeans moved their capital to the more accessible Marib.
The Sabeans control the trade line and started recording diplomatic relationships with Assyria.
The Qatabanians build Timna and rebel against the authority of Saba.
Karib'il Watar defeats the rebellion and brings all of South Arabia under the Sabean rule.
Saba reaches its height of power and extends its hegemony across the Red sea establishing the Dm't…
objets.notes: Saba reaches its height of power and extends its hegemony across the Red sea establishing the Dm't Kingdom, this will be the nucleus of the Semitic culture of East Africa. Although it is not the first attempt of the Qahtanis to expand their rule to the African coast.

objets.nom: Ma'een establishes itself as the dominant kingdom in the north of Yemen, extending its authority on the…
objets.notes: Ma'een establishes itself as the dominant kingdom in the north of Yemen, extending its authority on the northern Red Sea coasts, and establishes military/trading colonies as far as Sinai.

objets.nom: The Dam of Marib breaks, Saba suffers from drought and rebellions.
The Ma'een kingdom allied with the Qatabanians and Hadramites rebel against Saba and gain their independence.
Qahtani tribes attack the Persians out of Musqat in the Eastern tip of the Arabian peninsula
objets.notes: Qahtani tribes attack the Persians out of Musqat in the Eastern tip of the Arabian peninsula. From that time on Qahtanis replaced the Ancient Arabs 'Ad in Oman.

objets.nom: Himyar rises against Qataban.
Himyar allied itself with most of the Qahatni tribes of the lowlands and central highlands, annexing…
objets.notes: Himyar allied itself with most of the Qahatni tribes of the lowlands and central highlands, annexing most of Saba and Southern Qataban, but Hadhramout repels them.

objets.nom: Himyar starts expanding on the expense of the war-torn kingdom of Saba.
The remains of the Qhatani Jurhum tribe integrate their lineage under Nizar bin Ma'ad bin Adnan
objets.notes: The remains of the Qhatani Jurhum tribe integrate their lineage under Nizar bin Ma'ad bin Adnan. From this point on they become the Adnanites.

objets.nom: Sabean civil war, Himyar closes in on Saba and takes over most of the Sabean central highlands, red sea…
objets.notes: Sabean civil war, Himyar closes in on Saba and takes over most of the Sabean central highlands, red sea coasts territory. Saba breaks into two smaller states in the northern highlands and the desert region around the capital Marib.

objets.nom: The Kahlan tribes remain as the only tribes still loyal to the Sabean state at Marib, Kahlan tribes…
objets.notes: The Kahlan tribes remain as the only tribes still loyal to the Sabean state at Marib, Kahlan tribes cornered in the area between Sana'a and Marib in the north of Yemen.

objets.nom: The Kingdom of Aksum dominates East Africa and takesover the Sabean trading/military colonies.
After the loss of Marib Saba, Kahlans septs Azd, Hamdan, Lakhm, Tai headed north except for the Hashid…
objets.notes: After the loss of Marib Saba, Kahlans septs Azd, Hamdan, Lakhm, Tai headed north except for the Hashid and Bakil tribes of Hamdan of Gurat Saba (جرت) and Kindah in the Ramlah Desert.

objets.nom: Himyar captures most of Qataban.
Hadhramout allies itself with Qataban and Aksum attacking Himyar from the West and the east.
While the Himyarites are fighting the Hadhramout/Qataban alliance in the east, the Aksumites capture the…
objets.notes: While the Himyarites are fighting the Hadhramout/Qataban alliance in the east, the Aksumites capture the Himyarite capital Zafar.

objets.nom: Hadhramout annexes Qataban and reaches its height of power.
The Aksumites attempt to capture Hadhramout from the coast.
During the reign of Sha`irum Awtar the Himyarites/Sabeans attack the Kingdom of Hadhramout from the East…
objets.notes: During the reign of Sha`irum Awtar the Himyarites/Sabeans attack the Kingdom of Hadhramout from the East and capture their capital.

objets.nom: The Gurat Sabeans and Himyar ally themselves against the Aksumites and retake Zafar
objets.notes: The Gurat Sabeans and Himyar ally themselves against the Aksumites and retake Zafar. The Aksumites lose all their territories in South Arabia except for Tihama.

objets.nom: Himyar recaptures Southern Tihama and controls the Major East African ports across from Muza'a
objets.notes: Himyar recaptures Southern Tihama and controls the Major East African ports across from Muza'a. The Aksumites keep the Northern strip of Tihama.

objets.nom: The Kahlani Imran bin Azd branch expel the Persians from Oman.
The Kahlani Jifna bin Azd branch settles Syria and Lakhm settles Mesopotamia.
Himyar annexes the last Sabean enclave to its Kingdom.
Himyar annexes Hadhramout expanding its borders to Dhofar Oman
objets.notes: Himyar annexes Hadhramout expanding its borders to Dhofar Oman. to the East of their borders the Azd bin Imran (Azd Uman).

objets.nom: Himyar annexes Socotra.
From Al-Ramlah in Yemen, Shiekh of Kindah makes alliances with Adnani tribes of Najd.
Abu-Kariba Asad King of Himyar converts to Judaism and spreads the religion in the region.
Himyar appoints Akil al-Murar ibn Amr as the first Hujr of its Northern Kindite colonies.
Amr al-Mansur ibn Hudjr rises his status to the king (vassal to Himyar) and bring the Northern part of…
objets.notes: Amr al-Mansur ibn Hudjr rises his status to the king (vassal to Himyar) and bring the Northern part of the Arabian peninsula under Himyarite control.

objets.nom: Two Jews from Yathrib travel to Himyar in the hope of converting the people of Himyar to Judaism.
King Dhu Nuwas converts to Judaism, he begins a campaign to convert the Himyarites into Judaism
objets.notes: King Dhu Nuwas converts to Judaism, he begins a campaign to convert the Himyarites into Judaism. Himyarites convert in big numbers except in Najran.

objets.nom: At this time Himyar included all the Arabian Peninsula (via Kindah) and he was angered by the Najrani…
objets.notes: At this time Himyar included all the Arabian Peninsula (via Kindah) and he was angered by the Najrani chief refusal to leave Christianity. Dhu Nawas took Najran and massacred 20,000 Najrani Christians.

objets.nom: The Christian Aksumites defeat Dhu Nawas and annex Himyar, starting a period of persecution against the…
objets.notes: The Christian Aksumites defeat Dhu Nawas and annex Himyar, starting a period of persecution against the Yemenite Jews. A third of the population of Yemenite Jews is exiled to Aksum.

objets.nom: The Dam of Marib broke for the third and final time, triggering another migration of Yemeni tribes
objets.notes: The Dam of Marib broke for the third and final time, triggering another migration of Yemeni tribes. The Qur'an itself refers to the collapse of the Marib Dam as a punishment on the Sabaeans for their ungratefulness to God.

objets.nom: Under Khosrau I, Persian forces expel the Aksumites with the help of Dhu Yazin
objets.notes: Under Khosrau I, Persian forces expel the Aksumites with the help of Dhu Yazin. Persians later assassinate Dhu Yazin and try to establish their rule over all Yemen, but they fail and a number of autonomous kingdoms are established.

objets.nom: The final Persian governor of Yemen, Badhan, converted to Islam, thus nominally submitting the entirety…
objets.notes: The final Persian governor of Yemen, Badhan, converted to Islam, thus nominally submitting the entirety of Yemen to the new faith.

objets.nom: Al-Aswad al-Ansi proclaims himself prophet and attracts a large following
objets.notes: Al-Aswad al-Ansi proclaims himself prophet and attracts a large following. He captures Sana'a, but is killed by the Persian shortly after.

objets.nom: Yemen is captured by the pro-Umayyad forces during the First Fitna.
Kharijites under Najda ibn Amir attack Yemen during the Second Fitna.
Imam Zayd ibn Ali, founder of Fiver Islam leads revolt in Kufa against Umayyads
objets.notes: Imam Zayd ibn Ali, founder of Fiver Islam leads revolt in Kufa against Umayyads. The revolt is brutally crushed and Zayd killed. Some followers remained in Medina, when Imam Al-Hadi Yahya would bring Zaidiyyah to Sa'dah in the thirteenth century.

objets.nom: Imam al-Hadi ila'l-Haqq Yahya arrives in Yemen for the first time.
Saladin annexes both the Hejaz and Yemen to his Ayyubid sultanate.
In response to Portuguese occupation of Kamaran island, a fleet from the Mamluk Sultanate attack and…
objets.notes: In response to Portuguese occupation of Kamaran island, a fleet from the Mamluk Sultanate attack and occupy the western and southern shores of the Timurid territory in Yemen.

objets.nom: Ottomans capture Egypt and eliminate the Mamluk dynasty, then move on to Yemen, where they occupy Aden
objets.notes: Ottomans capture Egypt and eliminate the Mamluk dynasty, then move on to Yemen, where they occupy Aden. Sana'a and the rest of Yemen remain under the Zaidi dynasty.

objets.nom: Admiral Sulayman Pasha captures Aden for Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent in order to provide an Ottoman…
objets.notes: Admiral Sulayman Pasha captures Aden for Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent in order to provide an Ottoman base for raids against Portuguese possessions on the western coast of the Indian subcontinent.

objets.nom: The East India Company begins trade in coffee from Mocha, which held a monopoly on the plant at the time.
In response to an incident in which Arab traders plundered a British vessel, Captain Haines sailed…
objets.notes: In response to an incident in which Arab traders plundered a British vessel, Captain Haines sailed against Aden and finding resistance bombards then occupies it for the East India Company's Bombay Presidency, requiring the Sultan of Lahej to accept British protection. Aden will serve as a major refueling port when the Suez Canal opens in 1869.

objets.nom: Yahya Muhammad Hamid ed-Din, a descendant of Imam al-Qasim, becomes Imam and takes regnal name of…
objets.notes: Yahya Muhammad Hamid ed-Din, a descendant of Imam al-Qasim, becomes Imam and takes regnal name of al-Mutawakkil 'ala Allah ("He who relies on God").

objets.nom: At a time when the Ottoman Empire was trying to pacify Albania and was facing hostile moves by Italy…
objets.notes: At a time when the Ottoman Empire was trying to pacify Albania and was facing hostile moves by Italy against Libya, both Imam Yahya and Muhammad ibn Ali al-Idrisi, Emir of Asir rose up against the Turks, causing the Ottomans to send 30,000 troops from Libya to respond. Forced to fight in the highlands, Yemen became "the graveyard of the Turks."

objets.nom: Treaty of Daan
objets.notes: When war with Italy broke out, the Ottomans were forced to accept Zaidi autonomy in the highlands, while remaining in possession of the Red Sea coast. Turkey also provided financial aid to Imam Yahya. The agreement, which conceded most of the demands Imam Yahya had been making since 1908, stopped the almost continuous war between the Turks and…

objets.nom: Turkish governor of Yemen informs Imam Yahya that "Franks" (the European allies) had overrun Anatolia…
objets.notes: Turkish governor of Yemen informs Imam Yahya that "Franks" (the European allies) had overrun Anatolia and that the Ottomans would be forced to withdraw from Yemen. Through a series of alliances, tribal wars and intrigues Yahya would consolidate Zaidi hold over to the south of Sa'da (including Sana'a) and would begin moving north against the Idrisi…

objets.nom: As a concession to pro-Nasserite opinion and to avoid Egyptian aid to republican opposition, Yemen…
objets.notes: As a concession to pro-Nasserite opinion and to avoid Egyptian aid to republican opposition, Yemen enters loose federation with the United Arab Republic to form the United Arab States. The signing ceremony took place in Damascus between Egypt's President Nasser and crown prince Muhammad al-Badr.

objets.nom: During the night, the building in which Imam al-Badr worked was surrounded and shelled by tanks
objets.notes: During the night, the building in which Imam al-Badr worked was surrounded and shelled by tanks. Egypt-backed Junior army officers seize power and proclaim the Yemen Arab Republic, sparking an eight-year civil war between royalists supported by Saudi Arabia and republicans backed by Egypt. The British government, though divided, decides to support…

objets.nom: Two nationalist groups, the Front for the Liberation of Occupied South Yemen and the National Liberation…
objets.notes: Two nationalist groups, the Front for the Liberation of Occupied South Yemen and the National Liberation Front begin an armed revolt (Aden Emergency) against British control in South Yemen. Fighting began in Radfan, but the British quickly subdued it.

objets.nom: Ali Abdullah Saleh receives 99.3% of the vote in the first presidential election by universal suffrage.
While refueling at a water-borne platform off the port of Aden, the USS Cole, a guided-missile…
objets.notes: While refueling at a water-borne platform off the port of Aden, the USS Cole, a guided-missile destroyer, was attacked by terrorist affiliated with Al-Qaeda who detonated C-4 plastic explosives to tear a whole in the hull, killing 17 soldiers. The next day a bomb exploded at the British embassy in Sana'a but resulted in no casualties.

objets.nom: Police crack down on Zaidi demonstrators in capital and arrest large numbers
objets.notes: Police crack down on Zaidi demonstrators in capital and arrest large numbers. Fearing the followers of Hussein Badreddin al-Houthi to be an imminent treat and using claims that they were setting up unlicensed religious centers and engaging in violent demonstrations against the US and Israel, President Selah sends troops to northern province of…

objets.nom: Two packages, each containing a bomb consisting of 300 to 400 grams (11–14 oz) of plastic explosives and…
objets.notes: Two packages, each containing a bomb consisting of 300 to 400 grams (11–14 oz) of plastic explosives and a detonating mechanism, were found on separate cargo planes in transport from Yemen to the United States, an incident since referred to as "the October 2010 (Yemen) incident".

objets.nom: In ceremony in Riyadh President Saleh and opposition politicians sign Gulf Cooperation Council brokered…
objets.notes: In ceremony in Riyadh President Saleh and opposition politicians sign Gulf Cooperation Council brokered deal, whereby President Saleh would step down, transfer executive power to Vice President Hadi and a national unity cabinet would be formed.

objets.nom: Jumaa al-Karama (Friday of Dignity): Massacre of protestors against President Ali Abdullah Saleh leads…
objets.notes: Jumaa al-Karama (Friday of Dignity): Massacre of protestors against President Ali Abdullah Saleh leads to massive protests and the revolution that would end his 22-year rule.

objets.nom: Hours after Houthis force Prime Minister-designate Ahmed Awad bin Mubarak to turn down post, suicide…
objets.notes: Hours after Houthis force Prime Minister-designate Ahmed Awad bin Mubarak to turn down post, suicide bomber detonates bomb near Tahir Square in Sana'a just as a Houthi rally was to begin. Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula takes credit for the attack.

objets.nom: Houthi rebels sign peace agreement brokered by UN envoy Jamal Benomar designed to give the rebels…

Henri Namphy. In September, shortly after the St Jean Bosco massacre, Namphy is overthrown by Gen. Prosper Avril.

objets.nom: Aristide succeeds Préval for a second five-year term

For the next two years, and with Washington's support, Aristide's opponents use the OAS challenge to the 2000 elections to increase economic and political instability. Former Haitian soldiers carry out guerrilla attacks, primarily along the Dominican border and in the capital.

objets.nom: Battle of Muye
objets.notes: The forces of the predynastic Zhou, led by King Wu of Zhou and aided by Shang dynasty defectors, dealt a bloody defeat to Shang forces at Muye, near Yinxu.

objets.nom: Battle of Xuge
objets.notes: Huan, in coalition with the Zhou vassal states Chen, Cai and Wey, led a punitive expedition against Zheng. The coalition was defeated and Huan was wounded.

objets.nom: Battle of Bi
objets.notes: Chu decisively defeated Jin at Bi, near modern Xingyang.

objets.nom: Battle of Yanling
objets.notes: A numerically superior Chu force was defeated by Jin in modern Yanling County. King Gong of Chu was injured.

objets.nom: Battle of Boju
objets.notes: Wu decisively defeated a numerically superior Chu force at Boju.

objets.notes: Weilie recognized the Jin nobles Marquess Wen of Wei, Marquess Lie of Zhao and Marquess Jing of Han as marquesses, granting de jure independence from Jin to the states of Wei, Zhao and Han.

objets.notes: Han forces defeated the people of the Gushi culture, at that time subject to the Xiongnu, at Jiaohe in modern Turpan.

objets.notes: A Han force breached and destroyed a fortress occupied by the Xiongnu chanyu Zhizhi Chanyu at Taraz, killing him.

L'Inde et la Chine espèrent améliorer leurs relations afin de favoriser leurs échanges et leur développement. L'idée d'une immense zone de libre-échange a aussi été évoquée. Cela concernerait 2.5 milliards d'hommes.

objets.nom: Battle of the Altai Mountains
objets.notes: Han and allied forces defeated the army of the Northern Chanyu and accepted the surrender of two hundred thousand Xiongnu soldiers in the Altai Mountains.

objets.nom: Battle of Xiapi
objets.notes: The allied forces of the warlords Cao Cao and Liu Bei defeated an army loyal to Lü Bu in Xuzhou.

objets.nom: Battle of Guandu
objets.notes: Forces loyal to Cao Cao dealt a bloody defeat to Yuan Shao near the confluence of the Bian and Yellow Rivers.

objets.nom: Battle of Red Cliffs
objets.notes: Forces loyal to the warlords Liu Bei and Sun Quan decisively repelled Cao Cao in an attempted invasion across the Yangtze River.

objets.nom: Battle of Tong Pass
objets.notes: Cao Cao defeated an alliance of anti-Han rebels in modern Tongguan County, securing his control over Guanzhong.

objets.nom: Liu Bei's takeover of Yi Province
objets.notes: Liu Zhang, the governor of Yi Province in modern Sichuan and Chongqing, surrendered Chengdu to Liu Bei.

objets.nom: Battle of Fancheng
objets.notes: Cao Cao repelled an attack by Liu Bei's general Guan Yu in modern Fancheng District, at great cost to both sides.

objets.nom: Lü Meng's invasion of Jing Province
objets.notes: Liu Bei's generals Shi Ren and Mi Fang defected to Sun Quan, surrendering to his general Lü Meng the main defense posts of Jingzhou.

objets.nom: End of the Han dynasty
objets.notes: Cao Cao's son Cao Pi forced Xian to abdicate the throne and declared himself emperor of Cao Wei.

objets.nom: Battle of Xiaoting
objets.notes: The Shu Han generals Wu Ban and Feng Xi attacked and destroyed an Eastern Wu army at Wu Gorge.

objets.nom: Two generals of Eastern Wu lead 10,000 expedition troops land on an island known as Yizhou (suspected to…
objets.notes: Two generals of Eastern Wu lead 10,000 expedition troops land on an island known as Yizhou (suspected to be Taiwan or the Ryukyu islands) where most of them die but manage to capture and bring "several thousand" natives back to China

objets.nom: Battle of Wuzhang Plains
objets.notes: Shu Han forces made an orderly retreat from Cao Wei forces on the Wuzhang Plains after Zhuge Liang fell ill and died.

objets.nom: Jiang Wei's Northern Expeditions
objets.notes: Cao Wei pushed back an invasion by the Shu Han general Jiang Wei across the Tao River.

objets.nom: Incident at Gaoping Tombs
objets.notes: Sima Yi took control of the Cao Wei capital Luoyang during Cao Fang and Cao Shuang's absence.

objets.nom: Conquest of Shu by Wei
objets.notes: The Cao Wei general Deng Ai accepted the surrender of the Shu Han emperor Liu Shan outside the capital Chengdu.

objets.nom: War of the Eight Princes
objets.notes: Hui's wife Jia Nanfeng invited troops loyal to his brother Sima Wei into the Jin capital Luoyang to imprison the empress dowager Empress Yang Zhi and her relatives.

objets.nom: The Sui dynasty sends expeditions to an island known as Liuqiu, which possibly is Taiwan, but could also…
objets.notes: The Sui dynasty sends expeditions to an island known as Liuqiu, which possibly is Taiwan, but could also be the Ryukyu Islands

objets.nom: Xuanwu Gate Incident
objets.notes: Gaozu's son Emperor Taizong of Tang assassinated his brothers Li Yuanji and the crown prince Li Jiancheng.

objets.nom: Tang campaign against the Eastern Turks
objets.notes: Tang forces captured the khan of the Eastern Turkic Khaganate in the Yin Mountains.

objets.nom: Emperor Taizong's campaign against Tuyuhun
objets.notes: The Tuyuhun khan Murong Fuyun, in flight from Tang forces and with much of his army destroyed, was killed by his officers.

objets.nom: Emperor Taizong's campaign against Xueyantuo
objets.notes: Taizong sent his general Li Shiji to support the restoration of the Eastern Turkic Khaganate under Qilibi Khan against Xueyantuo.

objets.nom: Battle of Baekgang
objets.notes: The allied navies of Silla and the Tang dynasty defeated a combined Baekje restorationist and Japanese force in the lower reaches of the Geum River.

objets.nom: Battle of Talas
objets.notes: After the defection of their Karluk mercenaries, a Tang force was defeated by a vastly superior Abbasid-Tibetan allied army on the Talas River, probably near modern Talas.

objets.nom: An Lushan Rebellion
objets.notes: The Tang jiedushi An Lushan declared himself emperor of Yan.

objets.nom: Great Anti-Buddhist Persecution
objets.notes: Wuzong abolished Buddhist monasteries as well as establishments of Zoroastrianism and Christianity, which were thought to be Buddhist heresies.

objets.nom: Punti settlement

objets.nom: Founding of Li Ying College
Jingkang Incident
objets.notes: The Song capital Kaifeng fell to a Jin siege. Huizong and Qinzong were captured with much of their court.

objets.nom: Siege of Kaifeng (1232)
objets.notes: The Jin general in charge of the defense of the capital Kaifeng surrendered to the besieging Mongol army. Aizong had fled during the siege; his family members still in the city were executed.

objets.nom: Siege of Caizhou
objets.notes: Aizong passed the throne to his general Emperor Mo of Jin and hanged himself in the face of a Mongol siege of Caizhou. The Mongols breached the city.

objets.nom: Toluid Civil War
objets.notes: Möngke's brother Ariq Böke declared himself khagan of the Mongol Empire.

objets.nom: Sambyeolcho Rebellion
objets.notes: The Sambyeolcho rebelled against Wonjong of Goryeo, the Mongol-allied king of Goryeo.

objets.nom: China's Imperial court found refuge in Silvermine Bay on Lantau Island during the Battle of Yamen
Battle of Yamen
objets.notes: A Yuan fleet destroyed a vastly superior Song force near Yamen. The Song chancellor Lu Xiufu drowned himself with Bing.

objets.nom: Battle of Lake Poyang
objets.notes: A Red Turban fleet commanded by the Hongwu Emperor met a fleet led by Chen Youliang, the self-proclaimed king of the rebel state of Han, on Poyang Lake.

objets.nom: Ming conquest of Yunnan
objets.notes: Basalawarmi, the prince of Liang and a Yuan loyalist, committed suicide during a massive Ming invasion of Yunnan.

objets.nom: Treasure voyages
objets.notes: The Yongle Emperor ordered a fleet of Chinese treasure ships under the command of the admiral Zheng He to reestablish tributary relationships with states in the South China Sea and Indian Ocean.

objets.nom: Tumu Crisis
objets.notes: A Four Oirat force defeated a vastly superior Ming army at Tumu in modern Huailai County and captured the Zhengtong Emperor.

objets.nom: First Manchu invasion of Korea
objets.notes: Nurhaci's son Hong Taiji, the khan of the later Jin dynasty, invaded Joseon.

objets.notes: The Ming governor of Kaifeng destroyed the levees holding back the Yellow River in order to break the siege of the peasant army of Li Zicheng. The resulting flood destroyed Kaifeng and killed some three hundred thousand people.

objets.nom: The Dutch oust the Spaniards in Keelung; so ends Spanish Formosa
Battle of Shanhai Pass
objets.notes: A Shun army was dealt a heavy defeat by the Qing and the former Ming general Wu Sangui at Shanhai Pass.

objets.nom: Yangzhou Massacre
objets.notes: The Qing Dynasty slaughter the inhabitants of Yangzhou city in 6 days according to the contemporary account given by Wang Xiuchu. Xiuchu’s entire account spans 10 days and puts the death toll at 800,000 although Lynn A. Struve conjectures that the city’s population was hardly likely to have been more than 300,000.

Under Sosurim, Goguryeo imports Buddhism from Former Qin of China and adopts it as state sponsored religion.
