objets.notes: Goguryeo attacks Baekje and captures Hanseong (modern day Seoul). Baekje moves its capital south to Ungjin (modern-day Gongju) due to Goguryeo's pressure.

objets.nom: Silla vassalizes Usan (modern-day Ulleungdo).
Silla formally adopts Buddhism after Beopheung of Silla executes Ichadon, a Buddhist convert who had…
objets.notes: Silla formally adopts Buddhism after Beopheung of Silla executes Ichadon, a Buddhist convert who had tried to persuade the king to adopt Buddhism. Before he was executed, Ichadon predicted that milk colored blood would spill from his body after his death. This supposed miracle allegedly occurred according to the Samguk yusa and convinced Silla's…

objets.nom: Taebong ("Later Goguryeo") established in the northwest of the peninsula.
Goryeo completes the reunification of the Later Three Kingdoms, absorbing the entirety of Hubaekje and…
objets.notes: Goryeo completes the reunification of the Later Three Kingdoms, absorbing the entirety of Hubaekje and parts of former Balhae territory.

objets.nom: Tae Kwanghyŏn, the last Crown Prince of Balhae, flees to Goryeo with a great portion of the Balhae…
objets.notes: Tae Kwanghyŏn, the last Crown Prince of Balhae, flees to Goryeo with a great portion of the Balhae royalty and aristocracy and settles with tens of thousands of Balhae households there.

objets.nom: Yi Ŭi-bang overthrows Uijong of Goryeo, beginning a century of military rule known as the Goryeo…
objets.notes: Yi Ŭi-bang overthrows Uijong of Goryeo, beginning a century of military rule known as the Goryeo military regime.

objets.nom: The palace Gyeongbokgung is established in Hanyang.
The palace Changdeokgung is established in Hanyang.
The government research institute Hall of Worthies is established.
Goryeosa compiled.
The Hangul alphabet, created 3 years earlier, is promulgated by King Sejong the Great.
1597: The Chŏngyu War begins.
The Imjin War begins.
The Later Jin invasion of Joseon occurs.
Crown Prince Sado is ordered to commit suicide by his father Yeongjo of Joseon.
11 October – 22 November
objets.notes: 11 October – 22 November. The French conduct a punitive campaign in Korea, but eventually retreat without concessions from the Korean government.

objets.nom: Imo Incident
objets.notes: Mutiny by Korean soldiers in Seoul against the modernization policies of King Gojong.

objets.nom: 31 October
objets.notes: 31 October. The first native Korean newspaper, Hansŏng sunbo, is established by the Joseon monarchy. It is written in Classical Chinese.

objets.nom: July to October
objets.notes: July to October. The first Korean diplomatic mission to the United States also gives rise to the first Koreans to set foot in North America, the first Korean to study abroad in the United States (Yu Kil-chun), and the first Koreans to circumnavigate the globe (Min Yong Ik, Pyon Su, and Soh Kwang-pom).

objets.nom: 25th day, 1st month
objets.notes: 25th day, 1st month. The government newspaper Hansŏng jubo is established. It is the first newspaper written primarily in the Korean language (mixed script) and the first weekly newspaper in Korea.

objets.nom: The beginning of the Donghak Peasant Rebellion prompts the Kabo Reforms in an attempt to prevent Korea's…
objets.notes: The beginning of the Donghak Peasant Rebellion prompts the Kabo Reforms in an attempt to prevent Korea's colonization, and China and Japan fight over sovereignty of Korea in the First Sino-Japanese War.

objets.nom: 8 October
objets.notes: 8 October. Empress Myeongseong is assassinated by Japanese agents.

objets.nom: 1 January
objets.notes: 1 January. Joseon begins to use the Gregorian calendar.

objets.nom: January
objets.notes: January. Independence Gate is constructed in Seoul.

objets.nom: 18 July
objets.notes: 18 July. Landmark newspaper The Korea Daily News, predecessor to today's Seoul Shinmun, is founded by British journalist Ernest Bethell.

objets.nom: Imun Seolnongtang, now the oldest continually operating restaurant in South Korea, opens around this…
objets.notes: Imun Seolnongtang, now the oldest continually operating restaurant in South Korea, opens around this time in Seoul.

objets.nom: Philip Jaisohn becomes the first ethnic Korean to obtain a Western doctorate degree.
Japan–Korea Treaty of 1905. After being forced to sign the treaty, Korea becomes a protectorate of the…
objets.notes: Japan–Korea Treaty of 1905. After being forced to sign the treaty, Korea becomes a protectorate of the Empire of Japan.

objets.nom: 9 September – 15 November
objets.notes: 9 September – 15 November. The Kyŏngsŏng Exhibition () is held in Seoul.

objets.nom: 26 October
objets.notes: 26 October. The Japanese Resident-General of Korea Itō Hirobumi is assassinated by Korean independence activist An Jung-geun.

objets.nom: The Korean enclave Sinhanch'on is established in Vladivostok in Russia
objets.notes: The Korean enclave Sinhanch'on is established in Vladivostok in Russia. It becomes a hub of the Korean independence movement until it is dissolved in 1937.

objets.nom: 9 September – 30 October
objets.notes: 9 September – 30 October. The Chōsen Industrial Exhibition is held at the former royal palace Gyeongbokgung.

objets.nom: 15 April
objets.notes: 15 April. The Jeamni massacre occurs, during which Japanese soldiers lure Korean civilians into a church, kill them, and burn the building to destroy their bodies.

objets.nom: 27 October
objets.notes: 27 October. The kino-drama, Righteous Revenge, widely considered the first Korean film, premieres at Dansungsa. This marks the anniversary of the modern Korean Film Day, although whether it is truly the first Korean film has been disputed.

objets.nom: 8 February
objets.notes: 8 February. Inspired by the promotion of self-determination laid out in the Fourteen Points statement, Korean independence activists in Japan publish a February 8 Declaration of Independence. This directly inspires a similar act in Korea three weeks later.

objets.nom: September
objets.notes: September. Governor-General of Chōsen Hasegawa Yoshimichi resigns and Saitō Makoto replaces him. The period of "Cultural rule" (文化政治; bunka seiji) begins.

objets.nom: 21–26 October
objets.notes: 21–26 October. The Battle of Qingshanli between the Imperial Japanese Army and the Korean Independence Army (led by Kim Chwajin) takes place. Both sides claim victory.

objets.nom: 4 April
objets.notes: 4 April. The Shinhanchon Incident occurs, in which an estimated several hundred Koreans are massacred by the Japanese army in Vladivostok, Far Eastern Republic.

objets.nom: 4–6 June
objets.notes: 4–6 June. The Battle of Samdunja occurs between Korean rebels and the Empire of Japan.

objets.nom: 6–7 June
objets.notes: 6–7 June. The Battle of Fengwudong occurs between Korean rebels and the Empire of Japan.

objets.nom: November
objets.notes: November. The first time a Korean journalist is killed while reporting: The Dong-a Ilbo journalist Chang Tŏk-chun is killed by Japanese soldiers while investigating a Japanese massacre of Koreans in Hunchun, Manchuria.

objets.nom: October
objets.notes: October. The Gando Massacre occurs in Manchuria, where Japanese soldiers kill, rape, and steal from thousands of Korean civilians.

objets.nom: . It was established by the Japanese, who left the graves of Korean royal family members directly on the…
objets.notes: . It was established by the Japanese, who left the graves of Korean royal family members directly on the course (fenced-off area in center of photo; photo published 1925)]]June. The first golf course in Korea is established at Hyochangwon by the Japanese colonial government. The tombs of Joseon royal family members are controversially left…

objets.nom: 28 June
objets.notes: 28 June. The Free City Incident occurs, where Soviet forces kill Korean militants who refuse to surrender to them.

objets.nom: The Chōsen Art Exhibition is held for the first time
objets.notes: The Chōsen Art Exhibition is held for the first time. After 1945, it was succeeded by the Republic of Korea Art Exhibition.

objets.nom: 1 December
objets.notes: 1 December. The Government-General of Chōsen Library is established as part of the cultural rule movement. It is eventually succeeded by the National Library of Korea after liberation.

objets.nom: 1 March
objets.notes: 1 March. The Koryo-saram newspaper Sŏnbong is established. It changed names to the Lenin Kichi in 1938 and Koryo Ilbo in 1991. , it is the oldest active Korean-language newspaper outside of the Korean peninsula.

objets.nom: 1 September
objets.notes: 1 September. In the immediate aftermath of the Great Kantō earthquake in Japan, the Kantō Massacre occurs, and thousands of ethnic Koreans and others are massacred based on false rumors.

objets.nom: 9 April
objets.notes: 9 April. The Chōsen Folk Art Museum is established at Gyeongbokgung.

objets.nom: February
objets.notes: February. Kwon Ki-ok becomes the first female Korean aviator after attending a pilot training school in China.

objets.nom: 10 June
objets.notes: 10 June. The June Tenth Movement pro-independence protests occur and are suppressed.

objets.nom: 30 October
objets.notes: 30 October. The Gwangju Student Independence Movement begins, and is suppressed soon afterwards.

objets.nom: 29 April
objets.notes: 29 April. The Hongkou Park Incident occurs, in which Yun Bong-gil sets off a bomb in a park in Shanghai (now Lu Xun Park), killing several Japanese colonial and military leadership. In the aftermath, the KPG is forced to flee Shanghai.

objets.nom: 9 January
objets.notes: 9 January. The Sakuradamon incident occurs, in which KPO member Lee Bong-chang fails in his attempt to assassinate Emperor Hirohito in Tokyo.

objets.nom: 3 November
objets.notes: 3 November. Runner Sohn Kee-chung becomes the first Korean to win an Olympic gold medal, and sets a world record time. However, Sohn begrudgingly competed as an athlete of the Empire of Japan. The Dong-A Ilbo removes the Japanese flag from his uniform in an image, which leads to retaliation from the colonial government.

objets.nom: November/December
objets.notes: November/December. The KPG flees Nanjing just weeks before the Nanjing Massacre.

objets.nom: September
objets.notes: September. The deportation of Koreans in the Soviet Union occurs, in which roughly 172,000 Koryo-saram are forced to move from the Russian Far East to Central Asia. Many die on the journey.

objets.nom: The KPG settles in Chongqing, where they would remain until the end of the war.
17 September
objets.notes: 17 September. The KPG establishes the Korean Liberation Army, a guerrilla army that was intended to eventually fight to liberate the Korean peninsula.

objets.nom: October
objets.notes: October. The Korean Language Society incident occurs, under which members of the Korean Language Society are arrested and tortured on suspicion that they are Korean independence activists.

objets.nom: 15 August
objets.notes: 15 August. The surrender of Japan and the liberation of Korea. The Korean peninsula is haphazardly divided along the 38th parallel into the Soviet Civil Administration (SCA) in the North and the United States Army Military Government in Korea (USAMGIK) in the South.

objets.nom: 24 July
objets.notes: 24 July. The Bumingwan bombing incident occurs at the building Bumingwan in Seoul.

objets.nom: 8 February
objets.notes: 8 February. At the Yalta Conference, Roosevelt secretly proposes to Joseph Stalin that Korea be placed under a three-way trusteeship, and Stalin mostly agrees.

objets.nom: May
objets.notes: May. The Eagle Project, a joint operation between the KPG and the United States Office of Strategic Services, begins. The mission is halted in late August.

objets.nom: 1 July
objets.notes: 1 July. North Korea creates its first film: Our Construction.

objets.nom: 19 July
objets.notes: 19 July. Lyuh Woon-hyung, whom some Americans had been eyeing as a more moderate alternative candidate for leadership in the South, is assassinated by a member of the far-right terrorist group the White Shirts Society.

objets.nom: April
objets.notes: April. Protests occur in Jeju that lead to the Jeju Uprising and are violently suppressed by 1949. The estimated death toll is uncertain, but a significant portion (up to 30%) of the population is killed. This event and its aftermath significantly threaten the Jeju language, which , is considered critically endangered.

objets.nom: 26 June
objets.notes: 26 June. Kim Ku is murdered in his home by Ahn Doo-hee. The exact motives behind the murder still remain unclear.

objets.nom: 16 May
objets.notes: 16 May. The May 16 coup occurs, in which General Park Chung Hee overthrows the Second Republic of Korea.

objets.nom: 12 October
objets.notes: 12 October. The Sino-Korean Border Agreement is signed, beginning the process of establishing the modern border between China and North Korea. The process finishes with the agreement's 1964 companion, the Protocols on the Sino–Korean Border.

objets.nom: 18 August
objets.notes: 18 August. The Axe Murder Incident in Panmunjom, Joint Security Area. Triggers former North Korean leader Kim Il Sung's first official apology to the South.

objets.nom: 21 May
objets.notes: 21 May. The South Korean film Parasite premieres at the 2019 Cannes Film Festival, and becomes the first Korean film to win the top prize. At the 2020 Academy Awards, it becomes the first Korean film to receive any recognition from the academy, and the first non–English language film to win Best Picture.

objets.nom: 10 December
objets.notes: 10 December. South Korean writer Han Kang becomes the first ethnic Korean and first Asian woman to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.

objets.nom: 27 December
objets.notes: 27 December. Acting president Han Duck-soo is impeached, making deputy prime minister and finance minister Choi Sang-mok the acting president.

objets.nom: Qin armies evict Xiongnu nomadic tribes from their pastures on the Yellow River in the Ordos Loop
objets.notes: Qin armies evict Xiongnu nomadic tribes from their pastures on the Yellow River in the Ordos Loop. Xiongnu leader Touman forced to flee far into the Mongolian Plateau.

objets.nom: Modu Chanyu found the Xiongnu Empire
objets.notes: Modu Chanyu found the Xiongnu Empire. These nomadic peoples would inhabit the eastern Asian Steppe from the 3rd century BCE to the late 1st century CE.

objets.nom: Xiongnu launch second war against the Yuezhi, seizing a large swath of Yuezhi territory (modern day Xinjiang).
Modu Chanyu and the emperor Gaozu of China's Han dynasty sign a peace treaty, recognizing equality of…
objets.notes: Modu Chanyu and the emperor Gaozu of China's Han dynasty sign a peace treaty, recognizing equality of the Xiongnu.

objets.nom: The Battle of Mayi, an abortive ambush operation by Emperor Wu of Han (Han Wudi) against the invading…
objets.notes: The Battle of Mayi, an abortive ambush operation by Emperor Wu of Han (Han Wudi) against the invading Xiongnu forces, begins a decades-long Han dynasty offensive against the nomads.

objets.nom: The Battle of Mobei, Han forces invade the northern regions of the Gobi Desert forcing the Xiongnu to…
objets.notes: The Battle of Mobei, Han forces invade the northern regions of the Gobi Desert forcing the Xiongnu to flee into Siberia. After a series of further defeats, the Xiongnu are expelled from the Ordos Desert and Qilian Mountains.

objets.nom: Various tribes invade the Xiongnu territory from all fronts; Wusun from the west, Dingling from the…
objets.notes: Various tribes invade the Xiongnu territory from all fronts; Wusun from the west, Dingling from the north, Wuhuan from the east, and Han forces from the south.

objets.nom: At the Battle of Zhizhi General Chen Tang and Protector General Gan Yanshou, acting without explicit…
objets.notes: At the Battle of Zhizhi General Chen Tang and Protector General Gan Yanshou, acting without explicit permission from the Han court, kill Northern Xiongnu leader Zhizhi Chanyu at his capital city (present-day Taraz, Kazakhstan)

objets.nom: Tsi Yung, allied with the Wuhuan and Xianbei, attacked the northern Xiongnu kingdom
objets.notes: Tsi Yung, allied with the Wuhuan and Xianbei, attacked the northern Xiongnu kingdom. Xianbei move into Xiongnu territory.

objets.nom: The last khagan of the Xianbei, Kebineng, is assassinated by Cao Wei, successor state of the Eastern Han…
objets.notes: The last khagan of the Xianbei, Kebineng, is assassinated by Cao Wei, successor state of the Eastern Han (25–220). The Xianbei state disintegrates into a number of smaller independent domains (Murong, Tuoba, Khitan people, Shiwei, and Rouran Khaganate).

objets.nom: A branch of the Xianbei, the Rouran (also known as Nirun) establish a powerful nomadic empire over…
objets.notes: A branch of the Xianbei, the Rouran (also known as Nirun) establish a powerful nomadic empire over modern day Mongolia, eastern Kazakhstan, part of Gansu, northern Xinjiang, Inner Mongolia, parts of Northeast China and southern Siberia.

objets.nom: Yujiulü Shelun assumes the title of Khagan, landmarking the establishment of the state of the Rouran…
objets.notes: Yujiulü Shelun assumes the title of Khagan, landmarking the establishment of the state of the Rouran Khaganate.

objets.nom: The Göktürks join the Western Wei, successor state of the Northern Wei, to defeat the Rouran.
The Chinese Northern Qi and Northern Zhou dynasties begin paying tribute to the Göktürks.
The Göktürk Empire, which stretches west to Crimea, is partitioned into Eastern and Western Turkic Khaganates
objets.notes: The Göktürk Empire, which stretches west to Crimea, is partitioned into Eastern and Western Turkic Khaganates. Eastern Turk Göktürks recognize Sui dynasty suzerainty.

objets.nom: Turkic Khaganate revolts against Emperor of Sui and besiege the command seats at present-day Daixian in Shanxi
A Tang army under the command of Li Jing defeats the Eastern Turkic Khaganate under the command of Illig…
objets.notes: A Tang army under the command of Li Jing defeats the Eastern Turkic Khaganate under the command of Illig Qaghan at the Battle of Yinshan

objets.nom: A reunited China—under the Tang dynasty (618–906) destroys the Eastern Türk north of the Gobi and…
objets.notes: A reunited China—under the Tang dynasty (618–906) destroys the Eastern Türk north of the Gobi and establishes the Anbei Protectorate in the Mongolian Steppes. Uyghurs khagan are installed as Anbei protector.

objets.nom: Ilterish Qaghan (682–91) founds the Second Turkic Khaganate by uniting the tribes and subjugating the…
objets.notes: Ilterish Qaghan (682–91) founds the Second Turkic Khaganate by uniting the tribes and subjugating the nine Turkic tribes of the Toquz Oghuz (which included the Uyghurs) and joining with the Sir tribes, Basmyls and Karluks to the west. He would later defeat Chinese armies and raid China.

objets.nom: Ilterish Qaghan of the Second Turkic Khaganate dies and is succeeded by his brother Qapaghan Qaghan.
Qapaghan Qaghan of the Second Turkic Khaganate defeats the Khitans to the east and raids the Tang dynasty.
Uyghur Bayanchur Khan aids Emperor Suzong of the Tang dynasty against the An Lushan rebellion
objets.notes: Uyghur Bayanchur Khan aids Emperor Suzong of the Tang dynasty against the An Lushan rebellion. Approximately 4,000 Uyghur horsemen assisted Tang armies in retaking Chang'an and Luoyang in 757.

objets.nom: The Tang dynasty surreptitiously encouraged the Yenisei Kirghiz and the Karluks to attack the Uyghurs…
objets.notes: The Tang dynasty surreptitiously encouraged the Yenisei Kirghiz and the Karluks to attack the Uyghurs and the Uyghur Khaganate fell under an invasion of the Yenisei Kirghiz

objets.nom: Emperor Shizong of Liao is murdered by a relative and is succeeded by Yelü Jing, son of Emperor Taizong…
objets.notes: Emperor Shizong of Liao is murdered by a relative and is succeeded by Yelü Jing, son of Emperor Taizong of Liao, who becomes Emperor Muzong of Liao

objets.nom: Liao dynasty assists Northern Han in repelling Song dynasty
Emperor Muzong of Liao is murdered by his attendants and is succeeded by Yelü Xian, son of Emperor…
objets.notes: Emperor Muzong of Liao is murdered by his attendants and is succeeded by Yelü Xian, son of Emperor Shizong of Liao, who becomes Emperor Jingzong of Liao

objets.nom: Liao dynasty attempts to assist Northern Han in repelling Song dynasty but is defeated at the Battle of…
objets.notes: Liao dynasty attempts to assist Northern Han in repelling Song dynasty but is defeated at the Battle of Gaoliang River

objets.nom: Emperor Jingzong of Liao dies and his son Yelü Longxu succeeds him as Emperor Shengzong of Liao; Empress…
objets.notes: Emperor Jingzong of Liao dies and his son Yelü Longxu succeeds him as Emperor Shengzong of Liao; Empress Xiao Yanyan becomes regent

objets.nom: First conflict in the Goryeo–Khitan War
objets.notes: Khitans invade Goryeo and acquire nominal tributary status over Goryeo

objets.nom: Emperor Shengzong of Liao conducts a full-scale invasion of the Song dynasty which ends in stalemate and…
objets.notes: Emperor Shengzong of Liao conducts a full-scale invasion of the Song dynasty which ends in stalemate and the Chanyuan Treaty, an agreement to an annual payment of silk and silver from the Song to the Khitans

objets.nom: Second conflict in the Goryeo–Khitan War
objets.notes: Mokjong of Goryeo is murdered by Kang Cho and the Khitans send an expedition to punish him; Kang Cho is killed

objets.nom: Third conflict in the Goryeo–Khitan War
objets.notes: Khitans invade Goryeo but are defeated

objets.nom: Third conflict in the Goryeo–Khitan War
objets.notes: Khitans prepares another army to attack Goryeo

objets.nom: Emperor Shengzong of Liao dies and his son Yelü Zongzhen succeeds him as Emperor Xingzong of Liao;…
objets.notes: Emperor Shengzong of Liao dies and his son Yelü Zongzhen succeeds him as Emperor Xingzong of Liao; Empress Dowager Xiao Noujin becomes regent

objets.nom: Mogusi of the Zubu and the Dilie tribes of western Heilongjiang raid the Liao dynasty
Emperor Taizu of Jin defeats the Khitan army of the Liao dynasty
Emperor Tianzuo of Liao flees the Southern Capital and his uncle Yelü Chun is declared emperor of…
objets.notes: Emperor Tianzuo of Liao flees the Southern Capital and his uncle Yelü Chun is declared emperor of Northern Liao, however he dies three months later and the title is passed down to Yelü Ding, the son in hiding with his father the emperor also in hiding; real power goes to Empress Dowager Xiao Puxiannu

objets.nom: Yelü Dashi leaves the Orkhon River with 20,000 followers and travels to the Kingdom of Qocho where the…
objets.notes: Yelü Dashi leaves the Orkhon River with 20,000 followers and travels to the Kingdom of Qocho where the ruler welcomes him

objets.nom: Yelü Dashi attacks the Karakhanids at Kashgar but is repelled
Battle of Qatwan
objets.notes: Yelü Dashi annihilates the army of Ahmad Sanjar of the Seljuk Empire and vassalizes the Khwarazmian dynasty

objets.nom: Yelü Yilie, son of Yelü Dashi, becomes gurkhan of the Qara Khitai
Temüjin given the title Genghis Khan (Chinggis Khaan), first Khagan (Great Khan) of the Mongol Empire.
Kublai Khan, son of Tolui and grandson of Genghis Khan, becomes fifth Khagan of the Mongol Empire
objets.notes: Kublai Khan, son of Tolui and grandson of Genghis Khan, becomes fifth Khagan of the Mongol Empire. However, the Toluid Civil War begins as various members of the Tolui family line fight for the title of Khagan resulting in the division of the Mongol Empire.

objets.nom: Kublai Khan officially proclaims the founding of the Yuan dynasty with himself as first emperor
objets.notes: Kublai Khan officially proclaims the founding of the Yuan dynasty with himself as first emperor. Khanbaliq (modern Beijing) named the dynasty's capital.

objets.nom: Death of Kublai Khan (aged 78)
objets.notes: Death of Kublai Khan (aged 78). By this time the Mongol Empire had already fractured into four khanates: the Yuan dynasty based in China, the Golden Horde based in Russia, the Chagatai Khanate based in Central Asia, and the Ilkhanate based in Iran, although the Yuan emperors held the nominal title of Khagan.

objets.nom: A peace among the Mongol khanates establishes the nominal supremacy of the Yuan dynasty over the three…
objets.notes: A peace among the Mongol khanates establishes the nominal supremacy of the Yuan dynasty over the three western khanates (the Golden Horde, the Chagatai Khanate and the Ilkhanate). However, the peace itself was short-lived and the war soon resumed.

objets.nom: With the death of Temür Khan (aged 41), Külüg Khan, first son of Darmabala and Dagi of the Khunggirad…
objets.notes: With the death of Temür Khan (aged 41), Külüg Khan, first son of Darmabala and Dagi of the Khunggirad clan, and a great-grandson of Kublai Khan, becomes seventh Khagan of the Mongol Empire and third Emperor of the Yuan dynasty.

objets.nom: Külüg Khan dies (aged 29)
objets.notes: Külüg Khan dies (aged 29). Ayurbarwada Buyantu Khan, second son of Darmabala and Dagi of the Khunggirat, and a great-grandson of Kublai Khan, becomes eighth Khagan of the Mongol Empire and fourth Emperor of the Yuan dynasty.

objets.nom: Enthronement of Öz Beg Khan
objets.notes: Enthronement of Öz Beg Khan. Islamization of the Golden Horde.

objets.nom: Ayurbarwada Buyantu Khan dies (aged 34), Gegeen Khan, eldest son of Ayurbarwada Buyantu Khan and…
objets.notes: Ayurbarwada Buyantu Khan dies (aged 34), Gegeen Khan, eldest son of Ayurbarwada Buyantu Khan and Radnashiri, becomes ninth Khagan of the Mongol Empire and fifth Emperor of the Yuan dynasty.

objets.nom: Death of Gegeen Khan (aged 20)
objets.notes: Death of Gegeen Khan (aged 20). Yesün Temür, son of Gammala, grandson of Zhenjin and great-grandson of Kublai Khan, becomes tenth Khagan of the Mongol Empire and sixth Emperor of the Yuan dynasty.

objets.nom: Jayaatu Khan Tugh Temür, second son of Khayishan, becomes 12th Khagan of the Mongol Empire and eighth…
objets.notes: Jayaatu Khan Tugh Temür, second son of Khayishan, becomes 12th Khagan of the Mongol Empire and eighth Emperor of the Yuan dynasty. The War of the Two Capitals begins. His forces defeated, Ragibagh Khan disappears or dies at the age of 7–8, possibly murdered.

objets.nom: Toghon Temür flees Beijing for Shangdu in advance of approaching Ming dynasty forces
objets.notes: Toghon Temür flees Beijing for Shangdu in advance of approaching Ming dynasty forces. Yuan dynasty falls. The remnants of the Yuan known as the Northern Yuan dynasty continue in Mongolia.

objets.nom: Biligtü Khan Ayushiridara (1340–1378), son of Toghon Temür, is declared Khan of Mongolia at Karakorum
objets.notes: Biligtü Khan Ayushiridara (1340–1378), son of Toghon Temür, is declared Khan of Mongolia at Karakorum. Timur (Tamerlane) gains control of the western Chagatai Khanate.

objets.nom: The Golden Horde is defeated at the Battle of Kulikovo
objets.notes: The Golden Horde is defeated at the Battle of Kulikovo. Karakorum is destroyed by Chinese troops.

objets.nom: Uskhal Khan Tögüs Temür is murdered by an ally of the Oirats, thus launching the Oirat-Mongol wars in…
objets.notes: Uskhal Khan Tögüs Temür is murdered by an ally of the Oirats, thus launching the Oirat-Mongol wars in Northern Yuan dynasty. Jorightu Khan Yesüder (1358–1391) becomes Khan of a fractured and diminished Mongol Khanate.

objets.nom: Timur invades the Golden Horde and sacks Saray and Astrakhan.
Timur dies of illness at Farab (present day Kazakhstan) while preparing for war against Ming China.
Öljei Temür Khan (1379–1412) succeeds his father Elbeg Nigülesügchi Khan and older brother Gün Temür…
objets.notes: Öljei Temür Khan (1379–1412) succeeds his father Elbeg Nigülesügchi Khan and older brother Gün Temür Khan as Khan of the Yuan dynasty.

objets.nom: Oirat nobles place Oyiradai (died 1425) on the throne of Khagan of the Mongol Khan of the Northern Yuan…
objets.notes: Oirat nobles place Oyiradai (died 1425) on the throne of Khagan of the Mongol Khan of the Northern Yuan dynasty following the death of Delbeg Khan

objets.nom: Esen Taishi (Taisun Khan's military commander and later successor as Khan) captures the Zhentong Emperor…
objets.notes: Esen Taishi (Taisun Khan's military commander and later successor as Khan) captures the Zhentong Emperor of the Ming dynasty at the Battle of Tumu Fortress and lays siege to Beijing, but is pushed back.

objets.nom: The Ming begin construction of the Great Wall at the southern edge of the Ordos Desert to contain…
objets.notes: The Ming begin construction of the Great Wall at the southern edge of the Ordos Desert to contain resurgent Mongol tribes.

objets.nom: Madukhai Khatun, widow of the previous Chinggisid khan, marries Batu-Möngke Dayan Khan who defeats the…
objets.notes: Madukhai Khatun, widow of the previous Chinggisid khan, marries Batu-Möngke Dayan Khan who defeats the Oirats, beginning a Chinggisid revival in Mongolia. The Great Horde's attempt to invade Muscovy failed. Their leader Akhmat Khan dies.

objets.nom: The Qing dynasty seizes de facto control of Khalkha by defeating the Dzungars in the Battle of Jao Modo.
The Khoshut Lha-bzang Khan deposes the Sixth Dalai Lama in Tibet and kills the regent Sangs-rgyas rGya-mtsho.
Acting on an appeal by the Tibetan monasteries, the Dzungar army occupies Lhasa and kills The Khoshut…
objets.notes: Acting on an appeal by the Tibetan monasteries, the Dzungar army occupies Lhasa and kills The Khoshut Lha-bzang Khan.

objets.nom: Qing dynasty's Kangxi Emperor drives Dzungar forces from Tibet.
Dawaachi and Amursanaa overthrow the Dzungar ruler in Xinjiang; Dawaachi becomes new Khong Tayiji (ruler).
The Buriat Cossack Dorzhi Banzarov becomes first person of Mongol ancestry to earn a European Ph.D. at…
objets.notes: The Buriat Cossack Dorzhi Banzarov becomes first person of Mongol ancestry to earn a European Ph.D. at University of Kazan in Russia.

objets.nom: People's Revolution of 1921
objets.notes: Revolutionary guerrillas headed by Damdin Sükhbaatar, with the assistance of Red Army troops, defeated the Chinese garrison in Kyakhta.

objets.nom: People's Revolution of 1921: The Russian Red Army, with the support of Damdin Sükhbaatar, defeated the…
objets.notes: People's Revolution of 1921: The Russian Red Army, with the support of Damdin Sükhbaatar, defeated the forces of Ungern-Sternberg.

objets.nom: High-ranking figures, accused of anti-revolutionary conspiracy by Soliin Danzan, were shot dead
objets.notes: High-ranking figures, accused of anti-revolutionary conspiracy by Soliin Danzan, were shot dead. Notable victims included Dogsomyn Bodoo, Dambyn Chagdarjav, and Ja Lama.

objets.nom: 1932 armed uprising in Mongolia
objets.notes: The failure of collectivization led to widespread uprisings and a temporary thaw.

objets.nom: Stalinist purges in Mongolia
objets.notes: A Stalinist terror began which would lead to the deaths of more than thirty thousand people in the Mongolian People's Republic.

objets.nom: Battle of Khalkhyn Gol
objets.notes: Large scale fighting took place between Japanese and joint Soviet-Mongolian forces along Khalkhyn Gol on the border between Mongolia and Manchuria.

objets.nom: The Republic of China requested Soviet help in the war against Japan, and offered recognition of the…
objets.notes: The Republic of China requested Soviet help in the war against Japan, and offered recognition of the independence of Outer Mongolia in exchange according to the Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship and Alliance.

objets.nom: Sino-Soviet split
objets.notes: The MPRP leadership sided with the Soviet Union in a falling-out with China.

objets.nom: The first session of the newly established State Little Khural, the lower house of the People's Great…
objets.notes: The first session of the newly established State Little Khural, the lower house of the People's Great Khural, was convened with 50 members. The office of the Vice President of the Mongolian People's Republic was created with Little Khural chairman Radnaasümbereliin Gonchigdorj as its first and only officeholder.

objets.nom: An election was held for the first unicameral legislature, the State Great Khural
objets.notes: An election was held for the first unicameral legislature, the State Great Khural. The MPRP won a supermajority of 60 seats.

objets.nom: MPRP candidate Natsagiin Bagabandi defeated incumbent president and DUC candidate Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat…
objets.notes: MPRP candidate Natsagiin Bagabandi defeated incumbent president and DUC candidate Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat in the 1997 presidential election.

objets.nom: Macedonian king Amyntas I surrendered to the Thracians.
Sitalces invaded Macedon.
Thracian settlement of modern Plovdiv renamed to "Philippopolis".
Arrival of the Celtic tribes.
Abandonment of Tylis.
Thrace invaded by the Romans
Thrace was conquered by Rome.
The Goths raided Serdica.
The Council of Serdica takes place.
Huns start a fire in Sofia.
Great Bulgaria was formed after the unification of the tribes of Kutrigurs, Utigurs, and Onogurs (Onodonduri).
A peace treaty was signed by Kubrat with the Byzantine Empire.
Khazar's pressure caused Great Bulgaria to decline
objets.notes: Khazar's pressure caused Great Bulgaria to decline. Volga Bulgaria (7th century–1240s) is formed.

objets.nom: Asparukh died in a battle
objets.notes: Asparukh died in a battle. He was succeeded by Tervel.

objets.nom: Tervel received title as Caesar in 705 after recovering the throne of Justinian II.
Tervel died
objets.notes: Tervel died. He was succeeded by Kormesiy.

objets.nom: Sevar died
objets.notes: Sevar died. He was succeeded by Kormisosh.

objets.nom: Kormisosh was disposed
objets.notes: Kormisosh was disposed. He was succeeded by Vinekh.

objets.nom: Vinekh was assassinated
objets.notes: Vinekh was assassinated. He was succeeded by Telets.

objets.nom: Telets was assassinated
objets.notes: Telets was assassinated. He was succeeded by Sabin.

objets.nom: Sabin was disposed
objets.notes: Sabin was disposed. He was succeeded by Umor.

objets.nom: Umor was disposed after a 40-day rule
objets.notes: Umor was disposed after a 40-day rule. He was succeeded by Toktu.

objets.nom: Toktu was killed
objets.notes: Toktu was killed. He was succeeded by Pagan.

objets.nom: Pagan was killed by their servants
objets.notes: Pagan was killed by their servants. He was succeeded by Telerig.

objets.nom: Telerig was baptized after flying to Constantinople
objets.notes: Telerig was baptized after flying to Constantinople. He was succeeded by Kardam.

objets.nom: Kardam was baptized after fleeing to Constantinople
objets.notes: Kardam was baptized after fleeing to Constantinople. He was succeeded by Krum.

objets.nom: Byzantine Emperor Nicephorus I was killed after being involved in the Battle of Pliska.
Krum died
objets.notes: Krum died. He was succeeded by Omurtag.

objets.nom: Omurtag died
objets.notes: Omurtag died. He was succeeded by Malamir.

objets.nom: Malamir died
objets.notes: Malamir died. He was succeeded by Presian I.

objets.nom: Presian died
objets.notes: Presian died. He was succeeded by Boris I.

objets.nom: Boris I ended his rule
objets.notes: Boris I ended his rule. He was succeeded by Vladimir.

objets.nom: Vladimir was disposed and blinded
objets.notes: Vladimir was disposed and blinded. He was succeeded by Simeon I.

objets.nom: Simeon I died
objets.notes: Simeon I died. He was succeeded by Peter I.

objets.nom: Peter I died
objets.notes: Peter I died. He was succeeded by Boris II.

objets.nom: Boris II was killed by Bulgarian border guards after returning to Bulgaria
objets.notes: Boris II was killed by Bulgarian border guards after returning to Bulgaria. He was succeeded by Samuel.

objets.nom: Roman died in a Constantinople prison
objets.notes: Roman died in a Constantinople prison. He was succeeded by Boris II.

objets.nom: Samuel died
objets.notes: Samuel died. He was succeeded by Gavril Radomir.

objets.nom: Gavril Radomir died
objets.notes: Gavril Radomir died. He was succeeded by Ivan Vladislav.

objets.nom: The Byzantine Emperor Basil II annexed Bulgaria after the death of Ivan Vladislav.
Peter II donated his throne to his brother Ivan Asen I.
Ivan Asen I was murdered
objets.notes: Ivan Asen I was murdered. Peter II returned to the throne.

objets.nom: The Byzantine Empire created a large force after merging the eastern and western armies, but the large…
objets.notes: The Byzantine Empire created a large force after merging the eastern and western armies, but the large army was defeated at the Battle of Arcadiopolis.

objets.nom: Peter II was murdered
objets.notes: Peter II was murdered. He was succeeded by Kaloyan.

objets.nom: Siege of Varna (1201)
objets.notes: The Bulgarian Empire and the Byzantine Empire compete for the city of Varna.

objets.nom: Forces of the Latin Empire were defeated by Kaloyan at the Battle of Adrianople.
Kaloyan was murdered
objets.notes: Kaloyan was murdered. He was succeeded by Boril.

objets.nom: Boril was disposed
objets.notes: Boril was disposed. He was succeeded by Ivan Asen II.

objets.nom: Boril died
objets.notes: Boril died. He was succeeded by Kaliman Asen I.

objets.nom: Kaliman Asen I died
objets.notes: Kaliman Asen I died. He was succeeded by Michael II Asen.

objets.nom: Kaliman Asen II was killed
objets.notes: Kaliman Asen II was killed. He was succeeded by Mitso Asen.

objets.nom: Michael II Asen was killed
objets.notes: Michael II Asen was killed. He was succeeded by Kaliman Asen II.

objets.nom: Mitso Asen ended his rule
objets.notes: Mitso Asen ended his rule. He was succeeded by Constantine I.

objets.nom: Ivaylo was killed by the Mongols after arriving at the Golden Horde.
George I went to the Byzantine Empire.
Michael Shishman Bolyar of Vidin.
Battle of Velbuzhd
objets.notes: the Serbians won the battle and the Serbians after the battle dominated Bulgaria.

objets.nom: Ivan Stephen was disposed and went to Serbia.
The capital of the Second Bulgarian Empire, Tarnovo, was captured by the Ottoman Empire.
Karposh's rebellion against Ottoman rule: Strahil Vojvoda captured Kriva Palanka.
Great Plague of 1738
objets.notes: The plague affects Bulgaria.

objets.nom: The Treaty of Belgrade was signed and Habsburg monarchy/Austrian Empire was no longer active against the…
objets.notes: The Treaty of Belgrade was signed and Habsburg monarchy/Austrian Empire was no longer active against the Ottoman Empire for around a century.

objets.nom: Istoriya Slavyanobolgarskaya, one of the first ones and the most important early book about Bulgarian…
objets.notes: Istoriya Slavyanobolgarskaya, one of the first ones and the most important early book about Bulgarian History written by Saint Paisius of Hilendar.

objets.nom: Battle of Kozludzha
objets.notes: The battle took place near Kozludzha, Bulgaria.

objets.nom: The Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca gave Russia the right to interfere in Ottoman affairs to protect the…
objets.notes: The Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca gave Russia the right to interfere in Ottoman affairs to protect the Sultan's Christian subjects, including the Bulgarians.

objets.nom: An important book was written about the history of Bulgaria (История во кратце о болгарском народе…
objets.notes: An important book was written about the history of Bulgaria (История во кратце о болгарском народе словенском) by Spiridon Gabrovski .

objets.nom: Crimean War
objets.notes: British and French troops arrive in Bulgaria.

objets.nom: The Principality of Bulgaria and Eastern Rumelia became united formalized with the Tophane Agreement.
Treaty of Neuilly-sur-Seine
objets.notes: After it was signed at Neuilly-sur-Seine, France, Bulgaria gave away some of their territories

objets.nom: A coup d'état took place that resulted in the assassination of Aleksandar Stamboliyski.
War of the stray dog
objets.notes: The war began with Greece.

objets.nom: Bulgaria declared war on Britain, Yugoslavia, Greece, and the USA. Bulgaria left the war after the…
objets.notes: Bulgaria declared war on Britain, Yugoslavia, Greece, and the USA. Bulgaria left the war after the Soviet Union declared war on Bulgaria.

objets.nom: Georgi Dimitrov became the leader of the communist party.
Georgi Dimitrov died and Valko Chervenkov became the new leader of the communist party.
Pirin Macedonia was declared by Zhivkov as a part of Bulgaria.
Simeon II won in parliamentary elections.
Oktay Enimehmedov attempted to launch a gas pistol at Ahmed Dogan who was the leader of the Turkish…
objets.notes: Oktay Enimehmedov attempted to launch a gas pistol at Ahmed Dogan who was the leader of the Turkish political party. After the gun wasn't successful at releasing a bullet, Enimehmedov was beaten up.

objets.nom: Romanians and Bulgarians can work in the 28 European Union member states after the European Commission…
objets.notes: Romanians and Bulgarians can work in the 28 European Union member states after the European Commission announced it.

objets.nom: The classic Scythian culture spread across the Great Hungarian Plain between the 7th–6th century BC.
Celts invade the Balkan Peninsula from the Middle Danube region, reaching as far as Greece.
The Osi, Cotini and Anarti live in the northern regions of the Great Hungarian Plain
objets.notes: The Osi, Cotini and Anarti live in the northern regions of the Great Hungarian Plain. The Dacians take control of the lands to the east of the river Tisza.

objets.nom: The Dacian king, Burebista, defeats the Celtic ruler, Critasirus, and occupies lands east and north of…
objets.notes: The Dacian king, Burebista, defeats the Celtic ruler, Critasirus, and occupies lands east and north of the Middle Danube.

objets.nom: The Roman generals Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa and Tiberius crush the Pannonian tribes' revolt between the…
objets.notes: The Roman generals Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa and Tiberius crush the Pannonian tribes' revolt between the Sava and the Dráva. The young Pannonians are captured and sold as slaves.

objets.nom: The Germanic tribe of Marcomanni force the Boii to abandon the lands north of the Middle Danube.
The Romans include Pannonia in the Roman province of Illyricum, declaring the Danube as its northern border.
Tiberius wages war against the Marcomanni
objets.notes: Tiberius wages war against the Marcomanni. After the governor of Illyricum, Marcus Valerius Messalla Messallinus, orders the enlistment of the Pannonians in the Roman army, the Illyrian tribes rose up. Tiberius abandons his military campaign along the Elbe to fight against the rebels.

objets.nom: The Sarmatian tribe of the Iazyges settle in the plains between the Danube and the Tisza and force the…
objets.notes: The Sarmatian tribe of the Iazyges settle in the plains between the Danube and the Tisza and force the Dacians to withdraw to Transylvania. Emperor Tiberius settles veterans and civilians at Scarbantia (now Sopron) and Salla (now Zalalövő) on the Amber Road.

objets.nom: Allied with Rome, Vannius, king of the Germanic Quadi, forces the tribes of the Great Hungarian Plain to…
objets.notes: Allied with Rome, Vannius, king of the Germanic Quadi, forces the tribes of the Great Hungarian Plain to pay tribute to him.

objets.nom: Emperor Claudius establishes the colonia (or town) of Savaria (now Szombathely) on the Amber Road,…
objets.notes: Emperor Claudius establishes the colonia (or town) of Savaria (now Szombathely) on the Amber Road, settling veterans of the Legio XV Apollinaris in the town. Colonists from Aquilea and other north Italian towns move to Savaria and natives also live in the town. Pliny the Elder lists the Boii, Azali, Eravisci, Cotini, Arabiates and Hercuniates…

objets.nom: Emperor Claudius forbids the governor of Pannonia, Sextus Palpellius Hister, to assist Vannius against…
objets.notes: Emperor Claudius forbids the governor of Pannonia, Sextus Palpellius Hister, to assist Vannius against his rebellious nephews, Sido and Italicus. Vannius is forced to abdicate and flee to Pannonia. His nephews divide his realm among themselves. Natives are first recruited as auxiliaries in the Pannonian regions north of the Dráva. Auxiliary forts…

objets.nom: The governor of Pannonia, Lucius Tampius Flavianus, intervenes in the struggle for the imperial throne in Rome
objets.notes: The governor of Pannonia, Lucius Tampius Flavianus, intervenes in the struggle for the imperial throne in Rome. He dispatches Roman legionaries and the troops of Sido and Italicus to Rome to fight against Emperor Vitellius.

objets.nom: The Marcomanni and the Quadi refuse to support the Romans during Domitian's Dacian War
objets.notes: The Marcomanni and the Quadi refuse to support the Romans during Domitian's Dacian War. Emperor Domitian invade their territory, but he abandons the military campaign without defeating the Germanic peoples.

objets.nom: A new fortress is built at Brigetio and the Legio XI Claudia is transferred to there
objets.notes: A new fortress is built at Brigetio and the Legio XI Claudia is transferred to there. The Legio X Gemina is stationed at Aquincum. Gorsium (now Tác) is made the center for the imperial cult in Pannonia.

objets.nom: Pannonia is divided into two provinces, Pannonia Superior and Pannonia Inferior.
The Iazyges make raids against Pannonia Inferior
objets.notes: The Iazyges make raids against Pannonia Inferior. Emperor Hadrian charges Marcius Turbo with the united command of Pannonia Inferior and Dacia to secure the coordination of military actions against the Iazyges and their allies, the Roxolani.

objets.nom: The Legio I Adiutrix replaces XXX Ulpia at Brigetio and Legio II Adiutrix takes over Aquincum from X Gemina.
Vexillationes (or detachments) of the Danubian legions are sent to fight against the Parthian Empire
objets.notes: Vexillationes (or detachments) of the Danubian legions are sent to fight against the Parthian Empire. Marcus Aurelius plans to annex the territory of the Marcomanni and Iazyges and establishes two new legions, Legio II Italica and Legio III Italica.

objets.nom: Emperor Marcus Aurelius transfers the Legio II Adiutrix to the empire's eastern border at the beginning…
objets.notes: Emperor Marcus Aurelius transfers the Legio II Adiutrix to the empire's eastern border at the beginning of the Roman–Parthian War, replacing it with Legio IV Flavia Felix in Aquincum.

objets.nom: Start of the Marcomannic Wars
objets.notes: Start of the Marcomannic Wars. The Germanic Lombards and Ubii attack Pannonia near Brigetio, but the Roman troops defeat them. Ballomar, the king of the Marcomanni, and envoys from 10 other tribes dwelling along the Roman border enter into negotiations with the governor of Pannonia Superior, Marcus Jallius Bassus.

objets.nom: The Romans route the Iazyges
objets.notes: The Romans route the Iazyges. The Iazyges capture their king, Banadaspus, and elect Zanticus his successor.

objets.nom: Septimius Severus sends his son and heir, Caracalla, to Pannonia before his campaign against Clodius Albinus.
Emperor Philip the Arab appoints Pacatianus the commander of the troops both in Pannonia Inferior and in…
objets.notes: Emperor Philip the Arab appoints Pacatianus the commander of the troops both in Pannonia Inferior and in Moesia Superior. The Illyricianithe troops of the Danubian provincesproclaim Pacatianus emperor, but they murder him when the Emperor appoints one of their number, Decius, their commander.

objets.nom: The westward expansion of the Goths forces the Germanic Gepids and the Sarmatian Roxolani to move to the…
objets.notes: The westward expansion of the Goths forces the Germanic Gepids and the Sarmatian Roxolani to move to the Carpathian Basin. Sarmatian and Germanic tribes make a series of raids against Pannonia. Emperor Gallienus settles groups of Marcomanni in Pannonia.

objets.nom: Both Pannonian provinces are divided into two, with their parts north of the Dráva forming Pannonia…
objets.notes: Both Pannonian provinces are divided into two, with their parts north of the Dráva forming Pannonia Prima and Pannonia Valeria provinces.

objets.nom: A canal is built between the Lake Balaton and the Danube.
Battle of Cibalae
objets.notes: Constantine defeats Licinius, forcing him to abandon Pannonia.

objets.nom: The Goths invade Sarmatian territory, forcing the Argaragantes (the ruling Sarmatians) to arm their…
objets.notes: The Goths invade Sarmatian territory, forcing the Argaragantes (the ruling Sarmatians) to arm their unfree subjects, the Limigantes. The Romans intervene in the war on the Sarmatians' behalf and defeat the Goths. The Limigantes rose up and defeat the Argaragantes who flee to Vandal and Roman territory.

objets.nom: Emperor Valentinian I's magister militum, Aequitius, had new fortresses built along the Middle Danube.
Goths, Alans and Huns invade the Balkan provinces and Pannonia after their victory over the Romans in…
objets.notes: Goths, Alans and Huns invade the Balkan provinces and Pannonia after their victory over the Romans in the Battle of Adrianople.

objets.nom: The attacks of the Marcomanni, Hun and Goth armies devastate Pannonia.
The Visigoths led by Alaric arrives in Pannonia from Italy.
Pannonia Secunda and Pannonia Savia are ceded to the Huns.
After Attila's death, three Ostrogoth kingdoms come into existence
objets.notes: After Attila's death, three Ostrogoth kingdoms come into existence. Western Pannonia is ruled by Theodemir, Vidimir controls the center region, the eastern parts of Pannonia belong to king Valamir.

objets.nom: Successful campaigns by the Western Roman emperor Avitus in Pannonia, praised later by Sidonius Apollinaris.
The Langobards settle in Pannonia, permitted by Justinian I.
At the end of the reign of Justinian I, the Gepid-controlled Pannonian settlement of Sirmium is still a…
objets.notes: At the end of the reign of Justinian I, the Gepid-controlled Pannonian settlement of Sirmium is still a significant city, subsequently occupied by Justin II.

objets.nom: The Longobard king, Alboin, sends envoys to the Avar khagan, Bayan, offering an alliance against the…
objets.notes: The Longobard king, Alboin, sends envoys to the Avar khagan, Bayan, offering an alliance against the Gepids to him. Bayan accepts the offer only after Gepidia is promised to him.

objets.nom: The Longobards and the Avars invade Gepidia
objets.notes: The Longobards and the Avars invade Gepidia. Cunimund, the last king of the Gepids, dies fighting against the Longobards. The Avars occupy Gepidia.

objets.nom: The Avars, under Khagan Bayan I established an empire in the Carpathian Basin.
The Kutrigurs, related peoples from the east arrived in the Avar Kaganate.
The Onogurs
objets.notes: The Onogurs. related peoples from the east arrived in the Avar Kaganate.

objets.nom: The Avar khagan and send envoys to Charlemagne to Paderborn.
Charlemagne invades Avar territory, reaching as far as the river Rába, but an epidemic forces him to…
objets.notes: Charlemagne invades Avar territory, reaching as far as the river Rába, but an epidemic forces him to return to the Carolingian Empire.

objets.nom: Duke Eric of Friuli's Slav military commander, Vojnomir, sacks the khagan's seat.
Pepin of Italy invades Avar territory, forcing the khagan to yield without resistance and chasing Avar…
objets.notes: Pepin of Italy invades Avar territory, forcing the khagan to yield without resistance and chasing Avar leaders as far as the river Tisza. Paulinus II, Patriarch of Aquileia and other bishops in Pepin's army decide to start proselytizing among the Avars.

objets.nom: Archbishop Arno of Salzburg appoints Theoderic to proselytize among the Carantans and their neighbors to…
objets.notes: Archbishop Arno of Salzburg appoints Theoderic to proselytize among the Carantans and their neighbors to the north of the river Dráva. Gerold, Prefect of Bavaria who accompanies Theoderic is killed before a battle against rebellious Avars.

objets.nom: Charlemagne cedes the territory between Sabaria (now Szombathely in Hungary) and Carnuntum (now…
objets.notes: Charlemagne cedes the territory between Sabaria (now Szombathely in Hungary) and Carnuntum (now Petronell-Carnuntum in Austria) to the Christian Avar kapkhan, Theodorus, and his people whom Slavs forced to leave their homeland.

objets.nom: Krum, Khan of Bulgaria, invades Avar territory and defeats an Avar army.
Battle of Pliska
objets.notes: The Hungarians were in alliance with Krum of Bulgaria against Emperor Nikephoros.

objets.nom: The Magyars settle in Etelköz (in the Pontic steppes) and get rid of Khazar suzerainty
objets.notes: The Magyars settle in Etelköz (in the Pontic steppes) and get rid of Khazar suzerainty. The Kabarsa group of peoples who rose up against the Khaganjoin them.

objets.nom: Expelled across the Danube by Prince Mojmir I of Moravia, Pribina comes to Pannonia
objets.notes: Expelled across the Danube by Prince Mojmir I of Moravia, Pribina comes to Pannonia. He is baptised and joins the retinue of Radbod, the newly appointed prefect of the March of Pannonia.

objets.nom: The Bulgarians hire Magyar warriors to prevent a group of Byzantine prisoners from returning to their…
objets.notes: The Bulgarians hire Magyar warriors to prevent a group of Byzantine prisoners from returning to their homeland across the Lower Danube, but the Byzantines defeat the Magyars.

objets.nom: Liupramm, Archbishop of Salzburg consecrates a church dedicated to Mary the Virgin in Mosaburg.
The Hungarians took possession of the Carpathian Basin in a pre-planned manner, with a long move-in…
objets.notes: The Hungarians took possession of the Carpathian Basin in a pre-planned manner, with a long move-in between 862 and 895.

objets.nom: The Byzantine missionaries, Constantine and Methodius, stay in Mosaburg during their journey from…
objets.notes: The Byzantine missionaries, Constantine and Methodius, stay in Mosaburg during their journey from Moravia to Rome. Kocel learns the Glagolitic script and entrust 50 pupils to them.

objets.nom: Pope Hadrian II sanctions the use of Old Church Slavonic in liturgy
objets.notes: Pope Hadrian II sanctions the use of Old Church Slavonic in liturgy. Methodius returns to Mosaburg as papal legate, but Kocel sends him back to Rome, requesting the Pope to appoint Methodius bishop of Pannonia. The Pope makes Methodius archbishop of Sirmium with jurisdiction in Pannonia and Moravia.

objets.nom: The Magyars dominate the steppes between the Lower Danube and the river "Atil" (most probably the Don River)
objets.notes: The Magyars dominate the steppes between the Lower Danube and the river "Atil" (most probably the Don River). Their tribal confederation is headed by a paramount chief, the kende, and a military leader, the gyula.

objets.nom: Magyar raiders destroy Pannonia in alliance with Svatopluk I. After the Magyar leaders, Árpád and…
objets.notes: Magyar raiders destroy Pannonia in alliance with Svatopluk I. After the Magyar leaders, Árpád and Kurszán conclude an alliance with the Byzantines against King Simeon I of Bulgaria, Magyar troops invade Bulgaria.

objets.nom: Battle of Brenta
objets.notes: the Hungarians route Arnulf's opponent, King Berengar I of Italy.

objets.nom: Battle of Augsburg
objets.notes: An important victory by a Hungarian army over the combined forces of East Francia and Swabia under the nominal command of Louis the Child.

objets.nom: Battle of Eisenach
objets.notes: A crushing victory by a Hungarian army over an East Frankish army composed of troops from Franconia, Saxony, and Thuringia.

objets.nom: Battle of Pressburg
objets.notes: Three East Francian armies led by Luitpold, Margrave of Bavaria, which entered the Hungarian territory in order to expel the Hungarians from the Carpathian Basin, is annihilated by the Hungarian army. Luitpold, Margrave of Bavaria, Dietmar I, Archbishop of Salzburg, Prince Sieghard, 19 counts, 2 bishops, and 3 abbots are killed in the battle,…

objets.nom: Battle of Rednitz
objets.notes: The Hungarian army entered Franconia, and defeated a united army of the duchies of Franconia, Lotharingia and Bavaria.

objets.nom: Battle of Püchen
objets.notes: Hungarian victory over Henry the Fowler, the East Francian king.

objets.nom: Battle of Riade
objets.notes: Henry I defeats the Hungarians who has invaded the Duchy of Saxony.

objets.nom: A high-ranking Magyar chieftain, the horka Bulcsú visited the court of Byzantine Emperor Constantine…
objets.notes: A high-ranking Magyar chieftain, the horka Bulcsú visited the court of Byzantine Emperor Constantine VII, where he was received with a great pomp. Bulcsú adopted Christianity, the emperor became his godfather. He was a "guest friend of the Byzantine emperor" and was awarded the title of "Roman patrician".

objets.nom: The second-ranking Magyar chieftain, Gylas, is baptised in Constantinople
objets.notes: The second-ranking Magyar chieftain, Gylas, is baptised in Constantinople. The Ecumenical Patriarch consecrates a Greek monk, Hierotheos, bishop of Tourkia (or Hungary) and Hierotheos accompanies Gylas back to Hungary.

objets.nom: Second Battle of Lechfeld
