objets.fr: Le Pacte à quatre est signé à Rome par l'Italie, la France, le Royaume-Uni et l'Allemagne.

objets.nom: Tentative de putsch des nazis autrichiens qui assassinent le chancelier Engelbert Dollfuss et réclament…
objets.fr: Tentative de putsch des nazis autrichiens qui assassinent le chancelier Engelbert Dollfuss et réclament…
objets.notes: tentative de putsch des nazis autrichiens qui assassinent le chancelier Engelbert Dollfuss et réclament le rattachement de l'Autriche a l'Allemagne (Anschluss). Mussolini s'y oppose en envoyant deux divisions au col du Brenner.

objets.nom: Conférence de Munich où Mussolini, Hitler, Daladier pour la France et Chamberlain pour le Royaume-Uni…
objets.fr: Conférence de Munich où Mussolini, Hitler, Daladier pour la France et Chamberlain pour le Royaume-Uni…
objets.notes: conférence de Munich où Mussolini, Hitler, Daladier pour la France et Chamberlain pour le Royaume-Uni accordent au Troisième Reich la région des Sudètes prise à la Tchecoslovaquie.

objets.nom: 9 juillet, le CSIR, confié au général Italo Gariboldi (qui remplace le général Giovanni Messe), se…
objets.fr: 9 juillet, le CSIR, confié au général Italo Gariboldi (qui remplace le général Giovanni Messe), se…
objets.notes: 9 juillet, le CSIR, confié au général Italo Gariboldi (qui remplace le général Giovanni Messe), se transforme en ARMIR (armée italienne en Russie) et compte hommes.

objets.nom: Signature des accords de Paris qui reprennent les principes définis à Londres
objets.fr: Signature des accords de Paris qui reprennent les principes définis à Londres
objets.notes: signature des accords de Paris qui reprennent les principes définis à Londres. Mise en place de l'Union de l'Europe occidentale (UEO) qui se base sur le traité de Bruxelles modifié (Londres-Paris, 3-23 oct), auquel adhèrent la RFA et l'Italie, autorisant leur réarmement. L'Union soviétique proteste contre ces accords et renouvelle sa proposition…

objets.nom: Signature du traité de Rome : création, au 1 janvier 1958, de la Communauté économique européenne (CEE)…
objets.fr: Signature du traité de Rome : création, au 1 janvier 1958, de la Communauté économique européenne (CEE)…
objets.notes: signature du traité de Rome : création, au 1 janvier 1958, de la Communauté économique européenne (CEE) et de l'Euratom, ou Communauté européenne de l'énergie atomique (CEEA). Le processus d'intégration des pays européens prend une nouvelle dimension avec cette alliance regroupant la Belgique, la République fédérale d'Allemagne, la France,…

objets.nom: Ouverture à la circulation du tunnel du Grand-Saint-Bernard entre la Suisse et l'Italie.
objets.fr: Ouverture à la circulation du tunnel du Grand-Saint-Bernard entre la Suisse et l'Italie.

objets.nom: Inauguration du tunnel du Mont-Blanc par le président Giuseppe Saragat et le général de Gaulle.
objets.fr: Inauguration du tunnel du Mont-Blanc par le président Giuseppe Saragat et le général de Gaulle.

objets.nom: Inondations catastrophiques à Florence et à Venise.
objets.fr: Inondations catastrophiques à Florence et à Venise.

objets.nom: Bologna massacre
objets.notes: a terrorist bombing of the Central Station at Bologna kills 85 people and wounds more than 200. This was found to be a neo-fascist bombing, mainly organized by the Nuclei Armati Rivoluzionari: Francesca Mambro and Valerio Fioravanti were sentenced to life imprisonment. In April 2007 the Supreme Court confirmed the conviction of Luigi Ciavardini, a…

objets.nom: Ustica Massacre
objets.notes: a DC-9 operated by Itavia crashes into the Tyrrhenian Sea between Ponza and Ustica, killing all 81 people on board. The disaster led to numerous investigations, legal actions, and accusations, and continues to be a source of speculation, including claims of conspiracy by the Italian government and others.

objets.nom: En réponse à la crise albanaise de 1997, le Conseil de sécurité des Nations unies vote par la résolution…
objets.fr: En réponse à la crise albanaise de 1997, le Conseil de sécurité des Nations unies vote par la résolution…
objets.notes: en réponse à la crise albanaise de 1997, le Conseil de sécurité des Nations unies vote par la résolution 1101 l'envoi de l', mission de maintien de la paix sous commandement italien ; déployée du 15 avril au 3 août 1997, elle mobilise 7230 hommes dont 3800 Italiens.

objets.nom: Honorius gave land in Gallia Aquitania to his Visigoth federates in which to settle, forming the nucleus…
objets.notes: Honorius gave land in Gallia Aquitania to his Visigoth federates in which to settle, forming the nucleus of the future Visigothic Kingdom under king Wallia and then his son and heir Theodoric I.

objets.nom: Battle of Châlons: Romans, Visigoths under Theodoric I and their allies (including the Franks)…
objets.notes: Battle of Châlons: Romans, Visigoths under Theodoric I and their allies (including the Franks) definitively stop further Hunnic invasion in Gaul. Theodoric I died during the battle, he was succeeded by his son Thorismund who also had a decisive role during the battle.

objets.nom: The Domain of Soissons, last Roman province of Gaul, was created with Aegidius as magister militum of…
objets.notes: The Domain of Soissons, last Roman province of Gaul, was created with Aegidius as magister militum of the rump state.

objets.nom: Gothic war against Aegidius: Aegidius and Childeric I defeated the invading Visigoths in Orléans.
Theodoric II was murdered and succeeded by his younger brother Euric as king of the Visigoths, declaring…
objets.notes: Theodoric II was murdered and succeeded by his younger brother Euric as king of the Visigoths, declaring total independence from Roman influence and extending during his reign the Visigothic kingdom to most of the Iberian Peninsula.

objets.nom: Franco-Roman War of 486: Battle of Soissons: A Frankish army under Clovis I defeated Syagrius and…
objets.notes: Franco-Roman War of 486: Battle of Soissons: A Frankish army under Clovis I defeated Syagrius and conquered the Domain of Soissons. Syagrius sought refuge in Alaric II's kingdom, but was later handed back to Clovis and beheaded.

objets.nom: Franco-Gothic War (507–511)
objets.notes: Clovis defeated a Visigoth army under Alaric II in the Battle of Vouillé, and conquered Gallia Aquitania, thus forming the basis of modern-day France.

objets.nom: Clovis died
objets.notes: Clovis died. His kingdom was divided among his four sons; the territory with its seat at Paris went to Childebert I, the kingdom of Soissons went to Chlothar I, the kingdom of Orléans went to Chlodomer, and the kingdom of Rheims (Austrasia) went to Theuderic I.

objets.nom: Battle of Vézeronce
objets.notes: The united armies of Clovis' sons inflicted a serious defeat on the Burgundian king Godomar. Chlodomer, the king of Orléans, was killed in battle.

objets.nom: Chlothar I died
objets.notes: Chlothar I died. The kingdom was divided among his four sons; Paris went to Charibert I, Burgundy to Guntram, Austrasia to Sigebert I, Soissons to Chilperic I.

objets.nom: Childebert II died, his kingdom was divided between his two sons
objets.notes: Childebert II died, his kingdom was divided between his two sons. The kingdom of Austrasia went to Theudebert II, the kingdom of Burgundy to Theuderic II.

objets.nom: Sigebert II, the king of Burgundy and Austrasia, was executed by Chlothar II, who inherited his kingdoms…
objets.notes: Sigebert II, the king of Burgundy and Austrasia, was executed by Chlothar II, who inherited his kingdoms thus becoming sole king of the Franks.

objets.nom: Chlothar II died
objets.notes: Chlothar II died. Under an agreement forged after his death, Dagobert I succeeded him as king of Neustria but ceded what would become Aquitaine to his brother, Charibert II.

objets.nom: Chlothar III died
objets.notes: Chlothar III died. His kingdom was divided between his two younger brothers; Austrasia to Childeric II, and Neustria to Theuderic III (roi fainéant).

objets.nom: Battle of Tours
objets.notes: Frankish and Burgundian soldiers under the Mayor of the Palace Charles Martel inflicted a significant defeat on the invading armies of the Umayyad Caliphate.

objets.nom: Childeric III was dethroned as the last king of the Merovingian dynasty, Pepin the Short was later…
objets.notes: Childeric III was dethroned as the last king of the Merovingian dynasty, Pepin the Short was later crowned king of the Franks, thus starting the rule of the Carolingian dynasty.

objets.nom: Treaty of Verdun
objets.notes: An alliance between Louis the German and Charles the Bald, and their victories over Lothair I, compelled the elder brother to negotiate the division of the Frankish Empire. It was divided in three parts; West Francia for Charles the Bald, Middle Francia for Lothair I and East Francia for Louis the German, hence laying the foundations of modern…

objets.nom: Battle of Andernach
objets.notes: After Louis the German's death, Charles the Bald is badly defeated at Andernach by Louis' successor, Carloman of Bavaria, in an attempt to conquer his late brother's kingdom.

objets.nom: Carloman II dies, his cousin Charles the Fat (Louis the German's youngest son) already king of East…
objets.notes: Carloman II dies, his cousin Charles the Fat (Louis the German's youngest son) already king of East Francia, succeeds in the rule of West Francia reviving until his death the entire Carolingian Empire.

objets.nom: Odo of France dies leaving no surviving heir
objets.notes: Odo of France dies leaving no surviving heir. Charles the Simple, son of Louis the Stammerer, is declared king of West Francia, the Carolingian dynasty is thus again ruler of France.

objets.nom: Charles signed the Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte with Rollo, the king of the Vikings, allowing their…
objets.notes: Charles signed the Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte with Rollo, the king of the Vikings, allowing their settlement in what would become the Duchy of Normandy.

objets.nom: Battle of Soissons (923)
objets.notes: Robert was killed. Charles was captured by Rudolph, the duke of Burgundy.

objets.nom: Battle of Bouvines
objets.notes: The French army defeated a combined English–Flemish force, enabling the kingdom to consolidate its control over Anjou, Brittany, Maine, Normandy and the Touraine.

objets.nom: Louis IX announced that the County of Poitiers would go to his brother Alphonse – offending Isabella of…
objets.notes: Louis IX announced that the County of Poitiers would go to his brother Alphonse – offending Isabella of Angoulême, whose son would have inherited the territory had the English won the Battle of Bouvines.

objets.nom: Saintonge War
objets.notes: Henry III of England arrived with an army in support of Isabella's claim to Poitiers.

objets.nom: Battle of the Golden Spurs
objets.notes: Flemish insurrectionists soundly defeated a French occupation force.

objets.nom: Bruges Matins
objets.notes: The exiled citizens of Bruges, in Flanders, returned to their hometown and killed every Frenchman.

objets.nom: Battle of Agincourt
objets.notes: A major loss to the French in the Hundred Years' War (1415–1429)

objets.nom: Hundred Years' War (1415–1429)
objets.notes: An English army under King Henry V landed in the north of France.

objets.nom: The army of John the Fearless, duke of Burgundy, captured Paris
objets.notes: The army of John the Fearless, duke of Burgundy, captured Paris. The dauphin, the future Charles VII, fled.

objets.nom: Battle of Castillon
objets.notes: In what is considered the last battle of the Hundred Years' War, the French inflict a decisive victory on the English army, eventually gaining back all English-held territories of France.

objets.nom: War of the League of Cambrai
objets.notes: Representatives of the Papacy, France, and the Holy Roman Empire and Ferdinand I of Spain established the League of Cambrai, whose purpose was to defeat Venice and partition its territory.

objets.nom: Henry III died with no heir, thus ending the reign of the Valois branch of the Capetian dynasty
objets.notes: Henry III died with no heir, thus ending the reign of the Valois branch of the Capetian dynasty. He was succeeded by Henry IV, the first monarch of the House of Bourbon.

objets.nom: Fronde
objets.notes: Cardinal Mazarin ordered the arrest of the leaders of the parlement of Paris, which provoked widespread rioting.

objets.nom: Thirty Years' War
objets.notes: The Peace of Westphalia ended the war with France obtaining the better bargain, and annexing eastern territories.

objets.nom: Franco-Spanish War
objets.notes: Victorious France signs the Treaty of the Pyrenees with Spain and annexes northern Catalonia and French Flanders. The war confirms France as the dominant continental power and Bourbon strength over the Habsburgs.

objets.nom: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle
objets.notes: end of the War of Devolution. France obtains Lille and other territories of Flanders from Spain.

objets.nom: Treaties of Nijmegen
objets.notes: A series of treaties ending the Franco-Dutch War. France obtains the Franche-Comté and some cities in Flanders and Hainaut (from Spain).

objets.nom: Truce of Ratisbon
objets.notes: End of the War of the Reunions. France obtains further territories in the north-west from Spain.

objets.nom: Treaty of Ryswick
objets.notes: End of the Nine Years' War between France and the Grand Alliance. Territorial changes were made in Europe and the colonial empires of the countries involved.

objets.nom: Battle of Carpi
objets.notes: In what was the first battle of the War of the Spanish Succession, Austrian invaders encountered the French army at Carpi, and defeated them.

objets.nom: War of the Spanish Succession
objets.notes: France and England signed the Treaty of Utrecht, under which Philip V of Spain renounced for himself and his descendants any right to the French throne. Similarly, possible heirs to the French crown renounced all rights to the rulership of Spain.

objets.nom: Treaty of The Hague
objets.notes: France and its allies signed a treaty with Spain, thus ending the War of the Quadruple Alliance.

objets.nom: Treaty of Vienna
objets.notes: The signing of the treaty ended the War of the Polish Succession. France gained the Duchy of Lorraine and Bar.

objets.nom: War of the Austrian Succession
objets.notes: French forces defeat an Anglo-Dutch-Hanoverian army at the Battle of Fontenoy; Louis XV, and his son, the Dauphin, were present at the battle.

objets.nom: Yew Tree Ball
objets.notes: Masked ball given by the Louis XV in the Grand Gallery of the Chateau of Versailles, on the occasion of the marriage of Louis, Dauphin of France with Maria Teresa, Infanta of Spain. Fifteen thousand people attended including Jeanne Antoinette Poisson who met with the King for a second time.

objets.nom: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle
objets.notes: The signing of the treaty, dictated by France and Britain, ended the War of the Austrian Succession. The French population was dissatisfied with the terms, considering the French conquests during the war.

objets.nom: Seven Years' War
objets.notes: France and some allied and enemy nations sign the Treaty of Paris ending the Seven Years' War, resulting in a major blow on French colonial possessions.

objets.nom: Treaty of Versailles
objets.notes: In order to pay its debts and being no longer able to suppress struggle for independence, the Republic of Genoa ceded Corsica to France. Corsica remained French ever since.

objets.nom: Coup of 18 Brumaire
objets.notes: General Napoleon Bonaparte overthrew the French Directory, replacing it with the French Consulate.

objets.nom: War of the Second Coalition
objets.notes: The Treaty of Lunéville was signed after the victory of the French Republic against the Second Coalition states (led by the Austrian and Russian Empires), marking the end of the war with only Britain left fighting France.

objets.nom: Saint-Domingue expedition
objets.notes: French Army General Charles Leclerc and the first 5,000 of 20,000 troops arrive at Cap-François (now Cap-Haïtien) to suppress Toussaint L'Ouverture and the rebellion of the black population in Haiti.

objets.nom: Battle of Vertières
objets.notes: The viscount of Rochambeau was defeated and forced to surrender to the revolutionary army of Jean-Jacques Dessalines.

objets.nom: Louisiana Purchase
objets.notes: France sold Louisiana to the United States of America, renouncing its last territorial possessions on continental North America.

objets.nom: Haitian Revolution
objets.notes: Dessalines declared the independence of Haiti.

objets.nom: War of the Third Coalition
objets.notes: The French Empire is victorious at the decisive Battle of Austerlitz which marks the end of the Third Coalition (Austria, Russia, United Kingdom, Sweden and others) against France and its client states.

objets.nom: War of the Fourth Coalition
objets.notes: The French Empire is victorious at the decisive Battle of Friedland which marks the end of the Fourth Coalition (mainly Prussia, Russia, Saxony, Sweden, and the United Kingdom) against France and its client states.

objets.nom: War of the Fifth Coalition
objets.notes: The French Empire is victorious at the decisive Battle of Wagram which marks the end of the Fifth Coalition (mainly the Austrian Empire and the United Kingdom) against France and its client states. (to 6 July)

objets.nom: War of the Sixth Coalition
objets.notes: The Fire of Moscow marks the beginning of French retreat after the French invasion of Russia. The First French Empire reached the height of its power and declined henceforth with the disastrous Battle of Berezina. The Sixth Coalition will go on to win the war and Napoleon will be exiled in 1814 to Elba.

objets.nom: First Restoration
objets.notes: The House of Bourbon was briefly restored with Louis XVIII as King of France in an intermediate period of the Napoleonic Wars.

objets.nom: Hundred Days
objets.notes: Napoleon escapes from Elba.

objets.nom: Second Restoration
objets.notes: With Napoleon exiled in Saint Helena, the House of Bourbon was again restored. Louis XVIII became King of France until his death on 16 September 1824.

objets.nom: French invasion of Spain
objets.notes: France started its invasion of Spain, eventually succeeding and restoring the monarchy, ending the Liberal Triennium.

objets.nom: First Canut revolt
objets.notes: first clearly defined worker uprising of the Industrial Revolution.

objets.notes: The Entente Cordiale was signed, as an agreement mainly based on imperial issues. With the Anglo-Russian Entente of 1907, France, Britain and Russia were known as the Triple Entente in opposition to the Triple Alliance of Germany, Austria and Italy.

objets.nom: End of the 8-year long Indochina War
objets.notes: End of the 8-year long Indochina War. The following Geneva Conference (1954) agreed to dividing Vietnam. France departed from the country in a move that started worldwide decolonization of the French colonial empire.

objets.notes: The Inner Six countries (including France) signed two treaties establishing the European Economic Community (EEC) and the European Atomic Energy Community (EAEC).

objets.nom: Maastricht Treaty
objets.notes: Members of the European Community (including France) signed a treaty creating what is now known as the European Union.

objets.notes: A cargo truck was deliberately driven into crowds of people celebrating Bastille Day on the Promenade des Anglais, Nice resulting in the deaths of 86 people and the injury of 458 others.

objets.notes: The Cimbri and Teutons undertake migratory movements during which they clash with Roman forces (Battle of Noreia, Battle of Arausio, Battle of Aquae Sextiae, Battle of Vercellae). The Cimbri and Teutons are later added by Julius Caesar to the category of "Germans", even though they were perceived as Celts by the Romans of their own time.

objets.nom: Gallic Wars
objets.notes: Julius Caesar marches his forces into Gaul for purposes of conquest, broadly categorizing the people he encountered into "Gauls", "Aquitani", "Belgae", and "Germans" (using the Rhine river as a boundary between Germania and Gaul). He classifies Ariovistus as "King of the Germans", and defeats the forces of Ariovistus at the Battle of Vosges.…

objets.nom: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains
objets.notes: The Franks joined a coalition led by the Western Roman Empire which defeated the Huns in modern northeastern France.

objets.nom: Battle of Orleans (463)
objets.notes: The Salian Franks and forces loyal to the magister militum Aegidius defeated an attack by the Visigothic Kingdom at Orléans.

objets.nom: Franco-Roman war
objets.notes: An alliance of Franks led by Clovis conquer North-Gaul and put an end to the Roman enclaves of Syagrius and Arbogast. Syagrius, the king of Soissons fled to the Visigothic Kingdom.

objets.nom: Battle of Tolbiac
objets.notes: A Frankish force under Clovis defeated the Alemanni in modern Zülpich. The former credited his victory to Jesus.

objets.nom: Battle of Vouillé
objets.notes: A Frankish force led by Clovis defeated the Visigothic Kingdom at Vouillé. The Visigothic king Alaric II was killed. Clovis annexed Aquitaine.

objets.nom: First Council of Orléans
objets.notes: A synod of Catholic bishops called by Clovis at Orléans granted some legal powers and immunities to the Catholic Church.

objets.nom: Battle of Vézeronce
objets.notes: A Frankish invasion of Burgundy was halted near modern Vézeronce-Curtin. The Burgundian king Sigismund of Burgundy was captured and Chlodomer was killed.

objets.nom: Battle of Autun
objets.notes: Childebert and Chlothar defeated Burgundy near Autun.

objets.nom: Council of Clermont (535)
objets.notes: A synod was held in modern Clermont-Ferrand which limited the rights of Catholic bishops to appeal to the state and which condemned marriage between Christians and Jews and between relatives.

objets.nom: Fifth Council of Orléans
objets.notes: A synod presided over by Sacerdos of Lyon in Orléans condemned Nestorianism and simony.

objets.nom: Battle of the Volturnus (554)
objets.notes: A Byzantine force cut off and destroyed a joint Frankish-Ostrogothic army at their camp on the Volturno.

objets.nom: Synod of Rouen
objets.notes: A Catholic synod was held in Rouen which again condemned simony.

objets.nom: Battle of Tertry
objets.notes: Austrasian forces loyal to Pepin of Herstal defeated the invading army of Theuderic III at modern Tertry, Somme. Pepin of Herstal accepted Theuderic's unification of the Frankish kingdoms on the condition that he replace Berchar as his mayor of the palace.

objets.nom: Battle of Amblève
objets.notes: Charles defeated the forces of Frisia and Chilperic II at Amel.

objets.nom: Battle of Cologne
objets.notes: A Frisian army joined by the forces of Chilperic II conquered Cologne in Austrasia, forcing Charles to flee to the Eifel and compelling Plectrude to accept Chilperic II as king.

objets.nom: Battle of Vincy
objets.notes: Charles dealt Chilperic II a decisive defeat at modern Les Rues-des-Vignes and subsequently declared Chlothar IV king of Austrasia.

objets.nom: Battle of Soissons (718)
objets.notes: Charles defeated the armies of Chilperic II and Aquitaine at Soissons. Chilperic II fled to Aquitaine.

objets.nom: Battle of Tours
objets.notes: Charles, joined by the Duchy of Aquitaine and the Kingdom of the Lombards, dealt a decisive defeat to the Umayyad Caliphate near modern Vouneuil-sur-Vienne. Abdul Rahman Al Ghafiqi, the Umayyad governor of al-Andalus, was killed.

objets.nom: Battle of the Boarn
objets.notes: A Frankish army led by Charles defeated and annexed the Frisian Kingdom and killed its king, Bubo, Duke of the Frisians.

objets.nom: Battle of Nîmes
objets.notes: Charles destroyed the Umayyad Septimanian cities of Nîmes, Agde, Béziers and what is now Villeneuve-lès-Maguelone.

objets.nom: Battle of the River Berre
objets.notes: Charles intercepted and destroyed an Umayyad army sent to relieve his siege of Narbonne near the Étang de Berre.

objets.nom: Concilium Germanicum
objets.notes: A synod called by Carloman and presided over by Saint Boniface settled some issues of Catholic ritual and organization. The Rule of Saint Benedict became mandatory in Frankish monasteries.

objets.nom: Siege of Narbonne (752–59)
objets.notes: Pepin the Short laid siege to Narbonne, still held by forces loyal to Yusuf ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Fihri, governor of Al-Andalus under the defunct Umayyad Caliphate.

objets.nom: Charlemagne mène une série de campagnes pour soumettre et christianiser les Saxons.
objets.fr: Charlemagne mène une série de campagnes pour soumettre et christianiser les Saxons.

objets.nom: Saxon Wars
objets.notes: Charlemagne invaded the territory of the Saxons and destroyed their sacred symbol Irminsul near Paderborn.

objets.nom: Siege of Trsat
objets.notes: Eric of Friuli, the duke of Friuli and an officer of Charlemagne, was killed during a failed siege of Trsat, in Croatia.

objets.nom: Battle of Pancorbo (816)
objets.notes: Forces loyal to the Frankish vassal Velasco the Gascon were routed by the Emirate of Córdoba at Pancorbo.

objets.nom: Synods of Aachen (816–819)
objets.notes: A synod was called at the Palace of Aachen in Aachen which would conform monks to the Rule of Saint Benedict and separate them from canons, who were called to live according to the Institutio canonicorum Aquisgranensis.

objets.nom: Battle of Roncevaux Pass (824)
objets.notes: A combined Basque-Banu Qasi force defeated a Frankish pacifying expedition at Roncevaux Pass.

objets.nom: Synod of Thionville
objets.notes: Ebbo publicly recanted his charges against Louis the Pious at a synod at Thionville.

objets.nom: Battle of Fontenoy
objets.notes: The forces of Charles the Bald and Louis the German dealt a decisive defeat to Lothair I and Pepin the Younger at Fontenoy.

objets.nom: Battle of Andernach (876)
objets.notes: Louis the Younger defeated an attempted West Frankish invasion of East Francia across the Rhine near Andernach.

objets.nom: Frankish-Moravian War
objets.notes: Svatopluk I of Moravia, the king of Great Moravia, intervened in Pannonia on the side of Aribo.

objets.nom: Siege of Asselt
objets.notes: The Viking leader Godfrid, Duke of Frisia was besieged in his camp in the valley of the Meuse by East Frankish forces. After converting to Christianity he was granted the Kennemerland as a vassal of Charles the Fat.

objets.nom: Wilhelminer War
objets.notes: The Wilhelminers rebelled against Aribo of Austria, the margrave of the East Frankish March of Pannonia.

objets.nom: Battle of Pressburg
objets.notes: An East Frankish army was wiped out by a Hungarian force at modern Bratislava during an attempted reconquest of Pannonia.

objets.nom: Battle of Eisenach (908)
objets.notes: An East Frankish army was dealt a crushing defeat by a Hungarian force at Eisenach. Burchard, Duke of Thuringia, the duke of Thuringia, was killed. Thuringia was absorbed into Saxony.

objets.nom: Henri l'Oiseleur, roi de Germanie, soumet le pays des Slaves obodrites, à l'est de l'Elbe, et en fait la…
objets.fr: Henri l'Oiseleur, roi de Germanie, soumet le pays des Slaves obodrites, à l'est de l'Elbe, et en fait la…
objets.notes: Henri l'Oiseleur, roi de Germanie, soumet le pays des Slaves obodrites, à l'est de l'Elbe, et en fait la marche du Nord, future marche de Brandebourg.

objets.nom: Synod of Erfurt
objets.notes: A synod at Erfurt decided that Germany would cease paying tribute to Hungary.

objets.nom: Battle of Andernach
objets.notes: A rebellion of Franconia and Lotharingia against Otto the Great was decisively defeated at Andernach. The dukes of Franconia and Lotharingia Eberhard of Franconia and Gilbert were killed. Otto the Great prevented succession in both duchies and dissolved the former.

objets.nom: Battle on the Raxa
objets.notes: A German army defeated an Obotrite rebellion in the Billung March, probably on the Recknitz.

objets.nom: Battle of Cedynia
objets.notes: The forces of Odo I, Margrave of the Saxon Ostmark, the margrave of the Saxon Eastern March, were decisively repelled by the Polans near the Oder, possibly near Cedynia.

objets.nom: Battle of Stilo
objets.notes: A Sicilian army dealt heavy casualties to a Roman force at Capo Colonna. Gunther, Margrave of Merseburg, the margrave of Merseburg, died. Rikdag inherited his territory.

objets.nom: Great Slav Rising
objets.notes: An uprising by the Polabian Slavs overthrew German authority in the Northern March and the Billung March.

objets.nom: Walk to Canossa
objets.notes: After fasting outdoors in a blizzard for three days, Holy Roman Emperor Henry IV was allowed to enter Canossa Castle and receive forgiveness from Pope Gregory VII for the illegitimate appointment of bishops.

objets.nom: First Crusade
objets.notes: Pope Urban II called on all Catholics to assist the Byzantine Emperor Alexios I Komnenos in repelling the invading Seljuk Empire.

objets.nom: Battle of Bouvines
objets.notes: The combined forces of Flanders, England, Boulogne and the Holy Roman Empire were dealt a decisive defeat by the French at Bouvines.

objets.nom: Battle of Grunwald
objets.notes: The Teutonic Order was decisively defeated by the combined forces of Poland and Lithuania at Grunwald.

objets.nom: Council of Constance
objets.notes: An ecumenical council began which would condemn Jan Hus as a heretic, depose Antipopes John XXIII and Benedict XIII, and elect Pope Martin V.

objets.notes: Johannes Gutenberg, fabricant de Mayence, imprime la Bible de Gutenberg, premier emploi en Europe de l'imprimerie à caractères mobiles.

objets.notes: A war between the Old Swiss Confederacy and the House of Habsburg took place in which the Swiss would win an exemption from paying taxes to the Holy Roman Empire and participating in the Imperial Diet.

objets.notes: Six princes and the representatives of fourteen free imperial cities read out their objection to the imperial ban on Luther and his works at the Imperial Diet at Speyer.

objets.fr: Guerre de Trente Ans . Dans des coalitions aux contours variables, le Saint-Empire et la monarchie…

objets.notes: The combined forces of Saxony and the Swedish Empire dealt a decisive defeat to the Holy Roman Empire and its allies near Breitenfeld.

objets.nom: Sack of Magdeburg
objets.notes: Forces under the command of the Holy Roman Empire and the Catholic League breached the walls of the Protestant city of Magdeburg and murdered some twenty thousand of its thirty thousand inhabitants.

objets.nom: Battle of Lützen
objets.notes: Forces led by the Swedish Empire defeated forces under the command of the Holy Roman Empire near Lützen. The Swedish king Gustavus Adolphus was killed.

objets.fr: Guerres du Palatinat entre l'électeur palatin et le duc de Lorraine.

objets.notes: The combined forces of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth and the Holy Roman Empire and their allies broke an Ottoman siege of Vienna.

objets.fr: Second siège de Vienne par les Ottomans s'achevant par la victoire des troupes impériales et polonaises…

fin de la régence : Philippe II de Macédoine prend le titre royal. Conquête de Potidée en Chalcidique et de Pydna au sud de la Macédoine.
chute et exil de Denys II. Conquête macédonienne d'Amphipolis en Thrace.
mort d'Épaminondas à Mantinée. À Athènes, éviction de Callistrate et gouvernement du parti impérialiste. Troisième voyage de Platon en Sicile.
nouvelle Paix du Roi (traité de Suse). Tyrannie de Dion de Syracuse et second voyage de Platon en Sicile. Gouvernement de Denys II.

bataille de Leuctres. Rétablissement de la confédération béotienne. Jason de Phères proclamé tagos de Thessalie. Assassinat de Jason de Phères [soit par des conjurés thessaliens, soit commandité par Athènes].
occupation de Thèbes par les Spartiates (occupation de la Cadmée); Athènes accueille les exilés thébains. Naissance de Philippe II de Macédoine, dernier fils du roi Amyntas.
destruction de Mantinée. Réorganisation de la ligue péloponnésienne. Colonisation en Adriatique : fondation d'Issa.
paix du Roi (ou Paix d'Antalcidas). Siège et capitulation de Rhégion.
expédition navale d'Antalcidas en Ionie, puis dans l'Hellespont. Liberté de navigation pour les athéniens. Victoire de Denys sur la ligue.
retour de Conon à Athènes : reconstruction des Longs Murs et d'une flotte.
victoire de Cnide sur les Spartiates, qui les élimine de la mer Égée : début du redressement militaire d'Athènes. Sparte se retire d'Asie et des îles.
débarquement d'Himilcon à Palerme. Siège de Syracuse. Retraite d'Himilcon.
à Athènes, procès et mort de Socrate; à Sparte, conspiration de Cinadon.
défaite des Athéniens à Aigos Potamos. Conquête carthaginoise de Géla et de Camarina.
conquête carthaginoise d'Agrigente. Denys à la tête de Syracuse avec les pleins pouvoirs. Procès des stratèges athéniens.
Lysandre commandant de la flotte. Retour d'Alcibiade à Athènes. Défaite de Notion et retraite en Thrace. (Début de l'histoire de Xénophon).
en Sicile, avancée carthaginoise et destruction de Sélinonte et d'Himère.
coup d'État réactionnaire à Athènes (les Quatre-Cents). Intrigues d'Alcibiade, qui a quitté le camp spartiate pour Tissapherne et négocie l'alliance perse contre son retour à Athènes. Échec.
Tissapherne, satrape de Lydie, réduit la révolte de Pissouthnès.
bataille d'Amphipolis. Mort de Brasidas et de Cléon à Eion.

renouvellement de la paix entre Athènes et les Perses. Occupation athénienne de Cythère. Expédition spartiate en Chalcidique : conquête d'Amphipolis par Brasidas. Défaite athénienne face aux Béotiens à Délion. Retour de la flotte athénienne de Sicile.
ostracisme de Cimon et réformes d'Éphialtès, à Athènes.
chute de Thrasybule. Fin de la tyrannie en Sicile. Début de la révolte de Thasos.
mort de Hiéron. Thrasybule, le quatrième frère, devient tyran de Syracuse.
victoire navale de Hiéron sur la flotte étrusque, à Cumes.
Expulsion des Perses de Thrace et d'Europe. Fin de la tyrannie d'Anaxilas à Rhégion.
combats dans les Détroits. constitution par Athènes de la Ligue de Délos. À Syracuse, mort de Gélon et avènement de Hiéron. Le troisième frère, Polyzélos est gouverneur de Géla.
victoire de Platées, qui libère la Grèce. Victoire navale de Mycale et libération de l'Ionie.

avancée des Perses depuis les Détroits jusqu'en Grèce centrale. Défaite grecque aux Thermopyles. Sac d'Athènes. Victoire navale des Grecs à Salamine. Intervention de Carthage dans les affaires de Sicile. Victoire grecque d'Himère.
préparatifs de guerre à Carthage et en Sicile. Échec des négociations entre Gélon et la ligue panhellénique de Corinthe.
à Athènes, loi navale de Thémistocle et ostracisme d'Aristide. Annexions et expulsions à Géla, Camarina, Megara Hyblaea... Rérillos, tyran d'Himère, en appelle à Carthage.
expédition navale de Datis et d'Artapherne dans les îles et contre Athènes (première guerre médique).

intervention spartiate à Égine. Émissaires de Darios aux États grecs pour demander leur soumission. Début des hostilités entre Athènes et Égine. Mort d'Hippocrate de Géla. Gélon devient tyran de Géla. Expulsion des aristocrates de Syracuse.

réorganisation des cités d'Ionie. Mise en place de « démocraties » par les Perses. Expédition de Mardonios en Thrace. L'Athénien Miltiade abandonne les possessions ancestrales de Chersonèse de Thrace et regagne Athènes.

victoire de Sparte sur Argos à Sépeia. Réduction de Chypre. La flotte perse est en mer Égée. Pacification du littoral anatolien. Défaite des Ioniens à Ladé. Chute de Milet. Mission de Datis de Sardes à Persépolis pour préparer la contre-offensive en Égée. Début de la tyrannie d'Anaxilas II, à Rhégion. Attaque d'Hippocrate de Géla contre Syracuse.

Sparte refuse d'intervenir en Ionie. Sac de Sardes par les Ioniens, alliés aux Athéniens et aux Érétriens. La Carie et la Lycie et Chypre se joignent à la révolte. Athènes et Érétrie retirent leurs troupes. Fin de la tyrannie de Cléandre et début de la tyrannie d'Hippocrate de Géla.
expédition perse contre Naxos. Mission d'Aristagoras de Milet à Sparte et à Athènes. Faible place des importations grecques en Méditerranée occidentale.
premier traité entre Rome et Carthage qui se partagent la Méditerranée occidentale. Intervention spartiate à Athènes (échec). Réforme de Clisthène. Mise en place des cadres démocratiques.

intervention spartiate à Athènes contre le tyran. Renversement de la tyrannie à Athènes. Retour des exilés. Exil d'Hippias chez les Perses. Stasis entre Clisthène l'Alcméonide et Isagoras, chef des oligarques. Intervention de Cléomène de Sparte en faveur d'Isagoras.
tyrannicide à Athènes : assassinat d'Hipparque, frère d'Hippias, par les tyrannoctones Harmodios et Aristogiton.
Samos, Chios et Lesbos sous domination perse.
troisième coup d'État de Pisistrate appuyé par Thèbes et Lygdamis de Naxos. Bataille de Pallène. Expulsion d'Athènes de Miltiade l'Ancien en Chersonèse de Thrace.
conquête du royaume lydien par les Perses. destruction de Smyrne, Xanthe, Caunos. Émigration phocéenne.
avènement de Cyrus, issu du clan royal perse des Achéménides et héritier de la dynastie mède.
établissement de la tyrannie des Pisistratides à Athènes. Avènement de Crésus en Lydie.
premier affrontement entre Alyattes et Mèdes. Frontière de l'Halys.
Début de l'avancée des Mèdes, peuple iranien, en Haute-Mésopotamie.
fondation d'Istros, à l'embouchure du Danube et implantation grecque en mer Noire.
fondation de Byzance, à l'entrée du Bosphore, en face de Chalcédoine. Établissement de la tyrannie des Cypsélides à Corinthe selon la chronologie traditionnelle.
première bataille navale connue en Grèce antique ; elle oppose Corinthe et Corcyre.
Assassinat du roi Télestès à Corinthe, oligarchie des Bacchiades.
fondation de Cyzique, sur la Propontide (mer de Marmara).

objets.notes: le futur vice-roi de Nouvelle-Espagne Bernardo de Gálvez y Madrid aide les révolutionnaires américains. Il est considéré aux États-Unis comme un héros de la révolution.

objets.nom: Le vice-roi Martín de Mayorga ordonne la conservation des archives de Nouvelle-Espagne.
objets.fr: Le vice-roi Martín de Mayorga ordonne la conservation des archives de Nouvelle-Espagne.
