objets.fr: Fausto de Elhuyar est chargé par le Roi Charles III d'Espagne d'organiser le Real Seminario de Minería…
objets.notes: Fausto de Elhuyar est chargé par le Roi Charles III d'Espagne d'organiser le Real Seminario de Minería (École des Mines) de Mexico.

objets.nom: Battle of Monte de las Cruces
objets.notes: Insurgent forces under Hidalgo and Ignacio Allende defeated Spanish troops at Ocoyoacac.

objets.nom: Grito de Dolores
objets.notes: The Catholic priest Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla encouraged his congregation to revolt against the Spanish crown in a speech made at Dolores.

objets.nom: Mexican War of Independence: After Hidalgo orders Juan Antonio Riaño the surrender of Guanajuato, the…
objets.notes: Mexican War of Independence: After Hidalgo orders Juan Antonio Riaño the surrender of Guanajuato, the insurgent troops led by José Mariano Abasolo and Ignacio Camargo take the city.

objets.nom: *Miguel Hidalgo and Ignacio Allende arrive in Zacatecas.
*The insurgent caudillos Miguel Hidalgo, Ignacio Allende, José Mariano Jiménez, José Mariano Abasolo and…
objets.notes: *The insurgent caudillos Miguel Hidalgo, Ignacio Allende, José Mariano Jiménez, José Mariano Abasolo and Ignacio Aldama are captured by Ignacio Elizondo at the Wells of Baján and taken prisoner to Monclova and Chihuahua. The son of Ignacio Allende dies at the site of the capture.

objets.nom: {{Location map many|North America|width=180|float=center|caption=
*The Congress of Chilpancingo is inaugurated
objets.notes: *The Congress of Chilpancingo is inaugurated. Morelos delivers the inaugural speech and Juan Nepomuceno Rosáins reads the Sentimientos de la Nación.

objets.nom: *José María Morelos is executed by a firing squad in San Cristóbal de Ecatepec.
*The Inquisition declares Morelos a heretic and sentences him to life imprisonment in Africa if he is…
objets.notes: *The Inquisition declares Morelos a heretic and sentences him to life imprisonment in Africa if he is not sentenced to the death penalty. The ecclesiastical degradation of Morelos is carried out in the chapel of the Holy Office.

objets.nom: *Pope Pius VII publishes the encyclical Esti Longissimo Terrarum, where he exhorts obedience and peace…
objets.notes: *Pope Pius VII publishes the encyclical Esti Longissimo Terrarum, where he exhorts obedience and peace from the rebels in Spanish America, favoring Ferdinand VII.

objets.nom: Négociations secrète entre le général créole Agustín de Iturbide et l'indépendantiste Vicente Guerrero.
objets.fr: Négociations secrète entre le général créole Agustín de Iturbide et l'indépendantiste Vicente Guerrero.

objets.nom: Mexican War of Independence
objets.notes: The Spanish colonel Agustín de Iturbide and the insurgent leader Vicente Guerrero together issued the Plan of Iguala at a meeting in Iguala, under which Mexico was to become an independent, Catholic constitutional monarchy.

objets.nom: Mexican War of Independence: Iturbide and Spanish viceroy Juan O'Donojú signed the Treaty of Córdoba,…
objets.notes: Mexican War of Independence: Iturbide and Spanish viceroy Juan O'Donojú signed the Treaty of Córdoba, recognizing the independence of Mexico in personal union with Spain.

objets.nom: Mexican War of Independence: The armies under Iturbide and Guerrero were consolidated into Iturbide's…
objets.notes: Mexican War of Independence: The armies under Iturbide and Guerrero were consolidated into Iturbide's control in the Army of the Three Guarantees.

objets.nom: *After 12 days of siege, the Mexican army assaults the El Álamo
objets.notes: *After 12 days of siege, the Mexican army assaults the El Álamo. The rebel defenders ultimately surrender. Rebels forge the phrase "Remember the Alamo".

objets.nom: *General Santa Anna, commanding the battalions of Matamoros, Jiménez, San Luis, the regiment of Dolores…
objets.notes: *General Santa Anna, commanding the battalions of Matamoros, Jiménez, San Luis, the regiment of Dolores and eight pieces of artillery, occupies San Antonio Béjar The rebels retreat to the fort of El Álamo.

objets.nom: *Santa Anna's troops, stationed in a hill near the San Jacinto River receive the reinforcement of…
objets.notes: *Santa Anna's troops, stationed in a hill near the San Jacinto River receive the reinforcement of Perfecto of Cos. The enemy takes refuge in the forest and Santa Anna decides to offer rest to his troops. To his misfortune, Houston's men ambush him. The confrontation lasts for hours until the Mexican ranks disperse.

objets.nom: *Santa Anna, who had fled in the fray of the previous day, is captured by Texan forces.
{{Location map many|North America|width=180|float=center|caption=
*In the Metropolitan Cathedral of Mexico City, the funeral honors and the burial of the remains of…
objets.notes: *In the Metropolitan Cathedral of Mexico City, the funeral honors and the burial of the remains of Agustín de Iturbide take place.

objets.nom: *The remains of Agustín de Iturbide are transferred to the Metropolitan Cathedral of Mexico City in a…
objets.notes: *The remains of Agustín de Iturbide are transferred to the Metropolitan Cathedral of Mexico City in a sumptuous procession.

objets.nom: * The Thornton Affair is the first clash of the Mexican–American War as 80 cavalrymen under the command…
objets.notes: * The Thornton Affair is the first clash of the Mexican–American War as 80 cavalrymen under the command of U.S. Captain Seth B. Thornton are attacked by 1600 men under the leadership of Mexican General Anastasio Torrejón in the Nueces Strip between the Nueces River and the Rio Grande.

objets.nom: * The U.S. Congress declares war against Mexico.
*The United States begins the Blockade of Veracruz.
*After several days of fierce fighting, Mexico City falls.
*General Scott assaults Chapultepec Castle
objets.notes: *General Scott assaults Chapultepec Castle. Los Niños Héroes (six cadets between 12 and 18 years old who died in defense of the military academy) pass into legend. Some captured San Patricios members executed during the battle.

objets.nom: *Regular Mexican troops and Saint Patrick's Battalion under Manuel Rincón hold a fortified monastery…
objets.notes: *Regular Mexican troops and Saint Patrick's Battalion under Manuel Rincón hold a fortified monastery against Winfield Scott.

objets.nom: *The Battle of Buena Vista takes place
objets.notes: *The Battle of Buena Vista takes place. The Mexican army is superior in number, but it found poorly armed and exhausted by the march and severity of the weather; For its part, the US military is smaller, but is better organized and has more artillery. The result is indecisive.

objets.nom: Le Mexique entre en guerre et est envahi par les États-Unis, la moitié nord de son territoire est perdue.
objets.fr: Le Mexique entre en guerre et est envahi par les États-Unis, la moitié nord de son territoire est perdue.

objets.nom: {{Location map many|North America|width=180|float=center|caption=
*The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo goes into effect.
*The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, ending the Mexican–American War is signed in Mexico City
objets.notes: *The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, ending the Mexican–American War is signed in Mexico City. The U.S. agrees to pay US$15 million to Mexico and to pay off the claims of American citizens against Mexico. It gave the United States the Rio Grande as a boundary for Texas, and gave the U.S. ownership of Alta California and a large area comprising…

objets.nom: *The Plan de Ayutla is proclaimed, setting off a 19-month revolt against Antonio López de Santa Anna…
objets.notes: *The Plan de Ayutla is proclaimed, setting off a 19-month revolt against Antonio López de Santa Anna known as the Revolution of Ayutla, leading to La Reforma (The Reform) and the Constitution of 1857.

objets.nom: *Juan Álvarez takes office as Interim President of Mexico in Cuernavaca.
*The Reform laws begin, separating the Catholic Church and the government of Mexico
objets.notes: *The Reform laws begin, separating the Catholic Church and the government of Mexico. Principal leaders were Juan Álvarez, Ignacio Comonfort, Benito Juárez, and Sebastián Lerdo de Tejada.

objets.nom: *The Federal Constitution of the United Mexican States of 1857 goes into effect.
*The Reform War begins when the Plan of Tacubaya is proclaimed and conservative General Félix María…
objets.notes: *The Reform War begins when the Plan of Tacubaya is proclaimed and conservative General Félix María Zuloaga ousts president Ignacio Comonfort.

objets.nom: *Benito Juarez becomes president and he moves to Veracruz.
Début de la présidence de Benito Juárez.
objets.fr: Début de la présidence de Benito Juárez.

objets.nom: *France, Great Britain, and Spain agree to the Convention of London, a joint effort to extract loan…
objets.notes: *France, Great Britain, and Spain agree to the Convention of London, a joint effort to extract loan repayments from Mexico, which President Juarez had frozen three months earlier.

objets.nom: *France, Spain, and Great Britain disembark in Veracruz
objets.notes: *France, Spain, and Great Britain disembark in Veracruz. Spain and Britain later withdraw.

objets.nom: *Juarez recaptures Mexico City and goes on to defeat the Conservatives
objets.notes: *Juarez recaptures Mexico City and goes on to defeat the Conservatives. He is elected president in his own right in March.

objets.nom: *The Mexican Army under General Ignacio Zaragoza defeats the invading French army led by General Charles…
objets.notes: *The Mexican Army under General Ignacio Zaragoza defeats the invading French army led by General Charles de Lorencez in the Battle of Puebla. French forces took the city a year later, after the Siege of Puebla (1863).

objets.nom: 16 mars-17 mai 1863 : Seconde bataille de Puebla, au Mexique.
objets.fr: 16 mars-17 mai 1863 : Seconde bataille de Puebla, au Mexique.

objets.nom: Bataille de Camerone, au Mexique, fait d'armes de la Légion étrangère.
objets.fr: Bataille de Camerone, au Mexique, fait d'armes de la Légion étrangère.

objets.nom: Bataille de Las Cumbres.
objets.fr: Bataille de Las Cumbres.

objets.nom: Expédition du Mexique, éphémère empire de Maximilien de Habsbourg.
objets.fr: Expédition du Mexique, éphémère empire de Maximilien de Habsbourg.

objets.nom: *The Second Mexican Empire is declared, with the support of French Emperor Napoleon III, as well as the…
objets.notes: *The Second Mexican Empire is declared, with the support of French Emperor Napoleon III, as well as the Austrian and Belgian crowns. The Empire came to an end on 19 June 1867, with the execution of Emperor Maximilian I.

objets.nom: *Fernando Maximiliano José María de Habsburgo-Lorena, Archduke of Austria, was offered the Mexican crown…
objets.notes: *Fernando Maximiliano José María de Habsburgo-Lorena, Archduke of Austria, was offered the Mexican crown in October, 1863, which he accepted on 10 April. He and his wife, Charlotte of Belgium arrived in Veracruz on 29 May 1864, and they soon established their official residence at Chapultepec Castle in Mexico City.

objets.nom: *Napoleon III withdrew his army from Mexico in 1866, and Juarez's liberal forces captured Mexico City on…
objets.notes: *Napoleon III withdrew his army from Mexico in 1866, and Juarez's liberal forces captured Mexico City on 15 May 1867. Maximilian was captured the next day, and following a trial, he was sentenced to death. Maximilian, General Miguel Miramón, and General Tomás Mejía Camacho were executed by firing squad in Cerro de las Campanas, Querétaro City at…

objets.nom: Début de la présidence de Manuel González, intime de Díaz.
objets.fr: Début de la présidence de Manuel González, intime de Díaz.

objets.nom: Fin de la présidence de Manuel González, Díaz reprend le pouvoir.
objets.fr: Fin de la présidence de Manuel González, Díaz reprend le pouvoir.

objets.nom: Mexican Revolution
objets.notes: Francisco I. Madero calls for armed rebellion against the government of President Porfirio Díaz.

objets.nom: Francisco Madero est contraint de démissionner par Victoriano Huerta, son ministre de la guerre, qui…
objets.fr: Francisco Madero est contraint de démissionner par Victoriano Huerta, son ministre de la guerre, qui…
objets.notes: Francisco Madero est contraint de démissionner par Victoriano Huerta, son ministre de la guerre, qui s'était rebellé contre lui.

objets.nom: Mort de Porfirio Díaz à Paris.
objets.fr: Mort de Porfirio Díaz à Paris.

objets.nom: Mexican Revolution: The current constitution of Mexico was approved by a constituent assembly in Querétaro.
An earthquake of magnitude 7.8 hits Puebla and Veracruz, leaving 648–4,000 dead.
Mexican oil expropriation
objets.notes: President Lázaro Cárdenas expropriates the oil industry.

objets.nom: President Adolfo López Mateos nationalized the electrical system.
Tlatelolco massacre
objets.notes: The government fired on a crowd of student protesters in the Plaza de las Tres Culturas in Mexico City, killing between thirty and three hundred.

objets.nom: Dévaluation du peso
objets.fr: Dévaluation du peso

objets.nom: President José López Portillo nationalizes the banking industry.
1985 Mexico City earthquake
objets.notes: An earthquake centered off the Pacific coast of Michoacán caused ten thousand deaths and between three and four billion US$ in damage in Mexico City.

objets.nom: 1988 Mexican general election
objets.notes: Carlos Salinas de Gortari of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) was elected president in a rigged election, with an official 51% of the vote. The PRI maintained its majority in the Chamber of Deputies.

objets.nom: Constituent parties of the National Democratic Front (FDN) established the Party of the Democratic…
objets.notes: Constituent parties of the National Democratic Front (FDN) established the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) under the leadership of Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas.

objets.nom: Luis Donaldo Colosio is assassinated during his campaign to become the Mexican president in a rally in…
objets.notes: Luis Donaldo Colosio is assassinated during his campaign to become the Mexican president in a rally in Tijuana.

objets.nom: 2003 Mexican legislative election
objets.notes: The PRI won a plurality of seats in the Chamber of Deputies.

objets.nom: 2006 Mexican general election
objets.notes: Felipe Calderón of the National Action Party (PAN) won the presidency with 36% of the vote. The PAN won a plurality of seats in the Chamber of Deputies.

objets.nom: Andrés Manuel López Obrador of the PRD led hundreds of thousands in a protest against the election…
objets.notes: Andrés Manuel López Obrador of the PRD led hundreds of thousands in a protest against the election results at Zócalo in Mexico City.

objets.nom: 2009 Mexican legislative election
objets.notes: The PRI won a plurality of seats in the Chamber of Deputies.

objets.nom: 2012 Mexican general election
objets.notes: Enrique Pena Nieto of the PRI won the presidency with 39% of the vote. The PRI won a plurality of seats in the Chamber of Deputies.

objets.nom: 2017 Puebla earthquake
objets.notes: struck at 13:14 CDT on 19 September 2017 with a magnitude of Mw 7.1 and strong shaking for about 20 seconds. Its epicenter was about 55 km (34 mi) south of the city of Puebla. The earthquake caused damage in the Mexican states of Puebla and Morelos and in the Greater Mexico City area. 370 people were killed by the earthquake and related building…

objets.nom: Andrés Manuel López Obrador of Together we will make history (a coalition of MORENA and the Labor Party)…
objets.notes: Andrés Manuel López Obrador of Together we will make history (a coalition of MORENA and the Labor Party) is elected 58th president with 53% of the vote. Together we will make history also won majorities in both the Senate and the Chamber of Deputies and 5 governorships.

objets.nom: Exploitation of copper, urbanization and foundation of Enkomi, the first industrial centre in Cyprus.
Trading contacts between Cyprus and Egypt suggested by Egyptian artefacts from the Hyksos period found…
objets.notes: Trading contacts between Cyprus and Egypt suggested by Egyptian artefacts from the Hyksos period found in Cyprus.

objets.nom: Destruction of the Hyksos Kingdom by Ahmose I leads to a breakdown of political and economic bonds…
objets.notes: Destruction of the Hyksos Kingdom by Ahmose I leads to a breakdown of political and economic bonds between Cyprus and Hyksos. An incomplete weathered cartouche dating to the early XVIIIth Dynasty of Egypt found in Cyprus may be indicative of a new era of connections with the outside world.

objets.nom: Literacy is introduced on the island with the Cypro-Minoan syllabary, first attested in Enkomi.
Thutmose III extends his influence over Cyprus under the name of "Isy" or "Irs" (probably referring to…
objets.notes: Thutmose III extends his influence over Cyprus under the name of "Isy" or "Irs" (probably referring to Alasiya), which is reported offering minerals and timber as a tribute to the Pharaoh.

objets.nom: Tudhaliya IV annexes Cyprus (disputed).
The last king of the Hittites, Šuppiluliuma II, wins a decisive naval battle against Alashiya (Cypriots)…
objets.notes: The last king of the Hittites, Šuppiluliuma II, wins a decisive naval battle against Alashiya (Cypriots) off the coast of Cyprus, in the first recorded naval battle in history.

objets.nom: Invasion by the Sea Peoples.
Migrations of Aegean populations to Cyprus attested by abundant locally produced Mycenaean-style…
objets.notes: Migrations of Aegean populations to Cyprus attested by abundant locally produced Mycenaean-style (IIIC:1b) pottery and other Aegean/European features. The Hellenization process of the island begins.

objets.nom: A second, major wave of Greek settlements takes place following the Bronze Age collapse of Mycenaean…
objets.notes: A second, major wave of Greek settlements takes place following the Bronze Age collapse of Mycenaean Greece, accompanied by the appearance of further Aegean features including long dromoi graves and the introduction of the Greek language.

objets.nom: Appearance of the Cypriot syllabary, used both for Arcadocypriot Greek and Eteocypriot
objets.notes: Appearance of the Cypriot syllabary, used both for Arcadocypriot Greek and Eteocypriot. The script, which had evolved from the pre-existing Cypro-Minoan syllabary, lasted until the end of the 3rd Century BCE when it was eventually replaced by the Greek alphabet.

objets.nom: Emergence of the City States, which would eventually come to be known as the Ten City-Kingdoms of Cyprus.
Foundation of the city-kingdom of Amathus, the last autochthonous urban centre in Iron Age Cyprus where…
objets.notes: Foundation of the city-kingdom of Amathus, the last autochthonous urban centre in Iron Age Cyprus where the Eteocypriot language survived until about 400 BCE.

objets.nom: Phoenician merchants settle in Kition.
The kingdoms of Cyprus are subjugated by the Neo-Assyrian Empire, although no evidence of occupation is…
objets.notes: The kingdoms of Cyprus are subjugated by the Neo-Assyrian Empire, although no evidence of occupation is apparent in archaeological data and material culture; rather, the kingdoms seem to have "offered their submission to Sargon II" and had a client-state relationship.

objets.nom: Cyprus is conquered by the Egyptians under Amasis II.
Amasis II dies
objets.notes: Amasis II dies. His son Psammetichus III succeeds him as pharaoh.

objets.nom: Battle of Pelusium (525 BCE)
objets.notes: The Persian army defeat the Egyptian army at Pelusium.

objets.nom: The kingdoms of Cyprus gave naval support to Cambyses II of the Achaemenid Persian Empire in…
objets.notes: The kingdoms of Cyprus gave naval support to Cambyses II of the Achaemenid Persian Empire in anticipation of his invasion of Egypt.

objets.nom: Ionian Revolt
objets.notes: Aristagoras, the appointed tyrant of Miletus, rebells against Persian rule.

objets.nom: Ionian Revolt: With the support of Athens and Eretria, Aristagoras captures Sardis, the capital of the…
objets.notes: Ionian Revolt: With the support of Athens and Eretria, Aristagoras captures Sardis, the capital of the Persian satrapy of Lydia.

objets.nom: Ionian Revolt: The Persian army reestablished control over Cyprus.
Kition increases in importance and annexes Idalion.
Phoenician rulers establish themselves in Salamis.
The Teucrid Evagoras I regains the throne of Salamis.
Evagoras attempts to establish himself as an independent ruler on Cyprus with Athenian help.
Under the Treaty of Antakidas, Persian rule over Cyprus is accepted by Athens.
The Cypriot rebellion is crushed by Artaxerxes III.
The island is finally liberated from Persian rule by Alexander the Great.
Pythagoras of Salamis and other Cypriot kings plea to Alexander The Great during the beginning of the…
objets.notes: Pythagoras of Salamis and other Cypriot kings plea to Alexander The Great during the beginning of the siege of Tyre.

objets.nom: The siege of Tyre ends.
The rule of Nicocreon begins.
The rule of Nicocreon ends.
Antigonus begins his rule.
The Ptolemaic Lagid Dynasty begins.
Kingdoms are abolished under the Ptolemaic rule
objets.notes: Kingdoms are abolished under the Ptolemaic rule. Greek alphabet and koine Greek are established as the official administrative tools. Both the Eteocypriot and Phoenician languages become extinct and the island is thereafter fully Hellenised.

objets.nom: Cleopatra sends her son Ptolemy Philometor to Cyprus.
Cleopatra sends Alexander, her son and the brother of Ptolemy IX Lathyros, to Cyprus.
Alexander returns from Cyprus and becomes king of Egypt
objets.notes: Alexander returns from Cyprus and becomes king of Egypt. Ptolemy campaigns in Palestine.

objets.nom: Cyprus becomes a Roman province.
Cyprus is placed under the rule of Cleopatra VII, with its governor being Serapion
objets.notes: Cyprus is placed under the rule of Cleopatra VII, with its governor being Serapion. However, Serapion defected against Cleopatra.

objets.nom: The Ptolemaic Lagid Dynasty ends and Cyprus returns to Roman rule.
Apostle Paul, St
objets.notes: Apostle Paul, St. Barnabas and St. Mark introduced Christianity in Cyprus and converted the Roman governor Sergius Paulus.

objets.nom: Url=http://www.jewishencyclopedia.com/articles/4825-cyprus |title=Cyprus…
objets.notes: url=http://www.jewishencyclopedia.com/articles/4825-cyprus |title=Cyprus |publisher=JewishEncyclopedia.com}} Trajan intervenes to restore the peace and expels the Jews from Cyprus.

objets.nom: The revolt of the usurper Calocaerus is suppressed by Flavius Dalmatius.
Salamis is rebuilt by Constantius II, the son of Constantine, after being destroyed by earthquakes and…
objets.notes: Salamis is rebuilt by Constantius II, the son of Constantine, after being destroyed by earthquakes and renamed Constantia.

objets.nom: Cyprus becomes part of the Byzantine Empire.
The Church of Cyprus achieves its independence from the Patriarch of Antioch at the First Council of Ephesus.
The Arabs under Mu'awiya invade and occupy Cyprus.
The Arab garrison is withdrawn after its defeat at the hands of Constantine IV.
Emperor Justinian II and Caliph Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan sign a treaty under whose terms no garrisons are…
objets.notes: Emperor Justinian II and Caliph Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan sign a treaty under whose terms no garrisons are to be stationed on the island, and all taxes collected are to be divided between the Arabs and the Emperor.

objets.nom: Byzantine rule is restored on the island by Nicepheros Phokas.
Cyprus becomes an independent Empire under the reign of Isaak Comnenus.
Guy of Lusignan and his descendants begin their rule of the island as an independent kingdom, known as…
objets.notes: Guy of Lusignan and his descendants begin their rule of the island as an independent kingdom, known as the Kingdom of Cyprus.

objets.nom: The reign of Isaac Komnenos comes to an end after the island's ruler refuses to release prisoners and…
objets.notes: The reign of Isaac Komnenos comes to an end after the island's ruler refuses to release prisoners and treasure captured from three English ship wrecks on their way to Acre, and Richard I conquers Cyprus. The island is then sold to the Templar Order, who in turn sell it to Guy of Lusignan of the House of Lusignan.

objets.nom: Altheides of Cyprus, the traveling philosopher, is born.
Black Death hits Cyprus and wipes out one fifth to one third of its population.
Antalya and Corycus in Anatolia are briefly annexed by the Kingdom of Cyprus.
Catherine Cornaro becomes the last monarch of the Kingdom of Cyprus, succeeding James II.
Cyprus becomes an overseas colony of the Venetian Republic.
Ottoman Turks raid the Karpasia Peninsula.
The Venetian government forces Catherine to cede her rights over Cyprus because she had no heir
objets.notes: The Venetian government forces Catherine to cede her rights over Cyprus because she had no heir. The rule of the Lusignan dynasty comes to an end after nearly three centuries.

objets.nom: Having been under siege since the previous year, Famagusta also falls to the Ottomans marking the end of…
objets.notes: Having been under siege since the previous year, Famagusta also falls to the Ottomans marking the end of the Venetian rule. Most Christians still remaining in the city are massacred and the Venetian commander Marco Antonio Bragadin is tortured, mutilated and flayed alive.

objets.nom: The Chronological History of the island of Cyprus, later described as "the only scholarly monograph of…
objets.notes: The Chronological History of the island of Cyprus, later described as "the only scholarly monograph of modern Greek literature since the fall of Constantinople", is published by Kyprianos Kouriokourineos, one of the most prominent Greek-Cypriot intellectuals and clerics of the 18th century.

objets.nom: British occupation began
objets.notes: British occupation began. The British took over the administration of the island, by mutual agreement, in order to protect their sea route to India via the Suez Canal. In exchange, Britain agreed to help Ottoman against future Russian attacks.

objets.nom: Britain annexed Cyprus in response to Turkey's alliance with Germany and Austro-Hungary in World War I.
Cyprus became a British Crown Colony
objets.notes: Cyprus became a British Crown Colony. Sir Malcolm Stevenson was made governor.

objets.nom: Greek Cypriots demanding Enosis, the union with Greece, instigated their first serious riots
objets.notes: Greek Cypriots demanding Enosis, the union with Greece, instigated their first serious riots. The government-house in Nicosia was burned down; martial law was declared afterwards and the legislative council was abolished. The Greek National Anthem and the display of the Greek flag were banned. The British invented the terms "Greek Cypriot" and…

objets.nom: Cypriots fought with the British in World War II, Greek Cypriots demanding Enosis at war's end
objets.notes: Cypriots fought with the British in World War II, Greek Cypriots demanding Enosis at war's end. The Turkish Cypriots wanted British rule to continue.

objets.nom: Archbishop Makarios III was elected the political and spiritual leader of Cyprus, the head of the…
objets.notes: Archbishop Makarios III was elected the political and spiritual leader of Cyprus, the head of the autocephalous Cypriot Orthodox Church and leader of the campaign for Enosis with the support of Greece.

objets.nom: Cyprus Emergency
objets.notes: A series of bomb attacks marked the start of a violent campaign for Enosis by the National Organisation of Cypriot Fighters (EOKA) under George Grivas, a Cypriot ex-colonel in the Greek army. Grivas took the name Dighenis and conducted guerrilla warfare from a secret hideout in the Troodos Mountains.

objets.nom: Field Marshal Sir John Harding was replaced by the civilian governor Sir Hugh Foot in a conciliatory move.
Turkish press office in Nicosia is bombed
objets.notes: Turkish press office in Nicosia is bombed. Inter-communal clashes as Turkish Cypriots invade Greek sector. On 26 June 1984 the Turkish Cypriot leader, Rauf Denktaş, admitted on British channel ITV that the bomb was placed by the Turks themselves in order to create tension. On 9 January 1995 Rauf Denktaş repeated his claim in the Turkish newspaper,…

objets.nom: London and Zürich Agreements started with an agreement on 19 February 1959 in Lancaster House, London,…
objets.notes: London and Zürich Agreements started with an agreement on 19 February 1959 in Lancaster House, London, between Turkey, Greece, the United Kingdom and Cypriot community leaders. On that basis, a constitution was drafted and agreed together with two prior Treaties of Alliance and Guarantee in Zürich on 11 February 1959.

objets.nom: The British, Greek and Turkish governments signed a Treaty of Guarantee to provide for an independent…
objets.notes: The British, Greek and Turkish governments signed a Treaty of Guarantee to provide for an independent Cypriot state within the Commonwealth of Nations and allow for the retention of two Sovereign Base Areas at Akrotiri and Dhekelia. Under the treaty, each power received the right to take military action in the face of any threat to the…

objets.nom: Greek Cypriots began to view the constitution as unworkable and proposed changes abolishing all veto…
objets.notes: Greek Cypriots began to view the constitution as unworkable and proposed changes abolishing all veto rights and many ethnic clauses; these proposals were rejected by Turkish Cypriots and the Turkish government. Inter-communal fighting erupted. Tylliria was bombarded with napalm bombs. A UN Peace Keeping Force was sent in, but soon proved powerless…

objets.nom: Turks announced a Federate State in the north, with Rauf Denktaş as leader
objets.notes: Turks announced a Federate State in the north, with Rauf Denktaş as leader. UN Forces remained as buffer between the two zones.

objets.nom: 2004 Annan Plan Referendum
objets.notes: The Annan Plan was accepted by the majority of Turkish Cypriots but overwhelmingly rejected by the Greek Cypriots.

objets.nom: The sovereign Republic of Cyprus joined the European Union, however the EU acquis was suspended in the…
objets.notes: The sovereign Republic of Cyprus joined the European Union, however the EU acquis was suspended in the occupied north, Akrotiri and Dhekelia and the United Nations Buffer Zone.

objets.nom: Demetris Christofias replaced Tassos Papadopoulos as president of the Republic of Cyprus
objets.notes: Demetris Christofias replaced Tassos Papadopoulos as president of the Republic of Cyprus. It was the first time that a leader of the Greek Cypriot communist party, AKEL, had entered the presidential race. He was at the time the only communist leader in the European Union.

objets.nom: The First Aliyah describes the initial major wave of Jewish immigration to Palestine motivated by…
objets.notes: The First Aliyah describes the initial major wave of Jewish immigration to Palestine motivated by persecution and economic hardship.

objets.nom: Tsar Alexander II of Russia is assassinated, triggering multiple waves of Jewish pogroms after some…
objets.notes: Tsar Alexander II of Russia is assassinated, triggering multiple waves of Jewish pogroms after some blamed "agents of foreign influence", a term often directed at Jewish communities.

objets.nom: The Russian emperor Alexander III issued the May Laws, severely restricting the rights of Jews in the…
objets.notes: The Russian emperor Alexander III issued the May Laws, severely restricting the rights of Jews in the Pale of Settlement, and intensifying Jewish emmigration.

objets.nom: The Dreyfus Affair was a political scandal in France that involved the wrongful conviction of Jewish…
objets.notes: The Dreyfus Affair was a political scandal in France that involved the wrongful conviction of Jewish army officer, Alfred Dreyfus. It is one of the most notable examples of antisemitism and miscarriage of justice.

objets.nom: Theodor Herzl published Der Judenstaat, arguing for the establishment of an independent Jewish state.
The First Zionist Congress constituted 218 delegates of Zionist organizations, most from Eastern Europe,…
objets.notes: The First Zionist Congress constituted 218 delegates of Zionist organizations, most from Eastern Europe, convened in Basel. It was instrumental in the formation of the Zionist platform, founding of the World Zionist Organization, and helped unify the Zionist movement.

objets.nom: The Jewish National Fund is established to buy land and encourage Jewish settlement in Palestine.
British diplomats and the Sharif of Mecca exchange the McMahon-Hussein Correspondence, in which Britain…
objets.notes: British diplomats and the Sharif of Mecca exchange the McMahon-Hussein Correspondence, in which Britain promises an independent Arab state, which would include Palestine, in exchange for supporting the British against the Ottoman Empire in the First World War.

objets.nom: The Bolsheviks make the terms of the Sykes-Picot Agreement public, exposing contradicting promises made…
objets.notes: The Bolsheviks make the terms of the Sykes-Picot Agreement public, exposing contradicting promises made in the McMahon-Hussein Correspondence and the Balfour Declaration.

objets.nom: Chaim Weizmann and Emir Faisal, son of the Sharif of Mecca, sign the Faisal-Weizmann agreement,…
objets.notes: Chaim Weizmann and Emir Faisal, son of the Sharif of Mecca, sign the Faisal-Weizmann agreement, promising Jewish support and development in Palestine. Faisal's approval was contingent on the fulfillment of British promises to him.

objets.nom: The League of Nations assigns Britain the creation of Mandatory Palestine.
The Palin Commission is created to investigate the 1920 Jerusalem riots
objets.notes: The Palin Commission is created to investigate the 1920 Jerusalem riots. They report that Arab rioters attacked Jewish lives and property, and that the cause was attributed to the disappointment that stemmed from unfulfilled promises to them by the British.

objets.nom: The 1921 Cairo Conference convened by Britain aimed to organize the Middle East boundaries and develop a…
objets.notes: The 1921 Cairo Conference convened by Britain aimed to organize the Middle East boundaries and develop a policy of governance. Arab and Jewish delegations were invited to advise or provide input. The conference established the division of Mandatory Palestine into Transjordan, and Palestine with Emir Abdullah ruling semi-autonomously in the former.…

objets.nom: The Haycraft Commission is created to investigate the 1921 Jaffa riots
objets.notes: The Haycraft Commission is created to investigate the 1921 Jaffa riots. The report blamed Arabs for the violence but notes growing Arab resentment of British policy, seemingly favoring Jewish communities and ambitions at the expense of the Arab population.

objets.nom: Winston Churchill drafts the Churchill White Paper
objets.notes: Winston Churchill drafts the Churchill White Paper. In it contains Britain's will to maintain their commitment to the Balfour Declaration, calls for restrictions on Jewish immigration, clarification that Palestine would not become a Jewish State. This would be the governoring policy in the region until 1939.

objets.nom: 1929 Palestine riots were a series of violent demonstrations and riots involving access over the Western…
objets.notes: 1929 Palestine riots were a series of violent demonstrations and riots involving access over the Western Wall in Jerusalem. The riots lead to 472 Jewish casualties and 348 Arab casualties.

objets.nom: The Passfield White Paper is drafted to implement recommendations made by the Shaw Commission and Hope…
objets.notes: The Passfield White Paper is drafted to implement recommendations made by the Shaw Commission and Hope Simpson Enquiry. The tone of the paper was considered anti-zionist by many.

objets.nom: The MacDonald letter written by British prime minister Ramsay MacDonald to Chaim Weizmann to clarify the…
objets.notes: The MacDonald letter written by British prime minister Ramsay MacDonald to Chaim Weizmann to clarify the new Passfield White Paper. It is considered to be an informal withdrawal of the Passfield White Paper.

objets.nom: World War II
objets.notes: Germany invades Poland and The Holocaust occurred in German-occupied Europe killing 6 million Jews.

objets.nom: 1948 Arab–Israeli War
objets.notes: Hours after the expiration of the British Mandate of Palestine, Iraq, Egypt, Jordan and Syria invaded Israel.

objets.nom: On the last day of the British Mandate, David Ben-Gurion, executive head of the Zionist Organization and…
objets.notes: On the last day of the British Mandate, David Ben-Gurion, executive head of the Zionist Organization and chairman of the Jewish Agency for Palestine, issued the Israeli Declaration of Independence which declared the establishment of a Jewish state in the Land of Israel to be known as the State of Israel, which covered part of the territory of what…

objets.nom: 1948 Arab–Israeli War: The first of the 1949 Armistice Agreements ending the war was signed between…
objets.notes: 1948 Arab–Israeli War: The first of the 1949 Armistice Agreements ending the war was signed between Israel and Egypt. An armistice line was agreed along the prewar border with the exception that Egypt remained in control of the Gaza Strip.

objets.nom: 1949 Israeli legislative election
objets.notes: Elections were held to a constituent assembly. Ben-Gurion's center-left Mapai won a plurality of seats.

objets.nom: The first government of Israel, in which Mapai, the Jewish United Religious Front, the liberal…
objets.notes: The first government of Israel, in which Mapai, the Jewish United Religious Front, the liberal Progressive Party, the Sephardim and Oriental Communities and the Arab Democratic List of Nazareth ruled in coalition with Ben-Gurion as prime minister, was established.

objets.nom: The Israeli legislature the Knesset passed the Law of Return, which granted all Jews the right to…
objets.notes: The Israeli legislature the Knesset passed the Law of Return, which granted all Jews the right to migrate to and settle in Israel and obtain citizenship.

objets.nom: Suez Crisis
objets.notes: In a broadcast speech, Egyptian president Gamal Abdel Nasser gave a codeword order for the occupation and nationalization of the Suez Canal and the closure of the Straits of Tiran to Israeli shipping.

objets.nom: Eight agents of the Israeli internal security service Shin Bet and its foreign intelligence service…
objets.notes: Eight agents of the Israeli internal security service Shin Bet and its foreign intelligence service Mossad abducted Adolf Eichmann, the Nazi officer primarily responsible for the actual implementation of the Holocaust, near his home in San Fernando, Buenos Aires.

objets.nom: Mayor Teddy Kollek of Jerusalem announced that the city had been fully reunified.
Six-Day War
objets.notes: The Israeli air force destroyed the Egyptian air force on the ground over a period of three hours.

objets.nom: Six-Day War: Israel signed a ceasefire with its enemies Egypt, Syria, Jordan, Lebanon and Iraq
objets.notes: Six-Day War: Israel signed a ceasefire with its enemies Egypt, Syria, Jordan, Lebanon and Iraq. It remained in control of the formerly Egyptian Gaza Strip and Sinai Peninsula, the Syrian Golan Heights and the Jordanian West Bank and East Jerusalem.

objets.nom: A Boeing 727-200 serving as Libyan Arab Airlines Flight 114 from Tripoli to Cairo was shot down over the…
objets.notes: A Boeing 727-200 serving as Libyan Arab Airlines Flight 114 from Tripoli to Cairo was shot down over the Sinai Peninsula by Israeli fighter aircraft, killing over one hundred passengers and crew.

objets.nom: Lillehammer affair
objets.notes: A team of fifteen Mossad agents assassinated a Moroccan waiter in Lillehammer in a case of mistaken identity.

objets.nom: Operation Nickel Grass
objets.notes: The United States began an airlift of tanks, artillery, ammunition and supplies to Israel.

objets.nom: Yom Kippur War
objets.notes: Egyptian and Syrian forces simultaneously attacked Israeli positions in the Sinai Peninsula and the Golan Heights, respectively, on the Jewish holiday of Yom Kippur.

objets.nom: Yom Kippur War: Israel, Egypt and Syria agreed to a ceasefire
objets.notes: Yom Kippur War: Israel, Egypt and Syria agreed to a ceasefire. Israel remained in control of new territory north of the Golan Heights and west of the Suez Canal in the south.

objets.nom: Operation Entebbe
objets.notes: Sayeret Matkal freed some hundred hostages held at Entebbe International Airport by hijackers belonging to the Palestinian nationalist Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine – External Operations and the far-left Revolutionary Cells.

objets.nom: 1977 Israeli Air Force Sikorsky CH-53 Sea Stallion crash
objets.notes: An Israeli Air Force Sikorsky CH-53 Sea Stallion crashed in the Jordan Valley, killing fifty-four soldiers.

objets.nom: Israel and Egypt signed the Camp David Accords at the White House
objets.notes: Israel and Egypt signed the Camp David Accords at the White House. The framework agreement provided for the establishment of an autonomous authority in the West Bank and Gaza Strip and for withdrawal of Israeli forces from the Sinai Peninsula in exchange for the establishment of full diplomatic relations with Egypt.

objets.nom: Egypt and Israel signed the Egypt–Israel peace treaty under the framework of the Camp David Accords at…
objets.notes: Egypt and Israel signed the Egypt–Israel peace treaty under the framework of the Camp David Accords at the White House.

objets.nom: The Knesset passed the Jerusalem Law, asserting that Jerusalem was and would remain the undivided…
objets.notes: The Knesset passed the Jerusalem Law, asserting that Jerusalem was and would remain the undivided capital of Israel.

objets.nom: Operation Opera
objets.notes: Israel carried out a surprise air strike on an Iraqi nuclear reactor eleven miles southeast of Baghdad.

objets.nom: 1982 Lebanon War
objets.notes: The IDF invaded southern Lebanon in response to repeated attacks by the Palestinian nationalist Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO), whose militants were sheltered there, on Israeli civilians.

objets.nom: Shlomo Argov, the Israeli ambassador to the United Kingdom, was shot in the head in London in an…
objets.notes: Shlomo Argov, the Israeli ambassador to the United Kingdom, was shot in the head in London in an attempted assassination organized by Iraq's Iraqi Intelligence Service and carried out by the Palestinian nationalist Abu Nidal Organization.

objets.nom: The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) forcibly evacuated Yamit per the terms of the Egypt–Israel peace treaty.
Bus 300 affair
objets.notes: Four Palestinian nationalists hijacked a bus from Tel Aviv to Ashkelon and took its forty passengers hostage.

objets.nom: Operation Moses
objets.notes: The first of some eight thousand Ethiopian Jews were covertly evacuated to Israel from refugee camps in Sudan.

objets.nom: First Intifada
objets.notes: Protests began in the Jabalia Camp in response to the death of four Palestinian civilians in a car crash with an IDF truck.

objets.nom: Mount Carmel Forest Fire
objets.notes: A forest fire began on Mount Carmel which would burn over two square miles over the next three days.

objets.nom: Gulf War
objets.notes: An Iraqi Scud missile landed in Ramat Gan, killing three and injuring nearly a hundred.

objets.nom: Madrid Conference of 1991
objets.notes: A conference opened in Madrid with the goal of reviving the Israeli–Palestinian peace process.

objets.nom: Operation Solomon
objets.notes: An airlift began which would transport some fourteen thousand Ethiopian Jews from Ethiopia to Israel over a thirty-six-hour period.

objets.nom: Israel and the PLO signed the Oslo I Accord in Washington, D.C. The accords provided for the withdrawal…
objets.notes: Israel and the PLO signed the Oslo I Accord in Washington, D.C. The accords provided for the withdrawal of some IDF forces from the West Bank and Gaza Strip and for the establishment of a self-governing authority for the Palestinians, the Palestinian National Authority.

objets.nom: Israel and Jordan signed the Israel–Jordan peace treaty in the Arabah
objets.notes: Israel and Jordan signed the Israel–Jordan peace treaty in the Arabah. The treaty clarified the borders of the two countries and their water rights; each pledged that neither would allow a third country to use its territory to stage an attack on the other.

objets.nom: Assassination of Yitzhak Rabin
objets.notes: The radical nationalist Yigal Amir, an opponent of the Oslo Accords, shot and killed prime minister Yitzhak Rabin after a rally in Tel Aviv.

objets.nom: 1997 Israeli helicopter disaster
objets.notes: Two transport helicopters en route to southern Lebanon collided in midair above She'ar Yashuv, killing all on board.

objets.nom: Maccabiah bridge collapse
objets.notes: A pedestrian bridge collapsed over the Yarkon River in Tel Aviv, killing four.

objets.nom: 2000 Hezbollah cross-border raid
objets.notes: The Lebanese Shia Islamist militant group and political party Hezbollah abducted three Israeli soldiers from the Israeli administered side of the Blue Line, the internationally recognized border.

objets.nom: October 2000 events
objets.notes: The first of a series of riots began in which thirteen Arabs and one Jew would be killed over nine days.

objets.nom: Assassination of Rehavam Ze'evi
objets.notes: Tourism minister Rehavam Ze'evi was shot at a Jerusalem hotel by Hamdi Quran of the Palestinian nationalist Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine. He died of his injuries that night in hospital.

objets.nom: Some four hundred prisoners, the remains of sixty Lebanese militants and civilians, and maps showing the…
objets.notes: Some four hundred prisoners, the remains of sixty Lebanese militants and civilians, and maps showing the locations of Israeli mines in southern Lebanon, were transferred to Hezbollah in exchange for the bodies of the three soldiers abducted in 2000, as well as the abducted Israeli reservist Elhanan Tannenbaum.

objets.nom: Israeli disengagement from Gaza
objets.notes: The last Israeli settlers and security personnel were withdrawn from the Gaza Strip.

objets.nom: 2006 Hezbollah cross-border raid
objets.notes: Hezbollah forces crossed into Israel and ambushed two IDF vehicles, killing three soldiers and capturing two others.

objets.nom: 2006 Lebanon War
objets.notes: Israeli forces began shelling Lebanese territory in response to the Hezbollah attack of earlier that morning.

objets.nom: Operation Orchard
objets.notes: Israel carried out a surprise air strike on a suspected nuclear reactor in Syria's Deir ez-Zor Governorate.

objets.nom: Gaza War
objets.notes: Israel began conducting a series of airstrikes on assets of the Palestinian Sunni Islamist organization Hamas in the Gaza Strip in response to ongoing rocket fire on the western Negev.

objets.nom: Gaza flotilla raid
objets.notes: The navy boarded a flotilla organized by the Free Gaza Movement and the Turkish Foundation for Human Rights and Freedoms and Humanitarian Relief, which was attempting to break an Israeli and Egyptian blockade of the Gaza Strip, in international waters. During the takeover, a violent confrontation erupted on board the MV Mavi Marmara in which nine…

objets.nom: Mount Carmel Forest Fire
objets.notes: A forest fire began on Mount Carmel which would kill forty and burn nearly twenty square miles over the next three days.

objets.nom: 2011 Israeli social justice protests
objets.notes: Filmmaker Daphni Leef set up a tent in Habima Square and invited others to join a protest over the absence of affordable housing.

objets.nom: 2011 attack on the Israeli Embassy in Egypt
objets.notes: A crowd of thousands of Egyptian protestors breached the Israeli embassy in Cairo.

objets.nom: Gilad Shalit prisoner exchange
objets.notes: Hamas released the Israeli soldier Gilad Shalit to Egypt in exchange for one thousand Palestinian other Arab prisoners held in Israel, including some three hundred serving life sentences for planning and perpetrating terror attacks.

objets.nom: Operation Pillar of Defense
objets.notes: The IDF began an eight-day anti-Hamas operation in the Gaza Strip, a response to ongoing rocket fire on the western Negev, with an airstrike on the senior officer Ahmed Jabari.

objets.nom: 2014 Israel–Gaza conflict
objets.notes: The IDF launched a series of airstrikes against Hamas targets in the Gaza Strip.

objets.nom: United States recognition of Jerusalem as the capital of Israel
objets.notes: U.S. president Donald Trump formally announces the United States recognition of Jerusalem as the capital of Israel.

objets.nom: United States recognition of Israel's sovereignty over the Golan Heights
objets.notes: U.S. president Donald Trump signed a presidential proclamation to officially recognize Israel's sovereignty over the Golan Heights.

objets.nom: Israel–Morocco normalization agreement
objets.notes: Following the Abraham Accords, Israel and Morocco signed a security cooperation agreement and began normalizing relations.

objets.nom: 2021 Meron stampede
objets.notes: The deadliest civil disaster in Israel's history.

objets.nom: Naftali Bennett of the Yamina party was sworn in as Prime Minister, forming a coalition government with…
objets.notes: Naftali Bennett of the Yamina party was sworn in as Prime Minister, forming a coalition government with Yair Lapid of the Yesh Atid party, marking the end of Benjamin Netanyahu's 12-year tenure as prime minister.

objets.nom: 2023 Israeli judicial reform protests
objets.notes: Large-scale protests erupted across Israel in response to proposed judicial reforms by the Netanyahu government, which critics argued would undermine judicial independence.

objets.nom: October 7 attacks and Gaza war: Hamas and several other Palestinian militant groups launched coordinated…
objets.notes: October 7 attacks and Gaza war: Hamas and several other Palestinian militant groups launched coordinated armed incursions from the Gaza Strip into southern Israel, killing 1,143 and taking 250 hostages, marking the deadliest attack in Israeli history and the first invasion of Israeli territory since the 1948 Arab–Israeli War.

objets.nom: Operation Shield and Arrow
objets.notes: The IDF launched a series of airstrikes against Palestinian Islamic Jihad targets in Gaza following rocket fire towards southern Israel.

objets.nom: The height of the Canaanite town of Ugarit.
A crisis led to the Bronze Age collapse
objets.notes: A crisis led to the Bronze Age collapse. Cities all around the eastern Mediterranean were sacked within a span of a few decades by assorted raiders.

objets.nom: Phoenicians invent the alphabet and the Tyrian Purple which was a major component in their trade.
Vers -1200 : naissance de la civilisation phénicienne.
objets.fr: Vers -1200 : naissance de la civilisation phénicienne.

objets.nom: Shalmaneser III devastates the territory of Damascus; Palestine and the Phoenician cities send tribute.
Carthage is founded by Phoenicians.
The reign of king Pygmalion of Tyre ends.
Hiram II becomes king of Tyre.
Mattan II succeeds Hiram II as king.
The Assyrians under king Shalmaneser V start a four-year siege of Tyre that ends in 720 BC.
Judah, Tyre and Sidon revolt against Assyria.
The Assyrian siege of Tyre by king Sennacherib.
The Assyrian siege of Tyre by king Ashurbanipal.
The region is annexed to the Babylonian empire, while Jerusalem fell into their hands.
The Babylonians under king Nebuchadnezzar II sieged Tyre for thirteen years without success
objets.notes: The Babylonians under king Nebuchadnezzar II sieged Tyre for thirteen years without success. Later a compromise peace was made in which Tyre had to pay tribute to the Babylonians. (to 573 BC)

objets.nom: Cyrus the Great conquered Phoenicia.
A rebellion in Sidon led by Tennes was crushed by Artaxerxes III, and its destruction was dramatically…
objets.notes: A rebellion in Sidon led by Tennes was crushed by Artaxerxes III, and its destruction was dramatically described by Diodorus Siculus. (to 345 BC)

objets.nom: Alexander the Great took Tyre following the city's siege
objets.notes: Alexander the Great took Tyre following the city's siege. After Alexander's death Phoenicia witnessed a succession of Hellenistic rulers: Laomedon (323 BC), Ptolemy I (320 BC), Antigonus II (315 BC), Demetrius (301 BC), and Seleucus (296 BC).

objets.nom: Alexander's former general Antigonus begins his own siege of Tyre, taking the city a year later.
Phoenicia (except for Aradus) fell to the Ptolemies of Egypt.
Phoenicia along with Syria reverted to the Seleucids, and the region became increasingly Hellenized,…
objets.notes: Phoenicia along with Syria reverted to the Seleucids, and the region became increasingly Hellenized, although Tyre actually became autonomous in 126 BC, followed by Sidon in 111 BC.

objets.nom: Beirut was taken and destroyed by Diodotus Tryphon in his contest with Antiochus VII Sidetes for the…
objets.notes: Beirut was taken and destroyed by Diodotus Tryphon in his contest with Antiochus VII Sidetes for the throne of the Seleucid monarchy. It was later named Laodicea in Phoenicia (Λαοδικεια ή του Φοινίκη).

objets.nom: Syria, including Phoenicia, were seized by king Tigranes the Great who was later defeated by Lucullus
objets.notes: Syria, including Phoenicia, were seized by king Tigranes the Great who was later defeated by Lucullus. (to 69 BC)

objets.nom: Pompey finally incorporated Phoenicia as part of the Roman province of Syria.
Beirut was conquered by Agrippa and the city was renamed in honour of the emperor's daughter, Julia; its…
objets.notes: Beirut was conquered by Agrippa and the city was renamed in honour of the emperor's daughter, Julia; its full name became Colonia Julia Augusta Felix Berytus.

objets.nom: The Pax Romana period, inhabitants of the principal Phoenician cities of Byblos, Sidon, and Tyre were…
objets.notes: the Pax Romana period, inhabitants of the principal Phoenician cities of Byblos, Sidon, and Tyre were granted Roman citizenship, while economic and intellectual activities flourished. (to AD 180)

objets.nom: Le père jésuite Gérard de Martimprey, recteur de l'université Saint-Joseph de Beyrouth est contraint par…
objets.fr: Le père jésuite Gérard de Martimprey, recteur de l'université Saint-Joseph de Beyrouth est contraint par…
objets.notes: le père jésuite Gérard de Martimprey, recteur de l'université Saint-Joseph de Beyrouth est contraint par le sous-directeur de la police, Othman bey, accompagné de quelques policiers, de lui remettre les clés de l'établissement. Celui-ci, ainsi que tous les autres établissements français, est fermé en raison du droit de la guerre.

objets.nom: Beirut's school of law was founded, it later became widely known in the surrounding region
objets.notes: Beirut's school of law was founded, it later became widely known in the surrounding region. Two of Rome's most famous jurists, Papinian and Ulpian (both natives of Phoenicia), were taught at the law school under the Severan emperors.

objets.nom: Départ des Anglais et des Français de Beyrouth, par la mer
objets.fr: Départ des Anglais et des Français de Beyrouth, par la mer
objets.notes: départ des Anglais et des Français de Beyrouth, par la mer. Le gouvernement ottoman de Mehmed V s'approprie les écoles étrangères pour en faire des écoles ottomanes.

objets.nom: Saint Paul of Tarsus begins his third mission and preaches in Tyre.
The Maronites, a Christian community named after Saint Maron sought refuge in the mountains of Lebanon.
Beirut is destroyed by an earthquake and tsunami
objets.notes: Beirut is destroyed by an earthquake and tsunami. About 30,000 were killed in the city alone and, along the Phoenician coast, total casualties were close to 250,000.

objets.nom: The Marada, a group of autonomous Maronite communities, settled in Mount Lebanon and the surrounding…
objets.notes: The Marada, a group of autonomous Maronite communities, settled in Mount Lebanon and the surrounding highlands following the conquest of Syria by the Arab caliphate.

objets.nom: Calling for a jihad against non-Muslims, Muhammad's successor, Caliph Abu Bakr, brought Islam to the…
objets.notes: Calling for a jihad against non-Muslims, Muhammad's successor, Caliph Abu Bakr, brought Islam to the area surrounding Lebanon. (to 634)

objets.nom: Califat omeyyade
objets.fr: Califat omeyyade

objets.nom: Conquête du Liban par les Arabes musulmans.
objets.fr: Conquête du Liban par les Arabes musulmans.

objets.nom: After the Battle of Yarmuk, Caliph Umar appointed the Arab Muawiyah I, founder of the Umayyad dynasty,…
objets.notes: After the Battle of Yarmuk, Caliph Umar appointed the Arab Muawiyah I, founder of the Umayyad dynasty, as governor of Syria, an area that included present-day Lebanon.

objets.nom: Muawiyah negotiated an agreement with Constantine IV, the Byzantine emperor, whereby he agreed to pay…
objets.notes: Muawiyah negotiated an agreement with Constantine IV, the Byzantine emperor, whereby he agreed to pay Constantine an annual tribute in return for the cessation of Marada incursions.

objets.nom: Callinicus of Heliopolis, a Byzantine chemist from Heliopolis, invents the Greek fire in Constantinople.
Califat abbasside
objets.fr: Califat abbasside

objets.nom: An abortive rebellion of Lebanese mountaineers against the Abbasid rule after the harsh treatment of…
objets.notes: An abortive rebellion of Lebanese mountaineers against the Abbasid rule after the harsh treatment of people living in the Lebanese-Syrian region.

objets.nom: The Jordan valley is occupied by the Tulunids, extending in the north to the outposts in the…
objets.notes: The Jordan valley is occupied by the Tulunids, extending in the north to the outposts in the Anti-Lebanon mountains on the Byzantine border, enabling them to defend Egypt against Abbasid attack.

objets.nom: Prince 'Allaqa of Tyre proclaimed his independence from the Abbasids and coined money in his own name.
The Fatimides settled in Egypt and extended their authority to the coastal region of Bilad al-Sham and…
objets.notes: The Fatimides settled in Egypt and extended their authority to the coastal region of Bilad al-Sham and Damascus.

objets.nom: Under the Fatimid Caliph Al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah, a new religion was born and spread by a man called Ad-Darazi
objets.notes: Under the Fatimid Caliph Al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah, a new religion was born and spread by a man called Ad-Darazi. This was the beginning of the Druze religion and its expansion in several Lebanese regions.

objets.nom: Dans le cadre de la conquête par les Croisés du royaume de Jérusalem, les croisés forment les États…
objets.fr: Dans le cadre de la conquête par les Croisés du royaume de Jérusalem, les croisés forment les États…
objets.notes: Dans le cadre de la conquête par les Croisés du royaume de Jérusalem, les croisés forment les États latins d'Orient. Parmi eux, le comté de Tripoli forme l'essentiel du territoire de l'actuel Liban.

objets.nom: Beirut and Sidon are captured.
Tyre resisted the raids but finally capitulated after a long siege.
The Battle of Marj Ayyun took place on 10 June, where an Ayyubid army commanded by Saladin defeated a…
objets.notes: The Battle of Marj Ayyun took place on 10 June, where an Ayyubid army commanded by Saladin defeated a Crusader army led by King Baldwin IV of Jerusalem.

objets.nom: The Battle of Belvoir Castle in which a Crusader force led by King Baldwin IV of Jerusalem sparred…
objets.notes: The Battle of Belvoir Castle in which a Crusader force led by King Baldwin IV of Jerusalem sparred inconclusively with an Ayyubid army from Egypt commanded by Saladin. The theatre of operations included Eilat, the Transjordan, Galilee and Beirut (which witnessed a siege by Saladin that ended in August of the same year).

objets.nom: Saladin conquers virtually all of the Kingdom of Jerusalem with the exception of Tyre, which held out…
objets.notes: Saladin conquers virtually all of the Kingdom of Jerusalem with the exception of Tyre, which held out under Conrad of Montferrat.

objets.nom: Richard the Lionheart signed a treaty with Saladin, restoring the Kingdom of Jerusalem to a coastal…
objets.notes: Richard the Lionheart signed a treaty with Saladin, restoring the Kingdom of Jerusalem to a coastal strip between Jaffa and Beirut.

objets.nom: The county of Tripoli becomes a vassal state of the Mongol Empire.
The county of Tripoli falls into the hands of the Mamluks after the attack of Egyptian Sultan Qalawun in…
objets.notes: The county of Tripoli falls into the hands of the Mamluks after the attack of Egyptian Sultan Qalawun in March.

objets.nom: Conquête par le Sultanat mamelouk
objets.fr: Conquête par le Sultanat mamelouk

objets.nom: The Shia Muslims and Druze, in Lebanon, rebelled against the Mamluks who were busy fighting the European…
objets.notes: The Shia Muslims and Druze, in Lebanon, rebelled against the Mamluks who were busy fighting the European Crusaders and Mongols.

objets.nom: The Ottoman Sultan Selim I grants Emir Fakhr ad-Din I a semi-autonomous reign in Lebanon.
