objets.notes: victoires en Étrurie du Sud, création de 4 tribus rustiques et installation de colons romains sur ce territoire

objets.nom: Défaite romaine à l’Allia contre les Gaulois menés par Brennus
objets.fr: Défaite romaine à l’Allia contre les Gaulois menés par Brennus
objets.notes: Défaite romaine à l’Allia contre les Gaulois menés par Brennus. Les vestales et les prêtres sont mis en sécurité dans la ville étrusque de Caere (Cerveteri), Rome est mise à sac, des sénateurs restés sur place sont massacrés. Résistance de Marcus Manlius Capitolinus sur le Capitole (Épisode des oies du Capitole). Brennus évacue Rome contre rançon.…

objets.nom: Battle of the Frigidus
objets.notes: Forces loyal to Theodosius the Great defeated and killed Arbogast and Eugenius, probably near the Vipava.

objets.nom: Gildonic War
objets.notes: Gildo, comes of Africa, was killed following a failed rebellion against the Western Roman Empire.

objets.nom: Veies est prise par le dictateur Camille après 10 ans de siège, ainsi que ses alliés, les cités de…
objets.fr: Veies est prise par le dictateur Camille après 10 ans de siège, ainsi que ses alliés, les cités de…
objets.notes: Veies est prise par le dictateur Camille après 10 ans de siège, ainsi que ses alliés, les cités de Faléries et de Capenes.

objets.nom: Crossing of the Rhine
objets.notes: A coalition of foreign tribes including the Vandals, Alans and Suebi invaded the Western Roman Empire across the Rhine.

objets.nom: Sack of Rome (410)
objets.notes: Rome was sacked by the Visigoths under their king Alaric I.

objets.nom: Les plébéiens réclament l’égalité politique
objets.fr: Les plébéiens réclament l’égalité politique
objets.notes: Les plébéiens réclament l’égalité politique. Les patriciens remplacent le consulat par le tribunat militaire avec pouvoir consulaire, accessible aux plébéiens, et par la fonction de censeur réservée aux patriciens

objets.nom: Le tribun de la plèbe Caius Canuleius obtient l’autorisation du mariage entre plébéien et patricien (Lex…
objets.fr: Le tribun de la plèbe Caius Canuleius obtient l’autorisation du mariage entre plébéien et patricien (Lex…
objets.notes: Le tribun de la plèbe Caius Canuleius obtient l’autorisation du mariage entre plébéien et patricien (Lex Canuleia).

objets.nom: Battle of the Utus
objets.notes: The Huns under Attila defeated a Byzantine army in a bloody battle near the Utus.

objets.nom: Par la loi Horatia Valeria, les tribuns de la plèbe deviennent sacrés, leurs plébiscites ont force de…
objets.fr: Par la loi Horatia Valeria, les tribuns de la plèbe deviennent sacrés, leurs plébiscites ont force de…
objets.notes: Par la loi Horatia Valeria, les tribuns de la plèbe deviennent sacrés, leurs plébiscites ont force de loi et ils peuvent faire appel auprès du peuple (provocatio)

objets.nom: Les tribuns de la plèbe obtiennent enfin que les lois soient écrites et connues de tous
objets.fr: Les tribuns de la plèbe obtiennent enfin que les lois soient écrites et connues de tous
objets.notes: Les tribuns de la plèbe obtiennent enfin que les lois soient écrites et connues de tous. Dix anciens consuls, les Decemviri, investis du pouvoir absolu, rédigent la Loi des Douze Tables publiée sur le forum. Elle établit l’égalité devant la loi entre patriciens et plébéiens, mais interdit les mariages mixtes.

objets.nom: Sack of Rome (455)
objets.notes: The Vandals entered and began to sack Rome.

objets.nom: Battle of Cap Bon (468)
objets.notes: The Vandal Kingdom destroyed a combined Western Roman and Byzantine invasion fleet at Cap Bon.

objets.nom: ~495/493 Première sécession de la plèbe à la suite d'une nouvelle guerre contre les Volsques
objets.fr: ~495/493 Première sécession de la plèbe à la suite d'une nouvelle guerre contre les Volsques
objets.notes: ~495/493 Première sécession de la plèbe à la suite d'une nouvelle guerre contre les Volsques. La plèbe, accablée de dettes, refuse de se mobiliser et réclame des droits dans une République dirigée par les oligarques du Sénat, les patriciens. À la suite d'un édit protégeant les débiteurs, la plèbe calmée s'engage, et vainc les Volsques, les Sabins…

objets.nom: ~500/493 Guerre contre les Latins : création de la fonction de dictateur, patricien désigné pour six…
objets.fr: ~500/493 Guerre contre les Latins : création de la fonction de dictateur, patricien désigné pour six…
objets.notes: ~500/493 Guerre contre les Latins : création de la fonction de dictateur, patricien désigné pour six mois au maximum en cas de menace grave pour Rome pour faire face aux Latins menés par Octavius Mamilius et Tarquin le Superbe. Bataille du lac Régille (499 ou 496), victoire du dictateur Aulus Postumius Albus contre les Latins. Mort de Tarquin le…

objets.nom: Battle of Ad Decimum
objets.notes: A Byzantine army defeated a Vandal force near Carthage.

objets.nom: Battle of Tricamarum
objets.notes: The Byzantines defeated a Vandal army and forced their king Gelimer into flight.

objets.nom: Vandalic War
objets.notes: A Byzantine force under the general Belisarius departed for the Vandal Kingdom.

objets.nom: Gothic War (535–554)
objets.notes: Byzantine forces crossing from Africa invaded Sicily, then an Ostrogothic possession.

objets.nom: Battle of Taginae
objets.notes: A Byzantine army dealt a decisive defeat to the Ostrogoths at Gualdo Tadino. The Ostrogoth king Totila was killed.

objets.nom: Battle of Mons Lactarius
objets.notes: An Ostrogothic force was ambushed and destroyed at Monti Lattari on its way to relieve a Byzantine siege of Cumae. The Ostrogoth king Teia was killed.

objets.nom: Siege of Constantinople (626)
objets.notes: Sasanian and Avar forces laid siege to Constantinople.

objets.nom: Muslim conquest of the Levant
objets.notes: A Rashidun army departed Medina for the Levant.

objets.nom: Siege of Alexandria (641)
objets.notes: Byzantine authorities in the Egyptian capital Alexandria surrendered to the besieging Rashidun army.

objets.nom: Second Council of Nicaea
objets.notes: An ecumenical council in Nicaea ended which endorsed the veneration of images, ending the first Byzantine Iconoclasm.

objets.nom: Battle of Kleidion
objets.notes: Basil dealt a decisive and bloody defeat to Bulgarian forces in the Belasica near Klyuch.

objets.nom: East–West Schism
objets.notes: The papal legate Humbert of Silva Candida laid on the altar of Hagia Sophia a document proclaiming the excommunication of Michael I Cerularius, the patriarch of Constantinople.

objets.nom: Battle of Manzikert
objets.notes: The Byzantine Empire was decisively defeated by a Seljuk force near Malazgirt. The basileus Romanos IV Diogenes was captured.

objets.nom: Siege of Bari
objets.notes: Italo-Norman forces captured Bari, capital of the katepanikion of Italy.

objets.nom: Siege of Nicaea
objets.notes: The Rum occupants of Nicaea surrendered to Byzantine and First Crusader forces.

objets.nom: Siege of Constantinople (1204)
objets.notes: Fourth Crusaders breached and sacked Constantinople, deposed the basileus Alexios V Doukas and established the Latin Empire under their leader Baldwin I, Latin Emperor as Latin Emperor. Theodore I Laskaris was acclaimed basileus but forced to flee with his court to establish the Empire of Nicaea at Nicaea.

objets.nom: Byzantine civil war of 1341–47
objets.notes: The regent John VI Kantakouzenos was declared basileus by his supporters in opposition to the young John V Palaiologos.

objets.nom: Fall of Constantinople
objets.notes: Ottoman forces entered Constantinople. Basileus Constantine XI Palaiologos was killed.

objets.nom: Ceramics are found in Peru.
The Caral people disappear, but the Cupisnique culture starts to develop.
The Ilama culture develops near the Calima River in the Valle del Cauca.
Chavin culture emerges in the Andes, and the Pucara people appear in the South.
Cave paintings are created near the Inírida River in modern-day Vichada Department.
The farming and fishing town of Paracas emerges on the Southern coast.
The cultures of the Salinar, Gallinazo, Cajamarca and Vicus people are founded.
The Chavin culture collapsed, parallel to the first emergence of militarized cultures, such as Moche in…
objets.notes: The Chavin culture collapsed, parallel to the first emergence of militarized cultures, such as Moche in the North, Nazca in the South and Tihuanaco in the Highlands.

objets.nom: The earliest traces of humans are dated from the Paleolithic period, and there are further signs in the…
objets.notes: The earliest traces of humans are dated from the Paleolithic period, and there are further signs in the Mesolithic and Neolithic. However, large areas of the interior were apparently depopulated during an extensive dry period between 4000 and 2000 BC.

objets.nom: Several corn-based civilizations developed in the western and northwestern Andean region (Ansilta,…
objets.notes: Several corn-based civilizations developed in the western and northwestern Andean region (Ansilta, Condorhuasi, Cienaga, Aguada, Santa Maria, Huarpes, Diaguitas, Sanavirones, among others)

objets.nom: L'Espagne et le Portugal signent, contraints par le pape Alexandre VI, le traité de Tordesillas, par…
objets.fr: L'Espagne et le Portugal signent, contraints par le pape Alexandre VI, le traité de Tordesillas, par…
objets.notes: L'Espagne et le Portugal signent, contraints par le pape Alexandre VI, le traité de Tordesillas, par lequel, ces deux puissances s'entendent sur le partage des territoires du Nouveau Monde : tout ce qui serait découvert à l'ouest de la longitude 50° appartiendrait à l'Espagne, et tout ce qui serait à l'est (Afrique comprise) appartiendrait au…

objets.nom: First societies develop in the region of Norte Chico; amongst them the Caral, the oldest civilization in…
objets.notes: First societies develop in the region of Norte Chico; amongst them the Caral, the oldest civilization in the Americas.

objets.nom: Nomadic hunter-gatherer communities were established, including the Paccaicasa, Chivateros, Toquepala,…
objets.notes: Nomadic hunter-gatherer communities were established, including the Paccaicasa, Chivateros, Toquepala, Lauricocha and Paiján.

objets.nom: Sedentary lifestyles emerged, accompanied by agriculture and livestock farming, with it the people of…
objets.notes: Sedentary lifestyles emerged, accompanied by agriculture and livestock farming, with it the people of Tablada de Lurin, Cerro Paloma, Huaca Prieta and Kotosh.

objets.nom: Semi-nomadic horticulturist communities are established, such as the Guitarrero, Pikimachay, Chilca,…
objets.notes: Semi-nomadic horticulturist communities are established, such as the Guitarrero, Pikimachay, Chilca, Telamarchay and Jayhuamachay.

objets.nom: The first humans arrive on what is currently Peruvian land
objets.notes: The first humans arrive on what is currently Peruvian land. The first settlement in Peru takes place about 20.000 years ago.

objets.nom: The Chibcha civilization expands from the northern Andes including part of what is now Panama, the high…
objets.notes: the Chibcha civilization expands from the northern Andes including part of what is now Panama, the high plains of the Eastern Sierra of Colombia the areas of modern departments of Santander (North and South), Boyacá and Cundinamarca, becoming the most populous zone between the Mayan and Inca Empires.

objets.nom: Cueva de las Manos was last inhabited, with the final cave dwellers possibly being ancestors of the…
objets.notes: Cueva de las Manos was last inhabited, with the final cave dwellers possibly being ancestors of the Tehuelche tribes.

objets.nom: Tiwanaku Empire collapses ushering migratory and societal changes that reach as far south as Araucanía.
Sinchi Roca was succeeded by his son Lloque Yupanqui.
Lloque Yupanqui was succeeded by his son Mayta Cápac.
Possible date for a Cunco-Huilliche migration to Chiloé Island
objets.notes: Possible date for a Cunco-Huilliche migration to Chiloé Island. Chonos were possibly displaced further such to places like Guaitecas Archipelago.

objets.nom: Mayta Cápac was succeeded by his son Cápac Yupanqui.
Cápac Yupanqui was succeeded by his son Inca Roca.
Inca Roca died
objets.notes: Inca Roca died. His heir Quispe Yupanqui was killed in a coup, and the throne went to Yáhuar Huácac, another son.

objets.nom: Yáhuar Huácac was succeeded by his son Viracocha.
A 9.4 MS-strong earthquake shakes Chile's Atacama Region causing tsunamis in Chile as well as Hawaii and…
objets.notes: a 9.4 MS-strong earthquake shakes Chile's Atacama Region causing tsunamis in Chile as well as Hawaii and Japan.

objets.nom: Viracocha was succeeded by his son Pachacuti, who would expand Cuzco into the Inca Empire.
Hunzahúa becomes zaque of Hunza (to 1470).
Meicuchuca becomes zipa of Bacatá (to 1470).
Michuá becomes zaque of Hunza (to 1490).
At some point in this time interval the battle of the Maule between Incas and Mapuches may have occurred.
Pachacuti died
objets.notes: Pachacuti died. His son Tupac Inca Yupanqui succeeded him.

objets.nom: The Inca Empire, under the rule of emperor Pachacutec, launched an offensive and conquered present-day…
objets.notes: The Inca Empire, under the rule of emperor Pachacutec, launched an offensive and conquered present-day northwestern Argentina, integrating it into a region called Qullasuyu

objets.nom: Voyages of Christopher Columbus
objets.notes: navigator Christopher Columbus, sailing in the employ of Castile and Aragon, departed from Palos de la Frontera in search of a westward route to the East Indies.

objets.nom: Tupac Inca Yupanqui died and was succeeded by Huayna Capac.
Treaty of Tordesillas
objets.notes: Spain and Portugal divide the New World between themselves. Even though the treaty was negotiated without consulting the Pope, a few sources call the resulting line the "Papal Line of Demarcation".

objets.nom: Spanish explorer Juan de la Cosa lands on what is today called Cabo de la Vela (Cape of Sails) in the…
objets.notes: Spanish explorer Juan de la Cosa lands on what is today called Cabo de la Vela (Cape of Sails) in the Guajira Peninsula.

objets.nom: Portuguese explorers, led either by Gaspar de Lemos or Gonçalo Coelho, sail into Guanabara Bay, Brazil,…
objets.notes: Portuguese explorers, led either by Gaspar de Lemos or Gonçalo Coelho, sail into Guanabara Bay, Brazil, which they name Rio de Janeiro.

objets.nom: The Inca Emperor Túpac Yupanqui reached Itata River
The Fernando de Noronha island is discovered by a Portuguese expedition, organized and financed by a…
objets.notes: The Fernando de Noronha island is discovered by a Portuguese expedition, organized and financed by a private commercial consortium headed by the Lisbon merchant Fernão de Loronha. The expedition is under the overall command of captain Gonçalo Coelho and carries the Italian adventurer Amerigo Vespucci aboard, who writes an account of it.

objets.nom: Diego de Enciso and Vasco Núñez de Balboa founded the village of Santa María la Antigua del Darién,…
objets.notes: Diego de Enciso and Vasco Núñez de Balboa founded the village of Santa María la Antigua del Darién, initially called The Antigua

objets.nom: Vasco Núñez de Balboa becomes the first European to sight the Pacific Ocean from the New World; he calls…
objets.notes: Vasco Núñez de Balboa becomes the first European to sight the Pacific Ocean from the New World; he calls it Mar del Sur.

objets.nom: Spanish navigator Juan Díaz de Solís first European explorer to visit Río de la Plata, on territory…
objets.notes: Spanish navigator Juan Díaz de Solís first European explorer to visit Río de la Plata, on territory which is now Argentina; Díaz de Solís killed and supposedly cannibalised by native Charrúa, Querandí or Guaraní

objets.nom: Explorer Ferdinand Magellan's expedition finds the passage now known as the Strait of Magellan
objets.notes: Explorer Ferdinand Magellan's expedition finds the passage now known as the Strait of Magellan. In the process, they become the first Europeans to describe Chilean Patagonia and its inhabitants.

objets.nom: Sebastian Cabot sailed up Paraná River and built short-lived fort near modern Rosario
Huayna Capac died and was succeeded by his heir Ninan Cuyochi.
A possible date for the battle of the Maule between Incas and Mapuches.
At the Battle of Cajamarca, the Spanish army took the Inca emperor Atahualpa prisoner, marking the end…
objets.notes: At the Battle of Cajamarca, the Spanish army took the Inca emperor Atahualpa prisoner, marking the end of his empire.

objets.nom: Atahualpa's army, led by Quizquiz and Chalcuchimac, captures Huáscar at the Battle of Quipaipan
objets.notes: Atahualpa's army, led by Quizquiz and Chalcuchimac, captures Huáscar at the Battle of Quipaipan. Atahualpa proclaims himself Inca, thus ending the Civil War.

objets.nom: Atalhualpa's army, led by Quizquiz, captures Cuzco.
Francisco Pizarro arrives in Peru from Panamá. He begins the Conquest of the Inca Empire and captures…
objets.notes: Francisco Pizarro arrives in Peru from Panamá. He begins the Conquest of the Inca Empire and captures Emperor Atahualpa during the Battle of Cajamarca.

objets.nom: Francisco Pizarro, a conquistador, arrives with a troop of Spaniards at the Northern coast of Peru.
Pizarro arrives at Cajamarca, with the intention of meeting Atahualpa.
Pizarro founds the city of San Miguel, now Piura, considered the first city the Spanish founded in Peru.
The Spanish founded the port of San Francisco de la Buenaesperanza, now Paita, considered the oldest…
objets.notes: The Spanish founded the port of San Francisco de la Buenaesperanza, now Paita, considered the oldest port in Peru.

objets.nom: Spaniards founded the city of Lima.
Spanish Conquistador Diego de Almagro begins his expedition to the lands south of Peru through the…
objets.notes: Spanish Conquistador Diego de Almagro begins his expedition to the lands south of Peru through the eastern side of the Andes Mountains.

objets.nom: Almagro sends an expedition under :es:Gómez de Alvarado southwards toward the Bio-Bio region
objets.notes: Almagro sends an expedition under :es:Gómez de Alvarado southwards toward the Bio-Bio region. The expedition ends at the Battle of Reynogüelén, near the Itata River, being considered the first battle between Spaniards and Mapuches.

objets.nom: Almagro's expedition crosses the Andes into the Copiapó River valley and explores the central region of…
objets.notes: Almagro's expedition crosses the Andes into the Copiapó River valley and explores the central region of Chile as far south as the Aconcagua River valley.

objets.nom: Santa María del Buen Ayre founded by Pedro de Mendoza on site of modern Buenos Aires
Sagipa becomes the last zipa of Bacatá
The Sun Temple in Sogamoso (name in Muysccubun: Sugamuxi) was burned by Spanish soldiers
Zipa Tisquesusa is beaten in the Spanish conquest of the Muisca at Funza
The Panche are beaten by an alliance of zipa Sagipa and Spanish conquistadors in the Battle of Tocarema
Cacica Gaitana starts the Paezan revolt against the Spanish conquest
King Carlos V appointed Santa Fe de Bogotá the title of city
An uprising led by toqui Michimalonco attacks fledgling Santiago in an attempt to drive out the Spanish
objets.notes: An uprising led by toqui Michimalonco attacks fledgling Santiago in an attempt to drive out the Spanish. Key actions undertaken by Inés de Suárez, the first Spanish woman to set foot in Chile, are attributed with avoiding the complete destruction of the outnumbered settlement.

objets.nom: The Viceroyalty of Peru was established.
Foundation of the port of Arica
objets.notes: Foundation of the port of Arica. The port becomes a key staging point between the mines of Potosí in Upper Peru (now Bolivia) and Lima.

objets.nom: Mapuche child Lautaro is captured by the Spanish and made a yanacona
objets.notes: Mapuche child Lautaro is captured by the Spanish and made a yanacona. Eventually, Lautaro becomes personal page of Pedro de Valdivia.

objets.nom: Battle of Tucapel
objets.notes: Mapuches led by Lautaro defeat the Spanish at the ruins of Tucapel capturing Pedro de Valdivia who is then executed. A general Mapuche uprising develops under Lautaro.

objets.nom: Santiago del Estero founded by Francisco de Aguirre (some claim 1550)
Missionaries Joseph of Anchieta and Manuel da Nóbrega establish São Paulo, then named São Paulo dos…
objets.notes: Missionaries Joseph of Anchieta and Manuel da Nóbrega establish São Paulo, then named São Paulo dos Campos de Piratininga, in southeast Brazil.

objets.nom: Battle of Mataquito
objets.notes: A Spanish force led by Francisco de Villagra defeats the forces of Lautaro, killing him amidst the battle. Caupolicán assumes the role of Mapuche toqui (wartime chief).

objets.nom: Chiloé Archipelago is claimed by Spain
objets.notes: Chiloé Archipelago is claimed by Spain. Martín Ruiz de Gamboa founds Castro on the main island; the southernmost European settlement at that time.

objets.nom: End of the Neo-Inca State in Vilcabamba.
Córdoba and Santa Fe founded
Earthquake in Valdivia causes extensive damage in Valdivia and surrounding cities of Villarrica, Osorno,…
objets.notes: Earthquake in Valdivia causes extensive damage in Valdivia and surrounding cities of Villarrica, Osorno, and Castro. As in the 1960 Valdivia earthquake, the Riñihue Lake dams.

objets.nom: Francis Drake attacks the coast of Chile during his circumnavigation of the earth; La Serena and…
objets.notes: Francis Drake attacks the coast of Chile during his circumnavigation of the earth; La Serena and Valparaíso are plundered.

objets.nom: Birth of Saint Martin de Porres.
Iberian Union
objets.notes: King Philip II of Spain becomes King of Portugal under the name Philip I, following the death without heirs of King Henry of Portugal, in a personal union of the crowns, thus maintaining Portuguese independence (in Europe and throughout the Portuguese Empire, including Brazil). The Philippine Dynasty rule lasts until 1640.

objets.nom: Permanent colony re-established by Spain on the site of Buenos Aires as part of the Viceroyalty of Peru;…
objets.notes: Permanent colony re-established by Spain on the site of Buenos Aires as part of the Viceroyalty of Peru; initial settlement was primarily overland from Peru

objets.nom: Gamboa founds the settlement Rey Don Felipe in the Strait of Magellan
objets.notes: Gamboa founds the settlement Rey Don Felipe in the Strait of Magellan. By 1587 both settlements lay in ruins, leading English pirate Thomas Cavendish to dub Rey Don Felipe as Port Famine.

objets.nom: Pedro Sarmiento de Gamboa founds the settlement Nombre de Jesús on the eastern end of the Strait of Magellan.
Birth of Isabel Flores de Oliva, later Saint Rose of Lima.
English privateer Thomas Cavendish loots Santos and São Vicente before losing most of the crew in a…
objets.notes: English privateer Thomas Cavendish loots Santos and São Vicente before losing most of the crew in a battle against the Portuguese at the village of Vitória.

objets.nom: Anglo–Spanish War
objets.notes: an English military expedition led by James Lancaster captures Recife.

objets.nom: English corsair Francis Drake attacks Riohacha
Battle of Curalaba
objets.notes: Governor Martín García Óñez de Loyola killed in a Mapuche ambush.

objets.nom: The Real Situado, an annual payment of silver from Potosí to Chile, is established.
Huaynaputina volcano in Peru erupted catastrophically, in the largest volcanic explosion in South…
objets.notes: Huaynaputina volcano in Peru erupted catastrophically, in the largest volcanic explosion in South America in historic times causing a volcanic winter, with deadly effects reaching as far as Russia

objets.nom: General uprising of the Mapuches under Pelantaro
objets.notes: General uprising of the Mapuches under Pelantaro. All cities south of the Bío-Bío River are demolished, in what is now called Destruction of the Seven Cities.

objets.nom: Thornton expedition
objets.notes: a Tuscan expedition under Captain Robert Thornton, sent by Ferdinando I of Tuscany to explore northern Brazil and the Amazon River and prepare for the establishment of a settlement in northern coastal South America, which would serve as a base to export Brazilian wood to Renaissance Italy. which would be colonised by France in 1630. The expedition…

objets.nom: First Jesuit missions to the Guaraní founded in the Upper Paraná area
objets.notes: First Jesuit missions to the Guaraní founded in the Upper Paraná area. San Ignacio in Misiones

objets.nom: Eighty Years' War
objets.notes: a Spanish fleet under the command of admiral Antonio de Oquendo defeats a Dutch fleet off the coast of Brazil in the Battle of Albrolhos.

objets.nom: Guaraní forces living in the Jesuit missions defeat bandeirantes loyal to the Portuguese Empire at the…
objets.notes: Guaraní forces living in the Jesuit missions defeat bandeirantes loyal to the Portuguese Empire at the Battle of Mbororé in present-day Panambí, Argentina.

objets.nom: The first large shipment of Fitzroya wood leaves Chiloé Archipelago.
A Dutch expedition led by plunders Carelmapu and Castro soon after
objets.notes: A Dutch expedition led by plunders Carelmapu and Castro soon after. Governor of Chiloé Andrés Herrera dies in battle and is replaced by Fernando de Alvarado.

objets.nom: First Battle of Guararapes
objets.notes: the Portuguese army defeats the Dutch army in northeast Brazil.

objets.nom: Second Battle of Guararapes
objets.notes: decisive Portuguese victory against the Dutch in northeast Brazil.

objets.nom: Spanish ship San José with provisions aimed for Valdivia wrecks of the coast south of Valdivia
objets.notes: Spanish ship San José with provisions aimed for Valdivia wrecks of the coast south of Valdivia. Its surviving crew is killed by local Cuncos.

objets.nom: A Spanish army led by Juan de Salazar is defeated by local Mapuche-Huilliches as it tries to cross Bueno…
objets.notes: A Spanish army led by Juan de Salazar is defeated by local Mapuche-Huilliches as it tries to cross Bueno River in Southern Chile.

objets.nom: Mapuches launch a general insurrection creating turmoil as far north as Maule River, far beyond the…
objets.notes: Mapuches launch a general insurrection creating turmoil as far north as Maule River, far beyond the ordinary frontier.

objets.nom: Pedro Bohórquez announced to the Calchaqui Indians that he was the last living descendant of the Inca…
objets.notes: Pedro Bohórquez announced to the Calchaqui Indians that he was the last living descendant of the Inca emperors.

objets.nom: Diaguita rebellion led by Spanish rebel, Pedro Bohórquez
Bohórquez led the Calchaqui in an uprising against the Spanish crown.
Treaty of The Hague
objets.notes: the Dutch Republic recognizes Portuguese imperial sovereignty over New Holland (Dutch Brazil).

objets.nom: Bohórquez was executed and displayed in Lima.
The expedition of John Narborough leaves Corral Bay having surveyed the coast and lost four hostages to…
objets.notes: The expedition of John Narborough leaves Corral Bay having surveyed the coast and lost four hostages to the Spanish.

objets.nom: Jesuits established in Chiloé founds the Mission of Nahuel Huapi across the Andes.
Bartolomé Gallardo's expedition reaches the mouth of San Tadeo River after crossing the isthmus of Ofqui.
The Antonio de Vea expedition departs from Chiloé to explore the fjords and channels of Patagonia.
Peru is struck by a major earthquake and stem rust plague
objets.notes: Peru is struck by a major earthquake and stem rust plague. These events marks the beginning of an era of Chilean wheat exports to Peru.

objets.nom: Gold is found near modern-day cities of Sabará, Caeté and Ouro Preto, beginning of the Brazilian Gold Rush.
War of the Emboabas in modern-day Minas Gerais.
Alexander Selkirk, the inspiration for Defoe's Robinson Crusoe, is rescued from the Robinson Crusoe…
objets.notes: Alexander Selkirk, the inspiration for Defoe's Robinson Crusoe, is rescued from the Robinson Crusoe Island in the Juan Fernández Archipelago.

objets.nom: The New Kingdom of Granada became an independent viceroyalty under the Spanish crown.
Rapa Nui (Easter Island) is discovered by Dutch navigator Jacob Roggeveen.
Juan Santos Atahualpa led a failed uprising against the Spanish colonial government.
A violent earthquake and subsequent tsunami completely destroy the city of Concepción
objets.notes: A violent earthquake and subsequent tsunami completely destroy the city of Concepción. The earthquake causes severe destruction to cities as far away as Talca.

objets.nom: Jesuits all over Chile are arrested as the Spanish Empire suppresses the Society of Jesus.
The Kingdom of Portugal divides its colony of the State of Great-Pará and Maranhão into the State of…
objets.notes: The Kingdom of Portugal divides its colony of the State of Great-Pará and Maranhão into the State of Great-Pará (capital, Belém) and the State of Maranhão (capital, São Luis).

objets.nom: Establishment of the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata (Virreinato del Río de la Plata) comprising…
objets.notes: Establishment of the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata (Virreinato del Río de la Plata) comprising today's Argentina, Uruguay, and Paraguay, as well as much of present-day Bolivia, declared with Buenos Aires as its capital

objets.nom: The Governorate of the Río de la Plata was spun off as an independent viceroyalty.
The territories of Cuyo, previously governed as part of Chile, become part of the Viceroyalty of the Río…
objets.notes: The territories of Cuyo, previously governed as part of Chile, become part of the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata. (See History of Argentina.)

objets.nom: Battle of Sangarará
objets.notes: Indigenous rebels led by Túpac Amaru II soundly defeated a numerically inferior Spanish force while they attended church.

objets.nom: Túpac Amaru II was drawn and quartered in Cuzco.
Ambrosio O'Higgins, father of future Chilean independence leader Bernardo O'Higgins, is named governor…
objets.notes: Ambrosio O'Higgins, father of future Chilean independence leader Bernardo O'Higgins, is named governor of Chile.

objets.nom: Caicumeo, a road across forests and swamps that connects Castro with Ancud is opened.
The parliaments of Negrete and Las Canoas between Spanish and native Mapuche and Huilliche are celebrated
objets.notes: The parliaments of Negrete and Las Canoas between Spanish and native Mapuche and Huilliche are celebrated. The native chiefs accept the Spanish king as their de jure sovereign, but their own independence is also confirmed.

objets.nom: Research expedition of Alexander von Humboldt exploring the courses of the Orinoco River and Magdalena River
Rafael de Sobremonte, the Viceroy of the Río de la Plata, sends the first smallpox vaccines to Santiago…
objets.notes: Rafael de Sobremonte, the Viceroy of the Río de la Plata, sends the first smallpox vaccines to Santiago and Lima. Friar :es:Pedro Manuel Chaparro administers the vaccine throughout Santiago.

objets.nom: British invasions of the River Plate unsuccessfully attempt to establish control over Spain's southern…
objets.notes: British invasions of the River Plate unsuccessfully attempt to establish control over Spain's southern colonies as part of the Napoleonic Wars. Spanish troops offer no defence but British repelled by local civilians and militias (to 1807)

objets.nom: The South American branch, under Manuel Julián Grajales, of the Real expedición filantrópica de la…
objets.notes: The South American branch, under Manuel Julián Grajales, of the Real expedición filantrópica de la Vacuna (Royal Philanthropic Vaccine Expedition) reaches Santiago. Grajales proceeds to organize the Junta Central de Vacuna (Central Vaccine Board) to reinforce the smallpox immunization efforts of 1805.

objets.nom: Francisco Antonio García Carrasco is the unpopular Governor of Chile
objets.notes: Francisco Antonio García Carrasco is the unpopular Governor of Chile. The Spanish king Ferdinand VII is imprisoned by Napoleon during his invasion of Spain.

objets.nom: Napoleonic Wars
objets.notes: Brazilian and Portuguese forces conquer French Guiana.

objets.nom: Junta Grande, with delegates from other provinces of the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata,…
objets.notes: Junta Grande, with delegates from other provinces of the United Provinces of the Río de la Plata, replaced Primera Junta.

objets.nom: News of Napoleon's invasion of Spain caused a power vacuum in Buenos Aires leading to a series of events…
objets.notes: News of Napoleon's invasion of Spain caused a power vacuum in Buenos Aires leading to a series of events known as the May Revolution.

objets.nom: The assembly voted for the removal of the viceroy and the creation of the Primera Junta of locals to…
objets.notes: The assembly voted for the removal of the viceroy and the creation of the Primera Junta of locals to govern Buenos Aires, proclaiming loyalty to Ferdinand VII. This was properly agreed and the Junta sworn in on 25 May.

objets.nom: The petition was refused by viceroy Baltasar Hidalgo de Cisneros, but popular protest forced his hand on…
objets.notes: The petition was refused by viceroy Baltasar Hidalgo de Cisneros, but popular protest forced his hand on 22 May.

objets.nom: Viceroy José Fernando de Abascal y Sousa sent troops to Córdoba, Potosí, La Paz and Charcas and…
objets.notes: Viceroy José Fernando de Abascal y Sousa sent troops to Córdoba, Potosí, La Paz and Charcas and reincorporated them into the Viceroyalty of Peru.

objets.nom: Antonio Nariño is declared President of Cundinamarca and Vicegerent of the King's Person
First Triumvirate of Feliciano Chiclana, Juan José Paso and Manuel de Sarratea replaced Junta Grande.
Jorge Tadeo Lozano is declared President of Cundinamarca and Vicegerent of the King's Person
Near Vallenar the silver deposit of Agua Amarga is discovered.
Hostilities begin between the moderados, led by Bernardo O'Higgins, and the exaltados, led by Carrera
objets.notes: Hostilities begin between the moderados, led by Bernardo O'Higgins, and the exaltados, led by Carrera. Carrera institutes the first Chilean national symbols (flag, coat of arms, and national anthem), and Fray Camilo Henríquez begins to publish the Aurora de Chile, the first Chilean newspaper. The Chilean Constitution of 1812 comes into effect.…

objets.nom: Manuel Benito de Castro is declared President of Cundinamarca and Vicegerent of the King's Person
Second Triumvirate of Nicolás Rodriguez Peña, Antonio Álvarez Jonte and Juan José Paso replaced First…
objets.notes: Second Triumvirate of Nicolás Rodriguez Peña, Antonio Álvarez Jonte and Juan José Paso replaced First Triumvirate.

objets.nom: The Jujuy Exodus was led by Manuel Belgrano, with several thousand soldiers and civilians retreating…
objets.notes: The Jujuy Exodus was led by Manuel Belgrano, with several thousand soldiers and civilians retreating from Jujuy and Salta, to avoid military defeat and defections.

objets.nom: The Battle of San Lorenzo, the first battle of José de San Martín in the Argentine War of Independence.
The Spanish send military expeditions (under Antonio Pareja and Gabino Gaínza) from the Viceroyalty of Peru
objets.notes: The Spanish send military expeditions (under Antonio Pareja and Gabino Gaínza) from the Viceroyalty of Peru. In the ensuing battles O'Higgins rises to be seen as a figure of great stature, overshadowing the continually less popular Carrera, who ultimately resigns. Francisco de la Lastra becomes Supreme Director.

objets.nom: Manuel de Bernardo Álvarez del Casal is declared President of Cundinamarca and Vicegerent of the King's Person
The "Disaster of Rancagua". Mariano Osorio, in command of a third Spanish expedition, defeats O'Higgins…
objets.notes: The "Disaster of Rancagua". Mariano Osorio, in command of a third Spanish expedition, defeats O'Higgins (October 1 – 2). Osorio reconquers Santiago for Spain. Exodus of Chilean patriots to Mendoza, Argentina, where they receive the support of José de San Martín. Those patriots who remain in Chile are captured by the Spaniards are deported to the…

objets.nom: By royal order, Joaquín de la Pezuela was named viceroy of Peru to replace Abascal.
Custodio García Rovira is president of the United Provinces of the New Granada
objets.notes: Custodio García Rovira is president of the United Provinces of the New Granada. he was executed 1 month later by Pablo Morillo.

objets.nom: Guerrilla resistance against the Spanish begins, led by Manuel Rodríguez Erdoiza, and other spies such…
objets.notes: Guerrilla resistance against the Spanish begins, led by Manuel Rodríguez Erdoiza, and other spies such as Justo Estay. Increasing enmity between Osorio and Abascal leads Abascal to replace Osorio with Casimiro Marcó del Pont.

objets.nom: Liborio Mejía is president of the United Provinces of the New Granada making him the youngest person to…
objets.notes: Liborio Mejía is president of the United Provinces of the New Granada making him the youngest person to ever hold the presidency of Colombia at the age of 24. He was executed three months later during the Reconquest led by the Spaniard Pablo Morillo.

objets.nom: Manuel Fernando Serrano Uribe is the last president of the United Provinces of the New Granada before…
objets.notes: Manuel Fernando Serrano Uribe is the last president of the United Provinces of the New Granada before its dissolution and complete Reconquest.

objets.nom: San Martin's Argentina had declared its independence.
Battle of Chacabuco
objets.notes: Battle of Chacabuco. José de San Martín and O'Higgins defeat Rafael Maroto, reconquering Santiago. Captain San Bruno, hated chief of the talaveras, is captured and — less than 24 hours later — executed by firing squad. O'Higgins becomes dictator.

objets.nom: O'Higgins signs the Chilean Declaration of Independence (February 12)
objets.notes: O'Higgins signs the Chilean Declaration of Independence (February 12). Shortly afterwards, in the Battle of Maipú, O'Higgins defeats a new military expedition led by Mariano Osorio, and Chile definitively obtains independence from Spain (April 5). The rivalry between O'Higgins and Manuel Rodríguez ends with the ambush and assassination of the…

objets.nom: An Argentine army led by José de San Martín landed at Paracas.
The Battle of Cepeda took place between Unitarians who supported a strong centralised state, and…
objets.notes: The Battle of Cepeda took place between Unitarians who supported a strong centralised state, and Federals, largely provincial caudillo warlords who wanted decentralised authority. The Federals won and the February 1820 Treaty of Pilar declared Argentina as a federal country, although Unitarian ideals continued

objets.nom: Valdivia is captured by Lord Cochrane who commands the Chilean navy
objets.notes: Valdivia is captured by Lord Cochrane who commands the Chilean navy. The Freedom Expedition of Perú is organised by the government of Chile, and manages to free some parts of Peru from Spanish rule.

objets.nom: De la Serna moved the capital to Cuzco.
Peruvian War of Independence
objets.notes: San Martín declared the independence of Peru.

objets.nom: Pezuela was deposed
objets.notes: Pezuela was deposed. José de la Serna was proclaimed viceroy.

objets.nom: Prince regent Pedro of Braganza refuses to comply with the Portuguese cortes order to return to Portugal…
objets.notes: Prince regent Pedro of Braganza refuses to comply with the Portuguese cortes order to return to Portugal (Dia do Fico).

objets.nom: Battle of Ayacucho
objets.notes: The Spanish army was defeated, marking the end of Spanish rule in South America.

objets.nom: Deputies from the eastern bank of the Río de la Plata declare independence from Brazil, leading to the…
objets.notes: Deputies from the eastern bank of the Río de la Plata declare independence from Brazil, leading to the Cisplatine War. The 1827 Battle of Ituzaingó saw tactical success for Argentina. The war ended in 1828 with a treaty giving independence to Uruguay

objets.nom: Taking advantage of the un-surveyed border, and ignoring the royal decree of 1681 and the principal uti…
objets.notes: Taking advantage of the un-surveyed border, and ignoring the royal decree of 1681 and the principal uti possidetis, Simón Bolívar grants the port of Cobija to Bolivia. This gives Bolivia an outlet to the sea between Chile and Peru, which it will retain until the War of the Pacific.

objets.nom: Uruguay is declared independent of the Empire of Brazil by the Thirty-Three Orientals, a militant…
objets.notes: Uruguay is declared independent of the Empire of Brazil by the Thirty-Three Orientals, a militant revolutionary group led by Juan Antonio Lavalleja.

objets.nom: Freire incorporates Chiloé, the last area under Spanish control, into Chile
objets.notes: Freire incorporates Chiloé, the last area under Spanish control, into Chile. He later resigns, initiating an interregnum known as The Anarchy. First attempt in Chile of federal (as against centralized) government, led by the first president of Chile Manuel Blanco Encalada, and the federalist José Miguel Infante.

objets.nom: Treaty of Montevideo
objets.notes: Brazil and Argentina recognize the independence of Uruguay.

objets.nom: Chilean Civil War of 1829. After several battles, Joaquín Prieto defeats Ramón Freire in the Battle of Lircay.
Juan Manuel de Rosas became governor of Buenos Aires Province
Charles Saint Lambert introduces reverberatory furnaces to Chile initiating a revolution in copper…
objets.notes: Charles Saint Lambert introduces reverberatory furnaces to Chile initiating a revolution in copper mining in Chile.

objets.nom: Simón Bolívar dies in Quinta de San Pedro Alejandrino near Santa Marta
Yaghan aboriginal Jemmy Button (Orundellico) taken from Tierra del Fuego to England by Robert FitzRoy on
Argentine Governor of the Falkland Islands Luis Vernet is expelled by following his seizure of United…
objets.notes: Argentine Governor of the Falkland Islands Luis Vernet is expelled by following his seizure of United States interests. New governor murdered in 1832 mutiny

objets.nom: The Voyage of the Beagle with Charles Darwin and Robert FitzRoy visited the Río de la Plata, Patagonia…
objets.notes: The Voyage of the Beagle with Charles Darwin and Robert FitzRoy visited the Río de la Plata, Patagonia and Tierra del Fuego (to 1834)

objets.nom: Juan Manuel de Rosas begins the First Conquest of the Desert
Charles Darwin lands at Valparaíso, during the second voyage of . He also visits Santiago.
Southern Chile is affected by the worst earthquake for several decades on 20 February, an event…
objets.notes: Southern Chile is affected by the worst earthquake for several decades on 20 February, an event witnessed by Charles Darwin. Darwin visits Valdivia, Concepción and Mendoza.

objets.nom: An earthquake strikes Valdivia and Chiloé
objets.notes: An earthquake strikes Valdivia and Chiloé. The earthquake caused a tsunami that struck Hawaii, what is now French Polynesia and Japan.

objets.nom: The Peru-Bolivian Confederacy was established.
Rosas made Supreme Chief of the Argentine Confederation
The Peru-Bolivian Confederacy was officially dissolved.
The Aberdeen Act is passed by the Parliament of the United Kingdom empowering the British Royal Navy to…
objets.notes: The Aberdeen Act is passed by the Parliament of the United Kingdom empowering the British Royal Navy to search Brazilian ships as part of the abolition of the slave trade from Africa.

objets.nom: Mutiny of Cambiazo
objets.notes: Mutineers led by José Miguel Cambiazo ravages the nascent settlement of Punta Arenas.

objets.nom: Platine War: Battle of Caseros, Argentina: the Argentine provinces of Entre Rios and Corrientes allied…
objets.notes: Platine War: Battle of Caseros, Argentina: the Argentine provinces of Entre Rios and Corrientes allied with Brazil and members of Colorado Party of Uruguay, defeat the Argentine Confederation under Juan Manuel de Rosas.

objets.nom: Rosas overthrown by Justo José de Urquiza following Battle of Caseros
Constitution of Argentina agreed by assembly in Santa Fe, creating modern system of government
The Law of 15 June 1857, created the other states that would go on to form the Granadine Confederation:…
objets.notes: The Law of 15 June 1857, created the other states that would go on to form the Granadine Confederation: The Sovereign State of Bolívar, The Sovereign State of Santander, The Sovereign State of Cauca, and The Sovereign State of Magdalena

objets.nom: Defeat of Unitarian forces led by Bartolomé Mitre by Urquiza and federals at Battle of Cepeda; Buenos…
objets.notes: Defeat of Unitarian forces led by Bartolomé Mitre by Urquiza and federals at Battle of Cepeda; Buenos Aires re-enters confederation

objets.nom: Newly appointed Supreme Director of War Tomas Cipriano de Mosquera declared the Sovereign State of Cauca…
objets.notes: Newly appointed Supreme Director of War Tomas Cipriano de Mosquera declared the Sovereign State of Cauca a separate nation from the Granadine Confederation and Colombian Civil War (1860–1862) broke out

objets.nom: Mendoza earthquake kills 6,000 to 12,000 citizens of Mendoza.
American Civil War
objets.notes: Bahia incident: USS Wachusett illegally captures the Confederate raider while in port in Bahia, Brazil, in violation of Brazilian neutrality.

objets.nom: Manuel Murillo Toro is President of the United States of Colombia
Start of Paraguayan War between Paraguay and the Triple Alliance of Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay,…
objets.notes: Start of Paraguayan War between Paraguay and the Triple Alliance of Argentina, Brazil and Uruguay, leading to utter defeat of Paraguay by 1870

objets.nom: Uruguayan War
objets.notes: forces of the Empire of Brazil invade Uruguay in support of Venancio Flores' Colorado Party.

objets.nom: A Spanish fleet under the command of Admiral Casto Méndez Núñez besieged the port city of Callao.
The Treaty of Ayacucho is signed between the Empire of Brazil and Bolivia, Brazil assigns the land of…
objets.notes: The Treaty of Ayacucho is signed between the Empire of Brazil and Bolivia, Brazil assigns the land of Acre to Bolivia in exchange for 102,400 sq kilometers of territory further annexed to the Amazonas.

objets.nom: Eustorgio Salgar is President of the United States of Colombia
Manuel Murillo Toro is President of the United States of Colombia for second time
Santiago Pérez de Manosalbas is President of the United States of Colombia
Aquileo Parra is President of the United States of Colombia
Commencement of the Conquest of the Desert against indigenous inhabitants of the south led by Julio…
objets.notes: Commencement of the Conquest of the Desert against indigenous inhabitants of the south led by Julio Argentino Roca; final surrender by 1884

objets.nom: Julián Trujillo Largacha is President of the United States of Colombia
The War of the Pacific begins with Chilean troops occupying the then-Bolivian port city of Antofagasta
objets.notes: The War of the Pacific begins with Chilean troops occupying the then-Bolivian port city of Antofagasta. Bolivia's ally Peru attempts to mediate, but Chile refuses to negotiate and Peru enters the war on the side of Bolivia. Chile captures the provinces of Antofagasta from Bolivia and Tarapacá from Peru.

objets.nom: War of the Pacific
objets.notes: Chile declared war on Peru and Bolivia.

objets.nom: Rafael Nuñez is President of the United States of Colombia
Francisco Javier Zaldúa served as President of the Rionegro Convention, a constituent assembly that…
objets.notes: Francisco Javier Zaldúa served as President of the Rionegro Convention, a constituent assembly that created the United States of Colombia (now Colombia). As President of this legislative body, Zaldúa became the de facto President of the United States of Colombia for 6 days, when President Tomás Cipriano de Mosquera ceded executive power to the…

objets.nom: José Eusebio Otalora is President of the United States of Colombia, in his capacity as the Second…
objets.notes: José Eusebio Otalora is President of the United States of Colombia, in his capacity as the Second Presidential Designate following the death of President Francisco Javier Zaldúa, and the non-acceptance of the office by the First Designate Rafael Núñez.

objets.nom: The Treaty of Ancón is signed with Perú to end the war, but hostilities with Bolivia continue
objets.notes: The Treaty of Ancón is signed with Perú to end the war, but hostilities with Bolivia continue. Law of Civil Matrimony adopted. This secularization was fiercely resisted by the Roman Catholic Church. The "Pacification of Araucanía" ends, and according to some historians this concludes the long-running War of Arauco.

objets.nom: War of the Pacific: Under the Treaty of Ancón, the war ended with the cession of Peru's Tarapacá…
objets.notes: War of the Pacific: Under the Treaty of Ancón, the war ended with the cession of Peru's Tarapacá Province to Chile.

objets.nom: Gold is discovered near Cape Virgenes sparking the Tierra del Fuego gold rush
Rafael Nuñez is President of the United States of Colombia for second time
The pirate Pedro Ñancúpel is executed in Castro.
The Panic of 1890 brought the Baring Brothers bank in London close to collapse after disastrous…
objets.notes: The Panic of 1890 brought the Baring Brothers bank in London close to collapse after disastrous investments in Argentina

objets.nom: American James Harden-Hickey claimed the Trindade island and declares himself as James I, Prince of Trinidad
objets.notes: American James Harden-Hickey claimed the Trindade island and declares himself as James I, Prince of Trinidad. According to James Harden-Hickey's plans, Trinidad, after being recognized as an independent country, would become a military dictatorship and have him as dictator. He designed postage stamps, a national flag, and a coat of arms;…

objets.nom: Federalist Revolution
objets.notes: Battle of Passo Fundo in the state of Rio Grande do Sul

objets.nom: Rio de Janeiro Affair
objets.notes: a series of incidents during the Brazilian Naval Revolt.

objets.nom: Canudos War
objets.notes: after a long siege, Brazilian government troops take Canudos in Northeastern Brazil, crushing Antônio Conselheiro and his followers.

objets.nom: In the presidential election, Manuel Ferraz de Campos Sales of the Republican Party of São Paulo, is…
objets.notes: In the presidential election, Manuel Ferraz de Campos Sales of the Republican Party of São Paulo, is successful, with 90.9% of the vote.

objets.nom: Naturalist Soto Grimshaw dies of cholera during an expedition to the Caribbean region of Colombia
President Manuel Antonio Sanclemente extended the deadline for completion of the Panama Canal from 31…
objets.notes: President Manuel Antonio Sanclemente extended the deadline for completion of the Panama Canal from 31 October 1904 to 31 October 1910. The executive decree was granted without consent of the Colombian Congress.

objets.nom: Colombian Geographer Francisco Javier Vergara y Velasco publishes the first complete cartographic charts…
objets.notes: Colombian Geographer Francisco Javier Vergara y Velasco publishes the first complete cartographic charts of the country, the Atlas completo de geografía colombiana (1906–1910), through which he won the Charles Manoir price of the Paris Geographical Society.

objets.nom: Manuelita became the first Colombian sugar mill to move from mule to steam powered mills
Presidential election
objets.notes: Rodrigues Alves of the Republican Party of São Paulo receives 91.7% of the vote. Francisco Silviano de Almeida Brandão is elected vice president, but dies suddenly before the start of his term of office.

objets.nom: The Drago Doctrine is announced by the Argentine Minister of Foreign Affairs Luis María Drago.
Panama remained as a province of Colombia until this year, when – with backing from the United States in…
objets.notes: Panama remained as a province of Colombia until this year, when – with backing from the United States in exchange for allowing the US to build the Panama Canal – it became independent (Separation of Panama from Colombia)

objets.nom: The first auction of sheep farming lands in the Magallanes Territory takes place.
Date of death of Manuel Uribe Ángel, known for his great contributions to the advances of the practice…
objets.notes: Date of death of Manuel Uribe Ángel, known for his great contributions to the advances of the practice of medicine in Colombia and the Antioquia Department. He also served as President of the then Sovereign State of Antioquia

objets.nom: In the presidential election, Afonso Pena of the Minas Gerais Republican Party receives 97.9% of the vote.
The Vásquez Cobo–Martins treaty between Brazil and Colombia is signed, establishing the border from the…
objets.notes: The Vásquez Cobo–Martins treaty between Brazil and Colombia is signed, establishing the border from the Rio Negro northwestward along the Amazon River-Orinoco watershed divide, "then generally southward along various river courses and straight-line segments to the mouth of the Apaporis River".

objets.nom: The first Minas Geraes-class Dreadnought battleship for Brazil, Minas Geraes, is launched at Armstrong…
objets.notes: The first Minas Geraes-class Dreadnought battleship for Brazil, Minas Geraes, is launched at Armstrong Whitworth's yard on the River Tyne in England, catalysing the "South American dreadnought race".

objets.nom: Colombian astronomer Julio Garavito Armero discovers the crater on the Moon's far side which is named…
objets.notes: Colombian astronomer Julio Garavito Armero discovers the crater on the Moon's far side which is named after him (Garavito crater).

objets.nom: In the presidential election, Hermes da Fonseca receives 57.1% of the vote
objets.notes: In the presidential election, Hermes da Fonseca receives 57.1% of the vote. Fonseca is supported by several of the most influential Republican parties, whilst his main opponent, Ruy Barbosa, is supported by the Civilist Campaign.

objets.nom: Revolt of the Lash
objets.notes: the mostly black crews of four Brazilian warships, led by João Cândido, mutiny shortly after a sailor receives 250 lashes. The crews depose their white officers and threaten to bombard Rio de Janeiro.

objets.nom: 15 Mapuche-Huilliche are killed by Chilean police in the Forrahue massacre near Osorno.
Sáenz Peña Law introduces universal, secret and compulsory male suffrage, end of the Generation of '80
Roosevelt–Rondon Scientific Expedition
objets.notes: following a speaking tour in Brazil and Argentina, former US President Theodore Roosevelt meets up with Cândido Rondon to embark on a joint exploration of the "River of Doubt".

objets.nom: First World War
objets.notes: A German naval squadron decisively defeats a British squadron at the Battle of Coronel, off the coast of Chile.

objets.nom: World War I
objets.notes: Brazil declares war on the Central Powers.

objets.nom: Brazilian general election, 1918
objets.notes: former President Rodrigues Alves receives 99.1% of the vote.

objets.nom: In the Brazilian presidential election, Artur Bernardes of the Mineiro Republican Party receives 56.0%…
objets.notes: In the Brazilian presidential election, Artur Bernardes of the Mineiro Republican Party receives 56.0% of the vote.

objets.nom: The 18 of the Copacabana Fort revolt occurs in Rio de Janeiro, then Federal District of Brazil
objets.notes: The 18 of the Copacabana Fort revolt occurs in Rio de Janeiro, then Federal District of Brazil. It is the first revolt of the tenentista movement, in the context of the Brazilian Old Republic.

objets.nom: Fabrica Militar de Aviones aircraft factory founded in Cordoba
The Banana massacre, in Spanish, Matanza de las bananeras or Masacre de las bananeras: A massacre of…
objets.notes: The Banana massacre, in Spanish, Matanza de las bananeras or Masacre de las bananeras: A massacre of workers for the United Fruit Company that occurred in the town of Ciénaga near Santa Marta

objets.nom: The crash of 1929 begins to affect the Chilean economy
objets.notes: The crash of 1929 begins to affect the Chilean economy. The World Economic Survey of the League of Nations estimated that Chile was the worst affected nation by the Great Depression.

objets.nom: 1930 Curuçá River event
objets.notes: the area of Curuçá River near latitude 5° S and longitude 71.5° W experiences a meteoric air burst (also known as the Brazilian Tunguska event).

objets.nom: A general election is held; in the presidential elections, the result is a victory for Júlio Prestes of…
objets.notes: A general election is held; in the presidential elections, the result is a victory for Júlio Prestes of the Republican Party of São Paulo, who receives 57.7% of the vote. Vital Soares is elected vice president, but never takes office.

objets.nom: Constitutionalist Revolution
objets.notes: the population of the state of São Paulo revolt against the 1930 coup d'état.

objets.nom: Argentine singer Carlos Gardel dies in a plane crash in Medellín
President Vargas signed the decree, which gives the name of the aviator Alberto Santos Dumont Airport,…
objets.notes: President Vargas signed the decree, which gives the name of the aviator Alberto Santos Dumont Airport, located in Ponta do Calabouço, in the city of Rio de Janeiro, named Santos Dumont Airport, Brazil's first civilian airport.

objets.nom: Massacre of Seguro Obrero
objets.notes: the Carabineros execute members of the fascist National Socialist Movement of Chile (Nacistas), after the fascists attempted to oust the government in a coup d'état.

objets.nom: 'National Revolution' led by nationalist military officers including Colonel Juan Perón; ensured…
objets.notes: 'National Revolution' led by nationalist military officers including Colonel Juan Perón; ensured continued non-intervention in World War II

objets.nom: San Juan earthquake destroys provincial capital, kills 10,000.
Second World War
objets.notes: the first five thousand Brazilian Expeditionary Force soldiers, the 6th RCT, leave Brazil for Europe aboard the USNS General Mann.

objets.nom: A general election is held, the first since the establishment of Getúlio Vargas' Estado Novo
objets.notes: A general election is held, the first since the establishment of Getúlio Vargas' Estado Novo. The presidential election is won by Eurico Gaspar Dutra of the Social Democratic Party (PSD), which also wins a majority of seats in both the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate.

objets.nom: Argentina enters World War II on the side of the Allies and admitted as founding member of United Nations
Bishop Carlos Duarte Costa, an outspoken critic of the regime of President Getúlio Vargas and of the…
objets.notes: Bishop Carlos Duarte Costa, an outspoken critic of the regime of President Getúlio Vargas and of the Vatican's alleged relationship with fascist regimes, gives newspaper interviews accusing Brazil's Papal nuncio of Nazi-Fascist spying, and accusing Rome of having aided and abetted Hitler. Shortly afterwards he establishes the Brazilian Catholic…

objets.nom: Gabriel González Videla becomes president, backed by a broad alliance of parties, including the Radicals…
objets.notes: Gabriel González Videla becomes president, backed by a broad alliance of parties, including the Radicals and Communists. Once in power, he accedes to pressure from the United States and promulgates the Law of Permanent Defense of the Democracy, also known as the Ley Maldita ("accursed law"). The law outlawed his former allies the Communists, some…

objets.nom: Parliamentary elections are held, for 19 vacant seats in the Chamber of Deputies, one additional Senator…
objets.notes: Parliamentary elections are held, for 19 vacant seats in the Chamber of Deputies, one additional Senator for each state (except Santa Catarina, which elected two), and for all state Governors and legislatures. Introduction of Buddhism to the region which becomes a major religion alongside Zoroastrianism and ancient Hinduism.

objets.nom: Buddhist Apracharajas dynasty with territory covering Swat, Gandhara, Taxila, and parts of eastern Afghanistan
objets.notes: Buddhist Apracharajas dynasty with territory covering Swat, Gandhara, Taxila, and parts of eastern Afghanistan. (till 50 CE)

objets.nom: Suren kingdom founded by Gondophares with capitals in Kabul and Taxila, and territory covering southern…
objets.notes: Suren kingdom founded by Gondophares with capitals in Kabul and Taxila, and territory covering southern Afghanistan, eastern Iran and northwest regions of the Indian subcontinent. (till 226 CE)

objets.nom: Kushan Empire founded by Kujula Kadphises in the Arghandab River valley
objets.notes: Kushan Empire founded by Kujula Kadphises in the Arghandab River valley. (till 375 CE)

objets.nom: The Bronze Age Helmand culture in the middle and lower valley of the Helmand River, in southern…
objets.notes: The Bronze Age Helmand culture in the middle and lower valley of the Helmand River, in southern Afghanistan (Kandahar, Helmand and Nimruz province) and eastern Iran (Sistan and Baluchestan province).

objets.nom: Kanishka becomes emperor of the Kushan Empire
objets.notes: Kanishka becomes emperor of the Kushan Empire. He extends his empire from present-day southern Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, north of the Amu Darya (Oxus) in the north west to Northern India, as far as Pataliputra in the Gangetic Plains. A follower of Buddhism, he encourages Buddhist teachings, art and architecture.

objets.nom: Kanishka Stupa is built
objets.notes: Kanishka Stupa is built. Reported by modern archeologists and ancient Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang to have had a diameter of 87 metres, height of 180–210 metres and covered with jewels.

objets.nom: Hephthalite (White Huns) empire established with its capital at Kunduz
objets.notes: Hephthalite (White Huns) empire established with its capital at Kunduz. Buddhism, Manichaeism and Zoroastrianism were their major religions.

objets.nom: Chinese monk, scholar and traveler Xuanzang visits Balkh, reports about a 100 Buddhist convents, 30,000…
objets.notes: Chinese monk, scholar and traveler Xuanzang visits Balkh, reports about a 100 Buddhist convents, 30,000 monks, large number of stupas and other religious monuments. The most remarkable stupa was the Navbahara, which possessed a gigantic statue of the Buddha.

objets.nom: Establishment of the Buddhist Turk Shahi dynasty, with its capital in Kapisi near the present-day town…
objets.notes: Establishment of the Buddhist Turk Shahi dynasty, with its capital in Kapisi near the present-day town of Bagram.

objets.nom: Establishment of the Zunbil dynasty in present southern Afghanistan region, with its capital in Ghazni.
Turk Shahi king routs the Arab army of the Umayyad Caliphate led by Yazid ibn Ziyad, who is killed in…
objets.notes: Turk Shahi king routs the Arab army of the Umayyad Caliphate led by Yazid ibn Ziyad, who is killed in battle and an Arab invasion is decisively repulsed.

objets.nom: Defeat of the Turk Shahis by the Arab Abbasid Caliphate
objets.notes: Defeat of the Turk Shahis by the Arab Abbasid Caliphate. The Turk Shah is forced to convert to Islam and pay an annual tribute.

objets.nom: Jayapala of the Hindu Shahi dynasty conducts a number of invasions of Ghazni, the capital city of the…
objets.notes: Jayapala of the Hindu Shahi dynasty conducts a number of invasions of Ghazni, the capital city of the Ghaznavids.

objets.nom: Mahmud of Ghazni's army defeats the Hindu Shahi army of Jayapala in the Battle of Peshawar (1001)
Mongol invasion of Afghanistan as part of the Mongol conquest of the Khwarazmian Empire, resulting in…
objets.notes: Mongol invasion of Afghanistan as part of the Mongol conquest of the Khwarazmian Empire, resulting in thousands killed in the cities of Kabul, Kandahar, Jalalabad.

objets.nom: In pursuit of the fleeing Khwarazmian king Jalal al-Din Mangburni, Genghis Khan massacres the entire…
objets.notes: In pursuit of the fleeing Khwarazmian king Jalal al-Din Mangburni, Genghis Khan massacres the entire population of Bamiyan after his favorite grandson Mutukan is killed in the Siege of Bamyan, but leaves the Buddhas of Bamiyan unharmed.

objets.nom: Division of the Mongol Empire after Genghis's death
objets.notes: Division of the Mongol Empire after Genghis's death. Afghanistan become part of the Chagatai Khanate.

objets.nom: Invasion of Afghanistan by Timur, leader of neighboring Transoxiana (roughly modern-day Uzbekistan,…
objets.notes: Invasion of Afghanistan by Timur, leader of neighboring Transoxiana (roughly modern-day Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and adjacent areas), becomes a part of the Timurid Empire.

objets.nom: Babur, deposed ruler of Fergana and Samarkand captures Kabul (Siege of Kabul (1504)).
Mirwais Hotak, an influential Afghan tribal chief, gained independence at Kandahar after a successful…
objets.notes: Mirwais Hotak, an influential Afghan tribal chief, gained independence at Kandahar after a successful revolution against the Persian Safavid dynasty.

objets.nom: Mirwais died of a natural cause and his brother Abdul Aziz inherited the throne until he was killed by…
objets.notes: Mirwais died of a natural cause and his brother Abdul Aziz inherited the throne until he was killed by Mahmud Hotaki, son of Mirwais.

objets.nom: Battle of Gulnabad
objets.notes: Led by Mahmud, the Afghan army captured the Safavid capital of Isfahan and Mahmad was declared Shah of Persia.

objets.nom: Battle of Damghan
objets.notes: Afsharid forces led by Nader Shah defeated Ashraf and his forces.

objets.nom: Nader invaded and destroyed Kandahar, and restored the Abdali ethnic Pashtus to political prominence.
Ahmad Shah Durrani of the Abdali Pashtun confederacy declared the establishment of an independent…
objets.notes: Ahmad Shah Durrani of the Abdali Pashtun confederacy declared the establishment of an independent Afghanistan, with its capital at Kandahar.

objets.nom: Durrani signed a treaty of alliance with the United Kingdom.
Battle of Shopian
objets.notes: Sikh Khalsa Army of Ranjit Singh defeated the Durrani force led by governor Jabbar Khan, annexing Kashmir into the Sikh Empire.

objets.nom: Battle of Nowshera
objets.notes: Sikh Khalsa Army of Ranjit Singh defeated a Durrani force led by Azim Khan, capturing the Peshawar Valley.

objets.nom: Dost Mohammad Khan took the throne in Kabul, where he proclaimed himself emir.
Siege of Herat
objets.notes: A Persian force attempts to capture Herat but are defeated and leave in 1838.

objets.nom: British capture Ghazni in the Battle of Ghazni and install Shuja Shah Durrani as the puppet ruler of…
objets.notes: British capture Ghazni in the Battle of Ghazni and install Shuja Shah Durrani as the puppet ruler of Afghanistan.

objets.nom: First Anglo-Afghan War
objets.notes: A British expeditionary force captured Quetta.

objets.nom: Massacre of Elphinstone's army
objets.notes: A retreating British With mostly Indian regiment force of sixteen thousand was massacred by the Afghans.

objets.nom: Second Anglo-Afghan War
objets.notes: Afghanistan refused a British diplomatic mission, provoking a second Anglo-Afghan war.

objets.nom: Second Anglo-Afghan War: To prevent British occupation of a large part of the country, the Afghan…
objets.notes: Second Anglo-Afghan War: To prevent British occupation of a large part of the country, the Afghan government ceded much power to the United Kingdom in the Treaty of Gandamak.

objets.nom: Abdur Rahman Khan was officially recognized as emir of Afghanistan.
Abdur Rahman and British Raj representative Mortimer Durand signed an agreement establishing the Durand Line.
Habibullah Khan, son of Abdur Rahman, became emir of Afghanistan.
Afghan Foreign Minister Mahmud Tarzi negotiated the Treaty of Rawalpindi with the British at Rawalpindi.
Habibullah was assassinated
objets.notes: Habibullah was assassinated. His son Amanullah Khan declared himself King of Afghanistan.

objets.nom: Third Anglo-Afghan War
objets.notes: Amanullah led a surprise attack against the British.

objets.nom: Solar Hijri calendar officially adopted in Afghanistan.
Amanullah was forced to abdicate in favor of Habibullāh Kalakāni in the face of a popular uprising.
Nadir was assassinated
objets.notes: Nadir was assassinated. His son, Mohammad Zahir Shah, was proclaimed King.

objets.nom: The Marxist People's Democratic Party of Afghanistan (PDPA) held its first congress.
Mohammad Daoud Khan declares himself President in a coup against the king, Mohammad Zahir Shah.
Saur Revolution
objets.notes: Military units loyal to the PDPA assaulted the Afghan Presidential Palace, killing President Mohammad Daoud Khan and his family.

objets.nom: Saur Revolution: The PDPA installed its leader, Nur Muhammad Taraki, as President of Afghanistan.
Operation Storm-333
objets.notes: Soviet troops occupied major governmental, military and media buildings in Kabul, including the Tajbeg Palace, and executed Prime Minister Amin.

objets.nom: Soviet–Afghan War
objets.notes: Fearing the collapse of the Amin regime, the Soviet army invaded Afghanistan.

objets.nom: Taraki was murdered by supporters of Prime Minister Hafizullah Amin.
Soviet–Afghan War: The Soviet government signed the Geneva Accords, which included a timetable for…
objets.notes: Soviet–Afghan War: The Soviet government signed the Geneva Accords, which included a timetable for withdrawing their armed forces.

objets.nom: Afghan Civil War (1989–1992)
objets.notes: Afghan political parties signed the Peshawar Accord which created the Islamic State of Afghanistan and proclaimed Sibghatullah Mojaddedi its interim President.

objets.nom: As agreed upon in the Peshawar Accord, Jamiat-e Islami leader Burhanuddin Rabbani took over as President.
Gulbuddin Hekmatyar's Hezbi Islami, with the support of neighboring Pakistan, began a massive…
objets.notes: Gulbuddin Hekmatyar's Hezbi Islami, with the support of neighboring Pakistan, began a massive bombardment against the Islamic State in the capital Kabul.

objets.nom: Taliban attacks and looting of the National Museum of Afghanistan result in loss of 70% of the 100,000…
objets.notes: Taliban attacks and looting of the National Museum of Afghanistan result in loss of 70% of the 100,000 artifacts of Afghan culture and history.

objets.nom: The Taliban government began to form in a small village between Lashkargah and Kandahar.
Taliban tortured and killed Abdul Ali Mazari leader of the Hazara people.
The Taliban, with Pakistani support, initiated a military campaign against the Islamic State of…
objets.notes: The Taliban, with Pakistani support, initiated a military campaign against the Islamic State of Afghanistan and its capital Kabul.

objets.nom: Afghan Civil War (1996–2001)
objets.notes: The forces of the Islamic State retreated to northern Afghanistan.

objets.nom: Afghan Civil War (1996–2001): The Taliban conquered Kabul and declared the establishment of the Islamic…
objets.notes: Afghan Civil War (1996–2001): The Taliban conquered Kabul and declared the establishment of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan. Former President Mohammad Najibullah, who had been living under United Nations protection in Kabul, was tortured, castrated and executed by Taliban forces.

objets.nom: Afghan Civil War (1996–2001): The Taliban captured Mazar-i-Sharif, forcing Abdul Rashid Dostum into exile.
Operation Infinite Reach
objets.notes: Cruise missiles were fired by the United States Navy into four militant training camps in the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan.

objets.nom: After the September 11 attacks in the United States, U.S. President George W. Bush demanded the Taliban…
objets.notes: After the September 11 attacks in the United States, U.S. President George W. Bush demanded the Taliban government to hand over al-Qaeda head Osama bin Laden and close all terrorist training camps in the country, which the Taliban refuses the following day for lack of evidence connecting bin Laden to 9/11 attacks.

objets.nom: Destruction of the Buddhas of Bamiyan by the Taliban with dynamite, on orders from its leader Mullah Omar.
International Conference on Afghanistan in Germany
objets.notes: Hamid Karzai chosen as head of the Afghan Interim Administration.

objets.nom: Operation Enduring Freedom
objets.notes: The United States and the United Kingdom began an aerial bombing campaign against al-Qaeda and the Taliban.

objets.nom: Resistance leader Ahmad Shah Massoud was killed in a suicide bomb attack by two Arabs who were disguised…
objets.notes: Resistance leader Ahmad Shah Massoud was killed in a suicide bomb attack by two Arabs who were disguised as French news reporters.

objets.nom: The United Nations Security Council authorized the creation of the International Security Assistance…
objets.notes: The United Nations Security Council authorized the creation of the International Security Assistance Force (ISAF) to help maintain security in Afghanistan and assist the Karzai administration.

objets.nom: 2002 loya jirga
objets.notes: Hamid Karzai appointed as President of the Afghan Transitional Administration in Kabul, Afghanistan.

objets.nom: 2003 loya jirga
objets.notes: A 502-delegate loya jirga was held to consider a new Afghan constitution.

objets.nom: Taliban insurgency
objets.notes: An insurgency began after a Pakistani decision to station around 80,000 soldiers next to the porous Durand Line border with Afghanistan.

objets.nom: Afghanistan–Pakistan border skirmishes
objets.notes: Skirmishes began with Pakistan.

objets.nom: After the death of Osama bin Laden in Pakistan, many high-profile Afghan officials were assassinated,…
objets.notes: After the death of Osama bin Laden in Pakistan, many high-profile Afghan officials were assassinated, including among them were Mohammed Daud Daud, Ahmed Wali Karzai, Jan Mohammad Khan, Ghulam Haider Hamidi, and Burhanuddin Rabbani.

objets.nom: National Front of Afghanistan was created by Tajik leader Ahmad Zia Massoud, Hazara leader Muhammad…
objets.notes: National Front of Afghanistan was created by Tajik leader Ahmad Zia Massoud, Hazara leader Muhammad Mohaqiq and Uzbek leader Abdul Rashid Dostum

objets.nom: Kabul falls to Taliban (Fall of Kabul).
Tibetan ruler Songtsän Gampo (reigned 627–49) ordered the construction of many Buddhist temples,…
objets.notes: Tibetan ruler Songtsän Gampo (reigned 627–49) ordered the construction of many Buddhist temples, including two in Bhutan: Jambay Lhakhang at Bumthang in central Bhutan, and Kyichu Lhakhang on the Kyi River in the Paro Valley. The construction of these temples marked the arrival of Buddhism in Bhutan. (to 649)

objets.nom: Buddhist saint Padmasambhava, known as "Guru Rimpoche", comes to Bhutan from India at the invitation of…
objets.notes: Buddhist saint Padmasambhava, known as "Guru Rimpoche", comes to Bhutan from India at the invitation of Sindhu Raja of the Kingdom of Bumthang, one of the numerous kingdoms predating modern Bhutan. Padmasambhava converts the king to Buddhism and then continues to Tibet. When he returns to Bhutan at the invitation of Trisong Detsen, he oversees the…

objets.nom: Padmasambhava comes again to Bhutan
objets.notes: Padmasambhava comes again to Bhutan. Around the same time, independent monarchies develop.

objets.nom: Tibetan King Ralpacan (reigned 816–836), grandson of Trisong Detsen, goes to war with an Indian people…
objets.notes: Tibetan King Ralpacan (reigned 816–836), grandson of Trisong Detsen, goes to war with an Indian people ruler in Bhutan, driving him out. Tibetan troops who remained in Bhutan were called Milog, meaning "those that will not return." The region they settle is referred to as Tshochhen Gyed. Its eight parts or divisions are Wang, Be, Med, Kawang,…

objets.nom: Tibetan King Ralpacan is murdered by agents of his brother Langdarma
objets.notes: Tibetan King Ralpacan is murdered by agents of his brother Langdarma. Tibetans seek refuge in Bhutan from ensuing political and religious upheaval during the reign of Langdarma (836–842). After Langdarma's assassination in 842, Tibetans continue to flee to western Bhutan, thus creating the homeland of the modern Ngalop people. The centuries that…

objets.nom: By the 11th century, Tibetan-Mongol forces occupy the whole of Tibet
objets.notes: By the 11th century, Tibetan-Mongol forces occupy the whole of Tibet. More waves of Tibetans seek refuge in Bhutan from religious persecution. Charismatic lamas become the de facto leaders of regions in western Bhutan.

objets.nom: Before the arrival of Phajo Druggom, the followers of Nyoe Gyalwa Lhanangpa, a disciple of Kyobpa Jigten…
objets.notes: Before the arrival of Phajo Druggom, the followers of Nyoe Gyalwa Lhanangpa, a disciple of Kyobpa Jigten Sumgon (1143–1217), the founder of the Drikung Kagyud, known as Lhapa had great influence and controlled a large part of western Bhutan.

objets.nom: Tibetan lama Tsangpa Gyare (1161–1211) founds Ralung Monastery for the Drukpa Lineage of the Kagyu…
objets.notes: Tibetan lama Tsangpa Gyare (1161–1211) founds Ralung Monastery for the Drukpa Lineage of the Kagyu school, named after the thunder dragons (druk) he witnessed on his quest for an appropriate foundation site. With the proliferation of the Drukpa, the druk become synonymous with Bhutan and later its central national symbol.

objets.nom: Gelug monks flee to Bhutan from Tibet.
Pema Lingpa, a Bhutanese religious figure and tertön from Bumthang, discovered his first terma from Lake…
objets.notes: Pema Lingpa, a Bhutanese religious figure and tertön from Bumthang, discovered his first terma from Lake Membar near Bumthang.

objets.nom: Ngawang Namgyal, 1st Zhabdrung Rinpoche, facing arrest and following visions in which it is said that…
objets.notes: Ngawang Namgyal, 1st Zhabdrung Rinpoche, facing arrest and following visions in which it is said that the chief guardian deities of Bhutan offered him a home, leaves Tibet to establish a new base in western Bhutan, founding Chagri Monastery at the head of the Thimphu Valley.

objets.nom: Circa 1627, during the first war with Tibet, Portuguese Jesuits Estêvão Cacella and João Cabral were the…
objets.notes: Circa 1627, during the first war with Tibet, Portuguese Jesuits Estêvão Cacella and João Cabral were the first recorded Europeans to visit Bhutan on their way to Tibet. They met with Ngawang Namgyal, presented him with firearms, gunpowder and a telescope, and offered him their services in the war against Tibet, but the Zhabdrung declined the…

objets.nom: Shabdrung Ngawang Namgyal builds Simtokha Dzong at the entrance to Thimphu valley
objets.notes: Shabdrung Ngawang Namgyal builds Simtokha Dzong at the entrance to Thimphu valley. From this dzong, he exerts control over traffic between the powerful Paro Valley to the west and Trongsa Valley to the east.

objets.nom: Ngawang Namgyal prevails in the Battle of Five Lamas over the Tibetan Empire and Bhutanese forces allied…
objets.notes: Ngawang Namgyal prevails in the Battle of Five Lamas over the Tibetan Empire and Bhutanese forces allied against him. The Zhabdrung is thus the first to unite Bhutan into a single country. The Zhabdrung establishes the Drukpa Lineage as the state religion under the dual system of government, and codifies the system of laws known as the Tsa Yig,…

objets.nom: A joint Mongol-Tibetan force sought to destroy Nyingma refugees who had fled to Bhutan, Sikkim, and Nepal
objets.notes: A joint Mongol-Tibetan force sought to destroy Nyingma refugees who had fled to Bhutan, Sikkim, and Nepal. The Mongols had seized control of religious and civil power in Tibet in the 1630s and established the Gelug school as the state religion.
