Bhutanese rivals of Ngawang Namgyal encouraged the Mongol intrusion, but the Mongol force was easily…

objets.nom: Ngawang Namgyal dies; however, his death is kept a secret for fifty-four years in order to keep Bhutan…
objets.notes: Ngawang Namgyal dies; however, his death is kept a secret for fifty-four years in order to keep Bhutan from disintegrating. While the Zhabdrung was supposedly away on an extended religious retreat, his son reigned.

objets.nom: Bhutan invades Sikkim
objets.notes: Bhutan invades Sikkim. The same year, Ngawang Namgyal's son is succeeded by the Zhabdrung's stepbrother.

objets.nom: Tibetan forces, aided by the Mongols, invade Bhutan but fail to gain control.
Cooch Behar first requests Bhutanese assistance in repelling Mughal Empire encroachments, establishing a…
objets.notes: Cooch Behar first requests Bhutanese assistance in repelling Mughal Empire encroachments, establishing a dependent relationship with Bhutan.

objets.nom: Bhutan invades Sikkim, supported by troops from Cooch Behar.
British expeditionary forces drive Bhutanese garrisons out of Cooch Behar, until that time a Bhutanese…
objets.notes: British expeditionary forces drive Bhutanese garrisons out of Cooch Behar, until that time a Bhutanese dependency. The Druk Desi petitions Lhasa unsuccessfully for assistance. (to 1773)

objets.nom: In a succession dispute in Cooch Behar, the Druk Desi's nominee for the throne was opposed by a rival…
objets.notes: In a succession dispute in Cooch Behar, the Druk Desi's nominee for the throne was opposed by a rival who invited British troops; in effect, Cooch Behar became a dependency of the British East India Company.

objets.nom: The Druk Desi signs a Treaty of Peace with the British East India Company
objets.notes: The Druk Desi signs a Treaty of Peace with the British East India Company. Under the treaty, Bhutan returns to its pre-1730 boundaries and allows the British to harvest timber in Bhutan.

objets.nom: British government turns over to Bhutan the Bengal Duars territory, where boundaries had been poorly defined
objets.notes: British government turns over to Bhutan the Bengal Duars territory, where boundaries had been poorly defined. As in its other foreign territories, Bhutan left administration of the Bengal Duars territory to local officials and collected its revenues.

objets.nom: British mission to Thimphu offers Bhutan a treaty providing for the extradition of Bhutanese officials…
objets.notes: British mission to Thimphu offers Bhutan a treaty providing for the extradition of Bhutanese officials responsible for incursions into Assam, free and unrestricted commerce between India and Bhutan, and settlement of Bhutan's debt to the British. In an attempt to protect its independence, Bhutan rejected the British offer.

objets.nom: British annex Bhutanese controlled Assam Duars, paying a compensation of 10,000 rupees a year to Bhutan.
Bhutan cedes control of the troublesome Bengal Duars to Britain.
Britain declares war on Bhutan
objets.notes: Britain declares war on Bhutan. The Duar War lasts five months, resulting in Bhutan's defeat and cession of significant territory under the Treaty of Sinchula.

objets.nom: In the 1870s and 1880s, renewed competition among regional rivals – primarily the pro-British penlop of…
objets.notes: In the 1870s and 1880s, renewed competition among regional rivals – primarily the pro-British penlop of Trongsa and the anti-British, pro-Tibetan penlop of Paro – resulted in the ascendancy of Ugyen Wangchuck, the penlop of Trongsa. (to 1880)

objets.nom: Ugyen Wangchuck, penlop (governor) of Trongsa, puts down civil unrest across Bhutan, consolidates power,…
objets.notes: Ugyen Wangchuck, penlop (governor) of Trongsa, puts down civil unrest across Bhutan, consolidates power, and cultivates closer ties with British India.

objets.nom: The last reigning Shabdrung dies, and a successor is not found until 1906. In the meantime, the civil…
objets.notes: The last reigning Shabdrung dies, and a successor is not found until 1906. In the meantime, the civil administration comes under the power of the Ugyen Wangchuck as Druk Desi.

objets.nom: Ugyen Wangchuck is elected Bhutan's first hereditary ruler (Druk Gyalpo) after having politically…
objets.notes: Ugyen Wangchuck is elected Bhutan's first hereditary ruler (Druk Gyalpo) after having politically unified the country.

objets.nom: The Treaty of Punakha amends two articles of the 1865 Treaty of Sinchula: the British agree to double…
objets.notes: The Treaty of Punakha amends two articles of the 1865 Treaty of Sinchula: the British agree to double the annual stipend to 100,000 rupees and "to exercise no interference in the internal administration of Bhutan." In turn, Bhutan agrees "to be guided by the advice of the British Government in regard to its external relations."

objets.nom: The 7th Shabdrung Jigme Dorji dies at Talo monastery
objets.notes: The 7th Shabdrung Jigme Dorji dies at Talo monastery. Jigme Dorji is the last Shabdrung recognized by the government of Bhutan, though subsequent claimants to the incarnation continue today.

objets.nom: King Jigme Wangchuck dies; his son Jigme Dorji Wangchuck begins to reign
objets.notes: King Jigme Wangchuck dies; his son Jigme Dorji Wangchuck begins to reign. Bhutan begins a program of planned development and democratization. The same year, the National Assembly is established, and the post of Chief Minister (Gongzim) is abolished.

objets.nom: Major glacial lake outburst flood from glacial lakes.
The first Nationality Act is enacted, defining Bhutanese citizenship and introducing a compulsory…
objets.notes: The first Nationality Act is enacted, defining Bhutanese citizenship and introducing a compulsory registration process.

objets.nom: Major glacial lake outburst flood from glacial lakes.
Prime Minister Jigme Palden Dorji is assassinated in a dispute among competing political factions
objets.notes: Prime Minister Jigme Palden Dorji is assassinated in a dispute among competing political factions. The King's own uncle, a military cadre, was among those executed for their role in the attempted coup. After a brief tenure by acting Prime Minister Lhendup Dorji, the post of Prime Minister is abolished until 1998.

objets.nom: The capital is moved from Punakha to Thimphu through a transition period when Punakha was the winter…
objets.notes: The capital is moved from Punakha to Thimphu through a transition period when Punakha was the winter capital and Thimphu the summer capital.

objets.nom: King Jigme Dorji Wangchuck establishes the first Council of Ministers, or executive cabinet
objets.notes: King Jigme Dorji Wangchuck establishes the first Council of Ministers, or executive cabinet. At the same time, the king renounces his power of veto, which had never been used. The king also creates the High Court (the Thimkhang Gongma) and empowers it to review the king's decisions. The Bank of Bhutan is also founded as a central bank, charged…

objets.nom: Major glacial lake outburst flood from glacial lakes.
Strains between the Wangchucks and Dorjis were relieved with the return that year of the exiled members…
objets.notes: Strains between the Wangchucks and Dorjis were relieved with the return that year of the exiled members of the latter family. The reconciliation, however, was preceded by reports of a plot to assassinate the new Druk Gyalpo before his coronation could take place and to set fire to the Tashichho Dzong, the seat of government in Thimphu. Yangki, the…

objets.nom: The Royal Government establishes the Royal Monetary Authority, the central bank of Bhutan.
Gasa District is split up among Punakha and Thimphu Districts; Chhukha District is carved out from parts…
objets.notes: Gasa District is split up among Punakha and Thimphu Districts; Chhukha District is carved out from parts of Samtse, Paro, and Thimphu Districts.

objets.nom: After a census, the government begins evicting those it identifies as illegal immigrants among the…
objets.notes: After a census, the government begins evicting those it identifies as illegal immigrants among the Nepali-speaking population in southern Bhutan. Over two decades, the population of Bhutanese refugees in refugee camps in neighboring Nepal climbed to 107,000 by 2008 according to UNHCR.

objets.nom: Tek Nath Rizal, leader of the Bhutan Peoples' Party, is arrested and imprisoned.
The driglam namzha, the official behaviour and dress code, is elevated from recommended to mandatory in…
objets.notes: The driglam namzha, the official behaviour and dress code, is elevated from recommended to mandatory in public and educational settings. Nepali ceases to be a language of instruction in schools, escalating tensions between Ngalops and Lhotshampas.

objets.nom: Violent ethnic unrest and anti-government protests in southern Bhutan pressing for greater democracy and…
objets.notes: Violent ethnic unrest and anti-government protests in southern Bhutan pressing for greater democracy and respect for minority rights. The Bhutan Peoples' Party, whose members are mostly Lhotshampa, begin a campaign of violence against the government. Pro-government citizen militias form in response to rising crime and violence including clashes…

objets.nom: Jigme Singye Wangchuck threatens to abdicate in face of hardline opposition in the National Assembly to…
objets.notes: Jigme Singye Wangchuck threatens to abdicate in face of hardline opposition in the National Assembly to his efforts to resolve ethnic unrest, leaving an international summit to attend to unrest.

objets.nom: Gasa District is carved out from Punakha District; Tashi Yangtse District is split from Trashigang District
objets.notes: Gasa District is carved out from Punakha District; Tashi Yangtse District is split from Trashigang District. Other district boundaries are also changed

objets.nom: Tek Nath Rizal, leader of the illegal Bhutan Peoples' Party, is sentenced to life imprisonment.
The National Security Act is enacted
objets.notes: The National Security Act is enacted. The Act defines treason and speech crimes, as well as unlawful assembly, rioting, and states of emergency, providing for lengthy prison sentences, capital punishment, and the use of deadly force by the government to stop unlawful demonstrations.

objets.nom: Major glacial lake outburst flood from glacial lakes, devastating Punakha.
The Council of Ministers (Lhengye Zhungtshog) replaces the cabinet, and King Jigme Singye Wangchuck…
objets.notes: The Council of Ministers (Lhengye Zhungtshog) replaces the cabinet, and King Jigme Singye Wangchuck withdraws from his role in the decision-making of the cabinet. The post of Prime Minister (Lonchen) is restored. (to 1999)

objets.nom: Tek Nath Rizal, leader of the illegal Bhutan Peoples' Party, is pardoned and released from prison along…
objets.notes: Tek Nath Rizal, leader of the illegal Bhutan Peoples' Party, is pardoned and released from prison along with some 40 other political prisoners. He goes into exile in Nepal, a common condition of release among Lhotshampa political dissidents.

objets.nom: Bhutan and Nepal reach an agreement regarding the repatriation of certain classes of Bhutanese refugees…
objets.notes: Bhutan and Nepal reach an agreement regarding the repatriation of certain classes of Bhutanese refugees living in camps in Nepal, subject to joint government verification. Points of contention included that some camp inhabitants were never citizens – or some even residents – of Bhutan before attaining refugee status. Also, the Bhutanese government…

objets.nom: First verification of Bhutanese refugees eligible for repatriation commences in Nepalese refugee camps
objets.notes: First verification of Bhutanese refugees eligible for repatriation commences in Nepalese refugee camps. Actual repatriation is estimated to occur one year out. As of 2011 over 200 refugees in the Khudunabari refugee camp alone had been certified, however no Bhutanese refugees had been repatriated.

objets.nom: The Royal Bhutan Army began military operations against guerrilla camps in southern Bhutan, in…
objets.notes: The Royal Bhutan Army began military operations against guerrilla camps in southern Bhutan, in coordination with Indian armed forces who lined the border to the south to prevent the guerrillas from dispersing back into Assam. News sources indicated that of the 30 camps that were targeted, 13 were controlled by ULFA, 12 camps by the National…

objets.nom: Capital punishment in Bhutan is abolished.
Authorities arrest two civil servants in the village of Nago in Paro District, accusing them of engaging…
objets.notes: Authorities arrest two civil servants in the village of Nago in Paro District, accusing them of engaging in acts of proselytism under the false pretext of holding an official meeting, maligning the Spiritual Head of Bhutan (Je Khenpo), posing as officials on official business, and giving false information. In accordance with provisions in the…

objets.nom: Bhutanese refugees in Nepalese refugee camps protest, pressing for third-country resettlement
objets.notes: Bhutanese refugees in Nepalese refugee camps protest, pressing for third-country resettlement. (to August)

objets.nom: First National Council election for the 20 elected non-partisan seats in National Council, Bhutan's…
objets.notes: First National Council election for the 20 elected non-partisan seats in National Council, Bhutan's upper house. Only 15 out of 20 dzongkhags (districts), however, were set to begin voting. In Thimphu, Trashiyangtse, Gasa, Haa and Lhuntse Districts, there were either no candidates or a single candidate, and elections were delayed until 29 January…

objets.nom: Reports allege the current Zhabdrung Rinpoche, Pema Namgyel (b
objets.notes: Reports allege the current Zhabdrung Rinpoche, Pema Namgyel (b. 20 November 2003 – then a small child) had been held under house arrest in Bhutan along with his parents since October 2005, when the family traveled to meet the Reincarnation Committee. The Committee later denied his reincarnation status.

objets.nom: The Royal Government enacts the Immigration Act of 2007, amending the Bhutanese Citizenship Act 1985 and…
objets.notes: The Royal Government enacts the Immigration Act of 2007, amending the Bhutanese Citizenship Act 1985 and establishing the Department of Immigration under the Ministry of Home and Cultural Affairs to implement and administer immigration laws through immigration offices. The Act endowed officers of the Department of Immigration with broad police and…

objets.nom: In Bhutan's first parliamentary elections, the pro-monarchy Bhutan Peace and Prosperity Party wins 45…
objets.notes: In Bhutan's first parliamentary elections, the pro-monarchy Bhutan Peace and Prosperity Party wins 45 out of 47 seats in the National Assembly, Bhutan's lower house. Another pro-monarchy party, the People's Democratic Party, wins the remaining two seats in Gasa and Haa Districts.

objets.nom: The Constitution of Bhutan is enacted
objets.notes: The Constitution of Bhutan is enacted. The first ever Constitution of Bhutan, it sets forth a bicameral parliamentary democratic framework to safeguard human rights, while enshrining the institution of the monarchy, Drukpa Lineage Buddhism, and traditional Ngalop Bhutanese culture.

objets.nom: The government of India alleges links between Assamese separatists and the illegal Bhutanese Druk…
objets.notes: The government of India alleges links between Assamese separatists and the illegal Bhutanese Druk National Congress.

objets.nom: Parliament enacts the Local Government Act of Bhutan 2009, the sixth legislative reform of Bhutanese…
objets.notes: Parliament enacts the Local Government Act of Bhutan 2009, the sixth legislative reform of Bhutanese local governments since 1999. The Act devolves various administrative powers to Dzongkhags (districts), Dungkhags (subdistricts), Gewogs (village blocks), Chiwogs (constituencies), and Thromdes (municipalities) while retaining legislative authority…

objets.nom: The 6.1-magnitude 2009 Bhutan earthquake strikes Mongar District, causing at least 12 deaths, extensive…
objets.notes: The 6.1-magnitude 2009 Bhutan earthquake strikes Mongar District, causing at least 12 deaths, extensive destruction, and severe aftershocks in Bhutan.

objets.nom: A district court interprets the constitutional clause regarding religious "coercion or inducement" to…
objets.notes: A district court interprets the constitutional clause regarding religious "coercion or inducement" to prohibit not only forced conversion but also proselytism in the case of a Christian missionary pastor who used a generator and a projector in a private home on 21 May 2009. The pastor received a sentence of three years imprisonment for infringing…

objets.nom: Parliament enacts the Tobacco Control Act, restricting import and possession, and banning the sale of…
objets.notes: Parliament enacts the Tobacco Control Act, restricting import and possession, and banning the sale of tobacco in Bhutan.

objets.nom: King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck marries Jetsun Pema
objets.notes: King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck marries Jetsun Pema. Jetsun Pema, childhood friend of the Fifth King, becomes his Queen in a traditional Buddhist ceremony followed by three days of public holiday and celebrations. The much anticipated wedding, announced 20 May, was the largest media event in Bhutanese history.

objets.nom: Local government elections, originally slated for 2008, begin on a staggered scale in 3 of Bhutan's 20…
objets.notes: Local government elections, originally slated for 2008, begin on a staggered scale in 3 of Bhutan's 20 Dzongkhags: Thimphu, Phuntsholing, and Samdrup Jongkhar.

objets.nom: Sonam Tshering, a 23-year-old ordained monk from Langpa in Haa, was caught with 480 grams of chewing…
objets.notes: Sonam Tshering, a 23-year-old ordained monk from Langpa in Haa, was caught with 480 grams of chewing tobacco (purchased for Nu.120) en route from Phuntsholing to Thimphu. This presented the first prosecution under the Tobacco Control Act of Bhutan 2010 and was the result of a private individual informing the police that Tshering possessed tobacco.…

objets.nom: The Election Commission announces the results of the first local government elections under the…
objets.notes: The Election Commission announces the results of the first local government elections under the Constitution of Bhutan. Originally slated for 2008, elections faced multiple delays related to voter registration and constituency demarcation. Furthermore, voter turnout crept to 56% of eligible voters amid public sentiments of distrust and futility.…

objets.nom: The Supreme Court of Bhutan declares unconstitutional the government's raising of personal vehicle…
objets.notes: The Supreme Court of Bhutan declares unconstitutional the government's raising of personal vehicle import taxes in June 2010 without bicameral presentment and debate, affirming the judgment of the High Court Constitutional Bench against the Attorney General and for the Opposition in Parliament.

objets.nom: Final round of 2013 Bhutanese National Assembly election, held
objets.notes: Final round of 2013 Bhutanese National Assembly election, held. Results: PDP-32 seats; DPT—15 seats. New Prime Minister: Tshering Tobgay.

objets.nom: Primary round of National Assembly elections held
objets.notes: Primary round of National Assembly elections held. Results: DCT—12,457 votes; DNT—35,962 votes; PDP-68,650 votes; DPT—93,949 votes.

objets.nom: The Speaker of the National Assembly, Jigme Tshultim, sentenced to 2 years 6 months imprisonment for…
objets.notes: The Speaker of the National Assembly, Jigme Tshultim, sentenced to 2 years 6 months imprisonment for official misconduct, fraud, and deceptive practices; and the then Home Minister, Lyonpo Minjur Dorji, and 13 Plot Allotment committee members sentenced to a year imprisonment by the Mongar District Court for official misconduct in the Gyelpozhing…

objets.nom: Gautama Buddha is born in Kapilvastu in 563 BCE (died in 483 BCE) in Lumbini (present-day Nepal).
Amshuverma, who started as a feudal lord and now the prime minister, starts minting coins in his name…
objets.notes: Amshuverma, who started as a feudal lord and now the prime minister, starts minting coins in his name and assumes the title of Maharajadhiraj reducing the king to a mere figurehead. Eventually, he marries the king's daughter and succeeds Shiva Deva I as the ruler after the king's death. Amshuverma's reign is also characterized by architectural…

objets.nom: Following the death of Amshuverma, Uday Deva becomes the king reviving the Licchavi dynasty's rule.
Narendradeva reclaims his ancestral throne with the Tibetan Empire's help.
Narendradeva sends a cavalry of 7,000 troops to aid Tibet in the Battle of Chabuheluo against Arunasva…
objets.notes: Narendradeva sends a cavalry of 7,000 troops to aid Tibet in the Battle of Chabuheluo against Arunasva who attacked the emissary Wang Xuance from China.

objets.nom: Shivadeva II, the son of Narendradeva, starts his reign
objets.notes: Shivadeva II, the son of Narendradeva, starts his reign. He marries Batsa Devi, daughter of the prince Bhogvarma of Magadha.

objets.nom: Nanyadeva establishes the Karnat dynasty in Simraungadh.
King Nanyadeva of the Karnat dynasty dies
objets.notes: King Nanyadeva of the Karnat dynasty dies. He is succeeded by his son Gangadeva.

objets.nom: Arimalla, the first king of the Malla dynasty rules the Kathmandu valley.
King Arimalla is succeeded by his son Abhaya Malla.
Doya from Mithila (Karnat dynasty) invades Nepal three times within two years.
King Abhaya Malla dies in a massive earthquake that killed one-third of the whole population
objets.notes: King Abhaya Malla dies in a massive earthquake that killed one-third of the whole population. He is succeeded by his son Jayadeva Malla.

objets.nom: Following an agreement between the House of Tripura and the Tirhuts, along with other wealth,…
objets.notes: Following an agreement between the House of Tripura and the Tirhuts, along with other wealth, Devalakshmidevi, the daughter of Jayatunga Malla, is given in marriage to King Harisimhadeva.

objets.nom: Ripu Malla from the Khasa kingdom visits the Kathmandu valley.
King Harisimhadeva of Mithila, along with his wife Devalakshmidevi and so Jagatsimha flees to Kathmandu Valley
objets.notes: King Harisimhadeva of Mithila, along with his wife Devalakshmidevi and so Jagatsimha flees to Kathmandu Valley. Harisimha dies on the way and Devalakshmidevi, and Jagatsimha were welcomed by her brother, Jayarudra Malla.

objets.nom: The Karnat Kingdom of Mithila is annexed by the King of Delhi
objets.notes: The Karnat Kingdom of Mithila is annexed by the King of Delhi. The invader then sets up a vassal state appointing from the Oiniwar dynasty a ruler of the region.

objets.nom: Nayakadevi marries Jagatsimha, the son of Harisimhadeva and Devalakshmidevi
objets.notes: Nayakadevi marries Jagatsimha, the son of Harisimhadeva and Devalakshmidevi. This event connects all the later Mallas of Kathmandu valley to the Karnat dynasty.

objets.nom: Devalakshmidevi comes to an agreement with the House of Bhonta on the condition that a king would be…
objets.notes: Devalakshmidevi comes to an agreement with the House of Bhonta on the condition that a king would be from the House of Bhonta while Devalakshmidevi would act as the de facto ruler. Following this agreement, Jayarajadeva, the illegitimate son of the late King Jayanandadeva, becomes the King. Devalakshmidevi, however, is given royal titles higher…

objets.nom: Rajalladevi marries Jayasthiti Malla
objets.notes: Rajalladevi marries Jayasthiti Malla. It is generally accepted that Jayasthiti Malla was brought from Mithila by Devalakshmidevi to marry Rajalladevi.

objets.nom: Devalakshmidevi dies
objets.notes: Devalakshmidevi dies. Jayasthiti Malla starts on gathering political power.

objets.nom: King Jayasthiti Malla dies
objets.notes: King Jayasthiti Malla dies. His three sons Dharma Malla, Jyoti Malla, and Kiti Malla rule together.

objets.nom: Jyoti Malla rules as the sole king of Kathmandu Valley after the death of both his brothers.
King Jyoti Malla dies
objets.notes: King Jyoti Malla dies. His son Yakshya Malla succeeds him.

objets.nom: King Yakshya Malla dies
objets.notes: King Yakshya Malla dies. His kingdom is divided in three between his sons with Ratna Malla controlling Kantipur, and Raya Malla controlling Bhaktapur.

objets.nom: King Ratna Malla dies
objets.notes: King Ratna Malla dies. His son Surya Malla succeeds him as the king.

objets.nom: Mukunda Sen of Palpa attacks the entire Kathmandu valley and surrounds both Kantipur, and Patan
objets.notes: Mukunda Sen of Palpa attacks the entire Kathmandu valley and surrounds both Kantipur, and Patan. He is defeated by the combined forces of the valley.

objets.nom: King Surya Malla dies
objets.notes: King Surya Malla dies. He is succeeded by his son Amara Malla. Amara Malla annexed several villages north-west of Kantipur.

objets.nom: King Amara Malla dies
objets.notes: King Amara Malla dies. His son Mahendra Malla succeeds him. Mahendra Malla issued the first silver coins.

objets.nom: King Mahendra Malla is succeeded by his first son Sadashiva Malla.
Shivasimha Malla, the second son of Mahendra Malla, deposes his brother Sadashiva Malla and rules Kantipur
objets.notes: Shivasimha Malla, the second son of Mahendra Malla, deposes his brother Sadashiva Malla and rules Kantipur. Sadashiva takes refuge in Bhadgaon where he dies.

objets.nom: King Shivasimha Malla annexes Patan and installs his son Harisimhadeva as the governor
objets.notes: King Shivasimha Malla annexes Patan and installs his son Harisimhadeva as the governor. Harisimhadeva dies shortly afterwards, and his son Siddhi Narasimha Malla succeeds him as the governor.

objets.nom: King Shivasimha Malla dies
objets.notes: King Shivasimha Malla dies. His son Lakshmi Narasimha Malla succeeds him as the King of Kantipur, and his grandson Siddhi Narasimha Malla declares Patan independent from Kantipur.

objets.nom: King Lakshmi Narasimha Malla goes insane after executing his loyal minister
objets.notes: King Lakshmi Narasimha Malla goes insane after executing his loyal minister. Pratap Malla imprisons him and rules Kantipur.

objets.nom: Nripendra Malla starts his reign after his Pratap Malla's death defying the wishes of his father to…
objets.notes: Nripendra Malla starts his reign after his Pratap Malla's death defying the wishes of his father to install Mahipatendra Malla as the king.

objets.nom: Parthibendra Malla, another son of Pratap Malla, starts his reign after the death of King Nripendra Malla.
King Parthibendra Malla is poisoned by the nobles and on his death, as many as twenty-four women went Sati
objets.notes: King Parthibendra Malla is poisoned by the nobles and on his death, as many as twenty-four women went Sati. He is succeeded by his 14 years old son Bhupalendra Malla with his wife Riddhilakshmi acting as the regent.

objets.nom: King Bhupalendra Malla dies
objets.notes: King Bhupalendra Malla dies. He is succeeded by his son Bhaskara Malla.

objets.nom: King Bhaskara Malla proclaims the title of King of Patan and issues coins under the name Gajapati…
objets.notes: King Bhaskara Malla proclaims the title of King of Patan and issues coins under the name Gajapati Mahindra Simha.

objets.nom: An epidemic breaks out in Kantipur killing approximately 20,000 people.
After about six months in confinement to be safe from the plague, King Bhaskara Malla returns to the…
objets.notes: After about six months in confinement to be safe from the plague, King Bhaskara Malla returns to the palace after the death rate dropped. He dies some days later due to the plague. He is succeeded by Jagajjaya Malla, the grandson of Mahipatendra Malla.

objets.nom: Jayaprakash Malla succeeds King Jagajjaya Malla after the latter's death.
Kot massacre results in the killing of more than 40 members of the palace and starts the autocratic Rana…
objets.notes: Kot massacre results in the killing of more than 40 members of the palace and starts the autocratic Rana dynasty in Nepal with Jung Bahadur Rana as its first prime minister.

objets.nom: Jang Bahadur receives the title of Rana.
Prime minister Jung Bahadur Rana dies; Ranodip Singh Kunwar becomes the prime minister.
Prime minister Ranodip Singh Kunwar is assassinated by his nephews; Bir Shumsher becomes the prime minister.
Prime minister Bir Shumsher dies; Dev Shumsher becomes the prime minister.
Prime minister Dev Shumsher is deposed by his relatives; Chandra Shumsher becomes the prime minister.
Nepal's first political party, Nepal Praja Parishad is founded (led by Tanka Prasad Acharya).
Nepali National Congress is formed (led by BP Koirala, Matrika Prasad Koirala, Ganesh Man Singh, etc.).
Tribhuvan returns from exile and reclaims the title of King putting an end to the autocratic Rana dynasty
New Zealander Edmund Hillary and Nepal's Sherpa Tenzing Norgay become the first climbers to reach the…
objets.notes: New Zealander Edmund Hillary and Nepal's Sherpa Tenzing Norgay become the first climbers to reach the summit of Mount Everest.

objets.nom: King Mahendra leads a coup d'état dismissing the cabinet of B.P. Koirala and introduces the Panchayat, a…
objets.notes: King Mahendra leads a coup d'état dismissing the cabinet of B.P. Koirala and introduces the Panchayat, a partyless political system.

objets.nom: King Mahendra dies, succeeded by Birendra.
In the 1980 Nepalese governmental system referendum, the people vote in favor of the Panchayat system…
objets.notes: In the 1980 Nepalese governmental system referendum, the people vote in favor of the Panchayat system against a multi-party system. The Panchayat system receives a total of 2.4 million votes, while the multi-party system receives 2 million votes.

objets.nom: 1990 Nepalese revolution commences led by Nepali Congress and the communist parties.
First multi-party election is held
objets.notes: First multi-party election is held. NC wins a majority of 110 seats. The communist parties gather a total of 82 seats. Girija Prasad Koirala becomes the prime minister.

objets.nom: Division within the NC results in Girija Prasad Koirala losing the support of 36 congress members in a…
objets.notes: Division within the NC results in Girija Prasad Koirala losing the support of 36 congress members in a parliamentary vote. He resigns and King Birendra dismisses the cabinet announcing a new election.

objets.nom: Second multi-party election is held
objets.notes: Second multi-party election is held. CPN (UML) led by Man Mohan Adhikari wins the election with 88 votes. NC led by Girija Prasad Koirala wins 83 votes. RPP led by Surya Bahadur Thapa wins 20 votes. Man Mohan Adhikari heads a minority government.

objets.nom: King Dipendra is pronounced dead; His uncle Gyanendra becomes the king.
Maoist rebels step up campaign of violence
objets.notes: Maoist rebels step up campaign of violence. Prime Minister Girija Prasad Koirala quits over the violence; succeeded by Sher Bahadur Deuba.

objets.nom: Nepalese royal massacre occurs; King Birendra and his family dies, and Dipendra is crownd king while in…
objets.notes: Nepalese royal massacre occurs; King Birendra and his family dies, and Dipendra is crownd king while in hospital.

objets.nom: Prime minister Deuba formally asks the king to defer the election dates until November 2003. King…
objets.notes: Prime minister Deuba formally asks the king to defer the election dates until November 2003. King Gyanendra responds by dismissing the government headed by Deuba, removing Deuba as the prime minister, postponing the elections indefinitely, and assuming full executive power.

objets.nom: 2005 Nepal coup d'état by King Gyanendra after which he assumes absolute direct power, sacks the…
objets.notes: 2005 Nepal coup d'état by King Gyanendra after which he assumes absolute direct power, sacks the government, and declares a state of emergency restoring absolute monarchy. Many prominent leaders including the prime minister were placed under house arrest.

objets.nom: Several political parties and the CPN (Maoist Centre) sign an agreement to work together against the…
objets.notes: Several political parties and the CPN (Maoist Centre) sign an agreement to work together against the rule of King Gyanendra.

objets.nom: Comprehensive Peace Accord is signed between the Government of Nepal and Maoist Leader Prachanda which…
objets.notes: Comprehensive Peace Accord is signed between the Government of Nepal and Maoist Leader Prachanda which allows the Maoist to join mainstream politics.

objets.nom: King Gyanendra reinstates the dissolved parliament calling the Seven Party Alliance to lead the government.
Dr
objets.notes: Dr. Ram Baran Yadav becomes the first president of Nepal.

objets.nom: The First Nepalese Constituent Assembly election is held where the CPN (MC) emerged victorious winning…
objets.notes: The First Nepalese Constituent Assembly election is held where the CPN (MC) emerged victorious winning 220 out of the 575 seats. It forms the government with seven other communist parties including the CPN (UML).

objets.nom: Madhav Kumar Nepal of CPN (UML) becomes the prime minister with support from 22 of the 25 parties.
Prime minister Prachanda sacks General Rookmangud Katawal
objets.notes: Prime minister Prachanda sacks General Rookmangud Katawal. CPN (UML) withdraws its support from the government in protest. President Ram Baran Yadav overrides the decision resulting in the resignation of Prachanda the next day.

objets.nom: Prime minister Madhav Kumar Nepal announces his resignation blaming the CPN (MC) for their continuous…
objets.notes: Prime minister Madhav Kumar Nepal announces his resignation blaming the CPN (MC) for their continuous obstruction in the government.

objets.nom: CPN (MC) withdraws its candidate and backs Jhala Nath Khanal of CPN (UML)
objets.notes: CPN (MC) withdraws its candidate and backs Jhala Nath Khanal of CPN (UML). Khanal becomes the prime minister after more than seven months of political gridlock and more than sixteen rounds of voting in the parliament.

objets.nom: Dr
objets.notes: Dr. Baburam Bhattarai is elected as the prime minister after he gets support from some smaller parties after the resignation of Jhala Nath Khanal.

objets.nom: Prime minister Baburam Bhattarai resigns
objets.notes: Prime minister Baburam Bhattarai resigns. Chief Justice Khil Raj Regmi becomes the interim prime minister until the elections after four main political parties agreed to form a CJ-led electoral cabinet.

objets.nom: The Second Nepalese Constituent Assembly election is held where the NC led by Sushil Koirala emerges as…
objets.notes: The Second Nepalese Constituent Assembly election is held where the NC led by Sushil Koirala emerges as the largest party winning 196 out of the 576 seats. The CPN (UML) wins 175 seats while the CPN (MC) wins 80 seats.

objets.nom: Sushil Koirala of Nepali Congress is elected as the prime minister with CPN (UML) backing.
CPN (UML) leader KP Sharma Oli is elected as the prime minister by the parliament with the backing from…
objets.notes: CPN (UML) leader KP Sharma Oli is elected as the prime minister by the parliament with the backing from CPN (MC).

objets.nom: | President Dr
objets.notes: | President Dr. Ram Baran Yadav promulgates the Constitution of Nepal (2015) replacing the Interim Constitution of 2007.

objets.nom: | The 7.8 M w Nepal earthquake affected the country with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent),…
objets.notes: | The 7.8 M w Nepal earthquake affected the country with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent), the worst natural disaster to strike Nepal since the 1934 Nepal–Bihar earthquake, killing more than 8,000 people and injuring more than 20,000 people.

objets.nom: After weeks of deadly youth-led protests against corruption and a social media ban, Nepal's Prime…
objets.notes: After weeks of deadly youth-led protests against corruption and a social media ban, Nepal's Prime Minister KP Sharma Oli resigned. In the resulting turmoil, protesters set fire to government buildings, and security forces clashed with demonstrators, killing dozens. Former Chief Justice Sushila Karki was sworn in as interim Prime Minister, with…

objets.nom: Archaeological evidence for the beginnings of the Iron Age in Sri Lanka is found at Anuradhapura, where…
objets.notes: Archaeological evidence for the beginnings of the Iron Age in Sri Lanka is found at Anuradhapura, where a large city–settlement was founded before 900 BCE. The settlement was about 15 hectares in 900 BCE, but by 700 BC it had expanded to 50 hectares. A similar site from the same period has also been discovered near Aligala in Sigiriya.

objets.nom: During the reign of Vijaya, in addition to Tambapaṇṇī, the King and his ministers founded settlements…
objets.notes: During the reign of Vijaya, in addition to Tambapaṇṇī, the King and his ministers founded settlements like Anuraadhagaama, Upatissagāma, Ujjeni, Uruvelaa and Vijithapura located along the river banks of the Malwathu Oya and the Kala Oya in the northwestern region of Sri Lanka.

objets.nom: Prince Vijaya had his followers landed at a place called Supparaka; the women landed at a place called…
objets.notes: Prince Vijaya had his followers landed at a place called Supparaka; the women landed at a place called Mahiladipaka, and the children landed at a place called Naggadipa. Vijaya's ship later reached Sri Lanka, on the North west coast of present-day Puttalam, on the day of the Parinibbaana of The Buddha.

objets.nom: Vijaya, prince regent of Sinhabahu, the King of Vanga and Queen Sinhasivali, is exiled along with his…
objets.notes: Vijaya, prince regent of Sinhabahu, the King of Vanga and Queen Sinhasivali, is exiled along with his 700 followers, from Sinhapura after he and his band of followers became notorious for their violent deeds. The wives and children of these 700 men were also sent on separate ships.

objets.nom: Prince Pandukabhaya, nephew of Abhaya, rebels and goes to war with his uncles
objets.notes: Prince Pandukabhaya, nephew of Abhaya, rebels and goes to war with his uncles. Abhaya, upon losing the battle sent a letter to the prince in secret conferring on him the rule of the country south of the river, sharing sovereignty of Sri Lanka. Hearing of this plan angered Abhaya's brothers, Pandukabhaya's uncles, compelled Abhaya to abdicate and…

objets.nom: Sanghamitta Theri, daughter of Emperor Ashoka, sister of Mahinda, arrives in Sri Lanka from India to…
objets.notes: Sanghamitta Theri, daughter of Emperor Ashoka, sister of Mahinda, arrives in Sri Lanka from India to establish the Bhikkhuni Sangha, bringing a sapling of the Sacred Bodhi Tree, which was planted in the Mahamevnāwa Uyana at Anuradhapura.

objets.nom: Theravada Buddhism is officially introduced to Sri Lanka by the Mahinda Thero, son of Ashoka, during the…
objets.notes: Theravada Buddhism is officially introduced to Sri Lanka by the Mahinda Thero, son of Ashoka, during the reign of Devanampiya Tissa.

objets.nom: Dutugamunu, a descendant of Mahanaga, Prince of Ruhuna brother of Asela, defeats and kills Elara at the…
objets.notes: Dutugamunu, a descendant of Mahanaga, Prince of Ruhuna brother of Asela, defeats and kills Elara at the Battle of Vijithapura and restores Sinhalese sovereignty after a reign of 44 years.

objets.nom: During the reign of Valagamba, after the experience of the Beminitiya Seya, the Tipitaka and its…
objets.notes: During the reign of Valagamba, after the experience of the Beminitiya Seya, the Tipitaka and its commentaries were committed to writing for the first time on palm leaves at the Aluvihare Rock Temple.

objets.nom: During the reign of Valagamba, the first schism of the Buddhist Sangha occurred with the establishment…
objets.notes: During the reign of Valagamba, the first schism of the Buddhist Sangha occurred with the establishment of the Abhayagiri Vihāra, which broke away from the orthodox Anuradhapura Maha Viharaya.

objets.nom: Dhammapala composes commentaries on remaining portions of the Canon (such as the Udana, Itivuttaka,…
objets.notes: Dhammapala composes commentaries on remaining portions of the Canon (such as the Udana, Itivuttaka, Theragatha, and Therigatha) along with extensive sub-commentaries.

objets.nom: Chola conquest and occupation of Anuradhapura
objets.notes: The Cholas under Rajendra I attack and conquer parts of the Anuradhapura kingdom.

objets.nom: Chola conquest and occupation of Anuradhapura
objets.notes: Death of Mahinda V in captivity in India after 42 nominal years of reign. Kassapa VI (Vikramabahu), son of Mahinda V, leads southern resistance in Ruhuna.

objets.nom: In Myanmar, during the reign of Kyansittha, completes the building of the Shwezigon Pagoda, a shrine for…
objets.notes: In Myanmar, during the reign of Kyansittha, completes the building of the Shwezigon Pagoda, a shrine for relics of the Buddha, including a tooth brought from Sri Lanka. Various inscriptions refer to him as an incarnation of Vishnu, a chakravartin, a bodhisattva, and dharmaraja.

objets.nom: Velakkara Revolt
objets.notes: Tamil mercenaries named Velakkaras, mutiny against king Vijayabahu as he declared war with the Chola Empire due to arresting a group of Sinhalese ambassadors sent to Western Chalukya.

objets.nom: With the guidance of two forest monks – Ven
objets.notes: With the guidance of two forest monks – Ven. Mahākassapa Thera and Ven. Sāriputta Thera, Parakramabahu I reunites all bhikkhus in Sri Lanka into the Mahavihara sect.

objets.nom: In an effort to enhace his and his supporter's power over the monarchy and the royal court, the…
objets.notes: In an effort to enhace his and his supporter's power over the monarchy and the royal court, the Ekanayake of Kotte (head of the civil government), assisted by a noble named Kandure Bandara plotted to kill the three elder sons of Vijayabahu VI to ensure the succession of Vijayabahu's minor fourth son, by a second queen, Dewarajasinha. The three…

objets.nom: Portuguese conquest of the Jaffna kingdom
objets.notes: The Portuguese invade and annex the Jaffna kingdom and take king Cankili II as a POW.

objets.nom: Kusumasana Devi is deposed by Rajasinha I of Sitawaka beginning the Sitawaka occupation of Kandy.
The Kandyan Kingdom is invaded by the Portuguese Captain-general Pedro Lopes de Sousa, to reinstall…
objets.notes: The Kandyan Kingdom is invaded by the Portuguese Captain-general Pedro Lopes de Sousa, to reinstall Kusumasana Devi onto the throne.

objets.nom: Senarat marries Sūriya Mahadassin, daughter of Vimaladharmasuriya I and Kusumasana Devi.
At the request of Kirti Sri Rajasinha, the latter part of the Culavamsa, from 1326 onwards, was written…
objets.notes: At the request of Kirti Sri Rajasinha, the latter part of the Culavamsa, from 1326 onwards, was written by Tibbotuvāve Buddharakkhita, the chief incumbent of the Mavatta monastery.

objets.nom: First Kandyan War
objets.notes: British forces attack the Kingdom of Kandy after the King's Adigar Pilimatalawe defected.

objets.nom: A peasant uprising led by popular leaders Gongalegoda Banda and Puran Appu takes place against…
objets.notes: A peasant uprising led by popular leaders Gongalegoda Banda and Puran Appu takes place against oppressive colonial tax policies, marking a crucial transition from feudal revolts to modern independence struggles.

objets.nom: Ven
objets.notes: Ven. Hikkaduwe Sri Sumangala Thera establishes the Vidyodaya Pirivena and Ven. Ratmalane Sri Dharmaloka Thera establishes the Vidyalankara Pirivena (1875), launching a major modern revival of Buddhist monastic education.

objets.nom: Donoughmore Commission
objets.notes: The resulting Donoughmore Constitution officially went into effect with the opening of the first State Council of Ceylon and established Universal suffrage. The adult franchise was extended to women above the age of 21, regardless of their educational status. At the time Sri Lanka became one of the first Asian countries to allow voting rights to…

objets.nom: The major Trotskyist political party Lanka Sama Samaja Party is founded by Leslie Goonewardene, N. M.…
objets.notes: The major Trotskyist political party Lanka Sama Samaja Party is founded by Leslie Goonewardene, N. M. Perera, Colvin R. de Silva, Philip Gunawardena and Robert Gunawardena.

objets.nom: Ceylon in World War II
objets.notes: Colombo is attacked by air in the Easter Sunday raid by the Imperial Japanese Navy in an effort to destroy the British Eastern Fleet located at that port.

objets.nom: A group of three Sri Lankan Tamil politicians, S. J. V. Chelvanayakam, C. Vanniasingam and Senator E. M.…
objets.notes: A group of three Sri Lankan Tamil politicians, S. J. V. Chelvanayakam, C. Vanniasingam and Senator E. M. V. Naganathan, split from the All Ceylon Tamil Congress (ACTC) to form the Ilankai Tamil Arasu Kachchi (ITAK).

objets.nom: The Official Language Act (No
objets.notes: The Official Language Act (No. 33 of 1956), also known as the Sinhala Only Act, is passed by the Parliament of Ceylon. The act replaced English with Sinhala as the sole official language of Ceylon, with the controversial exclusion of Tamil.

objets.nom: The Sinhala Only Act is amended and the Tamil Language (Special Provisions) Act of 1958 is passed in…
objets.notes: The Sinhala Only Act is amended and the Tamil Language (Special Provisions) Act of 1958 is passed in Ceylon, thus making Tamil an official language of Ceylon.

objets.nom: The World Buddhist Sangha Council is convened by Theravadins in Sri Lanka with the hope of bridging…
objets.notes: The World Buddhist Sangha Council is convened by Theravadins in Sri Lanka with the hope of bridging differences and working together. The first convention is attended by leading monks from many countries and sects, Mahayana as well as Theravada. Nine Basic Points Unifying the Theravada and Mahayana are written by Ven. Walpola Rahula are approved…

objets.nom: The United Front is founded as a socialist republican political alliance, a coalition formed by the Sri…
objets.notes: The United Front is founded as a socialist republican political alliance, a coalition formed by the Sri Lanka Freedom Party (SLFP), the Lanka Sama Samaja Party (LSSP), and the Communist Party of Ceylon.

objets.nom: The Sri Lanka Freedom Party led United Front alliance wins the 1970 Ceylonese parliamentary elections in…
objets.notes: The Sri Lanka Freedom Party led United Front alliance wins the 1970 Ceylonese parliamentary elections in a landslide victory with SLFP leader Sirimavo Bandaranaike becoming Prime Minister.

objets.nom: 1971 JVP insurrection
objets.notes: Marxist insurrection conducted by the Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna against the government of Sri Lanka.

objets.nom: Sri Lankan civil war
objets.notes: Velupillai Prabhakaran founds the Tamil New Tigers, which would later be renamed as the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) in 1976, a Sri Lankan Tamil militant group which advocated for the creation of an independent state of Tamil Eelam in the Northern and the Eastern Provinces of Sri Lanka.

objets.nom: The Sacred City of Anuradhapura, the Ancient City of Polonnaruwa and the Ancient City of Sigiriya are…
objets.notes: The Sacred City of Anuradhapura, the Ancient City of Polonnaruwa and the Ancient City of Sigiriya are officially designated as UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

objets.nom: Sri Lankan civil war
objets.notes: Triggered by a LTTE ambush on 13 soldiers, anti-Tamil rioting begins in the capital and spreads to other parts of the country. This event is widely considered the beginning of the Sri Lankan civil war.

objets.nom: Sri Lankan civil war
objets.notes: Signing of the Indo-Lanka Accord, leading to the arrival of the Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) and the creation of Provincial Councils.]

objets.nom: Thirteenth Amendment to the 1978 Constitution is enacted under the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord, establishing…
objets.notes: Thirteenth Amendment to the 1978 Constitution is enacted under the Indo-Sri Lanka Accord, establishing nine Provincial Councils and recognizing Tamil as an official language.

objets.nom: The Old Town of Galle and its Fortifications, the Sacred City of Kandy and the Sinharaja Forest Reserve…
objets.notes: The Old Town of Galle and its Fortifications, the Sacred City of Kandy and the Sinharaja Forest Reserve is officially designated as UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

objets.nom: Sri Lankan civil war
objets.notes: Eelam War II, the second phase of the Sri Lankan civil war begins after the breakdown of peace talks.

objets.nom: Sri Lankan civil war
objets.notes: Former Indian Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi is assassinated by a female suicide bomber belonging to the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) at an election rally in Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu, killing Gandhi and 14 others.

objets.nom: Sri Lankan civil war
objets.notes: Vice Admiral Clancy Fernando, Commander of the Sri Lanka Navy is assassinated by a Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) suicide bomber becoming the highest-ranking military officer ever killed in action during the Sri Lankan civil war.

objets.nom: Sri Lankan civil war
objets.notes: President Ranasinghe Premadasa is assassinated by a LTTE suicide bomber who detonated an explosive belt during a United National Party May Day rally in central Colombo.

objets.nom: Sri Lankan civil war
objets.notes: Eelam War II ends following a ceasefire agreement and the start of peace talks between the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) and the newly elected government of President Chandrika Kumaratunga.

objets.nom: Sri Lankan civil war
objets.notes: A suicide truck bomb orchestrated by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) target the Central Bank of Sri Lanka in a bombing that kills 91 people, injures 1,400 others, and causes catastrophic destruction to the capital's financial district.

objets.nom: Sri Lankan civil war
objets.notes: The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam bomb the Galadari Hotel and the World Trade Center in Colombo.

objets.nom: Sri Lankan civil war
objets.notes: Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) terrorists commit a deadly suicide attack on Sri Lanka's most sacred Buddhist site and a UNESCO World Heritage centre: the Sri Dalada Maligawa, where Buddha's tooth relic is enshrined. Eight civilians are killed and 25 others are injured and significant damage is done to the temple structure, which was first…

objets.nom: Sri Lankan civil war
objets.notes: Attempted assassination of Chandrika Kumaratunga three days before reelection.

objets.nom: 2020 Sri Lankan parliamentary election
objets.notes: Mahinda Rajapaksa is officially sworn in as the 13th Prime Minister of Sri Lanka at Temple Trees.

objets.nom: The 2020 Sri Lankan parliamentary elections were held
objets.notes: The 2020 Sri Lankan parliamentary elections were held. The incumbent Sri Lanka People's Freedom Alliance (led by the Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna) won a landslide victory, claiming 145 seats and winning a two-thirds majority in the Parliament of Sri Lanka.

objets.nom: Aragalaya
objets.notes: Protests erupt against the government's mishandling of the economic crisis

objets.nom: Sri Lankan economic crisis (2019–2024)
objets.notes: The overall rate of inflation as measured by the National Consumer Price Index on Year-on-Year basis reaches a record high of 45.3% in May 2022.

objets.nom: 2024 Sri Lankan parliamentary election
objets.notes: The ruling National People's Power wins in a landslide victory, winning 61.56% of the popular vote and securing 159 seats, the most seats won by a single party in an election. The NPP becomes the first party to win a supermajority in parliament since 1977 and the first non-Tamil party to win the Jaffna district.

objets.nom: 2024 Sri Lankan presidential election
objets.notes: Over 17 million voters elect a new president. NPP candidate Anura Kumara Dissanayake wins a plurality of the vote with 42.31%, followed by Leader of the Opposition Sajith Premadasa with 32.76%. No candidate wins a majority in the first round, forcing a second round of vote counting for the first time in Sri Lanka's history.

objets.nom: 2024 Summer Paralympics
objets.notes: Dulan Kodithuwakku wins Silver in the Men's Javelin Throw (F64) event with a personal best distance of 67.03 meters and also broke his own previous World Record (66.49m) in the process in the F44 category.

objets.nom: President Dissanayake appoints MP Harini Amarasuriya as Prime Minister of Sri Lanka and swears in a new…
objets.notes: President Dissanayake appoints MP Harini Amarasuriya as Prime Minister of Sri Lanka and swears in a new three-member cabinet. Amarasuriya is the third woman to hold the position. President Dissanayake dissolves the current Parliament of Sri Lanka and calls for snap parliamentary elections in November 2024.

objets.nom: Red Sea crisis
objets.notes: The Sri Lanka Navy confirms that one of its ships has completed its maiden patrol in the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait and is set to return to the country. The vessel is later revealed to be SLNS Gajabahu and the Sri Lankan government confirms that patrols would continue.

objets.nom: Yevan David signs with AIX Racing to compete in the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Championship, becoming the first…
objets.notes: Yevan David signs with AIX Racing to compete in the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Championship, becoming the first Sri Lankan to compete in the series.

objets.nom: A United States Navy submarine sinks the Iranian Navy frigate IRIS Dena, approximately off the southern…
objets.notes: A United States Navy submarine sinks the Iranian Navy frigate IRIS Dena, approximately off the southern coast of Sri Lanka, outside the territorial waters but within the exclusive economic zone, in an event related to the 2026 Iran war. The Sri Lanka Navy rescues 32 survivors from the crew of 180 and recover 87 bodies, with about 60 sailors still…

objets.nom: Jayavarman II declared independence from Srivijaya under the Sailendra, proclaiming himself the divine…
objets.notes: Jayavarman II declared independence from Srivijaya under the Sailendra, proclaiming himself the divine king of Kambuja.

objets.nom: Jayavarman II died
objets.notes: Jayavarman II died. His son Jayavarman III succeeded him.

objets.nom: Jayavarman III died
objets.notes: Jayavarman III died. He was succeeded by his cousin Indravarman I.

objets.nom: Indravarman died
objets.notes: Indravarman died. His son Yasovarman succeeded him.

objets.nom: Jayavarman V succeeded Rajendravarman II as ruler of Kambuja, now the Khmer Empire.
Jayavarman V died
objets.notes: Jayavarman V died. He was succeeded by Udayadityavarman I.

objets.nom: The king died
objets.notes: The king died. A civil war ensued between Jayaviravarman and Suryavarman I, both of whom claimed the throne.

objets.nom: Suryavarman became the uncontested king of the Khmer Empire.
Suryavarman died
objets.notes: Suryavarman died. He was succeeded by Udayadityavarman II, a descendant of Yasovarman's wife.

objets.nom: Udayadityavarman died
objets.notes: Udayadityavarman died. Harshavarman III succeeded him.

objets.nom: Jayavarman VI died
objets.notes: Jayavarman VI died. He was succeeded by Dharanindravarman I.

objets.nom: Dharanidravarman died, possibly murdered by his great nephew Suryavarman II who succeeded him.
An attempted invasion of Vietnam was defeated.
Suryavarman II died, possibly in a military campaign against the Cham of Central Vietnam
objets.notes: Suryavarman II died, possibly in a military campaign against the Cham of Central Vietnam. Dharanindravarman II succeeded him.

objets.nom: Dharanindravarman died
objets.notes: Dharanindravarman died. He was succeeded by Yasovarman II.

objets.nom: Cham invaders took control of Yasodharapura, the Khmer capital, and executed the king.
Jayavarman VII forcibly annexed the south of Champa.
Jayavarman VII died
objets.notes: Jayavarman VII died. He was succeeded by Indravarman II.

objets.nom: Two Thai chieftains in the city of Sukhothai declared the establishment of the Sukhothai Kingdom and its…
objets.notes: Two Thai chieftains in the city of Sukhothai declared the establishment of the Sukhothai Kingdom and its independence from Angkorian dominion.

objets.nom: Indravarman II died
objets.notes: Indravarman II died. Jayavarman VIII succeeded him.

objets.nom: Jayavarman VIII agreed to pay tribute to the Mongol Empire in lieu of suffering invasion.
Jayavarman VIII was allowed to abdicate after being deposed by his son-in-law Indravarman III…
objets.notes: Jayavarman VIII was allowed to abdicate after being deposed by his son-in-law Indravarman III (Srindravarman), the first king to make Theravada Buddhism the state religion.

objets.nom: The Siamese Ayutthaya Kingdom laid siege to Angkor for a year and a half, then invaded and conquered it,…
objets.notes: The Siamese Ayutthaya Kingdom laid siege to Angkor for a year and a half, then invaded and conquered it, leaving an Ayutthayan prince to rule.

objets.nom: King Suryavong led the Khmer army in retaking Angkor from the Siamese.
The Thai invade Angkor
objets.notes: The Thai invade Angkor. The Khmer capital is relocated to Srei Santhor and next year to Chatumuk.

objets.nom: Thousands of Cham settle in Cambodia as refugees from the fall of Vijaya (northern section of Champa) to…
objets.notes: Thousands of Cham settle in Cambodia as refugees from the fall of Vijaya (northern section of Champa) to the Vietnamese.

objets.nom: The royal Khmer court moves to Oudong.
The royal Khmer court moves to Longvek.
King Sattha requested protection from the Spanish governor of the Philippines against the Thai.
The Thai captured the Cambodian capital, Longvek, and installed a military governor there.
Sattha died in Laos.
King Preah Ram I led the Khmer army to liberate Longvek from Siamese.
Spanish adventurers install a son of King Sattha on the throne.
The Spanish in Cambodia were massacred by Malay warlords.
King Suriyopear (nephew of Sattha) installed with help of Ayutthaya.
Nguyen Phuoc Nguyen, king of Hue, approaches Suriyopear to form a military alliance directed at their…
objets.notes: Nguyen Phuoc Nguyen, king of Hue, approaches Suriyopear to form a military alliance directed at their enemies Ayutthaya (for Suriyopear) and the Trinh dynasty of Hanoi (for Nguyen).

objets.nom: Suriyopear abdicates, enters a monastery (dies next year)
objets.notes: Suriyopear abdicates, enters a monastery (dies next year). His son Chey Chettha II becomes king.

objets.nom: According to the Chronicles and popular Cambodian belief, in this year King Chettha II allowed…
objets.notes: According to the Chronicles and popular Cambodian belief, in this year King Chettha II allowed Vietnamese refugees from the Trịnh–Nguyễn Civil War to settle in the Khmer sea port of Prey Nokor. Professional scholars do not believe this happened.

objets.nom: Death of Chettha II; followed as king by his son Ponhea Tu, while his younger brother Outhei takes the…
objets.notes: Death of Chettha II; followed as king by his son Ponhea Tu, while his younger brother Outhei takes the title Ubhayoraj, or senior king.

objets.nom: Ponhea Tu killed after rebelling against the Ubhayoraj
objets.notes: Ponhea Tu killed after rebelling against the Ubhayoraj. Followed by his younger half-brother Ponhea Nur

objets.nom: Death of Ponhea Nur in suspicious circumstances
objets.notes: Death of Ponhea Nur in suspicious circumstances. Followed by Padumaraja I, son of Outhei.

objets.nom: Murder of Padumaraja and Outhei by Ramadhipadi, son of Chettha II. Ramadhipati converts to Islam and…
objets.notes: Murder of Padumaraja and Outhei by Ramadhipadi, son of Chettha II. Ramadhipati converts to Islam and takes the name Ibrahim.

objets.nom: The Mekong Delta region of Cambodia (from Prey Nokor to Psar Dek and Moat Chrouk) was officially annexed…
objets.notes: The Mekong Delta region of Cambodia (from Prey Nokor to Psar Dek and Moat Chrouk) was officially annexed by Vietnam.

objets.nom: An emissary arrived in Prey Nokor to establish Vietnamese administration over the expatriate population.
The Vietnamese conquered the Mekong Delta.
A new Khmer king, Ang Eng, was installed under Thai protection.
A Khmer revolt took place against Vietnamese rule .
Ang Duong becomes king.
Cambodia successfully overthrew the Vietnamese occupation.
Ang Duong dispatches a letter to French Emperor Napoleon III requesting intervention to protect…
objets.notes: Ang Duong dispatches a letter to French Emperor Napoleon III requesting intervention to protect Cambodia's territorial integrity.

objets.nom: Ang Duong dies
objets.notes: Ang Duong dies. His son Norodom succeeds him.

objets.nom: In January, Angkor Wat is "rediscovered" by French naturalist and explorer Henri Mouhot.
Faced with a domestic rebellion, Norodom was forced to accept an offer of protection from the French.
Cambodia was subsumed into the Indochinese Union.
The Résident supérieur was granted the royal powers of tax collection, rule by decree, and appointment…
objets.notes: The Résident supérieur was granted the royal powers of tax collection, rule by decree, and appointment of royal officials and crown princes.

objets.nom: Japanese occupation of Cambodia
objets.notes: Japanese troops occupied Cambodia.

objets.nom: King Sisowath Monivong died
objets.notes: King Sisowath Monivong died. The French chose his grandson Norodom Sihanouk to succeed him.

objets.nom: After its defeat in World War II, Japan relinquished its Indochinese territories.
Cambodia officially gained its independence from France.
King Sihanouk abdicated in favour of his father, Norodom Suramarit.
Cambodia severed ties with South Vietnam.
General Lon Nol overthrew Sihanouk and established a republic
objets.notes: General Lon Nol overthrew Sihanouk and established a republic. Start of the Cambodian Civil War and the US Cambodian Campaign

objets.nom: The Khmer Rouge allied with Sihanouk captured Phnom Penh and declared the establishment of Kingdom of…
objets.notes: The Khmer Rouge allied with Sihanouk captured Phnom Penh and declared the establishment of Kingdom of Cambodia.

objets.nom: Sihanouk exiled and establishment of Democratic Kampuchea under total Khmer Rouge control.
Cambodia broke relations with the Socialist Republic of Vietnam.
Cambodian-Vietnamese War
objets.notes: Vietnamese troops captured Phnom Penh establishing the People's Republic of Kampuchea. The rule of the Khmer Rouge is over.

objets.nom: The last Vietnamese troops withdrew from Cambodia.
A United Nations peacekeeping force, the United Nations Transitional Authority in Cambodia (UNTAC),…
objets.notes: A United Nations peacekeeping force, the United Nations Transitional Authority in Cambodia (UNTAC), began monitoring Cambodia.

objets.nom: A new constitution was ratified, under which the Cambodian monarchy was restored
objets.notes: A new constitution was ratified, under which the Cambodian monarchy was restored. Norodom Sihanouk returned to the throne.

objets.nom: Cambodia held free elections
objets.notes: Cambodia held free elections. The Khmer Rouge boycotted them.

objets.nom: The Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia, a tribunal for the Khmer Rouge, was established.
Death of Pol Pot.
2003 Phnom Penh riots
objets.notes: Nationalist rioters destroyed the Thai embassy in Phnom Penh.

objets.nom: An Angkor newspaper reported that Suvanant Kongying, a Thai actress, had claimed that Angkor Wat…
objets.notes: An Angkor newspaper reported that Suvanant Kongying, a Thai actress, had claimed that Angkor Wat rightfully belonged to Thailand.

objets.nom: Cambodian parliamentary election
objets.notes: Prime Minister Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party won a majority of seats in the National Assembly.

objets.nom: Thai television programs were banned from broadcasting in Cambodia.
King Norodom Sihanouk abdicated
objets.notes: King Norodom Sihanouk abdicated. His son Norodom Sihamoni was crowned as his successor.

objets.nom: 2008 Cambodian-Thai stand-off
objets.notes: Clashes began with Thailand over territory immediately adjacent to Preah Vihear.

objets.nom: Former King of Cambodia Norodom Sihanouk died in Beijing at the age of 89.
Military police opened fire at opposition protesters, leaving 3 people dead and more than 20 injured.
A group of Dominican friars established the village of Lifau.
Portugal opened a trade route with East Timor.
The territory officially became a Portuguese colony, taking the name Portuguese Timor.
The capital was moved to Dili.
The border between Portuguese Timor and the Dutch East Indies was formally decided.
Beginning of the Great Rebellion
The rebellion was quashed with Portuguese troops from its colonies in Mozambique and Macau, resulting in…
objets.notes: The rebellion was quashed with Portuguese troops from its colonies in Mozambique and Macau, resulting in the deaths of three thousand people.

objets.nom: The Portuguese and Dutch agreed to a formal division of the island.
A definitive border between Portuguese and Dutch territories was drawn in the Hague.
Portuguese Timor was occupied by Australian and Dutch forces.
Carnation Revolution
objets.notes: A revolution installed a new government.

objets.nom: Indonesian invasion of East Timor
objets.notes: Indonesia invaded East Timor.

objets.nom: Indonesian occupation of East Timor
objets.notes: Indonesia declared East Timor its 27th province.

objets.nom: Santa Cruz massacre
objets.notes: Pro-independence demonstrators in the Santa Cruz cemetery are shot.

objets.nom: The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo and José Ramos-Horta for their ongoing…
objets.notes: The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo and José Ramos-Horta for their ongoing efforts to peacefully end the occupation.

objets.nom: East Timor Special Autonomy Referendum
objets.notes: A referendum resulted in 78% in favour of independence from Indonesia.

objets.nom: East Timor under United Nations administration (UNTAET).
The International Force for East Timor (INTERFET) arrived to address an ongoing humanitarian and…
objets.notes: The International Force for East Timor (INTERFET) arrived to address an ongoing humanitarian and security crisis.

objets.nom: Timor-Leste became an independent nation.
Timor-Leste joined the ASEAN Regional Forum, as a part of the country's bid for accession to ASEAN as a whole.
2006 East Timorese crisis
objets.notes: A national crisis that included a coup attempt swept the nation.

objets.nom: The prehistoric clay pottery Buni culture (near present-day Bekasi) flourished in coastal northern West Java.
"Dvipantara" or "Yawadvipa", a mystic Hindu kingdom is mentioned in India's earliest epic, the Ramayana;…
objets.notes: "Dvipantara" or "Yawadvipa", a mystic Hindu kingdom is mentioned in India's earliest epic, the Ramayana; Sugriva, the chief of Rama's army dispatched his men to Yawadvipa in search of Sita then later used by the Indianized islander of Java Island and kingdom of Portugal to name the island during the age of discovery.

objets.nom: Several stone inscriptions were created in West Java
objets.notes: Several stone inscriptions were created in West Java. Among others, the Tugu inscription announce decrees of Purnavarman, the king of Tarumanagara, one of the earliest Indianized kingdom in Java.

objets.nom: Dapunta Hyang Sri Jayanasa performed Siddhayatra as the journey to expand his influence
objets.notes: Dapunta Hyang Sri Jayanasa performed Siddhayatra as the journey to expand his influence. The event is mentioned in several inscriptions such as Telaga Batu inscription, Talang Tuwo inscription, and Kedukan Bukit Inscription. The beginning of Srivijaya hegemony over the maritime region around Malacca Strait and Sunda Strait.

objets.nom: I-tsing returned to Srivijaya on his way back from India to China
objets.notes: I-tsing returned to Srivijaya on his way back from India to China. In his record he reported that the kingdom of Malayu was captured by Srivijaya.

objets.nom: Sojomerto inscription possibly dated around late 7th century discovered in Batang Regency, Central Java,…
objets.notes: Sojomerto inscription possibly dated around late 7th century discovered in Batang Regency, Central Java, mentioned about Dapunta Selendra, possibly the ancestor of Shailendra dynasty. The inscription was written in old Malay suggested Srivijayan link to this family.

objets.nom: Sri Indravarman King of Srivijaya send a letter to the Caliph Umar bin Abdul Aziz of the Umayyad…
objets.notes: Sri Indravarman King of Srivijaya send a letter to the Caliph Umar bin Abdul Aziz of the Umayyad Caliphate in Damascus, signing early ancient Indonesian official contact with Islamic world in the Middle East.

objets.nom: Java launched series of naval raids on ports of Dai Viet, Champa and Cambodia; Sontay in Tonkin (767);…
objets.notes: Java launched series of naval raids on ports of Dai Viet, Champa and Cambodia; Sontay in Tonkin (767); Nha Trang (774); captured Indrapura in Cambodia (770); Phan Rang (787). The naval raids was probably launched by Shailendran-Srivijayan Maharaja Dharmasetu or Dharanindra.

objets.nom: The agriculturally based Buddhist Shailendra dynasty rules Sumatra and Java.
Prambanan is completed
objets.notes: Prambanan is completed. According to Shivagrha inscription Rakai Pikatan — the husband of Pramodhawardhani — defeated Balaputra.

objets.nom: Balaputra the Maharaja of Suvarnadvipa and the ruler of Srivijaya, constructs the buddhist temple and…
objets.notes: Balaputra the Maharaja of Suvarnadvipa and the ruler of Srivijaya, constructs the buddhist temple and monastery in Nalanda India, on the land given by King Devapaladeva of Pala in Benggala, according to the Nalanda inscription.

objets.nom: King Balitung created Mantyasih inscription containing the list of Mataram kings, moved the capital from…
objets.notes: King Balitung created Mantyasih inscription containing the list of Mataram kings, moved the capital from Mamratipura to Poh Pitu, and expanded Prambanan temple.

objets.nom: During the reign of King Wawa, the capital of Mataram in Mamratipura was devastated, probably by the…
objets.notes: During the reign of King Wawa, the capital of Mataram in Mamratipura was devastated, probably by the massive eruption of Mount Merapi.

objets.nom: Mpu Sindok moved the capital again from Tamwlang to Watugaluh, both near bank of Brantas River in modern…
objets.notes: Mpu Sindok moved the capital again from Tamwlang to Watugaluh, both near bank of Brantas River in modern Jombang in East Java.

objets.nom: Dynastic marriage between princess Mahendradatta of Javanese Isyanas and king Udayana of Balinese Warmadewas.
King Dharmawangsa of Mataram kingdom launches a naval invasion on Palembang in an unsuccessful attempt…
objets.notes: King Dharmawangsa of Mataram kingdom launches a naval invasion on Palembang in an unsuccessful attempt to conquer Srivijaya.

objets.nom: Rajendra Chola, the Chola king from Cholamandala in South India, conquered Pannai and Kadaram from…
objets.notes: Rajendra Chola, the Chola king from Cholamandala in South India, conquered Pannai and Kadaram from Srivijaya and occupied it for some time. The Cholas continued a series of raids and conquests of parts Srivijayan empire in Sumatra and Malay Peninsula.

objets.nom: Airlangga divided Kahuripan into two kingdoms Janggala and Kadiri and abdicated in favour of his successors.
King Kamesvara of Kadiri ascends to the throne
objets.notes: King Kamesvara of Kadiri ascends to the throne. Janggala ceases to exist and united under Kadiri domination, highly possible under royal marriage. During his reign Mpu Dharmaja writes Kakawin Smaradahana, a eulogy for the king and become the inspiration of Panji cycle, the tales that spreads across Southeast Asia.

objets.nom: Battle of Genter, Ken Arok defeated Kertajaya, the last king of Kediri, thus established Singhasari…
objets.notes: Battle of Genter, Ken Arok defeated Kertajaya, the last king of Kediri, thus established Singhasari kingdom Ken Arok ended the reign of Isyana Dynasty and started his own Rajasa dynasty.

objets.nom: King Kertanegara of Singhasari launched Pamalayu expedition against Melayu Kingdom in Sumatra.
Marco Polo, on his voyage from China to Persia visited Sumatra and reported that on the northern part of…
objets.notes: Marco Polo, on his voyage from China to Persia visited Sumatra and reported that on the northern part of Sumatra there were six trading ports including Ferlec, Samudera and Lambri.

objets.nom: Mongol invasion of Java, Kublai Khan of Yuan dynasty China, sent punitive attack against Kertanegara of…
objets.notes: Mongol invasion of Java, Kublai Khan of Yuan dynasty China, sent punitive attack against Kertanegara of Singhasari. The Mongol forces were repelled.

objets.nom: Footprint of Islam state is present in northern tip of Sumatra.
King Jayanegara succeeds Kertarajasa Jayawardhana as ruler of Majapahit.
An Italian Franciscan friar, Mattiussi visited Sumatra, Java, and Banjarmasin in Borneo
objets.notes: an Italian Franciscan friar, Mattiussi visited Sumatra, Java, and Banjarmasin in Borneo. In his record he described Majapahit kingdom.

objets.nom: Gajah Mada declared his Palapa oath.
Adityawarman moved the capital of Dharmasraya and established the kingdom of Malayupura in Pagarruyung,…
objets.notes: Adityawarman moved the capital of Dharmasraya and established the kingdom of Malayupura in Pagarruyung, West Sumatra.

objets.nom: Hayam Wuruk, styled Sri Rajasanagara succeeds Tribhuwana Wijayatunggadewi as ruler of Majapahit; his…
objets.notes: Hayam Wuruk, styled Sri Rajasanagara succeeds Tribhuwana Wijayatunggadewi as ruler of Majapahit; his reign is considered the empire's 'Golden Age'. Under its military commander Gajah Mada, Majapahit stretches over much of modern-day Indonesia.

objets.nom: Kingdom of Negara Dipa was established in South Kalimantan by Empu Jatmika.
In the Battle of Bubat, the Sundanese royal family were massacred by the Majapahit army under the order…
objets.notes: In the Battle of Bubat, the Sundanese royal family were massacred by the Majapahit army under the order of Gajah Mada. This event led to the death of Sundanese King Lingga Buana and the princess Dyah Pitaloka Citraresmi that committed suicide.

objets.nom: Majapahit sends a punitive expedition against rebelling Palembang in Sumatra
objets.notes: Majapahit sends a punitive expedition against rebelling Palembang in Sumatra. Palembang's prince, Parameswara, flees to Singapura, eventually became king of Singapura for several years.

objets.nom: The Portuguese king sends Diogo Lopes de Sequeira to find Malacca, the eastern terminus of Asian trade
objets.notes: The Portuguese king sends Diogo Lopes de Sequeira to find Malacca, the eastern terminus of Asian trade. After initially receiving Sequeira, Sultan Mahmud Syah captures and/or kills several of his men and attempts an assault on the four Portuguese ships, which escape. The Javanese fleet is also destroyed in Malacca.

objets.nom: Afonso de Albuquerque after sailing from Portuguese Goa conquers the Sultanate of Malacca with a force…
objets.notes: Afonso de Albuquerque after sailing from Portuguese Goa conquers the Sultanate of Malacca with a force of 1,200 and seventeen or eighteen ships.

objets.nom: The first Portuguese exploratory expedition was sent eastward from Malacca to search for the 'Spice…
objets.notes: The first Portuguese exploratory expedition was sent eastward from Malacca to search for the 'Spice Islands' (Maluku) led by Francisco Serrão. Serrao is shipwrecked but struggles on to Hitu (northern Ambon) and wins the favour of the local rulers.

objets.nom: Sultan Ali Mughayat Syah of Aceh begins an expansionist campaign capturing Dayak on the west Sumatran…
objets.notes: Sultan Ali Mughayat Syah of Aceh begins an expansionist campaign capturing Dayak on the west Sumatran coast, and the pepper and gold producing lands on the east coast.

objets.nom: The Portuguese established a trading post in the village of Lamakera on the eastern side of Solor as a…
objets.notes: The Portuguese established a trading post in the village of Lamakera on the eastern side of Solor as a transit harbour between Maluku and Malacca.

objets.nom: The establishment of Banjar Sultanate in South Kalimantan with Sultan Suriansyah as the first king.
Ferdinand Magellan's expedition reaches Maluku and after trade with Ternate returns to Europe with a…
objets.notes: Ferdinand Magellan's expedition reaches Maluku and after trade with Ternate returns to Europe with a load of cloves.

objets.nom: Luso Sundanese Treaty signed between Portugal and Sunda Kingdom granted Portuguese permit to build…
objets.notes: Luso Sundanese Treaty signed between Portugal and Sunda Kingdom granted Portuguese permit to build fortress in Sunda Kelapa

objets.nom: Portuguese Dominican priests build a palm-trunk fortress which Javanese Muslims burned down the following year
objets.notes: Portuguese Dominican priests build a palm-trunk fortress which Javanese Muslims burned down the following year. The fort was rebuilt from more durable materials and the Dominicans commenced the Christianisation of the local population.

objets.nom: The British navigator Sir Francis Drake passes through Maluku and transit in Ternate on his…
objets.notes: The British navigator Sir Francis Drake passes through Maluku and transit in Ternate on his circumnavigation of the world. The Portuguese establish a fort on Tidore but the main centre for Portuguese activities in Maluku becomes Ambon.

objets.nom: De Houtman's expedition reaches Banten the main pepper port of West Java where they clash with both the…
objets.notes: de Houtman's expedition reaches Banten the main pepper port of West Java where they clash with both the Portuguese and Indonesians. It then sails east along the north coast of Java losing twelve crew to a Javanese attack at Sidayu and killing a local ruler in Madura.

objets.nom: British East India Company's first voyage, commanded by Sir James Lancaster, arrives in Aceh and sails…
objets.notes: British East India Company's first voyage, commanded by Sir James Lancaster, arrives in Aceh and sails on to Bantam where he is allowed to build trading post which becomes the centre of British trade in Indonesia until 1682.

objets.nom: The English establish trading posts at Sukadana (southwest Kalimantan), Makassar, Jayakarta and Jepara…
objets.notes: The English establish trading posts at Sukadana (southwest Kalimantan), Makassar, Jayakarta and Jepara in Java, and Aceh, Pariaman and Jambi in (Sumatra) threatening Dutch ambitions for a monopoly on East Indies trade.

objets.nom: Sultan Agung of Mataram launched a failed campaign to conquer Dutch Batavia.
Iskandar Muda of Aceh Sultanate launched a failed attempt to take Portuguese Malacca.
As a result of the Treaty of Breda between Dutch and England, the Dutch secured a worldwide monopoly on…
objets.notes: As a result of the Treaty of Breda between Dutch and England, the Dutch secured a worldwide monopoly on nutmeg by forcing England to give up their claim on Run, the most remote of the Banda Islands. While the Dutch did not press their claims on New Netherland.

objets.nom: The Trunajaya rebellion
