objets.notes: The Trunajaya rebellion. Followers of the Madurese prince Trunajaya rebelled against the Mataram Sultanate. After initial defeats, Mataram requested help from the VOC in exchange for various concessions. VOC-Mataram forces ultimately defeated the rebellion.

objets.nom: Pakubuwono II established a new kraton in Sala village and established Surakarta Sunanate.
The Treaty of Giyanti is signed, effectively partitioning the Mataram Sultanate
objets.notes: The Treaty of Giyanti is signed, effectively partitioning the Mataram Sultanate. The VOC recognizes Mangkubumi as Sultan Hamengkubuwono I, who rules half of Central Java. Hamengkubuwono I then established Yogyakarta Sultanate, moves to Yogya and renames the city Yogyakarta

objets.nom: Salatiga treaty between Prince Sambernyawa with Pakubuwono III and Hamengkubuwono I further partitioning…
objets.notes: Salatiga treaty between Prince Sambernyawa with Pakubuwono III and Hamengkubuwono I further partitioning the remnant of Mataram Sultanate, the Mangkunegaran Grand Duchy was established.

objets.nom: The Batavian Republic, a client state of the French First Republic, and successor state to the Republic…
objets.notes: The Batavian Republic, a client state of the French First Republic, and successor state to the Republic of the Seven United Netherlands was proclaimed.

objets.nom: The Batavian Republic is dissolved and the Kingdom of Holland is created, a puppet kingdom set up by…
objets.notes: The Batavian Republic is dissolved and the Kingdom of Holland is created, a puppet kingdom set up by Napoléon Bonaparte.

objets.nom: Herman Willem Daendels the Governor-general of the Dutch East Indies, During the French interim…
objets.notes: Herman Willem Daendels the Governor-general of the Dutch East Indies, During the French interim (1806–1811) begins the construction of Java Great Post Road. against an Anglo-Dutch invasion.

objets.nom: British invasion of Java during the Napoleonic Wars
objets.notes: British invasion of Java during the Napoleonic Wars. Stamford Raffles was appointed as the Lieutenant-Governor of Java.

objets.nom: Mount Tambora in Sumbawa island erupted, it was the largest volcanic eruption in recorded history that…
objets.notes: Mount Tambora in Sumbawa island erupted, it was the largest volcanic eruption in recorded history that wiped out Tambora culture and killed at least 71,000 people in total (including the aftermath). The eruption created global climate anomalies known as "volcanic winter".

objets.nom: The first railway track in Indonesia was laid between Semarang and Tanggung, Central Java by the Dutch…
objets.notes: The first railway track in Indonesia was laid between Semarang and Tanggung, Central Java by the Dutch colonial government.

objets.nom: Mount Krakatoa in Sunda Strait erupted, killed 36,417 people.
Dutch intervention in Lombok and Karangasem The Dutch looted and destroyed the Cakranegara palace of Mataram
objets.notes: Dutch intervention in Lombok and Karangasem The Dutch looted and destroyed the Cakranegara palace of Mataram. J. L. A. Brandes, a Dutch philologist discovered and secured Nagarakretagama manuscript in Lombok royal library.

objets.nom: Dewi Sartika established the first school for women in Dutch East Indies in Bandung, she was considered…
objets.notes: Dewi Sartika established the first school for women in Dutch East Indies in Bandung, she was considered as the pioneer of women's rights in Indonesia.

objets.nom: Jo van Heutsz becomes Governor General
objets.notes: Jo van Heutsz becomes Governor General. Kartini established a school for women in Rembang, just like Dewi Sartika, she was considered as the pioneer of women's rights in Indonesia.

objets.nom: Battle of the Java Sea, Imperial Japanese Navy defeat Allied forces ABDACOM afterwards Imperial Japan…
objets.notes: Battle of the Java Sea, Imperial Japanese Navy defeat Allied forces ABDACOM afterwards Imperial Japan occupies Indonesia during World War II, over throwing the Dutch East Indies and install their own imperial structure.

objets.nom: Merauke Force formed, to reinforce the KNIL garrison in Merauke, West New Guinea.
Between January and July landing of Dutch KNIL troops at Biak, Tarakan and Balikpapan.
Madiun Affair
objets.notes: Nationalist leaders launch a revolt in Central Java in an attempt to take over the Revolution but are suppressed by Communist troops.

objets.nom: The city of Bandung hosts the Asia-Africa Conference
objets.notes: The city of Bandung hosts the Asia-Africa Conference. It is the first meeting of the Non-Aligned Movement and is attended by world leaders including China's Zhou Enlai, India's Nehru, Egypt's Nasser and Yugoslavia's Tito. (to 25 April)

objets.nom: US Air Force pilot Allen Pope is shot down over Ambon, revealing covert American support of regional…
objets.notes: US Air Force pilot Allen Pope is shot down over Ambon, revealing covert American support of regional rebellions, and ends the Dulles brothers', Allen and John, efforts to subvert the Sukarno government.

objets.nom: Second Lieutenant Daniel Alexander Maukar of the Indonesian Air Force uses a MiG-17 fighter to strafe…
objets.notes: Second Lieutenant Daniel Alexander Maukar of the Indonesian Air Force uses a MiG-17 fighter to strafe the Presidential Palace in Jakarta, oil tanks at Tanjung Priok in North Jakarta and then the Bogor Palace.

objets.nom: ASEAN established in Bangkok by Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand.
Suharto successfully defies Dutch efforts to link human rights to aid administered since 1967 by the…
objets.notes: Suharto successfully defies Dutch efforts to link human rights to aid administered since 1967 by the International Governmental Group on Indonesia (IGGI). Susi Susanti won Indonesia's first Olympic gold medal in 1992 Summer Olympics in Barcelona, Spain.

objets.nom: President Wahid's administration is marred by failures to stabilise the economy, patterns of political…
objets.notes: President Wahid's administration is marred by failures to stabilise the economy, patterns of political favouritism, economic corruption (although Wahid himself is not accused of corruption), inability to reform the military, personal eccentricity and pettiness, ineffectiveness in dealing with major religious violence in Maluku and Sulawesi, major…

objets.nom: Adam Air Flight 574 crashes into the sea in Makassar Strait off Sulawesi, killing all 102 on board.
Russian Sukhoi Superjet 100 crashed against Mount Salak, West Java, killing 45 people abroad during a…
objets.notes: Russian Sukhoi Superjet 100 crashed against Mount Salak, West Java, killing 45 people abroad during a demonstrational flight.

objets.nom: Indonesia held their legislative election, PDI-P dominate the People's Representative Council, followed…
objets.notes: Indonesia held their legislative election, PDI-P dominate the People's Representative Council, followed closely by Golkar and Gerindra.

objets.nom: Indonesia held their presidential election, according to quick count Jakarta's Governor Joko Widodo won…
objets.notes: Indonesia held their presidential election, according to quick count Jakarta's Governor Joko Widodo won against former military general Prabowo Subianto, however both sides claims victory.

objets.nom: Indonesian Election Commission announced Joko Widodo wins Indonesian presidential election with 53.15%…
objets.notes: Indonesian Election Commission announced Joko Widodo wins Indonesian presidential election with 53.15% of the vote with his rival, ex-general Prabowo Subianto, on 46.85%.

objets.nom: Joko Widodo and Jusuf Kalla sworn in as Indonesian President and Vice President for the period of…
objets.notes: Joko Widodo and Jusuf Kalla sworn in as Indonesian President and Vice President for the period of 2014–2019 in a plenary session of the People's Consultative Assembly (MPR). Thousands of people celebrating the inauguration ceremony by attending parade along Sudirman and Thamrin avenue, followed by a concert in Merdeka Square featuring Slank,…

objets.nom: Dozens of Indonesians are killed by respiratory illness and accidents due to poor visibility caused by…
objets.notes: Dozens of Indonesians are killed by respiratory illness and accidents due to poor visibility caused by severe haze. The haze occurs annually during dry season and is largely caused by illegal agricultural fires due to slash-and-burn practices in Indonesia, especially from the provinces of South Sumatra and Riau in Indonesia's Sumatra island, and…

objets.nom: President Joko Widodo has announced that the country's new capital city will be located in East…
objets.notes: President Joko Widodo has announced that the country's new capital city will be located in East Kalimantan on Borneo island. The new capital will replace Jakarta and will be built in part of Penajam North Paser regency and part of Kutai Kertanegara regency.

objets.nom: Hand axes from early hominids, probably Homo erectus, have been unearthed in Lenggong, making them some…
objets.notes: Hand axes from early hominids, probably Homo erectus, have been unearthed in Lenggong, making them some of the oldest evidence of hominid habitation in Southeast Asia.

objets.nom: The ancient Hindu Malay kingdom of Gangga Negara was founded by Ganji Sarjuna, a son of Merong Mahawangsa.
The ancient Hindu Malay kingdom of Langkasuka was founded by Merong Mahawangsa, a descendant of…
objets.notes: The ancient Hindu Malay kingdom of Langkasuka was founded by Merong Mahawangsa, a descendant of Alexander the Great or Dhu al-Qarnayn.

objets.nom: The Hindu Malay Kingdom of Kedah was founded by Maharaja Derbar Raja of Persia.
The Malay Peninsula fell under the dominance of the Buddhist Malay Srivijaya, based in Palembang.
The Sawaku Kingdom was founded by Datu Merpati near Santubong and Sarawak River
objets.notes: The Sawaku Kingdom was founded by Datu Merpati near Santubong and Sarawak River. The Samadong Kingdom was founded near Samarahan and Sadong.

objets.nom: Sang Sapurba, a legendary ancestor of significant dynasties in the Malay world and descendant of…
objets.notes: Sang Sapurba, a legendary ancestor of significant dynasties in the Malay world and descendant of Alexander the Great or Dhul-Qarnayn, entered into a sacred covenant with Demang Lebar Daun, the ruler of Palembang, and subsequently laid the basis of the relationship between the Malay rulers and subjects.

objets.nom: Siamese begun to occupy the northern Malay Peninsula
objets.notes: Siamese begun to occupy the northern Malay Peninsula. Negara Sri Dharmaraja and Patani, became Siamese vassals.

objets.nom: Islam reached Terengganu, proven by the discovery of the Terengganu Inscription Stone in Kuala Berang
objets.notes: Islam reached Terengganu, proven by the discovery of the Terengganu Inscription Stone in Kuala Berang. This is the earliest evidence of Jawi writing in Malay.

objets.nom: The Chinese traveler Wang Dayuan visited Singapura and recorded an attack by Siam, recording it…
objets.notes: The Chinese traveler Wang Dayuan visited Singapura and recorded an attack by Siam, recording it alongside Long Ya Men and Ban Zu.

objets.nom: Singapura Kingdom attacked and was defeated by the Hindu Buddhist Javanese Kingdom of Majapahit.
Parameswara, a prince of Srivijaya and the last king of Singapura fled from the Singapura.
Chinese admiral Yin Ching reached Malacca, and established diplomatic ties between China and Malacca.
The first Malay-Chinese dictionary was compiled in Chinese characters containing about 500 words related…
objets.notes: The first Malay-Chinese dictionary was compiled in Chinese characters containing about 500 words related to trade used in Malacca.

objets.nom: Chinese admiral Cheng Ho reached Malacca, strengthening diplomatic ties between China and Malacca.
Malacca established diplomatic ties with Pasai, when Megat Iskandar Shah married a princess of Pasai and…
objets.notes: Malacca established diplomatic ties with Pasai, when Megat Iskandar Shah married a princess of Pasai and converted to Islam.

objets.nom: Hang Tuah, the legendary Malaccan Laksamana, was born in Malacca.
Tun Perak, the Penghulu of Klang, lead the Malaccan army to victory by defeating Siamese invaders in Muar.
Sharif ul-Hashim arrived in Sulu from Malacca, married a daughter of Raja Baginda, and founded the…
objets.notes: Sharif ul-Hashim arrived in Sulu from Malacca, married a daughter of Raja Baginda, and founded the Sultanate of Sulu.

objets.nom: Tun Perak lead the Malaccan army to victory by defeating Siamese invaders in Batu Pahat
objets.notes: Tun Perak lead the Malaccan army to victory by defeating Siamese invaders in Batu Pahat. He was made Bendahara of Malacca.

objets.nom: Emperor of China sent his daughter Hang Li Po and 500 followers as a gift to Sultan Mansur Shah
objets.notes: Emperor of China sent his daughter Hang Li Po and 500 followers as a gift to Sultan Mansur Shah. Sultan Mansur Shah established Bukit Cina as a settlement for the Chinese.

objets.nom: Malacca established diplomatic ties with Ryukyu
objets.notes: Malacca established diplomatic ties with Ryukyu. Ryukyu traders were respected in Malacca.

objets.nom: Tun Besar, a son of Tun Perak was killed because he had accidentally displaced Raja Muhammad's destar, a…
objets.notes: Tun Besar, a son of Tun Perak was killed because he had accidentally displaced Raja Muhammad's destar, a prince of Malacca.

objets.nom: The Magellan Expedition was received with hostility by the Mactan natives, led by Lapu-Lapu
objets.notes: The Magellan Expedition was received with hostility by the Mactan natives, led by Lapu-Lapu. Panglima Awang was believed to have left Mactan and made his way back to the Malay Peninsula, becoming the first person in recorded history to circumnavigate the world.

objets.nom: The first Malay-Italian dictionary was compiled by Antonio Pigafetta, who accompanied Ferdinand Magellan…
objets.notes: The first Malay-Italian dictionary was compiled by Antonio Pigafetta, who accompanied Ferdinand Magellan around the globe. The dictionary contains about 426 words related to trade in the Moluccas.

objets.nom: Johor Sultanate was founded by Raja Alauddin, son of Mahmud Shah, the last king of Malacca.
Francis Xavier arrived in Malacca and devoted his life to missions in Asia, especially in Malacca and…
objets.notes: Francis Xavier arrived in Malacca and devoted his life to missions in Asia, especially in Malacca and Maluku Islands.

objets.nom: Francis Xavier met a Japanese man named Anjirō who had traveled from Kagoshima to Malacca to meet him…
objets.notes: Francis Xavier met a Japanese man named Anjirō who had traveled from Kagoshima to Malacca to meet him and become the first Japanese Christian.

objets.nom: Manuel Godinho de Erédia, a Malay-Portuguese writer and cartographer of early Malay Peninsula, was born…
objets.notes: Manuel Godinho de Erédia, a Malay-Portuguese writer and cartographer of early Malay Peninsula, was born in Malacca.

objets.nom: Raja Alauddin, a prince of Perak was married to an Acehnese princess and installed as the Sultan of Aceh.
Castilian War
objets.notes: War broke out between Brunei and Spain in Borneo and Mindanao.

objets.nom: Dutch led by Jacob van Heemskerk with the assistance of Johor, seized the Portuguese merchant vessel…
objets.notes: Dutch led by Jacob van Heemskerk with the assistance of Johor, seized the Portuguese merchant vessel Santa Catarina off the coast of Singapore.

objets.nom: Malay-Dutch vocabulary, the earliest Malay book printed in Europe, was published by Frederick de Houtman…
objets.notes: Malay-Dutch vocabulary, the earliest Malay book printed in Europe, was published by Frederick de Houtman in Amsterdam.

objets.nom: Perak nobles turned to Sultan Iskandar Thani of Aceh who sent his relative, Raja Sulong, to be the…
objets.notes: Perak nobles turned to Sultan Iskandar Thani of Aceh who sent his relative, Raja Sulong, to be the sultan of Perak because the previous sultan died without an heir and many royal family members died due to an epidemic that swept through the sultanate. Raja Sulong was a prince of Siak and was not genealogically linked to Perak royalty on his…

objets.nom: Dutch, with the help from Johor, conquered Malacca from the Portuguese
objets.notes: Dutch, with the help from Johor, conquered Malacca from the Portuguese. Hikayat Hang Tuah was composed by an unknown writer from Johor after the Portuguese defeat in Malacca.

objets.nom: Brunei Civil War
objets.notes: The Eastern part of Sabah was given to Sulu as the reward for assisting the Muhyiddin's forces.

objets.nom: Tun Abdul Jalil, the Bendahara of Johor was elected as the Sultan of Johor, after the dead of "Sultan…
objets.notes: Tun Abdul Jalil, the Bendahara of Johor was elected as the Sultan of Johor, after the dead of "Sultan Mahmud Mangkat Dijulang".

objets.nom: Penghulu Luak of Sungai Ujong, Jelebu, Johol and Rembau invited a prince of the Minangkabau in Sumatra…
objets.notes: Penghulu Luak of Sungai Ujong, Jelebu, Johol and Rembau invited a prince of the Minangkabau in Sumatra to rule Negeri Sembilan.

objets.nom: Malay gamelan was first performed in public in Pekan during the wedding ceremony of Tengku Hussain, the…
objets.notes: Malay gamelan was first performed in public in Pekan during the wedding ceremony of Tengku Hussain, the son of Sultan Mahmud Shah of Johor-Pahang-Riau-Lingga, with Wan Esah, a sister of Raja Bendahara Tun Ali of Pahang.

objets.nom: Sultan Mahmud Shah died in Lingga, the throne of Johor-Pahang-Riau-Lingga went instead to Tengku Jummat,…
objets.notes: Sultan Mahmud Shah died in Lingga, the throne of Johor-Pahang-Riau-Lingga went instead to Tengku Jummat, who was supported by the Bugis in Lingga but opposed by the Malay chiefs in Riau and Pahang who were supporters of Tengku Hussain

objets.nom: Cantonese-dominated Ghee Hin and Hakka-dominated Hai San, two main secret societies in Malaya were…
objets.notes: Cantonese-dominated Ghee Hin and Hakka-dominated Hai San, two main secret societies in Malaya were established.

objets.nom: Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 was signed by the United Kingdom and the Netherlands, partitioning the…
objets.notes: Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 was signed by the United Kingdom and the Netherlands, partitioning the southern Malay states, Johor-Pahang-Riau-Lingga between British Malaya and Dutch East Indies.

objets.nom: Burney Treaty was signed between Siam and the United Kingdom, partitioning the northern Malay states…
objets.notes: Burney Treaty was signed between Siam and the United Kingdom, partitioning the northern Malay states between British Malaya and Siam.

objets.nom: Naning War
objets.notes: The opposition of Dol Said to British taxation policy in Naning led to the Naning War.

objets.nom: Naning War
objets.notes: Dol Said surrendered to British forces in return for an official pardon, so ending the Naning War.

objets.nom: Kedah was divided into four administrative units by Siam, Setul, Perlis, Kubang Pasu and Kedah.
Baju Kurung Telok Belanga, a version of Baju Kurung was designed by Sultan Abu Bakar and named after the…
objets.notes: Baju Kurung Telok Belanga, a version of Baju Kurung was designed by Sultan Abu Bakar and named after the centre of the Johor at that time. Baju Kurung is the national dress of Malaysia.

objets.nom: Klang War
objets.notes: Raja Mahadi challenged Raja Abdullah for authority over Klang.

objets.nom: Klang War
objets.notes: Ghee Hin had joined Raja Mahadi's forces, and Hai San had sided with Tengku Kudin.

objets.nom: Third Larut War: Began with an affair between Ghee Hin's leader and a member of Hai San and conflict of…
objets.notes: Third Larut War: Began with an affair between Ghee Hin's leader and a member of Hai San and conflict of Perak succession between Raja Abdullah and Raja Ismail.

objets.nom: Perak War
objets.notes: James W. W. Birch, the first Resident of Perak was assassinated by Malay chief, Dato Maharaja Lela's forces in Pasir Salak.

objets.nom: Perak War
objets.notes: Raja Abdullah, Ngah Ibrahim and Mohammad Amin were exiled to the Seychelles.

objets.nom: Perak War
objets.notes: Dato' Maharaja Lela was executed by hanging in Taiping.

objets.nom: Selangor, Perak, Negeri Sembilan and Pahang joined to become the Federated Malay States, a federation of…
objets.notes: Selangor, Perak, Negeri Sembilan and Pahang joined to become the Federated Malay States, a federation of British protectorates.

objets.nom: Battle of Penang
objets.notes: The German cruiser sank two Allied warships in the Strait of Malacca.

objets.nom: Kelantan Rebellion
objets.notes: Villagers led by Tok Janggut resisted British taxes and land control before being suppressed.

objets.nom: Attack on Pearl Harbor
objets.notes: Japan opened hostilities with the Allies and their colonies.

objets.nom: Japanese occupation of British Borneo
objets.notes: Japanese forces invaded and began the occupation of British Borneo.

objets.nom: Japanese occupation of Malaya
objets.notes: Japanese forces invaded and began the occupation of British Malaya.

objets.nom: Battle of Pasir Panjang
objets.notes: A Malay regiment led by Lieutenant Adnan bin Saidi fought bravely against the Japanese at Pasir Panjang Ridge.

objets.nom: Battle of Singapore
objets.notes: The Japanese crossed the Strait of Johor in inflatable boats and landed in Singapore.

objets.nom: Battle of North Borneo
objets.notes: A battle was fought between the Australians and Japanese.

objets.nom: Death of Lau Yew
objets.notes: British security forces clashed with those of the Malayan Communist Party, resulting in the death of one of their key leaders, Lau Yew.

objets.nom: The Batang Kali massacre
objets.notes: The Scots Guards of the British Army murdered 24 unarmed civilians.

objets.nom: Rosli Dhobi and several members from Rukun 13 orchestrated the assassination of the Governor of Sarawak,…
objets.notes: Rosli Dhobi and several members from Rukun 13 orchestrated the assassination of the Governor of Sarawak, Sir Duncan Stewart in Sibu.

objets.nom: Assassination of Sir Henry Gurney
objets.notes: British High Commissioner Sir Henry Gurney was killed by members of the Malayan Communist Party in Fraser's Hill.

objets.nom: Baling Talks
objets.notes: A talk between representatives of the government of Malaya and Malayan Communist Party to resolve the Malayan Emergency situation. Tan Cheng Lock, David Marshall and Tunku Abdul Rahman represented the government whereas Chin Peng, Rashid Maidin and Chen Tien represented the communists. However, the talks were unsuccessful because the surrender…

objets.nom: Indonesia–Malaysia confrontation
objets.notes: Indonesian Foreign Minister Subandrio announced that Indonesia would declared Confrontation or konfrontasi against proposed Federation of Malaysia.

objets.nom: 1969 Malaysian general election
objets.notes: Alliance won 4th general election in West Malaysia but suffered a loss of two-thirds majority in Parliament for the first time since Independence. Alliance also lost government power to the Opposition in Perak, Selangor, Penang, and Kelantan.

objets.nom: 1975 AIA building hostage crisis
objets.notes: Japanese Red Army took more than 50 hostages at the AIA building, which housed several embassies.

objets.nom: 1977 Kelantan Emergency
objets.notes: The state of emergency was declared by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong (King of Malaysia) upon the request of the federal government following a political impasse and street violence in Kelantan.

objets.nom: Pedra Branca dispute
objets.notes: Singapore lodged a formal protest with Malaysia in response to a map published by Malaysia in 1979 claiming Pedra Branca.

objets.nom: 1993 amendments to the Constitution of Malaysia
objets.notes: The Parliament passed amendments to the Constitution to strip the royalty of legal immunity. A new chapter, Part XV of the Constitution entitled "Proceedings against the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and the Rulers" was also enshrined.

objets.nom: 2000 Sipadan kidnappings
objets.notes: 21 hostages were kidnapped by six Abu Sayyaf militants from a dive resort on the island of Sipadan, Sabah, and taken to the Abu Sayyaf base in Jolo, Sulu, in the southern Philippines.

objets.nom: Kajang Move
objets.notes: The attempted replacement of Khalid Ibrahim as Menteri Besar (Chief Minister) of Selangor with Anwar Ibrahim started a political crisis.

objets.nom: The 2018 anti-ICERD rally was organised by opposition right-wing political parties PAS and UMNO, with…
objets.notes: The 2018 anti-ICERD rally was organised by opposition right-wing political parties PAS and UMNO, with the support of various non-governmental organisations in response to the PH government plan to ratify the United Nations convention known as ICERD.

objets.nom: The High Court convicted former prime minister Najib Razak on all seven counts of abuse of power, money…
objets.notes: The High Court convicted former prime minister Najib Razak on all seven counts of abuse of power, money laundering and criminal breach of trust, becoming the first Prime Minister of Malaysia to be convicted of corruption, and was sentenced to 12 years imprisonment and fined RM210 million.

objets.nom: A Beechcraft 390 Premier I business jet carrying passengers, including Johari Harun, a member of the…
objets.notes: A Beechcraft 390 Premier I business jet carrying passengers, including Johari Harun, a member of the Pahang State Executive Council and the Pahang State Legislative Assembly representative for Pelangai, crashed onto an expressway interchange near Elmina in Sungai Buloh, Selangor, Malaysia, resulting in the deaths of 10 people.

objets.nom: The 47th ASEAN Summit was held in Kuala Lumpur
objets.notes: The 47th ASEAN Summit was held in Kuala Lumpur. Cambodia and Thailand signed the Kuala Lumpur Peace Accord, ending the 2025 Cambodia–Thailand conflict. Timor-Leste officially joined ASEAN.

objets.nom: Iron-working settlements south of present-day Mandalay.
Beikthano city fortified by Pyu people who had entered the Irrawaddy valley from north; beginning of Pyu…
objets.notes: Beikthano city fortified by Pyu people who had entered the Irrawaddy valley from north; beginning of Pyu city-states

objets.nom: Mon migrations to Lower Burma from Haribhunjaya and Dvaravati (present-day Thailand) (to 900)
Pyu city of Halin in existence
The Pyu of Sri Ksetra Kingdom launch the Burmese calendar with the start date of 22 March 638.
Pyu city-states (like Hanlin) destroyed by Nanzhao raids
Pyinbya founds Pagan (Bagan)
Earliest evidence of Burmese alphabet (according to an 18th-century recast stone inscription)
Pagan sends embassy to Song court at Bianjing
Earliest evidence of Burmese alphabet (at the Mahabodhi Temple, India)
Anawrahta ascends to Pagan throne
Anawrahta founds Pagan Kingdom including, Thaton, near Shan States, North Arakan, Malay Peninsula (to 1060)
Anawrahta converted to Theravada Buddhism by Shin Arahan
Pagan conquers Thaton Kingdom according to the Burmese chronicles
Anawrahta helps restart Theravada Buddhism in Ceylon
Rebellion in Lower Burma by Yamankan
Kyansittha becomes king
Kyansittha builds Ananda Temple
Earliest inscription of the word Mranma (Myanmar) in Mon script.
Burmese embassy to Song China
Myazedi inscription, earliest evidence of a more settled Burmese alphabet
Thatbyinnyu Temple by Alaungsithu is complete.
Narapatisithu founds the Royal Burmese Armed Forces, the first known standing army in Burmese history
Ceylonese raids to Bassein (Pathein)
Schism develops in Burmese Buddhism; majority of monks shift to Mahavihara school
Sithu II dies and Htilominlo succeeds
Htilominlo builds Htilominlo Temple, the last of the great temples
Kyaswa becomes king of Pagan
Narathihapate placed on Pagan throne
The first Mongol invasion begins
Thawun Gyi and Thawun Nge found Toungoo (Taungoo) as a frontier outpost
Wareru seizes governorship of Martaban (Mottama)
Burmese embassy led by Shin Ditha Pamauk leaves for Beijing
King Narathihapate is assassinated
Wareru declares independence and founds Kingdom of Ramanya
Kyawswa becomes king of Pagan
Mongols evacuate Tagaung, retreat to Yunnan
Wareru is assassinated and Hkun Law succeeds the Martaban throne
Thihathu founds Pinya Kingdom
Saw Yun's completes fortification of capital Sagaing
Binnya U raises the height of the Shwedagon Pagoda to 66 feet
Maw forces sack Sagaing
Ava conquers Shan States of Mohnyin, Mogaung, Hsipaw
Min Saw Mon founds city of Mrauk-U
Thado Minsaw successfully breaks away from Ava, founds Prome Kingdom
Ava cedes Kyaukse to Toungoo to buy its loyalty, and cedes Shwebo District to Mohnyin
Confederation of Shan States conquers Ava, and installs Thohanbwa as vassal king
Bayinnaung takes Toungoo
Bayinnaung annexes cis-Salween Shan States; abolishes animal sacrifice at Popa Hill and human sacrifice…
objets.notes: Bayinnaung annexes cis-Salween Shan States; abolishes animal sacrifice at Popa Hill and human sacrifice at Shan Hills

objets.nom: The Ayutthaya Kingdom becomes Burmese vassal following the Burmese–Siamese War (1563–64)
Burmese forces capture Vientiane, capital of Lan Xang
Repeated Burmese invasions fail to reconquer Siam
objets.notes: Repeated Burmese invasions fail to reconquer Siam. Siam regains Tenasserim coast up to Mawlamyaing

objets.nom: Fall of First Toungoo Empire after Pegu sacked by the Arakanese and Toungoo (city) forces
objets.notes: Fall of First Toungoo Empire after Pegu sacked by the Arakanese and Toungoo (city) forces. Siam captures the entire Tenasserim coast to Martaban. Arakanese capture delta ports; appoint Portuguese mercenary de Brito governor of Syriam

objets.nom: Min Khamaung recovers Sandwip
objets.notes: Min Khamaung recovers Sandwip. Beginning of Arakanese raids on Dakha

objets.nom: Alaungpaya founds the Konbaung dynasty
Burmese armies capture Laotian states of Luang Prabang and Vientiane
Burmese armies sack Ayutthaya; end of Ayutthaya Kingdom
Siamese invasion of Kengtung fails (to 1804)
Burmese invasion of Junkceylon (Phuket) fails (to 1812)
Mindon moves capital to newly founded city of Mandalay
Burma Independence Army formed with Japanese help
Aung San and most of his cabinet assassinated
objets.notes: Aung San and most of his cabinet assassinated. U Nu and his AFPFL party prepare to take power from the British by finishing Burma's first constitution

objets.nom: Panglong Agreement signed by Shan, Kachin, Chin and Burman leaders to gain independence from the British
Burma gains independence from the United Kingdom with U Nu as Prime Minister
Burmese Army repels Nationalist Chinese invasion of Shan State (to 1961)
U Thant becomes 3rd Secretary-General of the United Nations
objets.notes: U Thant becomes 3rd Secretary-General of the United Nations. Yangon hosts Second Southeast Asian Peninsular Games

objets.nom: Democratically elected government of U Nu is overthrown by Ne Win, who abolishes the federal system and…
objets.notes: Democratically elected government of U Nu is overthrown by Ne Win, who abolishes the federal system and inaugurates "the Burmese Way to Socialism" – nationalising the economy, forming a single-party state with the BSPP as the sole political party, and banning independent newspapers

objets.nom: Ne Win proclaims a new constitution
objets.notes: Ne Win proclaims a new constitution. Chin Special Division becomes Chin State; Mon State is created out of Tenasserim Division. Government guns down student protesters following U Thant's death

objets.nom: Nationwide uprising brings down Ne Win's government
objets.notes: Nationwide uprising brings down Ne Win's government. Military crushes protests, forms a ruling junta, promises elections

objets.nom: National League for Democracy wins 82% of the seats in the general election
objets.notes: National League for Democracy wins 82% of the seats in the general election. Junta refuses to hand over power, jails NLD leader Aung San Suu Kyi

objets.nom: 2008 Constitution reserves 25% of the seats in a bicameral Hluttaw to the military.
Cyclone Nargis kills nearly 140,000 people and devastates the Irrawaddy delta
The 2010 general election gives the victory to military-backed USDP
An earthquake occurs in Shan State
Thein Sein becomes President of Burma
Economic sanctions imposed by the European Union and the United States are eased
National League for Democracy wins in by-elections
The 2015 general election gives the victory to NLD
Aung San Suu Kyi becomes State Counsellor of Myanmar (de facto prime minister)
Htin Kyaw becomes President of Myanmar
The region was invaded and occupied by Rajendra Chola of the Chola empire in India, although there has…
objets.notes: The region was invaded and occupied by Rajendra Chola of the Chola empire in India, although there has been no record of them visiting the island itself.

objets.nom: According to the Malay Annals, the Kingdom of Singapura was founded by Sang Nila Utama, a prince of Srivijaya
objets.notes: According to the Malay Annals, the Kingdom of Singapura was founded by Sang Nila Utama, a prince of Srivijaya. The kingdom existed till 1398.

objets.nom: The Mongol court sends a mission to obtain elephants from Long Ya Men (or Dragon's Tooth Strait),…
objets.notes: The Mongol court sends a mission to obtain elephants from Long Ya Men (or Dragon's Tooth Strait), believed to be Keppel Harbour.

objets.nom: The Chinese traveller Wang Dayuan visits Temasek and records an attack by Siam, recording it down…
objets.notes: The Chinese traveller Wang Dayuan visits Temasek and records an attack by Siam, recording it down alongside Long Ya Men and Ban Zu.

objets.nom: Parameswara, the last Srivijayan prince, flees from Temasek.
Temasek becomes part of the Sultanate of Malacca established by Parameswara.
Malacca fell and was sacked by Afonso de Albuquerque of Portuguese Empire
objets.notes: Malacca fell and was sacked by Afonso de Albuquerque of Portuguese Empire. See Portuguese Malacca.

objets.nom: Sir Stamford Raffles arrives in Singapore with William Farquhar to establish a trading post for the…
objets.notes: Sir Stamford Raffles arrives in Singapore with William Farquhar to establish a trading post for the British East India Company.

objets.nom: The treaty is signed between Sultan Hussein of Johor, Temenggong Abdul Rahman and Sir Stamford Raffles.
Dr John Crawfurd appointed as second Resident of the settlement.
Raffles Institution is founded by Sir Stamford Raffles.
Robert Fullerton was installed as the first Governor of the Straits Settlements.
Singapore becomes part of the British colony of Straits Settlements under the rule of the East India…
objets.notes: Singapore becomes part of the British colony of Straits Settlements under the rule of the East India Company, together with Malacca and Penang.

objets.nom: Robert Ibbetson was appointed as the second Governor of the Straits Settlements.
Kenneth Murchison was appointed as the third Governor of the Straits Settlements.
Sir Samuel George Bonham was appointed as the fourth Governor of the Straits Settlements.
St
objets.notes: St. Margaret's Girls School was founded by Maria Tarn Dyer, the first and oldest all-girls school in Singapore.

objets.nom: Thomas Dunman, the first full-time police chief of Singapore, improves the police force as well as the…
objets.notes: Thomas Dunman, the first full-time police chief of Singapore, improves the police force as well as the pay and working hours of policemen.

objets.nom: William John Butterworth was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements.
Raffles Girls' School was established at Bras Basah Road.
Edmund Augustus Blundell was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements upon the retirement of…
objets.notes: Edmund Augustus Blundell was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements upon the retirement of William John Butterworth.

objets.nom: Major General Sir Orfeur Cavenagh was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements.
Major General Sir Harry St
objets.notes: Major General Sir Harry St. George Ord was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements.

objets.nom: Straits Settlements become a crown colony of British Empire.
Sir Andrew Clarke was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements upon the retirement of Sir Harry St
objets.notes: Sir Andrew Clarke was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements upon the retirement of Sir Harry St. George Ord.

objets.nom: Sir William Jervois was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements.
Major General Edward Archibald Harbord Anson was appointed as the Acting Governor of the Straits Settlements.
Sir William Cleaver Francis Robinson was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements.
The Chinese Protectorate is set up, and William Pickering was the first Protector appointed.
Major General Edward Archibald Harbord Anson was appointed as the Acting Governor of the Straits Settlements.
Sir Frederick Weld was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements.
Gan Eng Seng School was established at Telok Ayer Street.
Anglo-Chinese School was established at Amoy Street.
Sir Cecil Clementi Smith was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements.
Henry Ridley becomes the first scientific director of the Singapore Botanic Gardens.
William Edward Maxwell was appointed as the Acting Governor of the Straits Settlements.
Sir Charles Bullen Hugh Mitchell was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements.
James Alexander Swettenham was appointed as the Acting Governor of the Straits Settlements.
Singapore Chinese Girls' School was established at 52 Hill Street.
Sir Frank Swettenham was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements.
Sir John Anderson was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements.
The Nanyang branch of Tongmenghui was set up in Singapore.
Anderson Bridge was official opened by Governor Sir John Anderson.
Sir Arthur Young was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements.
The Singapore Mutiny occurred as British Muslim Indian sepoys rose up against the British.
Nanyang Girls' High School was established by Tan Chor Nam and Teo Eng Hock, partially due to Dr Sun Yat…
objets.notes: Nanyang Girls' High School was established by Tan Chor Nam and Teo Eng Hock, partially due to Dr Sun Yat Sen's belief in education for girls, in Dhoby Ghaut.

objets.nom: The Chinese High School established by Tan Kah Kee at 15 Niven Road.
Sir Laurence Guillemard was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements.
Sir Hugh Clifford was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements.
Singapore Police Academy was established at Mount Pleasant Road.
Sir Cecil Clementi was appointed as the Governor of the Straits Settlements.
Singapore completes the main British naval base, which is the largest drydock and third largest floating…
objets.notes: Singapore completes the main British naval base, which is the largest drydock and third largest floating dock in the world.

objets.nom: In an extensive three-pronged attack, Japan opens hostilities with the countries that opposed the Axis…
objets.notes: In an extensive three-pronged attack, Japan opens hostilities with the countries that opposed the Axis powers and their colonies. First air raid on Singapore at 4:15 am. The Imperial Japanese Army invades Malaya.

objets.nom: The University of Malaya is formed following the merger of Raffles College and King Edward Medical College.
3rd general elections (limited self-government) held
objets.notes: 3rd general elections (limited self-government) held. People's Action Party wins 43 of 51 seats and Lee Kuan Yew became the first Prime Minister.

objets.nom: Tunku Abdul Rahman, the Prime Minister of Malaya, proposes a merger between Singapore, Malaya, Sabah and…
objets.notes: Tunku Abdul Rahman, the Prime Minister of Malaya, proposes a merger between Singapore, Malaya, Sabah and Sarawak.

objets.nom: Encik Yusof bin Ishak becomes the Yang di-Pertuan Negara of Singapura.
The Malaysia Agreement is signed between leaders of Malaya, Singapore, Sabah and Sarawak.
The PAP wins the 1963 State Elections, defeating the Barisan Sosialis and UMNO.
Encik Yusof bin Ishak, first President of Singapore died while in office.
The first Chingay parade is held in Singapore.
Laju incident
objets.notes: Japanese Red Army bombs petroleum tanks at Pulau Bukom and hijacks a ferry boat.

objets.nom: The parliament passes the Maintenance of Parents law, a private member's bill introduced by Nominated…
objets.notes: The parliament passes the Maintenance of Parents law, a private member's bill introduced by Nominated Member of Parliament Woon Cheong Ming Walter.

objets.nom: PAP led by Goh Chok Tong wins a total of 81 out of 83 seats in the 1997 general election.
Silkair Flight 185 crashes into Musi River near Palembang, Sumatra, killing all 104 people on board.
A pipeline feeding gas to Singapore from Indonesia's Natuna field in South China Sea opens.
In the aftermath of 7 July 2005 – London bombings, Transport Minister Yeo Cheow Tong announces plan to…
objets.notes: In the aftermath of 7 July 2005 – London bombings, Transport Minister Yeo Cheow Tong announces plan to set up a new Police MRT Unit to enhance the security of Singapore's public transport. (CNA)

objets.nom: S R Nathan returns for his second term as President, following a walkover in the 2005 Singapore…
objets.notes: S R Nathan returns for his second term as President, following a walkover in the 2005 Singapore presidential election.

objets.nom: The PAP, led by Lee Hsien Loong, wins 82 of 84 seats in the General Election.
Singaporeans, for the first time since the establishment of Presidential Election, will be voting for…
objets.notes: Singaporeans, for the first time since the establishment of Presidential Election, will be voting for the next President after the 6th President of Singapore – SR Nathan stepped down on 31 August 2011. The candidates involves in this election includes – Dr Tan Keng Yam Tony, Mr Tan Jee Say, Mr Tan Kin Lian and Dr. Tan Cheng Bock.

objets.nom: More than 3000 Singaporeans gathered at the Speakers' Corner, Singapore at Hong Lim Park for a…
objets.notes: More than 3000 Singaporeans gathered at the Speakers' Corner, Singapore at Hong Lim Park for a non-partisan protest against the government's Population White Paper which projected a possible 6.9 million people in Singapore by 2030.

objets.nom: Minister of Transport S. Iswaran and tycoon Ong Beng Seng is arrested as part of a CPIB probe.
The CPIB of Singapore investigates Ministers K. Shanmugam and Vivian Balakrishnan after accusations…
objets.notes: The CPIB of Singapore investigates Ministers K. Shanmugam and Vivian Balakrishnan after accusations regarding their Ridout Road state-owned bungalows rentals.

objets.nom: An accident involving a Dutch-flagged dredger and a stationary Singapore-flagged bunker vessel occurs at…
objets.notes: An accident involving a Dutch-flagged dredger and a stationary Singapore-flagged bunker vessel occurs at the Pasir Panjang terminal, causing an oil spill that forces the closure of three beaches in Sentosa Island.

objets.nom: Former Raffles Institution headmaster and historian Eugene Wijeysingha, died at age 90.
Lawrence Wong is sworn in as the fourth Prime Minister of Singapore, succeeding Lee Hsien Loong.
Lee Hsien Loong announces his resignation as the 3rd Prime Minister of Singapore effective on 15 May…
objets.notes: Lee Hsien Loong announces his resignation as the 3rd Prime Minister of Singapore effective on 15 May 2024. Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Lawrence Wong will assume the position of the 4th Prime Minister of Singapore.

objets.nom: S. Iswaran resigns as Minister for Transport, Member of Parliament for West Coast GRC, and from People's…
objets.notes: S. Iswaran resigns as Minister for Transport, Member of Parliament for West Coast GRC, and from People's Action Party after being charged with 27 counts relating to bribery and corruption by the CPIB. Chee Hong Tat succeeds Iswaran as Transport Minister.

objets.nom: Singapore Airlines Flight 321, flying from London to Singapore makes an emergency landing at Bangkok's…
objets.notes: Singapore Airlines Flight 321, flying from London to Singapore makes an emergency landing at Bangkok's Suvarnabhumi Airport after experiencing severe air turbulence over the Bay of Bengal, resulting in one death and at least 71 injured.

objets.nom: Swimmer Joseph Schooling, who won Singapore's first ever Olympic gold medal, retires from swimming at 28.
The Ban Chiang culture flourishes
objets.notes: The Ban Chiang culture flourishes. This Bronze Age pre-Thai civilization was discovered in an archeological site situated in the Khorat plateau of Udon Thani province in the northeast of Thailand. The oldest bronze artefacts and grave date to 2100 BCE.

objets.nom: The semi-legendary Singhanavati Kingdom is founded along the Kok River in the Chiang Rai basin (Northern…
objets.notes: The semi-legendary Singhanavati Kingdom is founded along the Kok River in the Chiang Rai basin (Northern Thailand). It existed from circa 691 BCE to 638 CE.

objets.nom: Chinese T’ai migration recorded
objets.notes: Chinese T’ai migration recorded. Beginning of the migration of Tai people south towards Mainland Southeast Asia. These migrants speak Tai languages.

objets.nom: Buddhism reaches places in the region such as Nakhon Pathom from India as propagated by the Mauryan…
objets.notes: Buddhism reaches places in the region such as Nakhon Pathom from India as propagated by the Mauryan Emperor Ashoka. He sent monks during his reign to popularize Theravada Buddhism (268-232 BC). This is evident by excavated ruins in the city Nakhon Pathom in Thailand.

objets.nom: Influence of the Mon and Khmer kingdoms spreads into the region (present-day Thailand)
objets.notes: Influence of the Mon and Khmer kingdoms spreads into the region (present-day Thailand). Most important are the Funan Kingdom (50 CE–627), the Chenla Kingdom (550–802), Haripuñjaya (629–1281), the Lavo Kingdom (648–1388), and Dvaravati in Central Thailand (6th–11th century).

objets.nom: Hindu and Buddhist Dvaravati culture of the ethnic Mon people predominates in the region.
The Tai peoples migrate south from China into northern Thailand, Burma and Laos
objets.notes: The Tai peoples migrate south from China into northern Thailand, Burma and Laos. According to recent theories the Tai people migrated between the 8th and 10th centuries from Guangxi southwestward to Siam. The already present peoples of Thailand migrated to the southern side, while the ones from China went to north Thailand, Laos, and Burma.

objets.nom: The Khmer Empire is founded by prince Jayavarman II at Angkor in 802. Thailand is mostly under the…
objets.notes: The Khmer Empire is founded by prince Jayavarman II at Angkor in 802. Thailand is mostly under the influence of the Mon Kingdoms and the Khmer between 400 CE until 800 CE.

objets.nom: A skeleton of a woman of circa 13,640 years ago and another woman circa 12,100 years ago were excavated…
objets.notes: A skeleton of a woman of circa 13,640 years ago and another woman circa 12,100 years ago were excavated at Tham Lod rockshelter in Pang Ma Pa district, Mae Hong Son province.

objets.nom: The Last Glacial Maximum was the coldest period of the Last Glacial Period between 26,000 and 20,000 years ago
objets.notes: The Last Glacial Maximum was the coldest period of the Last Glacial Period between 26,000 and 20,000 years ago. The 3–4 km thick ice sheets in the Northern hemisphere lowered the sea level by about 120 meters. The climate was -6 Celsius colder than present in Thailand (between 12 and 32 °C). There were no ice sheets. There was no seawater in the…

objets.nom: The Youngest Toba eruption occurred circa 74,000 years ago
objets.notes: The Youngest Toba eruption occurred circa 74,000 years ago. The Toba Supervolcano in North Sumatra produced 439–631 million tons of sulfuric acid. The air-fall of this eruption blanketed Thailand and Mainland Southeast Asia with a layer of 5–10 cm ash.

objets.nom: The Homo Erectus fossil called Lampang man is dated 500,000 BCE. It was discovered in Hat Pudai Village,…
objets.notes: The Homo Erectus fossil called Lampang man is dated 500,000 BCE. It was discovered in Hat Pudai Village, Na Seng in Ko Kha district, Lampang, in 1999. Research shows that modern Thais and other Homo Sapiens in Southeast Asia are not related to Lampang man.

objets.nom: An earthquake causes Chiang Saen Lake to submerge the capital city of Singhanavati in Yonok Nahaphan…
objets.notes: An earthquake causes Chiang Saen Lake to submerge the capital city of Singhanavati in Yonok Nahaphan (Chiang Saen District, Chiang Rai). The capital is moved to Vieng Prueksa (Fang District). There is a submerged town "Wiang Nong Lom" (เวียงหนองหล่ม, "drowned town") in a swamp south of the lake.

objets.nom: The Singhanavati Kingdom evolves into the Northern Thai Ngoenyang Kingdom during the fourteen chiefdoms…
objets.notes: The Singhanavati Kingdom evolves into the Northern Thai Ngoenyang Kingdom during the fourteen chiefdoms era (545–638).

objets.nom: The first king of the Siamese dynasty is called Phraborom Suriyathep Northai Suwannabophit…
objets.notes: The first king of the Siamese dynasty is called Phraborom Suriyathep Northai Suwannabophit (พระบรมสุริยเทพนรไทยสุวรรณบพิตร) according to the record of Simon de la Loubère. His court is in Chaiburi Mahanakhon (Thai: ไชยบุรีมหานคร). Loubère did not know the exact location. His reign begins in 757 CE (1300 Buddhist Era).

objets.nom: The Mons from Burma settle in Central Thailand
objets.notes: The Mons from Burma settle in Central Thailand. A monarchy with a unified Thai kingdom called Ayutthaya is established by King Uthong (Ramathibodi I). A series of kings follow who rule what becomes known as Siam.

objets.nom: Sukhothai is taken by the Thais from the Khmers in 1220 and made their capital.
The Thai-speaking Sukhothai kingdom expands its rule further south to dominate much of modern-day…
objets.notes: The Thai-speaking Sukhothai kingdom expands its rule further south to dominate much of modern-day Thailand, before being eclipsed by a rival Thai kingdom of Ayutthaya.

objets.nom: The Mongol Armies led by Kublai Khan conquer the Kingdom of Nanzhao in southern China in 1253. This…
objets.notes: The Mongol Armies led by Kublai Khan conquer the Kingdom of Nanzhao in southern China in 1253. This causes a mass migration including Tai warriors who consolidate the independent Tai states. Ayutthaya is reinforced by the Tai migrants which ensures Tai supremacy over the Khmer in the Central Plain.

objets.nom: Siamese begin to occupy the northern Malay Peninsula
objets.notes: Siamese begin to occupy the northern Malay Peninsula. Negara Sri Dharmaraja and Patani, become Siamese vassals.

objets.nom: The reign of King Ramkhamhaeng is marked by major advancements and the inception of a unified Thai identity
objets.notes: The reign of King Ramkhamhaeng is marked by major advancements and the inception of a unified Thai identity. This begins with the creation and utilization of the Thai script in 1283 and significant flourishing of the arts. Ram Khamhaeng made major contributions to Thai governance, culture and religion. The people in the Central Plain call…

objets.nom: King Ramkhamhaeng of Sukhothai pursues good relations with Kublai Khan and negotiates a treaty of amity…
objets.notes: King Ramkhamhaeng of Sukhothai pursues good relations with Kublai Khan and negotiates a treaty of amity with the Yuan dynasty in 1282.Ramkhamhaeng makes a personal visit to China to see Kublai Khan shortly before his death in 1294. The Mongols threaten to destroy Burma and Vietnam, but Sukhothai could prosper at their expense. The Mongols have no…

objets.nom: The Lan Na kingdom is founded at Chiang Mai in 1292. The thriving Lan Na covers a large portion of…
objets.notes: The Lan Na kingdom is founded at Chiang Mai in 1292. The thriving Lan Na covers a large portion of northern Thailand and Laos which is controlled by King Mangrai.

objets.nom: The Thai ruler Mangrai from Mueang Ngoenyang unites several principalities and conquers the Mon Kingdom…
objets.notes: The Thai ruler Mangrai from Mueang Ngoenyang unites several principalities and conquers the Mon Kingdom Haripunjaya in 1292. This is achieved with Tai war parties of the Northern Thai people.

objets.nom: Prince Ramesuan of Ayutthaya conquers Chiang Mai in the north and Angkor the former capital of the Khmer…
objets.notes: Prince Ramesuan of Ayutthaya conquers Chiang Mai in the north and Angkor the former capital of the Khmer Empire.

objets.nom: The Little Ice Age causes modest cooling in the Northern Hemisphere
objets.notes: The Little Ice Age causes modest cooling in the Northern Hemisphere. The climate impact is negligible in Thailand and Southeast Asia.

objets.nom: A Khmer rebellion against the Suphannaphum-Mon dynasty of Ayutthaya results in a 7-month siege and the…
objets.notes: A Khmer rebellion against the Suphannaphum-Mon dynasty of Ayutthaya results in a 7-month siege and the Fall of Angkor. This marks the end of the Angkorian period.

objets.nom: King Borommarachathirat II dies in 1448. Prince Ramesuan is crowned King Borommatrailokkanat of…
objets.notes: King Borommarachathirat II dies in 1448. Prince Ramesuan is crowned King Borommatrailokkanat of Ayutthaya, making a personal union between Sukhothai and Ayutthaya.

objets.nom: The Burmese–Siamese War (1547–1549) (aka the Shwehti war) was the first war fought between the Toungoo…
objets.notes: The Burmese–Siamese War (1547–1549) (aka the Shwehti war) was the first war fought between the Toungoo dynasty of Burma and the Ayutthaya Kingdom of Siam. Notable for the introduction of early modern warfare to the region and the Siamese Queen Suriyothai died in battle on her elephant. The Burmese–Siamese wars continued until the mid 19th century.

objets.nom: Burmese–Siamese War (1563–1564), (aka the War over the White Elephants), the 2nd Siege of Ayutthaya
objets.notes: Burmese–Siamese War (1563–1564), (aka the War over the White Elephants), the 2nd Siege of Ayutthaya. After an extensive siege of the city of Ayutthaya, the Ayutthaya Kingdom becomes a vassal of the Toungoo dynasty for the first time. This vassal status lasts until 1568.

objets.nom: Naresuan becomes the 18th king of Ayutthaya in 1590. He abolishes a period of Burmese suzerainty
objets.notes: Naresuan becomes the 18th king of Ayutthaya in 1590. He abolishes a period of Burmese suzerainty. Ayuttaya expands rapidly to the detriment of the Burmese and Khmer realms. He also conquers Cambodia and parts of southern Burma.

objets.nom: Burmese–Siamese War (1593–1600) (aka the Naresuan War), The first Siamese invasion of Burma
objets.notes: Burmese–Siamese War (1593–1600) (aka the Naresuan War), The first Siamese invasion of Burma. Siam conquers the Tenasserim coastal region to Martaban. Lan Na (Chiang Mai) becomes a vassal of Siam, c. 1602.

objets.nom: Burmese–Siamese War (1609–1622), Wars of Nyaungyan restoration
objets.notes: Burmese–Siamese War (1609–1622), Wars of Nyaungyan restoration. Burma regains Martaban and Tavoy (1613), and Lan Na (1614).

objets.nom: The first Siamese embassy to France composed of two Siamese ambassadors and Father Bénigne Vachet who…
objets.notes: The first Siamese embassy to France composed of two Siamese ambassadors and Father Bénigne Vachet who left Siam for France on 5 January 1684.

objets.nom: The second Siamese embassy to France (1686) from Siam (Ayutthaya Kingdom)
objets.notes: The second Siamese embassy to France (1686) from Siam (Ayutthaya Kingdom). King Narai sent the embassy led by ambassador Kosa Pan.

objets.nom: The travel record Du royaume de Siam by French diplomat Simon de la Loubère is published
objets.notes: The travel record Du royaume de Siam by French diplomat Simon de la Loubère is published. This is one of the few remaining records of the history and society of the Ayutthaya Kingdom in 1687. Most Thai chronicles were lost during the Burmese sacking of Ayutthaya in 1767.

objets.nom: Burmese–Siamese War (1759–1760) (aka the Alaungpaya's War) the Fifth Siege of Ayutthaya
objets.notes: Burmese–Siamese War (1759–1760) (aka the Alaungpaya's War) the Fifth Siege of Ayutthaya. Burma conquers the Tenasserim coastal region down to the Tavoy–Mergui frontier. Burma besieges the Ayutthaya, but returns home when their King is injured and becomes ill.

objets.nom: Burmese–Siamese War (1765–1767) (aka the War of the second fall of Ayutthaya), Burma invades Siam and…
objets.notes: Burmese–Siamese War (1765–1767) (aka the War of the second fall of Ayutthaya), Burma invades Siam and besieges Ayutthaya. The invading Burmese forces sack the capital Ayutthaya city prior to being expunged by General Taksin. The Ayuthaya Kingdom collapses. Precious Thai historical records about the history of Siam were burned by the Burmese. The…

objets.nom: Taksin's reunification of Siam (1767–1771)
objets.notes: Taksin's reunification of Siam (1767–1771). The fall of Ayuthaya left Siam divided into 5 separate states—Phimai, Phitsanulok, Sawangburi, Nakhon Si Thammarat, and Thonburi. The state of Thonburi, led by Taksin, prevailed, subjugating its rivals to successfully reunify Siam under the Thonburi Kingdom (1767–1782) by 1770/71. The capital is moved…

objets.nom: Siamese conquest of Lan Na (1774–1775)
objets.notes: Siamese conquest of Lan Na (1774–1775). The Lan Na kingdom which was under Burmese rule for 2 centuries, is conquered by the Siamese armies of King Taksin of Thonburi. The Siamese take Burmese-held Chiang Mai in January 1775.

objets.nom: Bangkaeo Campaign (aka the Battle of Bangkaeo)
objets.notes: Bangkaeo Campaign (aka the Battle of Bangkaeo). The Burmese commander Maha Thiha Thura sent an expeditionary force to invade Western Siam through the Three Pagodas Pass. The Burmese force in Bangkaeo was encircled and defeated via starvation by the armies of Taksin.

objets.nom: Burmese–Siamese War (1775–1776) (aka the Athi Wungyi's War)
objets.notes: Burmese–Siamese War (1775–1776) (aka the Athi Wungyi's War). Lan Na declares independence in 1775 with support of King Taksin. Burma invades Lan Na and Siam. After the death of King Hsinbyushin, the Burmese withdraw from Siam. The Siamese claim Lan Na which ends over 2 centuries of Burmese rule in 1776.

objets.nom: The city Chiang Mai is captured and the Burmese are expelled
objets.notes: The city Chiang Mai is captured and the Burmese are expelled. The Emerald Buddha is brought from Vientiane in Laos, to Thonburi in Bangkok.

objets.nom: Burmese–Siamese War (1785–1786) (aka the Nine Armies' Wars)
objets.notes: Burmese–Siamese War (1785–1786) (aka the Nine Armies' Wars). The first war between the Konbaung dynasty of Burma and the Siamese Rattanakosin Kingdom of the Chakri dynasty. The Burmese invaded with 9 armies consisting of 144,000 soldiers via 5 directions and were soundly defeated.

objets.nom: Tha Din Daeng campaign (aka the Tha Din Daeng War)
objets.notes: Tha Din Daeng campaign (aka the Tha Din Daeng War). A short conflict, occurring in 1786 in Tha Din Daeng, now Kanchanaburi province in western Thailand. The Rattanakosin forces of Phraphutthayotfa Chulalok and Maha Sura Singhanat destroy the Burmese belligerents of King Bodawpaya of the Konbaung Dynasty.

objets.nom: Tavoy campaign (1788)
objets.notes: Tavoy campaign (1788). The Kingdom of Siam fails to reclaim the town of Tavoy and the Tenasserim Coast from the Burmese Konbaung dynasty.

objets.nom: Burmese–Siamese War (1797–1798)
objets.notes: Burmese–Siamese War (1797–1798). Burma invades Lan Na and besieges Chiang Mai. The city was taken, but King Kawila asks for reinforcement from Rama I, which helped them recapture the city.

objets.nom: Burmese–Siamese War (1802–1805)
objets.notes: Burmese–Siamese War (1802–1805). The Burmese forces of King Bodawpaya invade Chiang Mai in 1802. The Burmese are repelled by Prince Kawila with Siamese support. The Siamese under King Rama I retaliate and conquer the Burmese city Chiang Saen and the district in 1805.

objets.nom: The Kingdom of Chiang Mai is founded with the installation of Kawila in December 1802. This was a vassal…
objets.notes: The Kingdom of Chiang Mai is founded with the installation of Kawila in December 1802. This was a vassal state of the Rattanakosin Kingdom.

objets.nom: Burmese–Siamese War (1809–1812) (aka the Burmese Invasion of Thalang)
objets.notes: Burmese–Siamese War (1809–1812) (aka the Burmese Invasion of Thalang). The Burmese unsuccessfully attempt to capture Junk Ceylon. They are repelled by the Siamese in 1810 and 1812. The Kedah Sultanate helps Siam during the Burmese invasion of Tanjung Salang.

objets.nom: Siamese invasion of Kedah
objets.notes: Siamese invasion of Kedah. The Rattanakosin Kingdom invades the Kedah Sultanate in November 1821. It results in a Siamese victory and direct Siamese rule on Kedah.

objets.nom: First Anglo-Burmese War
objets.notes: First Anglo-Burmese War. Conflict mostly between Burma and the United Kingdom. Siam is a nominal British ally. The Royal Siamese Army supports with 20,000 troops. Siam secures the Burney Treaty in 1826.

objets.nom: Burney Treaty is signed between Siam and the United Kingdom which partitions the northern Malay states…
objets.notes: Burney Treaty is signed between Siam and the United Kingdom which partitions the northern Malay states between British Malaya and the Rattanakosin Kingdom.

objets.nom: Siamese–Vietnamese War between King Rama III and Emperor Minh Mạng
objets.notes: Siamese–Vietnamese War between King Rama III and Emperor Minh Mạng. Vietnam annexes eastern Cambodia (Tây Thành Province) in 1834.

objets.nom: The Phra Pathommachedi is completed in Nakhon Pathom
objets.notes: The Phra Pathommachedi is completed in Nakhon Pathom. Its height is 120 meters and it was the tallest stupa in the world until 1954.

objets.nom: 1893 Franco-Siamese crisis
objets.notes: 1893 Franco-Siamese crisis. French gunboats threaten Bangkok in the Paknam Incident. The French won which lead to substantial territorial concessions east of the Mekong river to the French which now forms most of Laos.

objets.nom: Sra Pathum Airfield is the first airport in Thailand, established in 1911 at the site of the Sra Pathum…
objets.notes: Sra Pathum Airfield is the first airport in Thailand, established in 1911 at the site of the Sra Pathum Racecourse in Bangkok.

objets.nom: The Siamese Revolution is a bloodless coup d’état against the absolute monarchy of King Prajadhipok
objets.notes: The Siamese Revolution is a bloodless coup d’état against the absolute monarchy of King Prajadhipok. It ends centuries of absolute royal rule. A Constitutional monarchy is officially established and democracy with parliamentary government.

objets.nom: The first two submarines of the Royal Siamese Navy (Matchanu-class) were completed and delivered on 4…
objets.notes: The first two submarines of the Royal Siamese Navy (Matchanu-class) were completed and delivered on 4 September 1937. These were built by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries.

objets.nom: Japan uses its influence with Vichy France to obtain concessions for Thailand in May 1941. Thailand…
objets.notes: Japan uses its influence with Vichy France to obtain concessions for Thailand in May 1941. Thailand annexes the territories Lan Chang Province, Nakhon Champassak Province, Phra Tabong Province, and Phibunsongkhram Province from Laos and Cambodia.

objets.nom: Japanese invasion of Thailand on 8 December 1941 during World War II. After negotiations Thailand lets…
objets.notes: Japanese invasion of Thailand on 8 December 1941 during World War II. After negotiations Thailand lets Japanese advance towards the British-controlled Malay Peninsula, Singapore and Burma. Thailand deploys troops to fight on the Japanese side against Allied forces and became a member of the Axis Powers.

objets.nom: Thai envoy Wan Waithayakon attends the Greater East Asia Conference in Tokyo from 5 to 6 November 1943.
Thailand annexes Saharat Thai Doem (Burma), and Sirat Malai (Malaysia), including Saiburi (Kedah State).
"Lèse-majesté" laws against insulting the king, dating back to the days of absolute monarchy, are…
objets.notes: "Lèse-majesté" laws against insulting the king, dating back to the days of absolute monarchy, are carried over into a new Criminal Code.

objets.nom: The Association of Southeast Asia (ASA) is formed on 31 July 1961 and consisting of Thailand, the…
objets.notes: The Association of Southeast Asia (ASA) is formed on 31 July 1961 and consisting of Thailand, the Philippines, and Malaya.

objets.nom: United States sends troops to Thailand during the Vietnam War
objets.notes: United States sends troops to Thailand during the Vietnam War. Thailand permits the United States to use bases there. Thai troops fight in South Vietnam.

objets.nom: ASEAN is created on 8 August 1967. Thailand is a founding member with Indonesia, Malaysia, the…
objets.notes: ASEAN is created on 8 August 1967. Thailand is a founding member with Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Singapore. This is the successor of ASA.

objets.nom: The 4th South East Asian Games is hosted in Bangkok, Thailand on 9–16 December 1967.
1970s peasant revolts in Thailand
objets.notes: 1970s peasant revolts in Thailand. Prime Minister Thanom Kittikachorn ignores their pleas to reduce their debt and ensure fair rice prices. The farmer representatives form the Farmers Federation of Thailand (FFT). The Land Rent Control Act (LRCA) is finally enacted in December 1974.

objets.nom: 18th South East Asian Games is hosted in Chiang Mai, Thailand on 9–17 December 1995.
Banharn government is accused of corruption and resigns
objets.notes: Banharn government is accused of corruption and resigns. Chavalit Yongchaiyudh of the New Aspiration Party wins the elections.

objets.nom: The 1997 Asian financial crisis: The Thai Baht currency falls sharply against the dollar, leading to…
objets.notes: The 1997 Asian financial crisis: The Thai Baht currency falls sharply against the dollar, leading to bankruptcies and unemployment. The IMF steps in. Chuan Leekpai becomes prime minister.

objets.nom: The HTMS Chakri Naruebet is the first aircraft carrier of Thailand
objets.notes: The HTMS Chakri Naruebet is the first aircraft carrier of Thailand. It was commissioned into the Royal Thai Navy on 27 March 1997.

objets.nom: The Rama III Bridge is completed
objets.notes: The Rama III Bridge is completed. It crosses the Chao Phraya River in Bangkok. It is the longest bridge in Thailand with a length of 2,170 m (7,120 ft).

objets.nom: Senators are democratically elected for the Senate for the first time
objets.notes: Senators are democratically elected for the Senate for the first time. The populist Thai Rak Thai Party founded by Thaksin Shinawatra, won the national polls for the House of Representatives. Billionaire businessman Thaksin Shinawatra is elected prime minister and forms a coalition government. Within a few years, Thailand is riven by rival…

objets.nom: Muslim nationalists step up terror operations in Yala, Pattani and Narathiwat provinces (South Thailand…
objets.notes: Muslim nationalists step up terror operations in Yala, Pattani and Narathiwat provinces (South Thailand insurgency).

objets.nom: 24th South East Asian Games is hosted in Nakhon Ratchasima, Thailand on 6–15 December 2007.
2011 Thailand floods are caused by the landfall of Tropical Storm Nock-ten
objets.notes: 2011 Thailand floods are caused by the landfall of Tropical Storm Nock-ten. The impact lasts for 175 days between 25 July 2011 – 16 January 2012. There are 815 deaths and property damage in 65 of Thailand's 77 provinces. The estimated damage costs is 1.425 trillion baht (US$46.5 billion).

objets.nom: The King Power Mahanakhon is recognized as the tallest building in Thailand (314 m) by the CTBUH on 4…
objets.notes: The King Power Mahanakhon is recognized as the tallest building in Thailand (314 m) by the CTBUH on 4 May 2016 .

objets.nom: Same-sex marriage is legalized by the House of Representatives, effective 23 January 2025. Thailand is…
objets.notes: Same-sex marriage is legalized by the House of Representatives, effective 23 January 2025. Thailand is the first country in Southeast Asia and the 38th in the world to legalize it.

objets.nom: Since at least the 3rd century, the indigenous peoples were in contact with other Southeast Asian and…
objets.notes: Since at least the 3rd century, the indigenous peoples were in contact with other Southeast Asian and East Asian nations. Fragmented ethnic groups established numerous city-states formed by the assimilation of several small political units known as barangay each headed by a Datu or headman (still in use among non-Hispanic Filipino ethnic groups)…

objets.nom: The Birth of Kawi script, this Abugida are become widely used in the Maritime Southeast Asia, the word…
objets.notes: The Birth of Kawi script, this Abugida are become widely used in the Maritime Southeast Asia, the word Kawi or Kawikaan means "Poetry" in Sanskrit.

objets.nom: The earliest date suggested for direct Chinese contact with the Philippines was 982. At the time,…
objets.notes: The earliest date suggested for direct Chinese contact with the Philippines was 982. At the time, merchants from "Ma-i" (now thought to be either in Bulalacao, Mindoro or Bay, Laguna on the shores of Laguna de Bay).

objets.nom: Buddhism and Hinduism along with the Animism became the religion of the most of Philippine archipelago…
objets.notes: Buddhism and Hinduism along with the Animism became the religion of the most of Philippine archipelago by the influence of its neighbors. Around the feet of Mt. Kamhatik near Mulanay town in Quezon Province once stood a 280-hectare ancient village where the archeologists found a 1000-year-old limestone coffins on a jungle-covered mountain top from…

objets.nom: At the time, the trade in large native Ruson-tsukuri (literally Luzon made in Japanese: 呂宋製 or 呂宋つくり)…
objets.notes: At the time, the trade in large native Ruson-tsukuri (literally Luzon made in Japanese: 呂宋製 or 呂宋つくり) clay jars used for storing green tea and rice wine with Japan flourished in the 12th century, and local Tagalog, Kapampangan and Pangasinense potters had marked each jar with Baybayin letters denoting the particular urn used and the kiln the jars…

objets.nom: The process of Kabayan mummification had begun in Ibaloi Benguet which is also called Fire mummies.
The Buddhist Ma-i was flourishing in the island of Mindoro
objets.notes: The Buddhist Ma-i was flourishing in the island of Mindoro. Zhao Rukuo, a superintendent of maritime trade in Fukien province wrote the book entitled Zhu Fan Zhi ("Account of the Various Barbarians") in which he described trade with a country called Ma-i in the island of Mindoro in Luzon (pronounced "Ma-yi") which was a precolonial Philippine…

objets.nom: Cebu was founded after the arrival of Sri Lumay from Sumatra
objets.notes: Cebu was founded after the arrival of Sri Lumay from Sumatra. Namayan instated Lakantagkan as its sovereign. The vast domain comprised what are now Quiapo, San Miguel, Santa Mesa, Paco, Pandacan, Malate, Santa Ana in Manila, Mandaluyong, San Juan, Makati, Pasay, Pateros, and portions of Pasig.

objets.nom: The Yongle Emperor instituted a Chinese envoy on Luzon during Zheng He's voyages and appointed Ko…
objets.notes: The Yongle Emperor instituted a Chinese envoy on Luzon during Zheng He's voyages and appointed Ko Ch'a-lao to that position in 1405. China also had vassals among the leaders in the archipelago. China attained ascendancy in trade with the area in Yongle's reign.

objets.nom: Paduka Pahala reigned as the King of Lupah Sug in Sulu
objets.notes: Paduka Pahala reigned as the King of Lupah Sug in Sulu. He and his family and 300 other people of noble descent sailed to China, he was to pay tribute to the Yongle Chinese emperor, Zhu Di, who was of the Ming dynasty. While he was welcomed by the emperor upon his arrival in China, he nevertheless contracted a mysterious disease on his way home…

objets.nom: The Lucoes, or warriors from Luzon send soldiers to the Burmese Siamese wars and faced the White…
objets.notes: The Lucoes, or warriors from Luzon send soldiers to the Burmese Siamese wars and faced the White elephants of the Royal Burmese Army, at the same time also aiding the Burmese King for the conquest of the Siamese capital, Ayuthaya.

objets.nom: Rajah Salalila of Maynila married the daughter of Sultan Bolkiah of Brunei, effectively uniting the…
objets.notes: Rajah Salalila of Maynila married the daughter of Sultan Bolkiah of Brunei, effectively uniting the royal families of Maynila and Brunei.

objets.nom: Discovery of the Philippines: Portuguese Ferdinand Magellan lands on Homonhon with three small ships,…
objets.notes: Discovery of the Philippines: Portuguese Ferdinand Magellan lands on Homonhon with three small ships, named the Concepcion, Trinidad and Victoria. Magellan calls the place the Archipelago de San Lazaro since March 16 is the feast day of Saint Lazarus. He also lands on Samar island.

objets.nom: Villalobos arrives in the Philippines and names the islands of Samar and Leyte as Las Islas Filipinas in…
objets.notes: Villalobos arrives in the Philippines and names the islands of Samar and Leyte as Las Islas Filipinas in honor of the crown prince of Spain, Philip of Asturias; he also becomes the first to explore Mindanao island, naming it "Cesarea Caroli."

objets.nom: Legazpi, representing King Philip II of Spain, and Rajah Tupas of Cebu signed the Treaty of Cebu,…
objets.notes: Legazpi, representing King Philip II of Spain, and Rajah Tupas of Cebu signed the Treaty of Cebu, effectively establishing Spanish suzerainty over Cebu.

objets.nom: Philip III issues a royal cedula requesting from Governor Juan de Silva and the Real Audiencia a report…
objets.notes: Philip III issues a royal cedula requesting from Governor Juan de Silva and the Real Audiencia a report on the projected college (the present-day University of Santo Tomas in Manila).

objets.nom: Moro pirates traveled all over the country and raids many fishing villages in Manila Bay, Mariveles,…
objets.notes: Moro pirates traveled all over the country and raids many fishing villages in Manila Bay, Mariveles, Parañaque, Pasay and Malate.

objets.nom: Priests Mariano Gomez, José Apolonio Burgos, and Jacinto Zamora (together known as Gomburza) are…
objets.notes: Priests Mariano Gomez, José Apolonio Burgos, and Jacinto Zamora (together known as Gomburza) are implicated in the Cavite Mutiny and executed.

objets.nom: Filipino forces, under Emilio Aguinaldo, defeat the Spaniards in a battle in Kawit, Cavite.
Revolutionary Battle at San Juan del Monte
objets.notes: Revolutionary Battle at San Juan del Monte. Governor Ramon Blanco proclaims a state of war in Manila, Laguna, Cavite, Batangas, Pampanga, Bulacan, Tarlac and Nueva Ecija.

objets.nom: Philippine Independence from Spain is declared by Filipino revolutionaries, led by Pres
objets.notes: Philippine Independence from Spain is declared by Filipino revolutionaries, led by Pres. Aguinaldo, in Kawit, Cavite.

objets.nom: The Malolos Republic (First Republic) government, Asia's first republic, is inaugurated at Barasoain…
objets.notes: The Malolos Republic (First Republic) government, Asia's first republic, is inaugurated at Barasoain Church in Malolos, Bulacan; Emilio Aguinaldo takes his oath of office as the first president of the Philippines.

objets.nom: The foundation of Iglesia Filipina Independiente separated from Roman Catholic Church was proclaimed by…
objets.notes: The foundation of Iglesia Filipina Independiente separated from Roman Catholic Church was proclaimed by the Union Obrera Democratica with Gregorio Aglipay as the 1st Obispo Maximo

objets.nom: Establishment of the Moro Province, consisting of the districts of Jolo, Lanao, Cotabato, Davao and Zamboanga.
An Act Amending the Administrative Code (Act No
objets.notes: An Act Amending the Administrative Code (Act No. 2711) reorganizes the territories in the Philippines, consisting of: * Forty-two organized provinces: Abra, Albay, Antique, Bataan, Batanes, Batangas, Bohol, Bulacan, Cagayan, Camarines Norte, Camarines Sur, Capiz, Cavite, Cebu, Ilocos Norte, Ilocos Sur, Iloilo, Isabela, Laguna, La Union, Leyte,…

objets.nom: RCP operates its first radio station outside Manila, also first provincial station in the country, with…
objets.notes: RCP operates its first radio station outside Manila, also first provincial station in the country, with KZRC (Radio Cebu) in Cebu, experimental station originally a relay station of KZRM in Manila.

objets.nom: Pres
objets.notes: Pres. Quezon and Vice Pres. Osmeña take their oath of office for their second term in Corregidor Island, Cavite.

objets.nom: Battle of Bataan
objets.notes: Bataan, under US commander Gen. Edward King, is the last province that surrenders to the Japanese armies.

objets.nom: Battle of Leyte Gulf
objets.notes: Battle of Sibuyan Sea

objets.nom: Battle of Manila (1945)
objets.notes: The US and Filipino troops recaptured Manila.

objets.nom: Raid at Cabanatuan
objets.notes: 121 American soldiers and 800 Filipino guerrillas free 813 American Prisoners of war from the Japanese-held camp in the city of Cabanatuan in the Philippines.

objets.nom: The final official Japanese Instrument of Surrender is accepted by the Supreme Allied Commander, General…
objets.notes: The final official Japanese Instrument of Surrender is accepted by the Supreme Allied Commander, General Douglas MacArthur, and Fleet Admiral Chester W. Nimitz for the United States, and delegates from Australia, New Zealand, the United Kingdom, The Netherlands, China, and others from a Japanese delegation led by Mamoru Shigemitsu, on board the…

objets.nom: U.S. troops led by Gen
objets.notes: U.S. troops led by Gen. MacArthur land on the shores of Pangasinan via Lingayen Gulf in an attempt to liberate the country from the Japanese.

objets.nom: Republic Act No
objets.notes: Republic Act No. 4221 divided old Samar into the new provinces of Western Samar, Northern Samar, and Eastern Samar.

objets.nom: Old Mountain Province is divided into the new provinces of Benguet, Mountain Province, Kalinga-Apayao…
objets.notes: Old Mountain Province is divided into the new provinces of Benguet, Mountain Province, Kalinga-Apayao and Ifugao. (Republic Act No. 4695)

objets.nom: Old Davao is divided into the new provinces of Davao del Norte, Davao del Sur, and Davao Oriental
objets.notes: Old Davao is divided into the new provinces of Davao del Norte, Davao del Sur, and Davao Oriental. (Republic Act No. 4867)

objets.nom: Jabidah massacre
objets.notes: A group of trainees of a Muslim special forces unit, part of a controversial operation, are allegedly killed in Corregidor.

objets.nom: New People's Army (NPA) is formally organized in Tarlac by Bernabe Buscayno (Kumander Dante) of PKP as…
objets.notes: New People's Army (NPA) is formally organized in Tarlac by Bernabe Buscayno (Kumander Dante) of PKP as the military arm of the CPP, upon merger with Jose Maria Sison's army.

objets.nom: First Quarter Storm * January 26 – It begins when protesting students confronted Pres
objets.notes: First Quarter Storm * January 26 – It begins when protesting students confronted Pres. Marcos after his Presidential Address in the Old Legislative Building, Manila. * January 30 – Battle of Mendiola occurs. * February 18 & 26 – People's Congresses held in Plaza Miranda. * March 3 – People's March is organized, route is from Welcome Rotonda to…
