objets.nom: Pope Paul VI makes his first papal visit in the Philippines, but survived an assassination attempt by…
objets.notes: Pope Paul VI makes his first papal visit in the Philippines, but survived an assassination attempt by Benjamín Mendoza y Amor Flores at Manila International Airport.

objets.nom: Tadhana (1978), the first feature-length animated film in the Philippines premiered one time at the…
objets.notes: Tadhana (1978), the first feature-length animated film in the Philippines premiered one time at the local television on GMA 7, RPN 9, and IBC 13 to commemorate the anniversary of Martial Law in 1978.

objets.nom: CPP founder Jose Maria Sison and NPA founder Dante Buscayno are freed by Pres
objets.notes: CPP founder Jose Maria Sison and NPA founder Dante Buscayno are freed by Pres. Cojuangco–Aquino.

objets.nom: EDSA I Revolution ousts Pres
objets.notes: EDSA I Revolution ousts Pres. Marcos; Corazon Cojuangco–Aquino becomes President. * February 22 – Defense Minister Juan Ponce Enrile and Constabulary Chief Gen. Fidel Ramos withdraw from the Marcos administration. Crowd gather outside camps Crame and Aguinaldo. RAM joins with them as attempted coup prevented. Cardinal Jaime Sin urges the public on…

objets.nom: A coup attempt, said to be the bloodiest of the attempts against Pres
objets.notes: A coup attempt, said to be the bloodiest of the attempts against Pres. Aquino, is launched by rebel soldiers of RAM, led by Col. objets.notes: Interisland passenger ferry Doña Paz, said to be overloaded, and oil tanker MT Vector collide and sink at Tablas Strait between Marinduque and Oriental Mindoro provinces and Tablas Island; death toll later estimated to be 4,386; the deadliest maritime disaster in peacetime world history.

objets.nom: Mendiola massacre
objets.notes: Thirteen from the farmers are killed in clashes with the forces of policemen and soldiers at Mendiola Bridge in Manila during their protest rally.

objets.nom: Pro-Marcos rebel soldiers, led by Col
objets.notes: Pro-Marcos rebel soldiers, led by Col. Oscar Canlas, seize GMA Network compound, for almost 3 days, and military bases in Sangley Point, Cavite and in Pasay wherein an assault with government military forces results in the death of a mutineer and 16 injuries.

objets.nom: The Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR) is created through Executive Order No
objets.notes: The Cordillera Administrative Region (CAR) is created through Executive Order No. 220 signed by Pres. Cojuangco–Aquino, consisting of, from Region 1, the provinces of Abra, Benguet and Mountain Province, and Baguio, and from Region 2, the provinces of Kalinga-Apayao and Ifugao.

objets.nom: A coup attempt is launched by RAM under Col
objets.notes: A coup attempt is launched by RAM under Col. Honasan and Marcos loyalists under retired Gen. Jose Ma. Zumel, with Malacañang bombarded on the 1st and several military bases seized; rebels surrender on the 9th; the most serious attempt against Pres. Aquino with 99 casualties.

objets.nom: A plebiscite is held in ARMM, resulting in the ratification of RA 6734 that established the region, with…
objets.notes: A plebiscite is held in ARMM, resulting in the ratification of RA 6734 that established the region, with the inclusion of the provinces of Lanao del Sur (except Marawi City), Maguindanao, Sulu and Tawi-Tawi.

objets.nom: Davao hostage crisis
objets.notes: Felipe Pugoy and Mohammad Nasser Samparini, perpetrators of an earlier hostage-taking incident in Davao Penal Colony on April, lead the prisoners who take five people hostage in Davao Metrodiscom; ending in gunfights with the authorities resulting in the death of the hostages as well as some hostage takers.

objets.nom: Typhoons Angela (Rubing), Dan (Saling), and Elsie (Tasing) impact the country in two weeks
objets.notes: Typhoons Angela (Rubing), Dan (Saling), and Elsie (Tasing) impact the country in two weeks. * Super typhoon Angela (Rubing), causes 119 fatalities and $8 million worth of damage. * Typhoon Dan (Saling) leaves 58 dead and hundreds of thousands homeless. * Typhoon Elsie (Tasing) leaves 47 dead, $35.4 million worth of damage, and 332 thousand people…

objets.nom: Luzon earthquake
objets.notes: An earthquake with a surface wave magnitude of 7.8, whose epicenter was recorded in Nueva Ecija, hits Northern and Central Luzon, affecting Cabanatuan, Dagupan, and Baguio cities, and parts of Nueva Ecija and Pangasinan provinces, causing a death toll of an estimated 1,621 and estimated damages worth ₱15 billion; produces a 125-km long ground…

objets.nom: Pinatubo eruption
objets.notes: Series of major eruptions from the dormant Mount Pinatubo, the most explosive occurred on the 15th, and worsened by Typhoon Yunya (Diding) causing massive lahar flows, affecting densely populated areas of Zambales, Tarlac and Pampanga; killing 847 people; total damages at least ₱12 billion; the second largest volcanic eruption of the 20th century.

objets.nom: Philippine Navy sights ships and structures being built, all by the Chinese, in Mischief Reef…
objets.notes: Philippine Navy sights ships and structures being built, all by the Chinese, in Mischief Reef (Panganiban Reef) in the South China Sea off Palawan; causing Manila to file legal diplomatic actions against Beijing over continuous occupation of the Kalayaan Island Group, and further resistance between the Philippines and China.

objets.nom: The Final Peace Agreement between the Philippine Government and the Moro National Liberation Front…
objets.notes: The Final Peace Agreement between the Philippine Government and the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF), led by Nur Misuari, is signed at the Malacañan Palace; implementing the 1976 Tripoli Agreement.

objets.nom: Fall of Camp Abubakar: Camp Abubakar in Maguindanao is captured by the Armed Forces of the Philippines…
objets.notes: Fall of Camp Abubakar: Camp Abubakar in Maguindanao is captured by the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) from the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), as part of a campaign against Moro insurgency in Mindanao.

objets.nom: Rizal Day bombings
objets.notes: Series of terrorist bombings occur in Metro Manila, with 22 fatalities and more than 120 injuries.

objets.notes: Twenty-one foreigners are abducted by Abu Sayyaf extremists from Sipadan Island, Malaysia and are later brought to Jolo Island; hostage crisis lasts five months.

Estrada, regarding his supposed link to a bank account…

objets.notes: Supporters of former Pres. Estrada stage protest following his arrest, ending in a violent dispersal and riots on the 1st, killing four.

objets.nom: Lamitan Siege
objets.notes: Abu Sayyaf takes a church and a hospital in Lamitan, Basilan hostage, with captives brought from Palawan, wherein four of them are reportedly escaped, and 20 more people; terrorists escape military operation.

objets.nom: Oakwood mutiny
objets.notes: Magdalo Group, led by Army Capt. Gerardo Gambala and LtSG. Antonio Trillanes IV, takes a mutiny at Oakwood Premier apartments in Makati.

Macapagal Arroyo and Election Commissioner Virgilio Garcillano, are released by media to the public, revealing the allegations of cheating in 2004 national elections.

objets.nom: Valentine's Day bombings
objets.notes: Three explosions occur in the cities of Makati, Davao, and General Santos, resulting to, in total, 8 deaths and at least 90 injuries; Abu Sayyaf claims responsibility for the attacks.

objets.notes: Fourteen Abu Sayyaf members are convicted by the Pasig Regional Trial Court regarding the 2001 kidnapping incident in Palawan.

objets.notes: Fourteen Marine soldiers are found beheaded following an encounter between government forces and Islamic rebels Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) and, allegedly, Abu Sayyaf, in Tipo-Tipo, Basilan.

objets.nom: Sandiganbayan and the Office of the Ombudsman convicts former Pres
objets.notes: Sandiganbayan and the Office of the Ombudsman convicts former Pres. Estrada for plunder and sentences him to reclusion perpetua, but acquits him and his co-accused on other charges.

objets.nom: Maguindanao massacre
objets.notes: Fifty-eight people being part of a convoy, including clan members and 32 journalists, are killed and buried in a mass grave in Ampatuan town by an estimated 100 gunmen belonging to a victims' political rival; single deadliest attack against journalists in world history.

objets.nom: Typhoon Juan, officially as Typhoon Megi, hits northeastern Luzon at Sierra Madre, creating widespread…
objets.notes: Typhoon Juan, officially as Typhoon Megi, hits northeastern Luzon at Sierra Madre, creating widespread damage over Luzon.

objets.nom: The Framework Agreement on the Bangsamoro is signed by the Philippine Government and the Moro Islamic…
objets.notes: The Framework Agreement on the Bangsamoro is signed by the Philippine Government and the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF), aiming to end war in the southern Philippines and also for the creation of a new autonomous political entity, Bangsamoro, replacing the Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao.

objets.nom: A magnitude 7.2 earthquake, whose released energy is found equivalent to 32 Hiroshima bombs, strikes…
objets.notes: A magnitude 7.2 earthquake, whose released energy is found equivalent to 32 Hiroshima bombs, strikes Bohol province, affecting Central Visayas, with 222 people died; the country's deadliest earthquake since 1990.

objets.notes: Hidilyn Diaz wins a gold medal at the Women's 55 kg event for weightlifting in Tokyo, Japan during the 2020 Tokyo Olympics. It is the Philippines' first Olympic gold medal.

objets.notes: The French priest Pierre Pigneau de Behaine signed the Treaty of Versailles on behalf of Nguyễn Thế Tổ. The French government agreed to support the latter in taking the throne of Đại Việt in exchange for Côn Sơn Island and exclusive trading rights.

objets.notes: Qing forces invaded Đại Việt in support of the deposed emperor Lê Chiêu Thống.

objets.notes: French troops begin the battle against the Viet Minh in Dien Bien Phu.

objets.notes: The First Indochina War ends with the Vietnam People's Army in North Vietnam, the Vietnamese National Army in South Vietnam, the Kingdom of Cambodia in Cambodia, and the Kingdom of Laos in Laos, emerging victorious against the French Army.

objets.nom: 1963 South Vietnamese coup d'état
objets.notes: Arrest and assassination of Ngo Dinh Diem, the South Vietnamese President.

objets.nom: Double Seven Day scuffle
objets.notes: Secret police loyal to Ngô Đình Nhu, brother of President Ngô Đình Diệm, attack American journalists including Peter Arnett and David Halberstam at a demonstration during the Buddhist crisis in South Vietnam.

objets.nom: Huế Phật Đản shootings
objets.notes: The Army of the Republic of Vietnam opens fire on Buddhists who defy a ban on the flying of the Buddhist flag on Vesak, the birthday of Gautama Buddha, killing 9. Earlier, President Ngô Đình Diệm allowed the flying of the Vatican flag in honour of his brother, Archbishop Ngô Đình Thục, triggering the Buddhist crisis in South Vietnam.

objets.nom: Huế chemical attacks
objets.notes: The Army of the Republic of Vietnam rains liquid chemicals on the heads of Buddhist protestors, injuring 67 people. The United States threatens to cut off aid to the regime of Ngô Đình Diệm.

objets.nom: Xá Lợi Pagoda raids
objets.notes: The Army of the Republic of Vietnam Special Forces loyal to Ngô Đình Nhu, brother of President Ngô Đình Diệm, vandalise Buddhist pagodas across South Vietnam, arresting thousands and leaving an estimated hundreds dead. In the wake of the raids, the Kennedy administration by Cable 243 orders the Embassy of the United States, Saigon to explore…

objets.nom: Vietnam War: Operation Rolling Thunder – The United States Air Force 2nd Air Division, United States…
objets.notes: Vietnam War: Operation Rolling Thunder – The United States Air Force 2nd Air Division, United States Navy and South Vietnam Air Force begin a 3½-year aerial bombardment campaign against North Vietnam.

objets.nom: Vietnam War: A Viet Cong officer named Nguyễn Văn Lém is executed by Nguyễn Ngọc Loan, a South…
objets.notes: Vietnam War: A Viet Cong officer named Nguyễn Văn Lém is executed by Nguyễn Ngọc Loan, a South Vietnamese National Police Chief. The event is photographed by Eddie Adams. The photo makes headlines around the world, eventually winning the 1969 Pulitzer Prize, and sways U.S. public opinion against the war.

objets.nom: Vietnam War: Associated Press photographer Nick Ut takes his Pulitzer Prize-winning photograph of a…
objets.notes: Vietnam War: Associated Press photographer Nick Ut takes his Pulitzer Prize-winning photograph of a naked nine-year-old Phan Thi Kim Phuc running down a road after being burned by napalm.

objets.nom: Vietnam War: The battle of the Paracel Islands between People's Republic of China and South Vietnam
objets.notes: Vietnam War: The battle of the Paracel Islands between People's Republic of China and South Vietnam. This is the most famous and the only major battle involve China in Vietnam War.

objets.nom: Vietnam War: North Vietnamese troops attack Ban Mê Thuột, South Vietnam, on their way to capturing Saigon.

objets.nom: The People's Republic of China invades northern Vietnam, launching the Sino-Vietnamese War
objets.notes: The People's Republic of China invades northern Vietnam, launching the Sino-Vietnamese War. The war ended with no border changes on 16 March. Vietnamese government signs treaty with Cambodia regime lifts blockade of the Cambodian coast same day.

objets.nom: Début de la politique d’ouverture économique du Viêt Nam (« Dôi moi »)
objets.fr: Début de la politique d’ouverture économique du Viêt Nam (« Dôi moi »)

objets.nom: Sixth National Party Congress
objets.notes: Sixth National Party Congress. Trường Chinh, Chairman of the State Council (1981–1987) ended his rule of Vietnam. Đổi Mới begins.

objets.nom: Hai Yang Shi You 981 standoff
objets.notes: Tensions arises from the Chinese state-owned China National Offshore Oil Corporation moving its Hai Yang Shi You 981 oil platform to waters near the disputed Paracel Islands, resulting in large anti-China protests across Vietnam.

objets.nom: Ptolemy's map shows the city of Albanopolis (located northeast of Durrës)
objets.notes: Ptolemy's map shows the city of Albanopolis (located northeast of Durrës). Ptolemy also mentions the Illyrian tribe named Albanoi, who lived around this city. The area was part of the Roman province of Macedonia.

objets.nom: Epirus Nova or New Epirus or Illyria Graeca or Illyris proper was a province of the Roman Empire…
objets.notes: Epirus Nova or New Epirus or Illyria Graeca or Illyris proper was a province of the Roman Empire established by Diocletian during his restructuring of provincial boundaries. The province, belonged to the Roman province of Macedonia. Later it became a theme of the Byzantine Empire. Dyrrachium was established as the capital of Epirus nova. The Roman…

objets.nom: In History written in 1079–1080, Byzantine historian Michael Attaliates referred to the Albanoi as…
objets.notes: In History written in 1079–1080, Byzantine historian Michael Attaliates referred to the Albanoi as having taken part in a revolt against Constantinople in 1043 and to the Arbanitai as subjects of the duke of Dyrrachium. It is disputed, however, whether the "Albanoi" of the events of 1043 refers to Albanians in an ethnic sense or whether "Albanoi"…

objets.nom: Arbanitai of Arbanon are recorded in an account by Anna Comnena of the troubles in that region during…
objets.notes: Arbanitai of Arbanon are recorded in an account by Anna Comnena of the troubles in that region during the reign of her father Alexius I Comnenus by the Normans.

objets.nom: Fourth Crusade
objets.notes: Venice won control over most of Albania.

objets.nom: Fourth Crusade: The Byzantines regained control of the southern portion of Albania and established the…
objets.notes: Fourth Crusade: The Byzantines regained control of the southern portion of Albania and established the Despotate of Epirus.

objets.nom: The Angevin Kingdom of Sicily seized the Albanian coast and much of the Epirus hinterland.
Forces allied to Angevin Charles I of Naples occupied Durrës and established the Kingdom of Albania.
Siege of Berat (1280–1281)
objets.notes: An Angevin offensive against Constantinople was repulsed by the Byzantines.

objets.nom: Karl Thopia captured Durrës from the Angevins.
Thopia invited the Ottoman Empire to intervene against his rival Balsha II.
Battle of Kosovo
objets.notes: Albanians, as part of a Serbian-led Balkan army, were crushed by Ottoman forces.

objets.nom: George Kastrioti, later Skanderbeg, was born.
Gjon Kastrioti led an unsuccessful uprising against the Ottoman Empire.
After being sent into battle near Niš, Skanderbeg entered Albania and embraced Roman Catholicism,…
objets.notes: After being sent into battle near Niš, Skanderbeg entered Albania and embraced Roman Catholicism, marking the beginning of a long war against the Ottoman Empire.

objets.nom: The Albanians, led by Skanderbeg, routed Ottoman forces.
Fourth Siege of Krujë (1478)
objets.notes: Krujë fell to the Ottoman Empire, causing many Albanians to flee to southern Italy, Greece, Egypt, and elsewhere.

objets.nom: Shkodër fell to the Ottoman Empire in Fourth siege of Shkodra the Albanians were helped by Venice but…
objets.notes: Shkodër fell to the Ottoman Empire in Fourth siege of Shkodra the Albanians were helped by Venice but still lost.

objets.nom: Kara Mahmud Bushati, an Albanian noble from the Bushati family based in Shkodër, attacked Montenegrin…
objets.notes: Kara Mahmud Bushati, an Albanian noble from the Bushati family based in Shkodër, attacked Montenegrin territory and was named governor of Shkodër by Ottoman authorities.

objets.nom: The Ottoman Sublime Porte divided Albanian-populated lands into the Ottoman-administered vilayets of…
objets.notes: The Ottoman Sublime Porte divided Albanian-populated lands into the Ottoman-administered vilayets of Janina and Rumelia.

objets.nom: Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878)
objets.notes: The war began.

objets.nom: Albanian leaders meeting in Prizren formed the League of Prizren to advocate a unified Albania under…
objets.notes: Albanian leaders meeting in Prizren formed the League of Prizren to advocate a unified Albania under Ottoman suzerainty.

objets.nom: Albanian intellectuals meeting in Bitola chose the Latin alphabet as the standard script for the…
objets.notes: Albanian intellectuals meeting in Bitola chose the Latin alphabet as the standard script for the Albanian language.

objets.nom: An ambassadorial conference in London gave half of Albanian territory to Serbia and Greece.
First Balkan War
objets.notes: The war began, encouraging Albanian leaders to affirm the independence of their state.

objets.nom: Second Balkan War
objets.notes: The war began.

objets.nom: William, Prince of Albania, of Wied was installed as head of the new Principality of Albania by the…
objets.notes: William, Prince of Albania, of Wied was installed as head of the new Principality of Albania by the International Commission of Control.

objets.nom: World War I
objets.notes: The new Albanian state collapsed.

objets.nom: World War I: The war ended with Albanian territory divided under Italian, Serbian, Greek and French…
objets.notes: World War I: The war ended with Albanian territory divided under Italian, Serbian, Greek and French military occupation.

objets.nom: Paris Peace Conference, 1919
objets.notes: Albania was divided between Greece, Italy and Yugoslavia at the conference, which did not admit Albanian representation.

objets.nom: Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople Patriarch Meletius IV of Constantinople recognized the Orthodox…
objets.notes: Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople Patriarch Meletius IV of Constantinople recognized the Orthodox Autocephalous Church of Albania.

objets.nom: A peasant-backed insurgency won control of Tirana, installed Fan S. Noli as Prime Minister and forced…
objets.notes: A peasant-backed insurgency won control of Tirana, installed Fan S. Noli as Prime Minister and forced Zog of Albania to flee to Yugoslavia.

objets.nom: Zog, backed by the Yugoslavian army, returned to power and forced Noli to flee to Italy.
Italian invasion of Albania
objets.notes: Fifty thousand Italian marines landed in the ports of Durrës, Vlorë, Shëngjin and Sarandë. See also: Albania under Italy, Albania under Nazi Germany, Albanian resistance during World War II

objets.nom: Zog fled with his wife, Queen Géraldine Apponyi de Nagyappony, and their infant son Leka, to Greece.
Greco-Italian War
objets.notes: The war began. The Italian army invaded Greece through Albania.

objets.nom: Axis occupation of Greece during World War II
objets.notes: Greece was partitioned between Germany, Italy and Bulgaria, with Italy occupying the bulk of the Greek mainland and most of the islands.

objets.nom: Battle of Greece
objets.notes: Germany invaded Greece.

objets.nom: Invasion of Yugoslavia
objets.notes: Germany, Italy, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania and the Croatian Ustaše invaded Yugoslavia.

objets.nom: Josip Broz Tito, leader of the Communist Party of Yugoslavia, began to organize Albanian Communists.
Conference of Pezë
objets.notes: The National Liberation Movement (Albania) was established.

objets.nom: Corfu Channel Incident
objets.notes: Two British ships were destroyed by mines off the Albanian coast in the Straits of Corfu.

objets.nom: Corfu Channel Incident: United Nations Security Council Resolution 22 recommended that the International…
objets.notes: Corfu Channel Incident: United Nations Security Council Resolution 22 recommended that the International Court of Justice settle the dispute between the UK and Albania regarding the sinking of two British ships in the Straits of Corfu.

objets.nom: Greek Civil War
objets.notes: A United Nations commission concluded that Albania, together with Bulgaria and Yugoslavia, supported Communist guerrillas.

objets.nom: Communist Party of the Soviet Union chief Nikita Khrushchev delivered the speech "On the Personality…
objets.notes: Communist Party of the Soviet Union chief Nikita Khrushchev delivered the speech "On the Personality Cult and its Consequences" in which he criticized his predecessor Joseph Stalin, and caused a chill in relations with Albania under the pro-Stalin Hoxha.

objets.nom: Soviet–Albanian split
objets.notes: Albania sided with the People's Republic of China, causing the Soviet Union to dramatically curtail economic support.

objets.nom: Warsaw Pact invasion of Czechoslovakia
objets.notes: Albania condemned the invasion and withdrew from the Warsaw Pact.

objets.nom: Chinese Communist Party Chairman Mao Zedong died, leading eventually to a cooling of relations with…
objets.notes: Chinese Communist Party Chairman Mao Zedong died, leading eventually to a cooling of relations with Albania known as the Sino-Albanian split.

objets.nom: Hoxha selected Ramiz Alia as the next party head, bypassing Mehmet Shehu.
Albania is granted membership of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference and in the same month…
objets.notes: Albania is granted membership of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference and in the same month applies to join NATO, becoming the first former Warsaw Pact country formally to seek membership in the Western alliance.

objets.nom: Albania's postcommunist transformation continues, with more progress in some areas than others
objets.notes: Albania's postcommunist transformation continues, with more progress in some areas than others. Greek-Albanian relations deteriorate, and Athens blocks European Union loans to Tirana, impeding Albania's much-needed integration into Europe. Gross domestic product grows by 8%, and inflation continues its downward spiral. Unemployment, however,…

objets.nom: Berisha forms a new enlarged (25-member) cabinet
objets.notes: Berisha forms a new enlarged (25-member) cabinet. Among the new ministers are Tritan Shehu as foreign minister and deputy premier, Ridvan Bode as finance minister, and Halit Shamata as interior minister. The government includes four female members, the widest female representation in the history of the country.

objets.nom: The former chief of the Sigurimi is arrested following bomb attacks in Tirana on February 26 and in…
objets.notes: The former chief of the Sigurimi is arrested following bomb attacks in Tirana on February 26 and in Durrës on March 6.

objets.nom: A national state of emergency is declared
objets.notes: A national state of emergency is declared. Rioters take control of the town of Sarandë, seizing weapons from police headquarters and army barracks. With astonishing speed the entire military establishment melts away, the security service dissolves, and the people arm themselves with every type of weapon, including Kalashnikovs and even tanks – an…

objets.nom: A new 20-member multiparty cabinet (excluding the Democratic Party) is presented by Nano, including…
objets.notes: A new 20-member multiparty cabinet (excluding the Democratic Party) is presented by Nano, including Paskal Milo as foreign minister, Sabit Brokaj as defense minister, Neritan Ceka as interior minister, and Arben Malaj retaining his post of finance minister.

objets.nom: Bashkim Fino of the opposition Socialist Party is appointed as prime minister
objets.notes: Bashkim Fino of the opposition Socialist Party is appointed as prime minister. Arjan Starova becomes foreign minister; Shaqir Vukaj, defense minister; Arben Malaj, finance minister; Belul Celo, interior minister. Unrest spreads to northern Albania, and by March 13 engulfs all major population centres, including Tirana. Alia flees jail during the…

objets.nom: Following the collapse of several "get-rich-quick" pyramid schemes, in which hundreds of thousands of…
objets.notes: Following the collapse of several "get-rich-quick" pyramid schemes, in which hundreds of thousands of Albanians lost their life savings, enraged investors go on the rampage in the southern town of Lushnjë. Foreign Minister Shehu is attacked by demonstrators there on January 25. On January 26, thousands of people converge on central Tirana and…

objets.nom: In the 1997 unrest in Albania the general elections of June 1997 brought the Socialists and their allies…
objets.notes: In the 1997 unrest in Albania the general elections of June 1997 brought the Socialists and their allies to power. President Berisha resigned from his post, and Socialists elected Rexhep Meidani as president of Albania. Albanian Socialist Party Chairman Fatos Nano was elected Prime Minister, a post which he held until October 1998, when he…

objets.nom: Parliament elects secretary of the Socialist Party of Albania and former physics professor Rexhep…
objets.notes: Parliament elects secretary of the Socialist Party of Albania and former physics professor Rexhep Meidani as President of Albania (110-3 with 2 abstentions). Meidani then accepts the resignation of Prime Minister Fino, and names Socialist Party leader Nano as new Prime minister of Albania.

objets.nom: More than 13,000 refugees flee into Albania after the eruption in February of civil war between the…
objets.notes: More than 13,000 refugees flee into Albania after the eruption in February of civil war between the Serbian police and army and the ethnic Albanian separatist Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) in the neighbouring province of Kosovo. The Albanian Foreign Ministry repeatedly charges Yugoslavia with border violations that include shelling and sniping and…

objets.nom: Police arrest former defense minister Safet Zhulali, former interior minister Halit Shamata, former…
objets.notes: Police arrest former defense minister Safet Zhulali, former interior minister Halit Shamata, former chairman of state control Blerim Cela, and three other former officials of Berisha's government on charges of crimes against humanity in conjunction with their alleged roles in the suppression of unrest in 1997. General Prosecutor Arben Rakipi…

objets.nom: During the 78 days of NATO bombing of Yugoslavia, about 450,000 of a total 750,000 Kosovar refugees flee…
objets.notes: During the 78 days of NATO bombing of Yugoslavia, about 450,000 of a total 750,000 Kosovar refugees flee into Albania. That figure is equal to almost 15% of Albania's total population. The hostilities turn Albania into a key operational theatre for international relief agencies and NATO forces in Albania, called Kosovo Force (KFOR), which launch a…

objets.nom: Spartak Poçi is appointed interior minister, replacing Petro Koçi
objets.notes: Spartak Poçi is appointed interior minister, replacing Petro Koçi. Poçi subsequently manages to break up 12 criminal gangs throughout the country, most notably those in Tropojë, where special police units restore order in September. Because of frequent armed robberies, Tropojë earlier had been a "no-go" area for international aid agencies. The…

objets.nom: Following the election of Vojislav Koštunica as president of Yugoslavia, Albanian Foreign Minister…
objets.notes: Following the election of Vojislav Koštunica as president of Yugoslavia, Albanian Foreign Minister Paskal Milo makes the resumption of regular bilateral relations dependent on Serbia freeing Kosovo Albanian prisoners and recognizing its responsibility for crimes against humanity in the Kosovo war.

objets.nom: Although Albania has made strides toward democratic reform and maintaining the rule of law, serious…
objets.notes: Although Albania has made strides toward democratic reform and maintaining the rule of law, serious deficiencies in the electoral code remain to be addressed, as demonstrated in the June 2001 parliamentary elections. International observers judged the 2001 elections to be acceptable, but the Union for Victory Coalition, the second-largest vote…

objets.nom: Parliament gives Prime Minister Ilir Meta's new government a vote of confidence
objets.notes: Parliament gives Prime Minister Ilir Meta's new government a vote of confidence. Within the governing coalition the Socialist Party controls all key ministries. Arta Dade becomes foreign minister (the first woman in Albanian history to hold that post), Ilir Gjoni interior minister, and Pandeli Majko defense minister; Anastas Angjeli remains…

objets.nom: The government is strongly criticized for its unsuccessful policy toward human trafficking
objets.notes: The government is strongly criticized for its unsuccessful policy toward human trafficking. The International Organization for Migration (IOM) joins Save the Children in highlighting the trade in eastern European women and even Albanian children, and accuses local Albanian police of colluding in the lucrative industry. IOM points out that there…

objets.nom: The large ethnic Albanian minority in neighbouring Macedonia stages an armed rebellion
objets.notes: The large ethnic Albanian minority in neighbouring Macedonia stages an armed rebellion. Although Albania's prime minister Ilir Meta supports international peace negotiations (which lead to a truce and a peace settlement in late August), there is evidence to suggest that Albanian border guards have at first failed to seal the border completely to…

objets.nom: Defense Minister Pandeli Majko receives the backing of the various warring factions within the ruling…
objets.notes: Defense Minister Pandeli Majko receives the backing of the various warring factions within the ruling Socialist Party to be the country's next prime minister. Nominated by outgoing premier Meta, Majko agrees to accommodate supporters of party leader Nano in a new cabinet. The previous deadlock led the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the…

objets.nom: Prime Minister of Albania Ilir Meta resigns in anger over a continuing row with the leader of his…
objets.notes: Prime Minister of Albania Ilir Meta resigns in anger over a continuing row with the leader of his Socialist Party, Fatos Nano, who has been resisting the appointment of ministers to vacant cabinet positions. Earlier that day the opposition Democratic Party ended its four-month boycott of the People's Assembly.

objets.nom: The Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe's chief of mission, Geert-Hinrich Ahrens,…
objets.notes: The Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe's chief of mission, Geert-Hinrich Ahrens, praises Albania in his end-of-mission address to the OSCE Permanent Council, reporting that the country is "in the forefront of reform in the region" and adding that recent achievements have "brought Albania to the threshold of opening negotiations…

objets.nom: Interior Minister Luan Rama is sacked
objets.notes: Interior Minister Luan Rama is sacked. He has been accused of punching the editor-in-chief of Vizion Plus television, Ilir Babaramo, in a Tirana restaurant on October 14 because of criticism broadcast by the TV station two months ago. On October 23 Prime Minister Nano's nominees for foreign minister, Namik Dokle, and for interior minister, Fatmir…

objets.nom: Parliament finally approves new ministers for the vacant posts
objets.notes: Parliament finally approves new ministers for the vacant posts. Kastriot Islami becomes foreign minister, Arben Malaj succeeds him as finance minister, and Igli Toska becomes interior minister.

objets.nom: Parliamentary elections end with a victory for the opposition Democratic Party (PD) and its allies,…
objets.notes: Parliamentary elections end with a victory for the opposition Democratic Party (PD) and its allies, prominently the Republican Party (PR). Former president Sali Berisha became prime minister as a result of the election.

objets.nom: A Stabilisation and Association Agreement is signed between Albania and the European Union
Bamir Topi, ruling party chairmanpresident, is elected by the Parliament as President of Albania, after…
objets.notes: Bamir Topi, ruling party chairmanpresident, is elected by the Parliament as President of Albania, after three failed round highlighted the risk of snap elections.

objets.nom: Despite the political situation, the economy of Albania grew at an estimated 5% in 2007. The Albanian…
objets.notes: Despite the political situation, the economy of Albania grew at an estimated 5% in 2007. The Albanian lek has strengthened from 143 lekë to the US dollar in 2000 to 92 lekë in 2007, mainly due to the depreciation of the US dollar, but also thanks to the overall improvement of the Albanian economy.

objets.nom: Protests begin in Tirana, led by opposition Socialist Party leader Edi Rama, against allegedly rigged…
objets.notes: Protests begin in Tirana, led by opposition Socialist Party leader Edi Rama, against allegedly rigged vote counting in the 2009 elections. Berisha has refused any recount of the votes, on the ground that the Albanian Constitution do not foresee such procedure. The political crisis between government and opposition has worsened over time, with the…

objets.nom: Sali Berisha's centre-right Democratic Party wins 2009 parliamentary elections by a narrow margin
objets.notes: Sali Berisha's centre-right Democratic Party wins 2009 parliamentary elections by a narrow margin. Prior to the election, the electoral law was changed to a regional proportionally system.Berisha's alliance won enough seats to form a government, though it fell one seat short of a majority during the elections of Jun 28, 2009, having to join forces…

objets.nom: Local elections see the victory of the Socialist Party of Albania (PS) in the main cities outside…
objets.notes: Local elections see the victory of the Socialist Party of Albania (PS) in the main cities outside Tirana, Lezha and Scutari; The Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe released a mixed evaluation of the electoral process, which was considered "competitive and transparent, but took place in an environment of high polarization and…

objets.nom: A Phoenician colony, Maleth, is founded in present-day Cospicua in the Grand Harbour Malta.
A Punic temple, dedicated to the mother goddess Astarte, is built over the remains of the Tas-Silġ…
objets.notes: A Punic temple, dedicated to the mother goddess Astarte, is built over the remains of the Tas-Silġ megalithic temples. (to 200 BC)

objets.nom: Cyrus the Great, founder of the Persian Empire, conquers Phoenicia.
A Roman temple, dedicated to the goddess Hera, is built over the remains of the Tas-Silġ megalithic temples
objets.notes: A Roman temple, dedicated to the goddess Hera, is built over the remains of the Tas-Silġ megalithic temples. The Cippi of Melqart, a pair of Phoenician marble cippi, are dedicated to the god Melqart by inscriptions in Ancient Greek and Phoenician, probably at the Temple of Hercules at Marsaxlokk. Their subsequent discovery in the late 17th century…

objets.nom: The Maltese are granted municipal privileges by Rome.
Malta becomes a municipium during the reign of Hadrian.
The fortified Roman settlement of Melita, on the highlands in the centre of Malta, is reduced in size,…
objets.notes: The fortified Roman settlement of Melita, on the highlands in the centre of Malta, is reduced in size, further fortified, and renamed Medina, precursor to the Medieval city of Mdina.

objets.nom: The Norman Count Roger I of Sicily invades Malta and the Muslim inhabitants negotiate a peaceful surrender
objets.notes: The Norman Count Roger I of Sicily invades Malta and the Muslim inhabitants negotiate a peaceful surrender. Gozo is sacked by the Normans.

objets.nom: The Catholic Church in Malta is incorporated into the See of Palermo.
Margaritus of Brindisi was created first Count of Malta, perhaps for his unexpected success in capturing…
objets.notes: Margaritus of Brindisi was created first Count of Malta, perhaps for his unexpected success in capturing Empress Constance contender to the Sicilian throne. (to 1194, forfeited by House of Hohenstaufen)

objets.nom: Malta and Sicily are ruled by the Swabians (House of Hohenstaufen)
objets.notes: Malta and Sicily are ruled by the Swabians (House of Hohenstaufen). (to 1266)

objets.nom: First Incorporation of the Maltese Islands into the Royal Domain (Kingdom of Sicily)
objets.notes: First Incorporation of the Maltese Islands into the Royal Domain (Kingdom of Sicily). (to 1357)

objets.nom: Maltese representatives appear before the same Court, offering to "redeem" the Islands by repaying the…
objets.notes: Maltese representatives appear before the same Court, offering to "redeem" the Islands by repaying the 30,000 florins originally paid by Monroy for his fiefdom over Malta, and asking King Alfonso to incorporate the Islands into his Royal Domains

objets.nom: Uprising by the Maltese against Don Gonsalvo Monroy during his absence from the island, Count of Malta.
King Alfonso incorporates Malta to the Crown of Aragon (Kingdom of Sicily), and promises never to grant…
objets.notes: King Alfonso incorporates Malta to the Crown of Aragon (Kingdom of Sicily), and promises never to grant Malta as a fief to any third party.

objets.nom: The Hafsid Berbers attempt to capture Malta.
Suleiman I drives the Military Hospitaller Knights of St
objets.notes: Suleiman I drives the Military Hospitaller Knights of St. John of Jerusalem out of Rhodes.

objets.nom: In an effort to protect Rome from Islamic invasion, Emperor Charles V grants the Maltese Islands to the…
objets.notes: In an effort to protect Rome from Islamic invasion, Emperor Charles V grants the Maltese Islands to the Knights of St. John of Jerusalem in perpetual fief.

objets.nom: The Knights stage their first attacks from their new naval base in Malta, forming part of a Christian…
objets.notes: The Knights stage their first attacks from their new naval base in Malta, forming part of a Christian fleet under the command of Admiral Andrea Doria in attacks on the Turks at Modone, on the Ottoman fort at Coronna and, in 1535, on Tunis.

objets.nom: The Ottomans and Barbary corsairs attack Gozo.
Andrea Doria and Claude de la Sengle, bailli of the French langue of the Knights, capture and massacre…
objets.notes: Andrea Doria and Claude de la Sengle, bailli of the French langue of the Knights, capture and massacre the population of Mahdia, in Tunisia. (to September)

objets.nom: An Ottoman fleet under the command of Sinan Pasha, Salah Rais and Dragut commences a series of attacks…
objets.notes: An Ottoman fleet under the command of Sinan Pasha, Salah Rais and Dragut commences a series of attacks on eastern Sicily and Malta, in revenge for the events in Mahdia.

objets.nom: Governor Gaspard de Vallier surrenders Tripoli to the Ottomans and negotiates a truce that ensures safe…
objets.notes: Governor Gaspard de Vallier surrenders Tripoli to the Ottomans and negotiates a truce that ensures safe passage to Malta for the Knights of the garrison, but excludes the Maltese, Calabrian and Rhodian soldiers, who are auctioned off into slavery.

objets.nom: Governor of Gozo Galatian de Sesse surrenders the Castello to Sinan Pasha; the majority of the island's…
objets.notes: Governor of Gozo Galatian de Sesse surrenders the Castello to Sinan Pasha; the majority of the island's inhabitants (some 5,000 to 7,000 people) are enslaved and are taken to North Africa and later to Constantinople.

objets.nom: Invasion of Gozo
objets.notes: The Ottoman fleet lands on Gozo and starts bombarding the island's Castello on 24 July.

objets.nom: Pope Julius III suggests that the Knights should abandon Malta, and retreat to Messina or Syracuse.
The Ottoman fleet arrives in Malta and lands some 10,000 men at Marsa Muscietto
objets.notes: The Ottoman fleet arrives in Malta and lands some 10,000 men at Marsa Muscietto. They reconnoiter Birgu and stage a short-lived siege on Mdina, but retreat and abandon the island by 21 July.

objets.nom: The Ottomans sail south to Tripoli, and besiege the city which was held by the Hospitallers.
Construction of Fort Saint Elmo, in what later became Valletta, commences.
Fearing further razzias by Turks and Barbary corsairs, one thousand Maltese flee Malta, seeking refuge…
objets.notes: Fearing further razzias by Turks and Barbary corsairs, one thousand Maltese flee Malta, seeking refuge in Sicily.

objets.nom: Jean Parisot de Valette is elected Grand Master of the Knights of Malta.
The Knights of Malta escalate their corsairing activities in the western Mediterranean
objets.notes: The Knights of Malta escalate their corsairing activities in the western Mediterranean. (to 1565)

objets.nom: The Ottoman war council in Constantinople decrees that Malta is to be invaded and conquered.
A storm prevents the Turkish fleet from landing at Marsaxlokk; the vessels are sheltered in Ġnejna Bay…
objets.notes: A storm prevents the Turkish fleet from landing at Marsaxlokk; the vessels are sheltered in Ġnejna Bay and at Għajn Tuffieħa.

objets.nom: Four galleys land in the north of Malta, bringing 600 soldiers, 42 knights, 56 gunners and numerous…
objets.notes: Four galleys land in the north of Malta, bringing 600 soldiers, 42 knights, 56 gunners and numerous volunteers, to reinforce the Island's defences; they walk to Mdina by night, and then on to Birgu the following morning.

objets.nom: Ottoman fleet leaves Constantinople for Malta; Queen Elizabeth remarks: "If the Turks should prevail…
objets.notes: Ottoman fleet leaves Constantinople for Malta; Queen Elizabeth remarks: "If the Turks should prevail against the Isle of Malta, it is uncertain what further peril might follow to the rest of Christendom."

objets.nom: The Spanish Viceroy of Sicily, Don García de Toledo y Osorio, a tours the Island's fortifications; he…
objets.notes: The Spanish Viceroy of Sicily, Don García de Toledo y Osorio, a tours the Island's fortifications; he promises the Knights that in the coming invasion they need only hold out until June, when he would bring his armada back to assist Malta.

objets.nom: The Turkish fleet anchors at Marsaxlokk, moved to Żejtun and sets up camp at Marsa.
The Turkish fleet is transported on rollers, overland, from Marsamxett Harbour to Grand Harbour, in…
objets.notes: The Turkish fleet is transported on rollers, overland, from Marsamxett Harbour to Grand Harbour, in preparation for an assault on Senglea. (to 12 July)

objets.nom: The Turkish forces are reinforced with the arrival of 29 vessels and 2,500 warriors accompanied by the…
objets.notes: The Turkish forces are reinforced with the arrival of 29 vessels and 2,500 warriors accompanied by the Bey of Algiers.

objets.nom: Turkish commanders order all the dead Knights found in St
objets.notes: Turkish commanders order all the dead Knights found in St. Elmo to be beheaded; their mutilated bodies are floated across Grand Harbour on planks towards the bastions of Senglea and Birgu.

objets.nom: The founding of Malta's new capital city, Valletta
objets.notes: The founding of Malta's new capital city, Valletta. A general strengthening of Malta's fortifications is undertaken.

objets.nom: Barbary corsairs from Bizerte attack Gozo, sack Rabat, and enslave 70 people.
The Manoel Theatre (then known as the Teatro Pubblico) opens in Valletta with a performance of Scipione…
objets.notes: The Manoel Theatre (then known as the Teatro Pubblico) opens in Valletta with a performance of Scipione Maffei's classic tragedy Merope.

objets.nom: Barbary corsairs from Sfax land at Ramla Bay, Gozo and enslave a family of 8 people.
Slavery, the Roman Inquisition, and all titles of nobility are abolished in Malta.
The French forces in Gozo surrender and the island becomes independent
objets.notes: The French forces in Gozo surrender and the island becomes independent. First petition for the establishment of a separate Roman Catholic diocese on Gozo, led by Archpriest Saverio Cassar sent a day later.

objets.nom: Tsar Paul I of Russia become de facto Grand Master of the Order, and orders the creation of a "Throne of…
objets.notes: Tsar Paul I of Russia become de facto Grand Master of the Order, and orders the creation of a "Throne of Malta," in the Vorontsov Palace in St. Petersburg (now on display in the State Hermitage Museum).

objets.nom: Maltese uprising against the French following extensive pillaging of Maltese churches and cathedrals
objets.notes: Maltese uprising against the French following extensive pillaging of Maltese churches and cathedrals. Britain takes Malta under its protection, in the name of the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies. The Union Jack flies over Valletta for the first time, alongside the Neapolitan flag.

objets.nom: Admiral Sir Alexander Ball is sent to Malta as Plenipotentiary Minister of His British Majesty for the…
objets.notes: Admiral Sir Alexander Ball is sent to Malta as Plenipotentiary Minister of His British Majesty for the Order of Saint John, with orders to evacuate the British forces from the Islands, and to prepare for their return to the Knights of St. John.

objets.nom: Under the Peace of Amiens, Britain is ordered to return Malta to the Knights of St John, but facing…
objets.notes: Under the Peace of Amiens, Britain is ordered to return Malta to the Knights of St John, but facing imminent hostilities by Napoleonic France, Britain chooses not to comply.

objets.nom: Beginning of the Froberg mutiny at Fort Ricasoli.
The Grand Harbour becomes an important shipping waystation, eventually serving as the headquarters for…
objets.notes: The Grand Harbour becomes an important shipping waystation, eventually serving as the headquarters for the Mediterranean Fleet. (to 1930)

objets.nom: Under the Treaty of Paris, and subsequently ratified by the Congress of Vienna, Malta status as a…
objets.notes: Under the Treaty of Paris, and subsequently ratified by the Congress of Vienna, Malta status as a British Crown Colony is confirmed.

objets.nom: Second petition for a separate Roman Catholic diocese for Gozo is presented to Pope Gregory XVI.
Three Gozitan representatives personally petition Pope Pius IX for a separate Roman Catholic diocese for…
objets.notes: Three Gozitan representatives personally petition Pope Pius IX for a separate Roman Catholic diocese for Gozo; the pontiff promises his support.

objets.nom: The Colonial Office in London approves the establishment of a separate Roman Catholic diocese for Gozo.
Pope Pius IX issues a papal bull entitled Singulari Amore (With remarkable love), separating the islands…
objets.notes: Pope Pius IX issues a papal bull entitled Singulari Amore (With remarkable love), separating the islands of Gozo and Comino from the diocese of Malta; seven days later, Michele Francesco Buttigieg is elected first Bishop of Gozo.

objets.nom: Opening of the Suez Canal
objets.notes: Opening of the Suez Canal. This greatly enhanced the importance of the Grand Harbour to British merchant marine and naval shipping.

objets.nom: J.S. Tucker proposes the construction of a railway from Valletta to Mdina.
The Malta Railway service is inaugurated, with service from Valletta to Floriana, Ħamrun, Msida,…
objets.notes: The Malta Railway service is inaugurated, with service from Valletta to Floriana, Ħamrun, Msida, Birkirkara, Lija, San Antonio, Attard, Mosta (San Salvatore), and Mdina.

objets.nom: (Otto Settembre) is recommended as a national holiday, commemorating the victory of the Knights and the…
objets.notes: (Otto Settembre) is recommended as a national holiday, commemorating the victory of the Knights and the Maltese over the Ottoman Empire in the Siege of Malta (1565).

objets.nom: An electric tramway service is introduced in Malta by McCartney, McElroy & Co
objets.notes: An electric tramway service is introduced in Malta by McCartney, McElroy & Co. Ltd., connecting Valletta, the Three Cities, and Żebbuġ and Ħamrun.

objets.nom: A tsunami associated with the 1908 Messina earthquake rushed into Marsamxett Harbour and damaged…
objets.notes: A tsunami associated with the 1908 Messina earthquake rushed into Marsamxett Harbour and damaged property in Msida.

objets.nom: Dr
objets.notes: Dr. Enrico Mizzi, a staunch supporter of the italianità of Malta, proposes in a journal article that Britain could exchange Malta for Eritrea with Italy, on the understanding that Britain would be granted access to Maltese harbours and facilities. The article proposes an Italo-Maltese federation, with elected Maltese representatives in the Italian…

objets.nom: Throughout World War I, especially following the failed invasion of Gallipoli, many casualties are…
objets.notes: Throughout World War I, especially following the failed invasion of Gallipoli, many casualties are shipped to hospitals in Malta, resuming its role as the Nurse of the Mediterranean. (to 1918)

objets.nom: Dr
objets.notes: Dr. Enrico Mizzi is court-martialled for sedition, and sentenced to one year imprisonment. His sentence is subsequently commuted, and a pardon is issued.

objets.nom: Mussolini's Abyssinian War and intervention on the side of Franco in the Spanish Civil War ends any…
objets.notes: Mussolini's Abyssinian War and intervention on the side of Franco in the Spanish Civil War ends any possibility of reconciliation between Italy and the United Kingdom. (to 1939)

objets.nom: Dr
objets.notes: Dr. Enrico Mizzi, co-leader of the Partito Nazionalista, is arrested and imprisoned in Fort San Salvatore, to secure "the public safety and the Defence of the [Maltese Islands]...in view of the hostile origin or association of Dr. Enrico Mizzi."

objets.nom: Throughout World War II, Malta plays an important role due to the strategic location of the Grand…
objets.notes: Throughout World War II, Malta plays an important role due to the strategic location of the Grand Harbour at the crossroads of the Axis shipping lanes.

objets.nom: A 200 kg bomb pierces the dome of the Rotunda of Sta
objets.notes: A 200 kg bomb pierces the dome of the Rotunda of Sta. Marija Assunta, Mosta, but skids across the floor without exploding; two other bombs bounce off the roof and fail to explode; 300 people were hearing Mass inside the church at the time.

objets.nom: Governor Dobbie issues a warrant for the deportation, exile and internment in Uganda of 47 Maltese…
objets.notes: Governor Dobbie issues a warrant for the deportation, exile and internment in Uganda of 47 Maltese (including Dr. Enrico Mizzi) who were suspected of pro-Italian sentiments. (to 8 March)

objets.nom: The Royal Opera House, Valletta, is destroyed by Luftwaffe bombers.
(Operation Husky); 2,760 ships and major landing craft converge in a rendezvous near Malta in…
objets.notes: (Operation Husky); 2,760 ships and major landing craft converge in a rendezvous near Malta in preparation for the Allied invasion of Sicily, under the command of U.S. General Dwight D. Eisenhower, who was stationed in the Lascaris War Rooms, in Valletta.

objets.nom: On the national holiday that commemorates the lifting of the Siege of Malta (1565), Italy announces its…
objets.notes: On the national holiday that commemorates the lifting of the Siege of Malta (1565), Italy announces its unconditional surrender to the Allied forces, thus ending the second Siege of Malta (1940).

objets.nom: The 21st Engineer Aviation Regiment of the USAAF arrives on Gozo to construct a landing strip at Xewkija…
objets.notes: The 21st Engineer Aviation Regiment of the USAAF arrives on Gozo to construct a landing strip at Xewkija in preparation for the Allied invasion of Italy; the airfield is constructed in 18 days.

objets.nom: Malta Conference (1945); President Franklin D. Roosevelt of the United States and Prime Minister Winston…
objets.notes: Malta Conference (1945); President Franklin D. Roosevelt of the United States and Prime Minister Winston Churchill of the United Kingdom meet on Malta to plan the final campaign against the Germans with the combined Chiefs of Staff, and to prepare for the Yalta Conference. (to 3 February)

objets.nom: Malta is granted independence from the United Kingdom as a Constitutional Monarchy, with Queen Elizabeth…
objets.notes: Malta is granted independence from the United Kingdom as a Constitutional Monarchy, with Queen Elizabeth II as its Head of State.

objets.nom: Malta becomes a Republic, with the last Governor-General, Sir Anthony Mamo, serving as its first President
objets.notes: Malta becomes a Republic, with the last Governor-General, Sir Anthony Mamo, serving as its first President. Malta remains a member of the Commonwealth of Nations.

objets.nom: Malta votes in favour of divorce in a referendum
objets.notes: Malta votes in favour of divorce in a referendum. Parliament approved the law on 25 July and the law came into effect on 1 October.

objets.nom: After being defeated by Fabius Maximus Caepius, Viriathus sends his most trusted friends Audax, Ditalcus…
objets.notes: After being defeated by Fabius Maximus Caepius, Viriathus sends his most trusted friends Audax, Ditalcus and Minurus to negotiate peace terms with Caepio. They are bribed by Caepius to kill Viriathus and do. After the death of Viriathus, the Lusitanians attempt to raid Saguntum, but fail. On crossing the river Baetis on their return, they are…

objets.nom: The Roman Republic is over and the Roman Empire begins in the aftermath of the War of Actium, in which…
objets.notes: The Roman Republic is over and the Roman Empire begins in the aftermath of the War of Actium, in which Augustus wins and becomes Emperor. He replaces the old Hispania Ulterior and Citerior division with a new one: Lusitania (Centre and South of modern Portugal and some territory of Modern Spain, namely the capital of Lusitania, Mérida), Hispania…

objets.nom: Diocletian reorganises the provinces of Hispania, creating some new ones
objets.notes: Diocletian reorganises the provinces of Hispania, creating some new ones. Of interest, Gallaecia is split from the Tarraconensis province. Gallaecia includes the North of Portugal (starting with Portus Cale/Porto) and extending to the North of Spain (Galicia). Bracara Augusta (Braga) is the administrative centre of Conventus Bracarensis, one of…

objets.nom: Potamius, the first recorded bishop of Lisbon, takes part in the Councils of Sirmium, in which he is…
objets.notes: Potamius, the first recorded bishop of Lisbon, takes part in the Councils of Sirmium, in which he is recorded as having defended Arianism.

objets.nom: Cindazunda, daughter of King Hermeric, marries Attaces, King of the Alans as part of a peace deal after…
objets.notes: Cindazunda, daughter of King Hermeric, marries Attaces, King of the Alans as part of a peace deal after a battle in Coimbra.

objets.nom: In the context of the Migration Period, the Kingdom of the Suebi is established with King Hermeric, a…
objets.notes: In the context of the Migration Period, the Kingdom of the Suebi is established with King Hermeric, a believer of Germanic paganism, as its leader and Braga as its capital. The Kingdom includes Gallaecia and varying other parts of Portugal. Other groups that enter the Portuguese area are the Germanic Vandals, led by Gunderic, and the Iranic Alans,…

objets.nom: The second Gothic War in Spain (456) takes place between the Suebi (led by Rechila's son, Rechiar) and…
objets.notes: The second Gothic War in Spain (456) takes place between the Suebi (led by Rechila's son, Rechiar) and the Romans, Visigoths, Franks and Burgundians. Rechiar flees to Porto, where he is killed. The Battle of Órbigo culminates with the sacking of (Suebi) Braga and nearby cities.

objets.nom: The Breviary of Alaric is published by the order of Alaric II, King of the Visigoths
objets.notes: The Breviary of Alaric is published by the order of Alaric II, King of the Visigoths. This collection of Roman law applied, not to the Visigothic nobles who lived under their own law, but to the Hispano-Roman and Gallo-Roman population, living under Visigoth rule.

objets.nom: Emperor Justinian I, of the Byzantine Empire, establishes the province of Spania
objets.notes: Emperor Justinian I, of the Byzantine Empire, establishes the province of Spania. In its greatest extent, Spania would include parts of modern-day Algarve.

objets.nom: In the Third Council of Toledo, the Visigothic Kingdom joins the Catholic Church
objets.notes: In the Third Council of Toledo, the Visigothic Kingdom joins the Catholic Church. The bishops of Viseu and of Porto attend the council.

objets.nom: The Fourteenth Council of Toledo is convened, in response to a request by Pope Leo II to confirm the…
objets.notes: The Fourteenth Council of Toledo is convened, in response to a request by Pope Leo II to confirm the decisions of the ecumenical Third Council of Constantinople against monothelitism. The Council confirms the decisions of the Constantinople Council.

objets.nom: The Umayyad conquest of Hispania begins with Tariq ibn Ziyad crossing the Strait of Gibraltar and…
objets.notes: The Umayyad conquest of Hispania begins with Tariq ibn Ziyad crossing the Strait of Gibraltar and entering the Visigothic Kingdom. King Roderic of the Visigoths dies in the Battle of Guadalete. By 716, most of the Iberian Peninsula is under Islamic rule.

objets.nom: Abd al-Aziz ibn Musa becomes Governor of al-Andalus, with al-Andalus constituting a single province…
objets.notes: Abd al-Aziz ibn Musa becomes Governor of al-Andalus, with al-Andalus constituting a single province within the Umayyad Caliphate. Al-Andalus was formally a province subordinate to the Umayyad governor of Kairouan in Ifriqiya, rather than directly dependent on the Umayyad Caliph in Damascus, with Kairouan appointing most of the governors of…

objets.nom: Following the Battle of Covadonga, the Visigothic nobleman Pelagius of Asturias founds the Kingdom of Asturias
objets.notes: Following the Battle of Covadonga, the Visigothic nobleman Pelagius of Asturias founds the Kingdom of Asturias. He begins the Astur-Leonese dynasty.

objets.nom: Abd ar-Rahman II sent an embassy under al-Ghazal to Constantinople to sign a pact with the Byzantine…
objets.notes: Abd ar-Rahman II sent an embassy under al-Ghazal to Constantinople to sign a pact with the Byzantine Empire against the Abbasids.

objets.nom: While during most Islamic rule Christians were considered part of the Dhimmi, and thus allowed to exist…
objets.notes: While during most Islamic rule Christians were considered part of the Dhimmi, and thus allowed to exist and worship in private, the Emirs of Córdoba would execute 48 Christians between 850 and 859, known collectively as the Martyrs of Córdoba. The Martyrs included at least two Mozarabs born in present-day Portugal: Sisenandus of Beja (patron saint…

objets.nom: Vímara Peres was made count of Portugal by Alfonso III of Asturias, king of Asturias, after conquering…
objets.notes: Vímara Peres was made count of Portugal by Alfonso III of Asturias, king of Asturias, after conquering from the Emirate of Córdoba the Atlantic coast between the Minho and Douro rivers.

objets.nom: Abd al-Rahman III proclaims himself Caliph in Córdoba and transforms the Emirate of Córdoba into an…
objets.notes: Abd al-Rahman III proclaims himself Caliph in Córdoba and transforms the Emirate of Córdoba into an independent caliphate no longer under even theoretical control from Baghdad.

objets.nom: Vikings raid Galicia and kill the bishop of Santiago de Compostela in battle, but his successor St
objets.notes: Vikings raid Galicia and kill the bishop of Santiago de Compostela in battle, but his successor St. Rudesind rallies the local forces and kills the Viking King Gundered.

objets.nom: Abu al-Qasim Muhammad ibn Abbad, Abbadid Emir of Seville, captures two castles at Alafões to the…
objets.notes: Abu al-Qasim Muhammad ibn Abbad, Abbadid Emir of Seville, captures two castles at Alafões to the north-west of Viseu.

objets.nom: Ferdinand of Castile, son of Sancho III of Navarre, acquires the Kingdom of León in the Battle of Tamarón
objets.notes: Ferdinand of Castile, son of Sancho III of Navarre, acquires the Kingdom of León in the Battle of Tamarón. The first Castilian king, Ferdinand I, defeats and kills his father-in-law, Bermudo III of León, thus inheriting his kingdom. With Bermudo III's death, the Astur-Leonese dynasty ends and is replaced by the Jiménez dynasty.

objets.nom: The Taifa of the Algarve is annexed by the Taifa of Seville
objets.notes: The Taifa of the Algarve is annexed by the Taifa of Seville. Abu al-Qasim ibn Qasi, governor of Silves and who had aided Afonso I of Portugal against the Almohads, is beheaded.

objets.nom: Raymond of Burgundy, son of William I, Count of Burgundy, comes to Iberia for the 1st time to fight…
objets.notes: Raymond of Burgundy, son of William I, Count of Burgundy, comes to Iberia for the 1st time to fight against the Moors, bringing with him his younger cousin Henry of Burgundy, grandson of Robert I, Duke of Burgundy.

objets.nom: Several Muslim Emirs (namely Abbad III al-Mu'tamid) ask the Almoravids leader Yusuf ibn Tashfin for help…
objets.notes: Several Muslim Emirs (namely Abbad III al-Mu'tamid) ask the Almoravids leader Yusuf ibn Tashfin for help against Alfonso VI of Castile. In this year Yusuf ibn Tashfin passed the straits to Algeciras and inflicted a severe defeat on the Christians at the Battle of az-Zallaqah (North of Badajoz). He was debarred from following up his victory by…

objets.nom: Alfonso VI of Castile gives her daughter Urraca of Castile in marriage to Raymond of Burgundy together…
objets.notes: Alfonso VI of Castile gives her daughter Urraca of Castile in marriage to Raymond of Burgundy together with the fiefdom of Galicia.

objets.nom: Raymond of Burgundy and Henry of Burgundy sign a treaty whereby Henry promises to recognise Raymond as…
objets.notes: Raymond of Burgundy and Henry of Burgundy sign a treaty whereby Henry promises to recognise Raymond as king upon the death of Alfonso VI of Castile, receiving in exchange the Kingdom of Toledo or of Portugal.

objets.nom: Almoravid Sir ibn Abi Bakr takes Badajoz and Lisbon
objets.notes: Almoravid Sir ibn Abi Bakr takes Badajoz and Lisbon. Fall of the Taifa of Badajoz.

objets.nom: Henri de Bourgogne reçoit d'Alphonse VI de Castille et de León, le comté de Portugal.
objets.fr: Henri de Bourgogne reçoit d'Alphonse VI de Castille et de León, le comté de Portugal.

objets.nom: Diego Gemírez, Bishop of Santiago de Compostela, uses force to carry off the relics of St
objets.notes: Diego Gemírez, Bishop of Santiago de Compostela, uses force to carry off the relics of St. Victor and St. Fructuosus of Dumes from Braga – recently reinstated as a Metropolitan See.

objets.nom: In the absence of Henry, Count of Portugal in Rome or Jerusalem, Theresa, Countess of Portugal, aided by…
objets.notes: In the absence of Henry, Count of Portugal in Rome or Jerusalem, Theresa, Countess of Portugal, aided by Soeiro Mendes, governs Portugal.

objets.nom: The Almohads, founded by Ibn Tumart, began as a religious movement to rid Islam of impurities
objets.notes: The Almohads, founded by Ibn Tumart, began as a religious movement to rid Islam of impurities. Most specifically, the Almohades were opposed to anthropomorphisms which had slipped into Iberian Islam. Ibn Tumart's successor, Abd al-Mu'min, turned the movement against non-Muslims, specifically Jews and Christians. Sweeping across North Africa and…

objets.nom: Alfonso VI of Castile and León dies

objets.nom: First live event of the Portuguese National Television and the beginning of the regular broadcasting
objets.notes: First live event of the Portuguese National Television and the beginning of the regular broadcasting. It was opened by the famous and former BBC war reporter, Fernando Pessa.

objets.nom: L'Inde annexe Goa ; révoltes en Angola, Guinée-Bissau et Mozambique, la dictature militaire s'engage…
objets.fr: L'Inde annexe Goa ; révoltes en Angola, Guinée-Bissau et Mozambique, la dictature militaire s'engage…

objets.nom: The Salazar Bridge is inaugurated in Lisbon above the Tagus river
objets.notes: The Salazar Bridge is inaugurated in Lisbon above the Tagus river. It is the longest suspension bridge in Europe and a replica (made by the same engineers) of the Golden Gate bridge in San Francisco.

objets.nom: Salazar tombe malade et est remplacé par Marcelo Caetano.
objets.fr: Salazar tombe malade et est remplacé par Marcelo Caetano.

objets.nom: Mort de Salazar.
objets.fr: Mort de Salazar.

objets.notes: Amílcar Cabral, leader of the PAIGC, is assassinated in Conakry by a disgruntled former associate under influence of the Portuguese Political Police DGS.

objets.nom: Révolution des Œillets
objets.fr: Révolution des Œillets
objets.notes: fin de la dictature militaire, début de la décolonisation.

objets.nom: The Carnation Revolution puts an end to the authoritarian regime of Estado Novo
objets.notes: The Carnation Revolution puts an end to the authoritarian regime of Estado Novo. Prime-minister Marcello Caetano exiled to Brazil

objets.nom: A meeting takes place in Haga (near Stockholm in Sweden) where the Committee for Friendship and…
objets.notes: A meeting takes place in Haga (near Stockholm in Sweden) where the Committee for Friendship and Solidarity with Democracy and Socialism in Portugal is created. This Committee supported democratic trends in Portugal and opposed pro-soviet communist tendencies. In the meeting were present Olof Palme, Harold Wilson, Helmut Schmidt, Bruno Kreisky,…

objets.nom: Le général António Ramalho Eanes est élu à la présidence de la République.
objets.fr: Le général António Ramalho Eanes est élu à la présidence de la République.

objets.fr: Entrée du Portugal dans la Communauté économique européenne
objets.notes: entrée du Portugal dans la Communauté économique européenne. Mário Soares est élu président.

objets.fr: Jorge Sampaio est élu président de la République (14 janvier).

objets.notes: In the first Portuguese abortion referendum, the proposal to allow the abortion until 10 weeks of pregnancy is rejected by 50.91% of the voters. This is the first referendum in the History of the Portuguese democracy.

objets.notes: in the regionalisation referendum, a proposal to establish, in mainland Portugal, 8 administrative regions and to disestablish the 18 districts, is rejected in the polls: in the first question, the simple institution of the administrative regions is rejected by 60.67% of the voters; in the second question, the proposal to create 8 regions is…

objets.fr: Macao, colonie, est rétrocédée à la Chine.

objets.nom: L'escudo (monnaie portugaise) laisse place à l'euro ().
objets.fr: L'escudo (monnaie portugaise) laisse place à l'euro ().

objets.nom: Hintze Ribeiro Bridge disaster
objets.notes: 59 people die in the collapse of an old bridge on the Douro river. Hours after the accident, Jorge Coelho, Minister of Transportation, resigns.

objets.nom: Jorge Sampaio est réélu président de la République (14 janvier).
objets.fr: Jorge Sampaio est réélu président de la République (14 janvier).

objets.fr: Législatives anticipées : le Parti social-démocrate (centre-droit) forme une coalition de gouvernement…

objets.fr: Barroso devient le président de la Commission européenne.

objets.fr: Victoire aux élections législatives, à la majorité absolue, du parti socialiste portugais.

objets.fr: Élection au premier tour de la présidentielle d'Anibal Cavaco Silva (droite).

objets.notes: In 2010, the official infant mortality rate was 2.53 per mil, the lowest ever recorded in Portugal (1.6‰ below the UE-27, 2010 average), placing the country among the top-5 in the European Union in this particular value of Human Development.

objets.nom: Nouvelle division de l'Ibérie et naissance de la Lusitanie, de la Bétique et de la Tarraconaise.
objets.fr: Nouvelle division de l'Ibérie et naissance de la Lusitanie, de la Bétique et de la Tarraconaise.

objets.notes: guerres contre les Cantabres et les Asturiens (-29/-19). Rome domine la totalité de l'espace ibérique.
César vainc les partisans de Pompée à Ilerda et définitivement à Munda en -45.
Jules César commande une seconde invasion en Galice, en débarquant à Brigantium (La Corogne). Les Galiciens deviennent la plus importante force auxiliaire des légions romaines.

objets.nom: Le bétique Sénèque et son neveu Lucain meurent à Rome par ordre de Néron.
objets.fr: Le bétique Sénèque et son neveu Lucain meurent à Rome par ordre de Néron.

objets.notes: Marcus Perperna se rallie à Pompée et assassine Sertorius à Osca (Huesca). Fin des guerres sertoriennes.

objets.nom: L'empereur Vespasien concède la citoyenneté romaine aux Hispaniques.
objets.fr: L'empereur Vespasien concède la citoyenneté romaine aux Hispaniques.

objets.notes: guerres sertoriennes en Hispanie.
prise et destruction de Numance par Scipion Émilien. L'occupation romaine continue à travers la vallée de l'Èbre et la Meseta.

le proconsul romain Decimus Iunius Brutus mène des campagnes victorieuses en Ibérie, au sud de l'actuel Portugal, avant de se diriger plus au nord. 60 000 combattants de la tribu des Gallaeci sont défaits par les légions romaines à la bataille du Douro. Brutus reçoit le nom de Gallaicus.
début de la guerre lusitano-romaine dans laquelle Viriato s'impose comme le chef des peuples indigènes jusqu'à son assassinat en -139.

conquête de Cadix, dernier bastion carthaginois dans la péninsule et victoire romaine de Ilipa. L'Hispanie demeure sous le contrôle de Rome et est divisée en Hispanie ultérieure et Hispanie citérieure.
résistance et chute de Sagonte, alliée de Rome, assiégée par Hannibal Barca. Début de la deuxième guerre punique.
fondation de Carthago Nova (Carthagène), capitale de l'empire barcide en occident.
traité de l'Èbre entre Romains et Carthaginois.
Hamilcar Barca déplace vers le sud de la Péninsule la base des opérations militaires carthaginoises.

objets.nom: Des Francs et des Alamans envahissent la Péninsule, ils y restent 10 ans.
objets.fr: Des Francs et des Alamans envahissent la Péninsule, ils y restent 10 ans.

objets.fr: Nouvelle division de l'Hispanie en Gallécie, Tarraconaise, Carthaginoise, Bétique et Lusitanie.

objets.notes: fondation de la ville celtibère de Numance.

objets.fr: Concile d'Elvire (aujourd'hui Grenade), premier synode de l'Église hispanique.
