objets.fr: Théodose , originaire de Gallécie, est nommé empereur romain et byzantin, le dernier à régner sur un…
objets.notes: Théodose , originaire de Gallécie, est nommé empereur romain et byzantin, le dernier à régner sur un empire réunifié.

objets.nom: Le concile de Caesaraugusta (Saragosse) se prononce contre le priscillianisme, reconnu comme hérésie en…
objets.fr: Le concile de Caesaraugusta (Saragosse) se prononce contre le priscillianisme, reconnu comme hérésie en…
objets.notes: le concile de Caesaraugusta (Saragosse) se prononce contre le priscillianisme, reconnu comme hérésie en 384, au concile de Bordeaux.

objets.nom: Des peuplades germaniques (Suèves, Wisigoths et Vandales) arrivent en Hispanie.
objets.fr: Des peuplades germaniques (Suèves, Wisigoths et Vandales) arrivent en Hispanie.

objets.nom: Rechila, roi suève, conquiert Séville pendant que les Bagaudes ravagent la vallée de l'Èbre.
objets.fr: Rechila, roi suève, conquiert Séville pendant que les Bagaudes ravagent la vallée de l'Èbre.

objets.nom: Bataille de la rivière Órbigo, défaite des Suèves près d'Astorga face aux Wisigoths.
objets.fr: Bataille de la rivière Órbigo, défaite des Suèves près d'Astorga face aux Wisigoths.

objets.nom: Bréviaire d'Alaric, recueil de droit romain promulgué par le roi wisigoth Alaric II, en 506. Cette…
objets.fr: Bréviaire d'Alaric, recueil de droit romain promulgué par le roi wisigoth Alaric II, en 506. Cette…
objets.notes: bréviaire d'Alaric, recueil de droit romain promulgué par le roi wisigoth Alaric II, en 506. Cette dénomination n'apparaît qu'au XVIe siècle pour remplacer la lex romana wisigothorum. Il s'agit principalement de la compilation et de l'interprétation du Code de Théodose (438), destinée aux sujets gallo-romains et romano-hispaniques des Wisigoths.

objets.nom: IIIe concile de Tolède
objets.fr: IIIe concile de Tolède
objets.notes: IIIe concile de Tolède. Le catholicisme devient la religion officielle du royaume wisigoth, anciennement disciples de l'arianisme. Les conciles deviennent les piliers de l'organisation politique.
Arganthonios, roi de Tartessos. Voyage de Colaios de Samos au-delà des Colonnes d'Hercule décrit par Hérodote. Nouvelle vague celtique vers la Meseta.
civilisation du fer dans la Meseta (Las Cogotas)

objets.nom: Luttes intestines entre Rodéric et le clan de Wittiza
objets.fr: Luttes intestines entre Rodéric et le clan de Wittiza
objets.notes: luttes intestines entre Rodéric et le clan de Wittiza. Campagne du roi contre les Vascons. Conquête de l'Espagne wisigothique par l'armée maure de Tariq ibn Ziyad venue aider Witiza.

objets.nom: Victoire de Pélage sur des troupes musulmanes à Covadonga
objets.fr: Victoire de Pélage sur des troupes musulmanes à Covadonga
objets.notes: victoire de Pélage sur des troupes musulmanes à Covadonga. Début de la Reconquista.

objets.nom: Battle of Covadonga
objets.notes: Forces loyal to Pelagius decimated an Umayyad army sent to reconquer them in a valley in the Picos de Europa.

objets.nom: Grande famine dans la Péninsule
objets.fr: Grande famine dans la Péninsule
objets.notes: grande famine dans la Péninsule. Rébellion des Berbères dans la Péninsule Ibérique contre le pouvoir arabe, ce qui permet aux chrétiens du nord de reconquérir la Galice. Mise en place du désert du Douro, stratégie d'Alphonse des Asturies pour pallier une insuffisance d'hommes et freiner l'expansion maure vers le nord.

objets.nom: Bataille de Roncevaux entre l'armée de Charlemagne, venue prendre en vain Saragosse, et les Vascons.
objets.fr: Bataille de Roncevaux entre l'armée de Charlemagne, venue prendre en vain Saragosse, et les Vascons.

objets.nom: Battle of the Burbia River
objets.notes: An Asturian force attacked a Cordoban army near Villafranca del Bierzo on its return to Córdoba and was defeated.

objets.nom: Battle of Lutos
objets.notes: A Cordoban army returning from a scorched earth campaign in modern Álava was wiped out by an Asturian force.

objets.nom: Battle of Las Babias
objets.notes: Córdoba attacked and routed an Asturian force near Astorga, Spain.
entrée de groupes celtes dans la Péninsule en provenance de la vallée du Rhône. Ils s'installent dans la partie septentrionale.

objets.nom: Battle of Pancorbo (816)
objets.notes: Córdoba slaughtered a Basque-Asturian force defending the Basque homeland in the Pyrenees at Pancorbo.

objets.nom: Battle of Roncevaux Pass (824)
objets.notes: A combined force of Basques and the Banu Qasi, both vassals of the emirate of Córdoba, defeated a Carolingian military expedition in the Roncevaux Pass. The Basque chieftain Íñigo Arista of Pamplona was crowned king of Navarre at Pamplona.

objets.nom: Battle of the Bridge of Cornellana
objets.notes: Forces loyal to Bermudo's son Ramiro I of Asturias defeated Nepotian in modern Salas, Asturias.

objets.nom: Attaques normandes contre Gijón, Lisbonne, Cadix...
objets.fr: Attaques normandes contre Gijón, Lisbonne, Cadix...

objets.nom: Battle of Albelda (851)
objets.notes: Ordoño suppressed a Basque revolt in northeastern Asturias and expelled an opportunistic Cordoban invasion near Albelda.

objets.nom: Battle of Guadalacete
objets.notes: Asturian and Pamplonan forces arriving in support of a revolt of the people of Toledo, Spain were routed by a Cordoban army.

objets.nom: Battle of the Morcuera
objets.notes: Córdoba attacked Asturias, forcing the retreat of Asturian forces and their Castilian allies along the valley of the Ebro.

objets.nom: First Battle of Cellorigo
objets.notes: Vela Jiménez, count of the Asturian county of Álava, repelled an attempted conquest by the Emirate of Córdoba of an important mountain pass at Cellorigo.

objets.nom: Second Battle of Cellorigo
objets.notes: Vela Jiménez repelled an attempted conquest by the Emirate of Córdoba of an important mountain pass at Cellorigo.

objets.nom: Day of Zamora
objets.notes: The Asturian defenders of Zamora, Spain dealt heavy casualties to a Cordoban force attempting to conquer it. The heads of the besiegers were displayed on the city walls.

objets.nom: Battle of San Esteban de Gormaz (917)
objets.notes: Leonese forces broke a Cordoban siege of San Esteban de Gormaz.

objets.nom: Victoire des armées de la Navarre et du Léon à San Esteban de Gormaz
objets.fr: Victoire des armées de la Navarre et du Léon à San Esteban de Gormaz
objets.notes: victoire des armées de la Navarre et du Léon à San Esteban de Gormaz. Repeuplement des terres du Douro.

objets.nom: Battle of Valdejunquera
objets.notes: A Cordoban army invading Castile routed a joint Leonese-Navarrese force at Valdejunquera, probably between modern Estella-Lizarra and Pamplona, forcing the abandonment by León of Clunia.

objets.nom: Battle of Alhandic
objets.notes: Cordoban forces conquered the Leonese city of Zamora, Spain with great cost in lives to both sides.

objets.nom: Battle of Simancas
objets.notes: A battle began near Simancas which would see a joint Leonese-Navarrese force repel an attempted Cordoban conquest of the lands around the Douro.

objets.nom: Battle of Rueda
objets.notes: A Cordoban force dealt a decisive defeat to a joint Leonese-Navarrese army in Rueda, Valladolid.

objets.nom: Battle of Torrevicente
objets.notes: A Cordoban force dealt a bloody defeat to a rebel Cordoban general and his Vigueran and Castilian allies, probably near Atienza.
début de l'Âge du fer dans la Péninsule.

objets.nom: Battle of Cervera
objets.notes: Córdoba defeated the combined forces of García of the Good Laws and García Gómez, count of Saldaña, Carrión and Liébana on a punitive expedition near modern Espinosa de Cervera.

objets.nom: Sanche III de Navarre, dit le Grand, roi d'Aragon et roi de Navarre et comte de Castille à partir de 1029.
objets.fr: Sanche III de Navarre, dit le Grand, roi d'Aragon et roi de Navarre et comte de Castille à partir de 1029.

objets.nom: Première union des royaumes de Galice, de Léon et de Castille sous Ferdinand le Grand.
objets.fr: Première union des royaumes de Galice, de Léon et de Castille sous Ferdinand le Grand.

objets.nom: Battle of Atapuerca
objets.notes: Navarrese and Leonese forces met near modern Atapuerca, Province of Burgos. García Sánchez III and his tutor Fortún Sánchez were killed. García Sánchez III's son Sancho IV of Peñalén of Pamplona succeeded him as king under the regency of Stephanie, Queen of Navarre. León annexed Navarrese territories south of the Ebro.

objets.nom: Battle of Graus
objets.notes: Ramiro I died in a failed attempt to take Graus from the taifa of Zaragoza. He was succeeded by his son Sancho Ramírez.

objets.nom: Synod of Jaca (1063)
objets.notes: Ramiro I presided over a synod in Jaca which reestablished the Roman Catholic Diocese of Huesca.

objets.nom: Crusade of Barbastro
objets.notes: At the urging of the pope Pope Alexander II, a coalition of Aragon, Urgell, Aquitaine and the Papal States conquered Barbastro from the taifa of Lérida.

objets.nom: Battle of Paterna
objets.notes: Valencian forces pursuing the army of Ferdinand the Great, then in retreat from a failed siege of Valencia, were ambushed and wiped out at Paterna.

objets.nom: Battle of Llantada
objets.notes: Sancho the Strong defeated Alfonso the Brave at Llantadilla, in the taifa of Badajoz near modern Melgar de Fernamental.

objets.nom: Battle of Golpejera
objets.notes: Sancho the Strong defeated and captured Alfonso the Brave near Carrión de los Condes. The latter was released and sent into exile in Toledo.

objets.nom: Battle of Cabra
objets.notes: Seville defeated the invading forces of Granada. Both sides were aided by Castilian knights.

objets.nom: Battle of Morella
objets.notes: A Zaragozan army led by the general El Cid decisively defeated the forces of Sancho Ramírez near Tortosa.

objets.nom: Battle of Piedra Pisada
objets.notes: A Zaragozan army skirmished with the forces of Alfonso the Brave, then following the valley of the Cinca from Naval, Huesca to El Grado.

objets.nom: Battle of Sagrajas
objets.notes: Yusuf ibn Tashfin, the sultan of the Almoravid dynasty, at the head of a coalition of Andalusian taifas, defeated León and Castile and Aragon in a bloody battle near Badajoz. The taifas renounced payment of the parias.

objets.nom: Siege of Tudela
objets.notes: Alfonso the Brave, Sancho Ramírez, Odo I, Duke of Burgundy, the duke of Burgundy, and William the Carpenter, viscount of Melun, laid siege to the Zaragozan fortress at Tudela, Navarre.

objets.nom: Battle of Alcoraz
objets.notes: Peter I defeated the Zaragozan forces sent to relieve his siege of Huesca.

objets.nom: Battle of Bairén
objets.notes: An Aragonese army pinned between Almoravid forces and the Mediterranean Sea routed their enemies near modern Gandia.

objets.nom: Battle of Consuegra
objets.notes: An Almoravid force defeated one of Alfonso the Brave's armies near Consuegra.
les Phéniciens fondent Gadès (aujourd'hui Cadix). Entrée de groupes indo-Européens dans la Péninsule.

objets.nom: Battle of Uclés (1108)
objets.notes: The Almoravids dealt a decisive defeat to the forces of Alfonso the Brave at Uclés, reconquering the city as well as Cuenca, Spain, Huete and Ocaña, Spain. Alfonso the Brave's son and heir Sancho Alfónsez was killed in flight by local Muslims.

objets.nom: Battle of Candespina
objets.notes: Alfonso the Battler, joined by Henry, Count of Portugal, the count of Portugal, defeated forces loyal to the former's wife Urraca the Restless at Fresno de Cantespino.

objets.nom: Battle of Viadangos
objets.notes: The noble Pedro Fróilaz de Traba and Diego Gelmírez, archbishop of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Santiago de Compostela, marching in support of Urraca the Restless, were routed at Villadangos del Páramo by a superior force led by Alfonso the Battler.

objets.nom: Battle of Cutanda
objets.notes: Alfonso the Battler defeated forces of the Almoravid dynasty at Cutanda near Calamocha, conquering that town as well as Calatayud and Daroca for Aragon.

objets.nom: Siege of Bayonne
objets.notes: Alfonso the Battler laid siege to the Aquitainian city of Bayonne, probably with the intent of impressing Alfonso the Emperor's vassal Alfonso Jordan, the count of Toulouse.

objets.nom: Battle of Fraga
objets.notes: The Almoravids broke an Aragonese siege of Fraga. Alfonso the Battler was wounded.

objets.nom: Siege of Coria (1138)
objets.notes: Alfonso the Emperor failed to take the Almoravid city of Coria, Caceres. His commanding general Rodrigo Martínez was killed in the assault.

objets.nom: Battle of Ourique
objets.notes: Afonso defeated an Almoravid force deep inside Almoravid territory at Ourique. His soldiers proclaimed him king of Portugal.

objets.nom: Siege of Oreja
objets.notes: Alfonso the Emperor laid siege to the Almoravid castle at Colmenar de Oreja.

objets.nom: Traité de Carrión entre Alphonse VII de Castille, roi de Galice, de Léon et de Castille, et…
objets.fr: Traité de Carrión entre Alphonse VII de Castille, roi de Galice, de Léon et de Castille, et…
objets.notes: traité de Carrión entre Alphonse VII de Castille, roi de Galice, de Léon et de Castille, et Raimond-Bérenger IV de Barcelone pour le partage du royaume de Navarre.

objets.nom: Battle of Valdevez
objets.notes: Afonso invaded Galicia. Alfonso the Emperor met him at Arcos de Valdevez and was defeated.

objets.nom: Siege of Coria (1142)
objets.notes: Alfonso the Emperor laid siege to the Almoravid city of Coria, Caceres.

objets.nom: Second Crusade
objets.notes: Alfonso the Emperor, Ramon Berenguer the Saint and García Ramírez, with the support of the Genoese and Pisan navies, conquered the Almoravid port city of Almería. One-third of the city was granted to Genoa, the rest to Castile.

objets.nom: Le calife almohade Abu Yaqub Yusuf débarque en Espagne et s'installe à Séville.
objets.fr: Le calife almohade Abu Yaqub Yusuf débarque en Espagne et s'installe à Séville.

objets.nom: Traité de Cazola entre Alphonse II d'Aragon et Alphonse VIII de Castille pour le partage des futurs…
objets.fr: Traité de Cazola entre Alphonse II d'Aragon et Alphonse VIII de Castille pour le partage des futurs…
objets.notes: traité de Cazola entre Alphonse II d'Aragon et Alphonse VIII de Castille pour le partage des futurs territoires conquis sur les musulmans au sud de la Péninsule Ibérique.

objets.nom: Battle of Alarcos
objets.notes: The Almohad Caliphate decisively defeated a Castilian force in what is now the province of Ciudad Real, forcing the latter's retreat to Toledo, Spain and cession of Trujillo, Cáceres, Montánchez and Talavera de la Reina.
civilisation des champs d'urnes. Origine mythique de Tartessos.

objets.nom: Albigensian Crusade
objets.notes: The pope Pope Innocent III called for a crusade to exterminate Catharism in Languedoc.

objets.nom: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
objets.notes: A coalition of Castilian, Aragonese, Portuguese and Navarrese forces, joined by the Order of Santiago, the Order of Calatrava, the Knights Templar and French and Leonese volunteers, decisively defeated an Almohad army in what is now the Province of Jaén. The caliph Muhammad al-Nasir was forced into flight.

objets.nom: Battle of Muret

The synod focuses on the evangelization of the Slavs.

objets.nom: Siege of Trsat
objets.notes: Invading Frankish forces were repelled from Trsat, resulting in the death of their commander Eric of Friuli.

objets.nom: Ljudevit Posavski, Prince of Pannonian Slavs, becomes a Prince of Serbs in Paganias city of Srb as the…
objets.notes: Ljudevit Posavski, Prince of Pannonian Slavs, becomes a Prince of Serbs in Paganias city of Srb as the Franks approach the Serbian lands. This Serbo-Croatian defence union expires in 823.

objets.nom: In the Principality of Serbia, the House of Višeslavić-Vlastimirović strengthens the state against its…
objets.notes: In the Principality of Serbia, the House of Višeslavić-Vlastimirović strengthens the state against its immediate neighbors the Frankish Empire, the First Bulgarian Empire and the Byzantine Empire. Vlastimir of Serbia repels Bulgarian attacks led by Khan Boris.

objets.nom: The Balaton Principality emerges in Pannonia.
The principality of Prince Kocelj (Balaton Principality) loses its independence.
Arnulf of Carinthia (850–899) a grandson of Louis the German assumes his title of King of the East…
objets.notes: Arnulf of Carinthia (850–899) a grandson of Louis the German assumes his title of King of the East Franks and becomes the first Duke of Carinthia.

objets.nom: Accord between Arnulf of Carinthia and the Bohemian Duke Bořivoj (reigned 870–895), Bohemia is freed…
objets.notes: Accord between Arnulf of Carinthia and the Bohemian Duke Bořivoj (reigned 870–895), Bohemia is freed from the danger of invasion.

objets.nom: Finno-Ugric Magyars, led by Árpád, settle in the Pannonian plain
objets.notes: Finno-Ugric Magyars, led by Árpád, settle in the Pannonian plain. The centre of their settlement becomes the region around the Theiss River (Hungary).

objets.nom: The Magyars settle in Slavic Pannonia (Modern-day Hungary) effectively splitting the South Slavs from…
objets.notes: The Magyars settle in Slavic Pannonia (Modern-day Hungary) effectively splitting the South Slavs from the West Slavs. Occasional clashes with Byzantine, Bulgarian and Serbian forces in frontier regions.

objets.nom: Višeslav's son, or grandson, ruled during the uprisings of Ljudevit Posavski against the Franks in…
objets.notes: Višeslav's son, or grandson, ruled during the uprisings of Ljudevit Posavski against the Franks in 819–822. According to the Royal Frankish Annals, in 822, Ljudevit went from his seat in Sisak to the Serbs somewhere in western Balkans – the Serbs are mentioned as reportedly holding the great/large part of Dalmatia ("Sorabos, quae natio magnam…

objets.nom: Croatian–Bulgarian battle of 926
objets.notes: Tomislav defeated the invading forces of the Bulgarian Empire.

objets.nom: German king Otto I (912–973, reigned 936–973) defeats the Magyars at the Battle of Lechfeld near…
objets.notes: German king Otto I (912–973, reigned 936–973) defeats the Magyars at the Battle of Lechfeld near Augsburg, halting their advance in Central Europe.

objets.nom: The March of Austria is established
objets.notes: The March of Austria is established. Carantania becomes a duchy in its own right, including Styria and today's East Tirol

objets.nom: Siege of Zadar
objets.notes: Emperor Samuil of Western Bulgarian Tsardom launched a military campaign against Kingdom of Croatia and besieged the city of Zadar.

objets.nom: Battle of Lastovo
objets.notes: Doge Pietro II Orseolo of the Republic of Venice attacked the Town of Lastovo in the Kingdom of Croatia and destroyed it.

objets.nom: Carinthia, Styria and Carniola provinces emerge on the territory of Carantania.
The Freising Manuscripts, the first Latin-script continuous text in a Slavic language and the oldest…
objets.notes: The Freising Manuscripts, the first Latin-script continuous text in a Slavic language and the oldest document in Slovene, are written.

objets.nom: Byzantine rule is imposed upon inner Serbia; it becomes a thema (region) directly subjugated to Constantinople
objets.notes: Byzantine rule is imposed upon inner Serbia; it becomes a thema (region) directly subjugated to Constantinople. Constantine Diogenes (a Greek) is mentioned as the strategos of Serbia. The rise of the Vojislavljević dynasty in Duklja. Littoral Serbia remains independent and wages wars against the Byzantines and eventually succeeds in freeing the…

objets.nom: The Vojislavljević dynasty claims the Serbian throne of Duklja as legal heir of the Vlastimirović dynasty
objets.notes: The Vojislavljević dynasty claims the Serbian throne of Duklja as legal heir of the Vlastimirović dynasty. Under Stefan Vojislav Duklja becomes independent as the First Serbian Realm becoming the new core of the Serbian world.

objets.nom: The East-West Schism splits Christianity in 1054. vast majority of Serbs opt for Orthodox Christianity…
objets.notes: The East-West Schism splits Christianity in 1054. vast majority of Serbs opt for Orthodox Christianity due to deep Byzantine influences, but many in the coastal lands embrace Catholicism influenced by Venice. The Archbishopric of Bar is established by the Vatican in 1089.

objets.nom: Mihailo I Vojislavljević assumes the title of the King of Duklja in Ston becoming the first…
objets.notes: Mihailo I Vojislavljević assumes the title of the King of Duklja in Ston becoming the first internationally recognized Serbian king. His title was Ruler of Tribals and Serbs and ruled most of today's Montenegro and Dalmatia. His son Konstantin Bodin asserts the throne of Second Bulgarian Empire and annexes large parts of Bulgaria to the Serbian…

objets.nom: Battle of Gvozd Mountain
objets.notes: King Petar Snačić died in a loss to King Coloman of Hungary.

objets.nom: Raymond IV of Toulouse, leader of the Crusaders, meets with King Bodin in the city of Skadar
objets.notes: Raymond IV of Toulouse, leader of the Crusaders, meets with King Bodin in the city of Skadar. The Vukanović family will rule most of the aforementioned territories for decades to come. Tensions will rise among the noble families of inner Serbia, Duklja and its dominions leading to the disintegration of the Realm in the mid-12th century and a…

objets.nom: King Konstantin Bodin's relative Stefan Nemanja is born in Ribnica, Duklja
objets.notes: King Konstantin Bodin's relative Stefan Nemanja is born in Ribnica, Duklja. Exiled by his father's opponents he settles in Ras, in the region of Raška. He is the founder of the most powerful royal house of Medieval Serbia: the Nemanjić dynasty. The dynasty will have a decisive role in shaping and reaffirming the national identity of the Serbs…

objets.nom: The first mention of Celje in the early Middle Ages under the name of Cylie in Admont's Chronicle
objets.notes: The first mention of Celje in the early Middle Ages under the name of Cylie in Admont's Chronicle. (to 1137)

objets.nom: The Grand Prince Stefan Nemanja sides with Venice, Duchy of Austria and Principality of Hungary…
objets.notes: the Grand Prince Stefan Nemanja sides with Venice, Duchy of Austria and Principality of Hungary undermining Byzantine authority in the Adriatic Sea.

objets.nom: Stefan Nemanja repels the Byzantine forces proclaiming the independence of Serbia which triggers an…
objets.notes: Stefan Nemanja repels the Byzantine forces proclaiming the independence of Serbia which triggers an anti-Byzantine revolt in Bulgaria and Wallacia.

objets.nom: Holy Roman Emperor Friedrich Barbarossa and his 100,000 man army are hosted by Grand Prince Stefan…
objets.notes: Holy Roman Emperor Friedrich Barbarossa and his 100,000 man army are hosted by Grand Prince Stefan Nemanja in Niš during the Third Crusade. Their alliance would give the Serbian Grand Prince enough time to take parts of Kosovo from the Byzantine Empire.

objets.nom: King Stefan the First-Crowned's brother, Prince Rastko Nemanjić (Saint Sava), establishes an…
objets.notes: King Stefan the First-Crowned's brother, Prince Rastko Nemanjić (Saint Sava), establishes an autocephalous Serbian Orthodox Church with the support of the Patriarch of Constantinople putting an end to religious divisions among Serbs. Stefan Nemanja becomes another patron saint of the Serbian Orthodox Church and is known as Saint Simeon.

objets.nom: Bohemian king Ottokar II. (reigned as a king 1253–1278) a candidate for the German throne refuses to…
objets.notes: Bohemian king Ottokar II. (reigned as a king 1253–1278) a candidate for the German throne refuses to appear or to restore the provinces of Austria, Styria, Carinthia and Carniola, which he has seized.

objets.nom: The Kingdom of Syrmia is annexed by the Medieval Kingdom of Serbia following the death of King Stefan…
objets.notes: The Kingdom of Syrmia is annexed by the Medieval Kingdom of Serbia following the death of King Stefan Dragutin of Syrmia. Belgrade is returned to the control of the Kingdom of Hungary. Clashes with the Kingdom of Hungary over northern Serbia results in the division of the former Kingdom of Syrmia with the Kingdom of Hungary gaining all territories…

objets.nom: Battle of Bliska
objets.notes: Mladen lost to a coalition of Croatian noblemen at Trogir.

objets.nom: King Stefan Dušan conquers most of European Byzantium launching his first Siege of Constantinople
objets.notes: King Stefan Dušan conquers most of European Byzantium launching his first Siege of Constantinople. The Second Serbian Kingdom becomes the largest state in Southern and Eastern Europe.

objets.nom: Czar Stefan Dušan The Great dies of poisoning following clashes with Hungarians and invading Turks
objets.notes: Czar Stefan Dušan The Great dies of poisoning following clashes with Hungarians and invading Turks. Stefan Uroš V of Serbia assumes the throne of the Serbian Empire triggering dynastic clashes among Serbian nobility. Simeon Uroš declares himself Emperor in Thessaly, Balšići took over Montenegro, Mrnjavčevići Macedonia, Lazarevići – Moravian…

objets.nom: The Ottoman Turks break into Europe and the Serbian domain of Macedonia clashing with the Christian…
objets.notes: The Ottoman Turks break into Europe and the Serbian domain of Macedonia clashing with the Christian League led by Vukašin Mrnjavčević in the Battle of Maritsa in the region of Thrace. This was a decisive Ottoman victory.

objets.nom: A 20,000 strong Serbian army led by Prince Lazar Hrebeljanović of Rascia, Vlatko Vuković of Bosnia,…
objets.notes: A 20,000 strong Serbian army led by Prince Lazar Hrebeljanović of Rascia, Vlatko Vuković of Bosnia, Miloš Obilić and most other prominent nobles faced the better equipped and trained Ottoman army in the Battle of Kosovo. Casualties on both sides were extremely high – both leaders died in the battle (Serbian Lazar Hrebeljanović and Ottoman sultan…

objets.nom: According to myth Miloš Obilić establishes the Order of the Dragon of St George, an alliance of Serb…
objets.notes: According to myth Miloš Obilić establishes the Order of the Dragon of St George, an alliance of Serb aristocracy against the Ottoman invaders. Out of 12 knights only 1 survives the battle passing his credentials to Stefan Lazarević and various European draconists (knights of Austria, Naples, Kingdom of Hungary, Spain, etc.)

objets.nom: Bloody Sabor of Križevci
objets.notes: Croatian Ban Stjepan II Lacković was killed in Križevci for supporting Ladislaus against King Sigismund.

objets.nom: The Habsburg Duke Ernest the Iron (1377–1424) thrones according to the ancient Karantanian ritual of…
objets.notes: The Habsburg Duke Ernest the Iron (1377–1424) thrones according to the ancient Karantanian ritual of installing dukes on the Duke's Stone and he addresses again as an archduke.

objets.nom: Belgrade is returned to the control of the Kingdom of Hungary following the death of Despot Stefan…
objets.notes: Belgrade is returned to the control of the Kingdom of Hungary following the death of Despot Stefan Lazarević. Đurađ Branković moves his capital to Smederevo.

objets.nom: Battle of Varna
objets.notes: Władysław died in a battlefield loss to the Ottoman Empire. The Hungarian nobility elected Ladislaus, then imprisoned in Schloss Ort by his second cousin Frederick III, Holy Roman Emperor, King of Hungary, with John Hunyadi acting as regent.

objets.nom: The Siege of Belgrade, one of the greatest crusade wars of medieval times takes place in Belgrade as…
objets.notes: The Siege of Belgrade, one of the greatest crusade wars of medieval times takes place in Belgrade as Sultan Mehmed II besieges the city with 150,000 soldiers and over 100 ships. Joint Hungarian and Serbian troops, aided by other Christian nations, repel the Ottoman forces. Pope Calixtus III praises Belgrade and its defender John Hunyadi as the…

objets.nom: Battle of Mohács
objets.notes: Louis died childless in a crushing defeat at the hands of the Ottoman Empire near Mohács.

objets.nom: 1527 election in Cetin
objets.notes: The Croatian nobility unanimously elected Ferdinand King and confirmed the succession to his heirs, ending the personal union with Hungary.

objets.nom: Battle of Tarcal
objets.notes: Forces allied to Ferdinand dealt a bloody defeat to supporters of Zápolya.

objets.nom: Battle of Szina
objets.notes: Zápolya was defeated and forced to flee to Poland.

objets.nom: Klis Fortress succumbs to the Ottomans enabling Senj to become a Croatian Habsburg Uskok (pirate)…
objets.notes: Klis Fortress succumbs to the Ottomans enabling Senj to become a Croatian Habsburg Uskok (pirate) stronghold in the Adriatic Sea. Although nominally accepting the sovereignty of the Habsburg Emperor Ferdinand I, Uskoci were a law unto themselves, comprise by refugees from Croatia, Bosnia and Serbia.

objets.nom: Primož Trubar publishes the first books in Slovene, Catechismus and Abecedarium.
Siege of Szigetvár
objets.notes: The forces of the Ottoman Empire suffered losses taking the fortress at Szigetvár that forced them to abandon their advance on Vienna.

objets.nom: The region of Prekmurje is occupied by Ottomans during the Siege of Szigetvar.
The Republic of Venice and the Ottoman Empire clash over Uskoks and their allegiance
objets.notes: The Republic of Venice and the Ottoman Empire clash over Uskoks and their allegiance. The Kingdom of Spain, the Habsburg Empire and the Papal States join the war in support of the Venetians and Uskoks ultimately defeating the Turks. Stojan Janković was one of the military leaders of Dalmatian uskoks and a high-ranking Venetian military officer.

objets.nom: Battle of Slunj
objets.notes: Invading Ottoman forces were defeated by the defending Croatian army.

objets.nom: Battle of Sisak
objets.notes: Croatia dealt the Ottoman Empire a crushing defeat at Sisak.

objets.nom: The Battle of Sisak restores the balance of power and brings the expansion of the Ottoman Empire into…
objets.notes: The Battle of Sisak restores the balance of power and brings the expansion of the Ottoman Empire into the Slovene Lands to a halt.

objets.nom: An earthquake occurs near Ljubljana
objets.notes: An earthquake occurs near Ljubljana. It measures about 5 on the Moment magnitude scale or 4.9 on the Richter scale

objets.nom: Austro-Turkish War (1663–1664)
objets.notes: An Ottoman army invaded Hungary.

objets.nom: Battle of Saint Gotthard (1664)
objets.notes: Ottoman forces were dealt a decisive defeat by the League of the Rhine at Szentgotthárd.

objets.nom: Siege of Novi Zrin (1664)
objets.notes: Ottoman forces started to besiege the fortress in Međimurje County.

objets.nom: The Prekmurje region is occupied by Austrians.
Members of the Holy League – the Habsburg monarchy, the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, the Republic of…
objets.notes: Members of the Holy League – the Habsburg monarchy, the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, the Republic of Venice and the Russian Empire – conclude a peace treaty with the Ottoman Empire in which the territories of modern Vojvodina and Slavonia are passed to the Habsburg Empire in the Treaty of Karlovci. Following the Congress Sremski Karlovci and…

objets.nom: Holy Roman Empress Maria Theresa gives royal city rights to Novi Sad, the biggest Serbian settlement in…
objets.notes: Holy Roman Empress Maria Theresa gives royal city rights to Novi Sad, the biggest Serbian settlement in this Empire, following the capitulation of Habsburg Serbia. The city becomes known as Serbian Athens and a place of Serbian national revival. Most of Serbian culture, including its patriarchy (Metropolitanate of Karlovci), is now "in exile"…

objets.nom: Serbs permanently settle in the Russian Empire fleeing from Ottoman onslaughts in the Balkans
objets.notes: Serbs permanently settle in the Russian Empire fleeing from Ottoman onslaughts in the Balkans. The Czar gives them the territories of New Serbia and Slavo-Serbia. Today these Serbs are mostly assimilated into Ukraine although their traces still reflect in toponyms such as the city of Slovianoserbsk and the district of Slovianoserbsk in…

objets.nom: Turks abolish the Serbian Orthodox Church, subjugating it to Constantinople
objets.notes: Turks abolish the Serbian Orthodox Church, subjugating it to Constantinople. Two Serbian Patriarchs have found refuge in the Habsburg Empire during the preceding migrations. Southern Serbia slowly becomes Muslim in character, following the colonization of Muslim Albanians and Turkish peoples.

objets.nom: Napoleon annexes the Bay of Kotor to the First French Empire as a part of the Illyrian provinces
objets.notes: Napoleon annexes the Bay of Kotor to the First French Empire as a part of the Illyrian provinces. The Venetian Republic collapses after almost 1000 years of existence.

objets.nom: The Revolutionary Serbia is crushed facing the Ottomans as they invade the country with 200,000 soldiers
objets.notes: The Revolutionary Serbia is crushed facing the Ottomans as they invade the country with 200,000 soldiers. The lack of support from Imperial Russia, who were at war against Napoleon at the time, also contributed to the Serbian defeat. Widespread revenge attacks upon civilians, nobles and "Intelligentsia" trigger a second insurrection.

objets.nom: First works, tracings on Slovene territory of a railway route Vienna – Trieste in a so-called "Southern…
objets.notes: First works, tracings on Slovene territory of a railway route Vienna – Trieste in a so-called "Southern Railway" (Južna železnica) begin.

objets.nom: First works on the "Southern Railway" between Celje and Ljubljana begin
Battle of Pákozd
objets.notes: A revolutionary army seeking Hungarian independence from Austria forced a Croatian retreat.

objets.nom: Hungarian Revolution of 1848
objets.notes: Revolutionaries read the 12 points of the Hungarian Revolutionaries of 1848 before a crowd in Buda. The crowd marched on the Imperial Governing Council and forced Ferdinand's representatives to sign them.

objets.nom: The Spring of Nations erupts in Europe
objets.notes: The Spring of Nations erupts in Europe. The Serbs of Habsburg Empire demand self-rule according to the 1691 charter of Leopold I, Emperor of Austria. The Serbs proclaimed the creation of autonomous Serbian Vojvodina in Sremski Karlovci as the Serb army in the Habsburg monarchy clashes with the Hungarians.

objets.nom: Hermagoras Society (Mohorjeva družba), the first Slovene publisher, is established in Klagenfurt and…
objets.notes: Hermagoras Society (Mohorjeva družba), the first Slovene publisher, is established in Klagenfurt and publishes books in Slovene.

objets.nom: The "Carinthian railway" between Maribor and Klagenfurt is being built.
Austro-Prussian War
objets.notes: Prussia declared war on Austria.

objets.nom: Battle of Königgrätz
objets.notes: Austria suffered a devastating defeat at Prussian hands at Königgrätz.

objets.nom: Southwards, in the Principality of Serbia, Serbs rebel against the Ottoman authorities following the…
objets.notes: Southwards, in the Principality of Serbia, Serbs rebel against the Ottoman authorities following the bombardment of Belgrade. Great Britain and France urge the Ottomans to withdraw their troops from Serbia. The Principality of Serbia is now de facto independent— 50 years after the Second Serbian Uprising.

objets.nom: Rakovica Revolt
objets.notes: Politician Eugen Kvaternik declared the establishment of an independent Croatian government, seated at Rakovica and incorporating the Croatian Military Frontier.

objets.nom: Banat Krajina is abolished and included into Transleithania; despite the wishes of the majority Serbs…
objets.notes: Banat Krajina is abolished and included into Transleithania; despite the wishes of the majority Serbs and Germans. This is the first step towards the destruction of the Serb-populated Military Frontier inherited from the Habsburg Empire. By 1883 the Military Frontier is entirely abolished and incorporated into the Kingdom of Hungary and the…

objets.nom: The Russo-Turkish War begins
objets.notes: The Russo-Turkish War begins. The majority peoples, the Bosnian Serbs, launch an uprising against the Ottomans in Nevesinje declaring their unification with the Principality of Serbia. Nikola Pašić and Nicholas I of Montenegro proclaim the formal independence of Serbia and Montenegro. The Ottoman Empire declares war on Serbia and Montenegro.

objets.nom: Christian troops besiege Istanbul
objets.notes: Christian troops besiege Istanbul. Western interference stops the collapse of Ottoman Turkey by acknowledging de jure independence of Montenegro, Serbia and Romania with the Treaty of Berlin: all of whom have already been sovereign for some time prior to the Congress.

objets.nom: Strike of coal miners in the Central Sava Valley in Zagorje and Trbovlje.
The railway line on the route Radgona – Ljutomer is built.
1895 visit of Emperor Franz Joseph to Zagreb
objets.notes: Student protesters burned the Hungarian flag in Ban Jelačić Square.

objets.nom: The Young Turk Revolution starts within the Ottoman Empire
objets.notes: The Young Turk Revolution starts within the Ottoman Empire. As Bulgaria proclaims independence Serbia starts looking toward Kosovo and Macedonia in the south having to accept the Bosnian occupation.

objets.nom: The Kingdom of Montenegro is proclaimed in Cetinje under King Nicholas I of Montenegro
objets.notes: The Kingdom of Montenegro is proclaimed in Cetinje under King Nicholas I of Montenegro. His long-term programme is the restoration of the Serbian Empire with himself as an Emperor. Two rival Serbian dynasties now fight for supremacy among Serbs.

objets.nom: The Balkan Wars begin as Montenegro and Serbia declare war on the Ottoman Empire followed by Bulgaria…
objets.notes: The Balkan Wars begin as Montenegro and Serbia declare war on the Ottoman Empire followed by Bulgaria and Greece. The Balkan League besieges Constantinople.

objets.nom: Ivan Cankar in Ljubljana gives a speech Slovenes and Yugoslavs for the socialist society Vzajemnost…
objets.notes: Ivan Cankar in Ljubljana gives a speech Slovenes and Yugoslavs for the socialist society Vzajemnost (Mutuality) about Slovenes to unite politically but not culturally with other South Slavs and Yugoslavism.

objets.nom: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria
objets.notes: Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria was assassinated by Gavrilo Princip of the Bosnian separatist group Young Bosnia.

objets.nom: Austrian Archduke Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austrian throne, and his wife Countess Sophie, are killed…
objets.notes: Austrian Archduke Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austrian throne, and his wife Countess Sophie, are killed in Sarajevo, Bosnia at the hands of a pro-Serb nationalist assassin (a Bosnian Serb student Gavrilo Princip, a member of the Young Bosnia). World War I begins.

objets.nom: July Crisis
objets.notes: Austria-Hungary issued an ultimatum to Serbia, demanding, among other things, the right to participate in the investigation into the assassination of Franz Ferdinand, which Serbia refused.

objets.nom: The Assassination in Sarajevo of Archduke Franz Ferdinand sparks a major European crisis
objets.notes: The Assassination in Sarajevo of Archduke Franz Ferdinand sparks a major European crisis. The July Ultimatum is delivered to Serbian authorities demanding that Austro-Hungarian troops march into Serbia. The Kingdom of Serbia rejects the proposal supported by Imperial Russia, France and Great Britain. Austria-Hungary and the German Empire declare…

objets.nom: The Battle of Cer marks the First Allied Victory in the War as the Serbian First Army under field…
objets.notes: The Battle of Cer marks the First Allied Victory in the War as the Serbian First Army under field marshal Stepa Stepanović pushes the Austro-Hungarian Army across the Drina and Sava rivers expelling them from the Kingdom of Serbia. Serbia suffers 16,000 casualties, compared to 30,000 Austro-Hungarian casualties in this part of the Serbian Campaign.

objets.nom: Three months later Austria-Hungary launches the 2nd invasion on the Kingdom of Serbia
objets.notes: Three months later Austria-Hungary launches the 2nd invasion on the Kingdom of Serbia. Belgrade population falls from 110,000 to 20,000 following the bombing from the Sava and Danube rivers. The Battle of Kolubara begins resulting in the second decisive victory of the Serbian First Army and retreat of Austria-Hungary across the rivers a month…

objets.nom: World War I
objets.notes: Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia.

objets.nom: The 3rd invasion of Serbia begins in October
objets.notes: The 3rd invasion of Serbia begins in October. Austria-Hungary conquers Belgrade marching toward the south. Bulgaria invades Serbia cutting its supply route from Greece. The Serbian First Army is forced to retreat across the Sar Mountains of Albania and Kosovo. Despite Austro-Hungarian and Bulgarian occupation and the retreat of Serbian Army the…

objets.nom: The Soča River front
objets.notes: The Soča River front. In 11 Soča offensives Italians captured just Gorizia (Gorica) and a few frontier sites. On these battlefields many Slovenes in Austro-Hungarian army died (for example at the Battle of Doberdò). (to 1918)

objets.nom: The Yugoslav Committee, founded by the Austro-Hungarian Serbs and Croats in exile, is proclaimed in London
objets.notes: The Yugoslav Committee, founded by the Austro-Hungarian Serbs and Croats in exile, is proclaimed in London. Its primary goal is the liberation of the South Slavic lands from Austro-Hungary with the intention of joining the Kingdom of Serbia.

objets.nom: The secret London Pact offers, among many other European territories, western Dalmatia to the Kingdom of…
objets.notes: The secret London Pact offers, among many other European territories, western Dalmatia to the Kingdom of Italy and the eastern parts to the Kingdom of Serbia that would also be combined with Bosnia and Herzegovina, most of Slavonia and a large part of Vojvodina and northern Albania.

objets.nom: The Battle of Kobarid between Austrian forces, reinforced by German units and the Italian army
objets.notes: The Battle of Kobarid between Austrian forces, reinforced by German units and the Italian army. The Italian army withdraws to the Piave River, where they blocked the enemy before the arrive of the military assistance of the British and French. (to 9 November)

objets.nom: State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs is established in Zagreb
objets.notes: State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs is established in Zagreb. It becomes the political representative body of South Slavs in Austria-Hungary.

objets.nom: The Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes (First Yugoslavia) is proclaimed in Belgrade under Regent…
objets.notes: The Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes (First Yugoslavia) is proclaimed in Belgrade under Regent Alexander I. Belgrade unites with Zemun and Pančevo (formerly Serb-populated cities under the Habsburg Monarchy).

objets.nom: The State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs joins the Kingdom of Serbia fearing the possible Italian invasion
objets.notes: The State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs joins the Kingdom of Serbia fearing the possible Italian invasion. The newly created South Slavic state is considered a legal successor of the Kingdom of Serbia and is openly labelled as hostile by the Kingdom of Italy which was hoping to annex the rest of Istria, Dalmatia and Montenegro

objets.nom: The State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs joins with the Kingdom of Serbia and the Kingdom of Montenegro…
objets.notes: The State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs joins with the Kingdom of Serbia and the Kingdom of Montenegro to form the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes (SHS). Today it is believed that this was a great historical fault although at that time this was probably the only sensible decision because Italy according to the London Pact with the victorious…

objets.nom: The Paris Peace Conference begins
objets.notes: The Paris Peace Conference begins. Woodrow Wilson gives his "14 Points" address. The ninth and the 10th are crucial for Slovenes within former Austro-Hungarian borders.

objets.nom: The Treaty of Saint-Germain with republic of Austria
objets.notes: The Treaty of Saint-Germain with republic of Austria. It confirms the break of Austria-Hungary. Its territory comes down to newly formed countries Austria, Hungary, Czechoslovakia, Poland, Romania, and the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes. South Tyrol with its German population and Trentino fall to Italy.

objets.nom: The Treaty of Versailles is signed between Germany and victorious three Entente powers.
Croatian National hall in Pula and Slovene national hall in Trieste are burned down by Italian fascists.
Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes Constitutional Assembly election, 1920
objets.notes: The Democratic Party, People's Radical Party and Communist Party were the three most successful parties by number of seats received in the Assembly.

objets.nom: The Treaty of Rapallo between Italy and the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, where Slovenia loses…
objets.notes: The Treaty of Rapallo between Italy and the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, where Slovenia loses almost the whole province of Primorska, which is incorporated back again after the Second World War. Italy also gets the whole Istria together with the Trieste region (Tržaško).

objets.nom: The Treaty of Trianon with Hungary Burgenland (Gradiščansko) falls to Austria and Transmuraland…
objets.notes: The Treaty of Trianon with Hungary Burgenland (Gradiščansko) falls to Austria and Transmuraland (Prekmurje) to the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes.

objets.nom: St
objets.notes: St. Vitus Day Constitution (Vidovdanska ustava) is adopted. It legalizes a monarchal regulation and centralism in a new state and also the supremacy of the court and the Serb politics linked with it.

objets.nom: The Balkan Entente is formed by the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, the Kingdom of Romania,…
objets.notes: the Balkan Entente is formed by the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, the Kingdom of Romania, Greece and Turkey as a counterbalance to the revisionists (chiefly Italy and Hungary). It also served as a buffer-zone with the Soviet Union.

objets.nom: Founding of the TIGR at Goriško, Slovene anti-fascist organisation, first such European organization and…
objets.notes: Founding of the TIGR at Goriško, Slovene anti-fascist organisation, first such European organization and a secret youth organization Borba (The fight) at the Trieste region.

objets.nom: 6 January Dictatorship
objets.notes: Alexander issued a decree dissolving Parliament and abolishing the Constitution.

objets.nom: January 6 Dictatorship is introduced by King Alexander of Yugoslavia following the assassination of the…
objets.notes: January 6 Dictatorship is introduced by King Alexander of Yugoslavia following the assassination of the Croatian Peasant Party leader and the most important Croatian politician at the time, Stjepan Radić, by a Montenegrin Serb member of the Serbian People's Radical Party, Puniša Račić. The Constitution is suspended and the Parliament dissolved as…

objets.nom: The Balkan Entente formed between Romania, the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, Greece and Turkey.
The king Alexander I. Karađorđević, who reigned since 1921, is assassinated in Marseille together with a…
objets.notes: The king Alexander I. Karađorđević, who reigned since 1921, is assassinated in Marseille together with a French foreign minister Louis Barthou by Croatian extremist nationalists.

objets.nom: Adolf Hitler annexes Austria to the Nazi Germany
objets.notes: Adolf Hitler annexes Austria to the Nazi Germany. Slovenes in Austrian Carinthia practically become German citizens.

objets.nom: Dragiša Cvetković becomes prime minister
objets.notes: Dragiša Cvetković becomes prime minister. He signs an agreement with the leader of Croatian opposition Vladko Maček allowing for the foundation of the Banovina of Croatia as the sole autonomous political and territorial unit in the Kingdom of Yugoslavia. This agreement does not solve the national problem since it just distributes the authority…

objets.nom: Some members of TIGR plan an attempt on Italian Fascist leader Benito Mussolini's life, when he visits…
objets.notes: Some members of TIGR plan an attempt on Italian Fascist leader Benito Mussolini's life, when he visits Kobarid.

objets.nom: Former political prisoner Vlatko Maček is appointed vice premier of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia following…
objets.notes: Former political prisoner Vlatko Maček is appointed vice premier of the Kingdom of Yugoslavia following an appeasement policy of the Royal Court towards the Croats. An autonomous Banovina of Croatia is carved out of large parts of Croatia as well as parts of Bosnia and Vojvodina. As Vlatko Maček announces the potential independence of the province…

objets.nom: A Nazi politician and SS chief leader Heinrich Himmler visits Celje and among other he inspects the…
objets.notes: A Nazi politician and SS chief leader Heinrich Himmler visits Celje and among other he inspects the prison of the Stari pisker ("Old pot").

objets.nom: After the coup d'état, conducted under command of generals Simović and Mirković and supported by British…
objets.notes: After the coup d'état, conducted under command of generals Simović and Mirković and supported by British intelligence with 300,000 pound sterling, massive demonstrations erupt in downtown Belgrade as an overwhelming majority of Serbs denounce the Pact Treaty. Following a military coup d'état 17-year-old Peter II assumes the throne naming Dušan…

objets.nom: An anti-fascist organization, the Liberation Front of Slovene nation (Osvobodilna fronta Slovenskega…
objets.notes: An anti-fascist organization, the Liberation Front of Slovene nation (Osvobodilna fronta Slovenskega naroda) (OF) is established in Ljubljana. It is active on all Slovene ethnical territory, as well in Carinthia, Primorska region in the Venetian province and Slovene Rába region (Slovene Slovensko Porabje, Hungarian Szlovén-vidék or Rába-vidék).

objets.nom: Glina massacre
objets.notes: The Ustaše killed several hundred Serb civilians in a church in Glina.

objets.nom: Invasion of Yugoslavia
objets.notes: Germany opened an invasion of Yugoslavia with an air attack on Belgrade.

objets.nom: Massive Luftwaffe airstrikes hit the Yugoslav capital as Hitler decides to crush the rebellion causing…
objets.notes: Massive Luftwaffe airstrikes hit the Yugoslav capital as Hitler decides to crush the rebellion causing 17,000 casualties in the Battle of Belgrade. Other Serbian cities follow suit such as Leskovac, Kraljevo and Niš.

objets.nom: Operation Barbarossa
objets.notes: Germany launched an invasion of the Soviet Union.

objets.nom: Several joint Axis offensives, made of German, Italian, NDH, Bulgarian and Chetnik units, is launched in…
objets.notes: Several joint Axis offensives, made of German, Italian, NDH, Bulgarian and Chetnik units, is launched in Bosnia and Herzegovina, aimed at crushing the partisan strongholds in the area. The decisive victory of the Yugoslav National Liberation Army (YNLA) in the Battle of Neretva results in the devastation of Chetnik forces in Bosnia.

objets.nom: The Kingdom of Italy, Third Reich, Fascist Hungary and Fascist Bulgaria invade and dismantle the Kingdom…
objets.notes: The Kingdom of Italy, Third Reich, Fascist Hungary and Fascist Bulgaria invade and dismantle the Kingdom of Yugoslavia aided by Banovina of Croatia, Albania and some domestic minorities.

objets.nom: The Kingdom of Yugoslavia capitulates as its royal army disintegrates following the evacuation of the…
objets.notes: The Kingdom of Yugoslavia capitulates as its royal army disintegrates following the evacuation of the royal family to Africa and a multi-party occupation. Greece succumbs to the Axis 10 days later. Operation Barbarossa begins with a months delay enabling the Soviet Union to regroup during the Axis invasion of Southern Europe.

objets.nom: The Serbian division of the Partisan resistance movement, loyal to communists of Josip Broz Tito,…
objets.notes: The Serbian division of the Partisan resistance movement, loyal to communists of Josip Broz Tito, launches an uprising in the Nazi-occupied town of Užice proclaiming it a free state, The Republic of Užice. Uprisings also erupt in Italian-held Montenegro, Bosnia and Slovenia. Užice succumbs to the Germans 4 months later.

objets.nom: The Yugoslav Army in the Fatherland, a guerilla force loyal to the Kingdom of Yugoslavia's government in…
objets.notes: The Yugoslav Army in the Fatherland, a guerilla force loyal to the Kingdom of Yugoslavia's government in exile, is founded on Ravna Gora by Colonel Draža Mihajlović. Until the Yalta Conference in 1943 this royal army would be considered a chief ally to Great Britain, the US and the Soviet Union. Their chief opponents within the country would be…

objets.nom: World War II
objets.notes: Prince Paul signed the Tripartite Pact, pledging support to the Axis powers.

objets.nom: Operation Alfa
objets.notes: Italian and Chetnik forces attacked the Partisan-held town of Prozor.

objets.nom: Battle of the Sutjeska
objets.notes: Axis troops surrounded the main Partisan force on the east bank of the Sutjeska river in Bosnia.

objets.nom: Operation Delphin
objets.notes: Croatian forces undertook a campaign to capture several islands in the Adriatic Sea off the cost of central Dalmatia.

objets.nom: Second session of AVNOJ in Jajce.
The 2nd Congress of AVNOJ (Anti-Fascist Council of National Liberation of Yugoslavia) proclaims the…
objets.notes: The 2nd Congress of AVNOJ (Anti-Fascist Council of National Liberation of Yugoslavia) proclaims the Yugoslav federation, denouncing the King's right to return to the country after World War II is over. The next day, the Tehran Conference, a meeting between Joseph Stalin, Franklin D. Roosevelt and Winston Churchill, decides to shift their support…

objets.nom: Raid on Drvar
objets.notes: German paratroopers attacked Partisan headquarters near Drvar. Tito escaped.

objets.nom: The Royal Yugoslav government in exile recognizes the partisans as Yugoslavia's legitimate armed forces,…
objets.notes: The Royal Yugoslav government in exile recognizes the partisans as Yugoslavia's legitimate armed forces, ordering the Royal Army to join the newly named Partisan Yugoslav army, following the Tito-Šubašić agreement on the Adriatic island of Vis. The King calls for Serbs, Croats and Slovenes to unite into a single army under partisan flag. Draža…

objets.nom: Aided by the Soviet army, Yugoslav Partisans expel fascist and Nazi forces from the country, ultimately…
objets.notes: Aided by the Soviet army, Yugoslav Partisans expel fascist and Nazi forces from the country, ultimately defeating the royalists as well. Ustaše flee the country as well, among whom also Ante Pavelić, Petar Brzica, etc. Yugoslav Danube Swabians are also forced to leave the country, as well as many Hungarians and Italians.

objets.nom: Battle of Poljana
objets.notes: Retreating Axis troops were forced to surrender to the Partisans.

objets.nom: Battle on Lijevče field
objets.notes: Croatian and Chetnik forces met at Lijevče.

objets.nom: Bleiburg repatriations
objets.notes: After the retreating Axis column is stopped at Bleiburg, Austria, and forced by the British Army to surrender instead to the Yugoslav Partisans, the Yugoslav Partisans commit thousands of reprisals against the remnants of the Ustaše and the civilians who fled Croatia alongside them, as well as some Slovene, Serb, and Montenegrin collaborators.

objets.nom: British 8th Army together with Slovene partisan troops and motorized detachment of Yugoslav 4th Army…
objets.notes: British 8th Army together with Slovene partisan troops and motorized detachment of Yugoslav 4th Army arrives to Carinthia and Klagenfurt.

objets.nom: First postwar Slovene national government is named and elected by the SNOS (Slovene National Liberation…
objets.notes: First postwar Slovene national government is named and elected by the SNOS (Slovene National Liberation Council) at the Bratina Hall in Ajdovščina.

objets.nom: Forced repatriation of Slovene military and civilians from Viktring, Austria to various postwar…
objets.notes: Forced repatriation of Slovene military and civilians from Viktring, Austria to various postwar execution sites including the Kočevski Rog massacre and the Teharje camp.

objets.nom: General Alexander Löhr Commander of German Army Group E near Topolšica, Slovenia signs unconditional…
objets.notes: General Alexander Löhr Commander of German Army Group E near Topolšica, Slovenia signs unconditional capitulation of German occupation troops. World War II in Slovenia ends.

objets.nom: Serbian lands are dismantled under a pretext of Serbian hegemony and self-determination, being given to…
objets.notes: Serbian lands are dismantled under a pretext of Serbian hegemony and self-determination, being given to republic of Montenegro, provinces of Kosovo and Vojvodina, republic of Macedonia, republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, even to republic of Croatia (Baranja region), leaving Serbia, in form of Serbia proper, crippled in territory and population…

objets.nom: Soviet Union calls back all its specialists from Yugoslavia
objets.notes: Soviet Union calls back all its specialists from Yugoslavia. The Communist Party of the Soviet Union accuses the Communist Party of Yugoslavia of not being democratic, that it leans toward imperial powers, that returns to capitalism, and that it diverts from Marxism. The Informbiro begins. Economic blockade and a threat of military intervention…

objets.nom: The SFRY is expelled from the World Communist League, after refusing to accept the Soviet Union's…
objets.notes: The SFRY is expelled from the World Communist League, after refusing to accept the Soviet Union's supremacy in the communist world. Yugoslavia, therefore, has never signed the Warsaw Pact nor has it been, consequently, behind the Iron Curtain, unlike its immediate neighbours. From that point on Yugoslav history differs from that of cold-war…

objets.nom: Tito–Stalin split
objets.notes: Croatian Communist Party member Andrija Hebrang was arrested after supporting the Soviet Union in a dispute with Yugoslavia.

objets.nom: L'indépendance de Trieste expire après le London Memorandum qui est signé par les États-Unis, le…
objets.fr: L'indépendance de Trieste expire après le London Memorandum qui est signé par les États-Unis, le…
objets.notes: l'indépendance de Trieste expire après le London Memorandum qui est signé par les États-Unis, le Royaume-Uni, l'Italie et la Yougoslavie. Trieste devient italienne. La Slovénie garde le nord de l'Istrie.

objets.nom: Informbiro ends
objets.notes: Informbiro ends. Josip Broz Tito and Nikita Khrushchev sign the Belgrade declaration, which also recognizes a Yugoslav form of socialism.

objets.nom: Josip Broz Tito et Nikita Khrouchtchev signent la déclaration de Belgrade, qui reconnait la Yougoslavie…
objets.fr: Josip Broz Tito et Nikita Khrouchtchev signent la déclaration de Belgrade, qui reconnait la Yougoslavie…
objets.notes: Josip Broz Tito et Nikita Khrouchtchev signent la déclaration de Belgrade, qui reconnait la Yougoslavie comme un pays socialiste.

objets.nom: Croatian Spring
objets.notes: The Declaration on the Status and Name of the Croatian Literary Language was published, demanding equal status for the Croatian language.

objets.nom: Le chemin de fer du sud est électrifié.
objets.fr: Le chemin de fer du sud est électrifié.

objets.nom: Riots erupt among Albanians of Kosovo, as they ask for the recognition of the State of Kosovo
objets.notes: Riots erupt among Albanians of Kosovo, as they ask for the recognition of the State of Kosovo. The uprising was brutally suppressed by the JNA, as Kosovo Serbs fear being pulled into a civil war. By this date, the population share of Kosovo Serbs has dropped down to 15% compared to 25% a decade earlier.

objets.nom: The Memorandum of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts is proclaimed in Belgrade, calling for a…
objets.notes: The Memorandum of the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts is proclaimed in Belgrade, calling for a fundamental change and the country's reorganization. This document marks the rise of Serbian nationalism within SFRY, opening the Serbian Question, at the time the country was battling ever-high recession and unemployment rate. Kosovo Serbs and…

objets.nom: Log Revolution
objets.notes: Secessionist Serbs barricaded roads connecting Kninska Krajina to the rest of Croatia.

objets.nom: Milan Kučan wins the presidential election, which is still held within the SFR Yugoslavia.
Serb-populated regions of Croatia organize a poll on their self-rule within Croatia
objets.notes: Serb-populated regions of Croatia organize a poll on their self-rule within Croatia. The Log Revolution is also launched in the hinterland of Dalmatia, the Serbian city of Knin, blocking Croatian roads and splitting the country into two parts. The National Council of the Croatian Serbs, led by Milan Babić, declares "the autonomy of the Serbian…

objets.nom: The League of Communists of Yugoslavia dissolves along ethnic lines, as Slovene and Croatian…
objets.notes: The League of Communists of Yugoslavia dissolves along ethnic lines, as Slovene and Croatian representatives storm out of the Congress after opposing the strengthening of the Union. The first free elections are held several months later in Croatia (Croatian parliamentary election, 1990) and Slovenia, where separatist options have prevailed…

objets.nom: The Parliament of Croatia ratifies a new Constitution, declaring the indigenous Serbs of Croatia (12.2%)…
objets.notes: The Parliament of Croatia ratifies a new Constitution, declaring the indigenous Serbs of Croatia (12.2%) a national minority rather than a constituent nation. Serbs have enjoyed that autonomy de facto since the Croat-Hungarian Ausgleich in the 19th century. Franjo Tuđman, leader of the Croatian Democratic Union, publicly denies the Serbian…

objets.nom: 120 Serbs are massacred in the town of Gospić (region of Lika, Croatia) by members of a Croatian…
objets.notes: 120 Serbs are massacred in the town of Gospić (region of Lika, Croatia) by members of a Croatian paramilitary unit in what the Croatian human rights activists called the first major massacre of civilians in the Yugoslav civil wars. The mastermind of the massacre, Mirko Norac, was charged with crimes against humanity by both Croatia and the ICTY…

objets.nom: A series of Yugoslav wars begin as Croatia and Slovenia declare independence from the SFRY opposed by…
objets.notes: A series of Yugoslav wars begin as Croatia and Slovenia declare independence from the SFRY opposed by the Serbs and the JNA. Slovenia is granted its independence following a Ten-Day War, however the conflict in Croatia is bound to last, as the Republic of Serbian Krajina emerges.

objets.nom: Battle of Vukovar
objets.notes: The Yugoslavian army and Serb militias laid siege to the town of Vukovar.

objets.nom: Battle of the Barracks
objets.notes: The Yugoslavian barracks in Sisak surrendered to Croatian forces.

objets.nom: Battle of the Dalmatian channels
objets.notes: A Yugoslavian ship was sunk by the Croatian navy near Split.

objets.nom: Battle of Šibenik (1991)
objets.notes: The Yugoslavian army attacked Croatian forces in Šibenik.

objets.nom: Bombing of Banski dvori
objets.notes: The Yugoslavian army bombed the government residence, the Banski dvori in Zagreb.

objets.nom: Bosnian War
objets.notes: The Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina (HDZBiH) established Croatian Community of Herzeg-Bosnia at municipalities with majority of Croatian people on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

objets.nom: Bruška massacre
objets.notes: Serb forces killed ten civilians in Bruška.

objets.nom: Croatian War of Independence begins, following the Plitvice Lakes incident
objets.notes: Croatian War of Independence begins, following the Plitvice Lakes incident. Security forces of the Republic of Croatia clash with rebel Serbs of Croatia as they take over the Serb-populated territory of the national park. 2 policemen die – one from each side. An emergency session of the Federal Parliament decides to send the troops of the JNA into…

objets.nom: Dalj massacre
objets.notes: Serb rebels killed twenty-eight police officers and eleven Croat civilians in Dalj.

objets.nom: Erdut massacre
objets.notes: Serb rebels executed the first ten of the thirty-seven Hungarian and Croat civilians they would eventually massacre in Erdut.

objets.nom: Joševica massacre
objets.notes: Serb forces killed twenty-one civilians in Joševica.

objets.nom: Lovas massacre
objets.notes: Serbs forced a group of Croat civilians to walk across a minefield, killing twenty-one.

objets.nom: Operation Coast-91
objets.notes: JNA and SAO Krajina forces attacked the town of Biograd but were rebuffed.

objets.nom: Operation Opera Orientalis
objets.notes: Yugoslavian intelligence bombed Jewish cemeteries in an attempt to turn international opinion against Croatian independence.

objets.nom: Operation Otkos 10
objets.notes: Croatian forces moved to block a Yugoslavian advance on Zagreb.

objets.nom: Operation Whirlwind
objets.notes: The Croatian army attempted to cross the Kupa river against Krajina forces.

objets.nom: Pakrac clash
objets.notes: Croatian police arrested 180 Serb rebels who had occupied the town of Pakrac.

objets.nom: Plitvice Lakes incident
objets.notes: Croatian police entered the Plitvice Lakes National Park to expel the secessionist forces of Krajina. Two combatants were killed.

objets.nom: Saborsko massacre
objets.notes: Serb rebel forces killed twenty-nine civilians in Saborsko.

objets.nom: Siege of Dubrovnik
objets.notes: Yugoslavian forces surrounded Dubrovnik.

objets.nom: Slovenia removes Yugoslav border signs and marks its own
objets.notes: Slovenia removes Yugoslav border signs and marks its own. The Yugoslav People's Army sends 2,000 soldiers from barracks across Slovenia to reclaim all border checkpoints and the Ten-Day War starts.

objets.nom: The Borovo Selo massacre takes place in the Serb-populated village of Borovo Selo in eastern Croatia as…
objets.notes: The Borovo Selo massacre takes place in the Serb-populated village of Borovo Selo in eastern Croatia as 4 Croatian police-officers attempt to change the Yugoslav flag with the Croatian one after which they are captured by Vojislav Šešelj's troops. Attempting to free them Croatian policemen are led into an ambush and twelve are killed and some…

objets.nom: The Brioni Agreement between Slovenia and the SFR Yugoslavia is signed, under political patronage of the…
objets.notes: The Brioni Agreement between Slovenia and the SFR Yugoslavia is signed, under political patronage of the European Economic Community (EEC). The Ten-Day War ends and the Yugoslav People's Army is given three months to leave the territory of the Republic of Slovenia. In all, fewer than a hundred people died in the clashes, mostl of whom were…

objets.nom: Voćin massacre
objets.notes: A Serb paramilitary group, the White Eagles, killed several dozen people before retreating from Voćin.

objets.nom: Vukovar massacre
objets.notes: Some 264 civilians, mostly Croats, were murdered by Serb militias near Vukovar.

objets.nom: Škabrnja massacre
objets.notes: Serb forces took the town of Škabrnja and began a massacre which would eventually claim eighty-six lives.

objets.nom: Croat–Bosniak War
objets.notes: First armed clashes between the Croatian Defence Council (HVO) and the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina (ARBiH).

objets.nom: Operation Corridor
objets.notes: The Army of Republika Srpska launched an offensive against the joint forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia and Herzeg-Bosnia.

objets.nom: Operation Vrbas '92
objets.notes: Military offensive of the Army of Republika Srpska against the HVO and ARBiH in Jajce.

objets.nom: A Croatian military operation in the Medak Pocket is launched in September 1993 led by Mirko Norac and…
objets.notes: A Croatian military operation in the Medak Pocket is launched in September 1993 led by Mirko Norac and Rahim Ademi, the Hague Tribunal indictees. The predominantly Serbian population of the several adjacent villages, 400 strong, leaves the area. 16 are killed.

objets.nom: Operation Maslenica
objets.notes: The Croatian army launched an offensive to reconquer Krajina territory in northern Dalmatia.

objets.nom: Operation Medak Pocket
objets.notes: Croatian forces launched a southeastward offensive against Krajina towards the village of Medak.

objets.nom: Operation Neretva '93
objets.notes: ARBiH forces attack the HVO in Herzegovina and central Bosnia.

objets.nom: After coming under international pressure, Serbia cut off support for the RSK in early 1995. In early…
objets.notes: After coming under international pressure, Serbia cut off support for the RSK in early 1995. In early May 1995, Croatian forces recaptured western Slavonia. In August 1995, Croatian forces recaptured Krajina, leaving only eastern Slavonia under RSK control. On August 3, 1995, under UN mediation in Geneva, the RSK and Croatia engaged in discussions…

objets.nom: Amidst intense pressure by the Contact Group, the Dayton Peace Agreement, is reached by the three…
objets.notes: Amidst intense pressure by the Contact Group, the Dayton Peace Agreement, is reached by the three leaders Franjo Tuđman of Croatia, Alija Izetbegović of Bosnia and Slobodan Milošević of Yugoslavia putting an end to a three-year-long Bosnian war which claimed 100,000 lives. Bosnia and Herzegovina is acknowledged as a sovereign state of 2…

objets.nom: Operation Flash, conducted by the Croatian Army in May, successfully recaptures Republic of Serbian…
objets.notes: Operation Flash, conducted by the Croatian Army in May, successfully recaptures Republic of Serbian Krajina-held west Slavonia. 30.000 Croatian Serbs were forced out of the area and 285 have been killed during this action. 1,500 were arrested and imprisoned.

objets.nom: Operation Mistral 2
objets.notes: Croatian and Bosnia and Herzegovina forces attacked Republika Srpska forces in western Bosnia and Herzegovina.

objets.nom: Operation Storm, a large-scale military operation is carried out throughout the self-proclaimed Republic…
objets.notes: Operation Storm, a large-scale military operation is carried out throughout the self-proclaimed Republic of Serbian Krajina (RSK) by the Croatian Army in August 1995 de facto ending the Croatian War which took 20,000 lives. In the aftermath of the operation 250,000 Croatian Serb civilians fled the area. More than 1,200 civilians who had remained…

objets.nom: Operation Summer '95
objets.notes: Croatian forces launched a northward offensive from Bosnia and Herzegovina against Krajina forces.

objets.nom: Srebrenica massacre, the largest mass murder in Europe since the end of World War II, takes place in a…
objets.notes: Srebrenica massacre, the largest mass murder in Europe since the end of World War II, takes place in a Bosniak enclave within Republika Srpska following the retreat of the Dutch soldiers from this "UN safe zone". More than 8,000 Bosniak men, mostly civilians, are systematically executed by the Police and Army of Republika Srpska under the command…

objets.nom: Zagreb rocket attacks
objets.notes: A two-day series of rocket attacks by Serb forces on Zagreb began which would kill seven civilians.

objets.nom: An ethnic cleansing of the Serbian population begins following the retreat of the Yugoslav Army and the…
objets.notes: An ethnic cleansing of the Serbian population begins following the retreat of the Yugoslav Army and the arrival of Albanians protected by the UN and NATO. 200,000 Kosovo Serbs are expelled from or escape from Kosovo leaving only a fraction of pre-war Serbian population behind – about 140,000. Serbs fall to a mere 7% of the overall population as…

objets.nom: There are numerous killings of Albanians and Serbs following the armed clashes between the two
objets.notes: There are numerous killings of Albanians and Serbs following the armed clashes between the two. NATO bombs major Serbian cities including downtown Belgrade as well as Niš city market, the bridges of Novi Sad and the oil refinery of Pančevo.

objets.nom: Croatian presidential election, 2000
objets.notes: Mesić, running with the Croatian People's Party – Liberal Democrats (HNS), and Dražen Budiša of the Croatian Social Liberal Party (HSLS) qualified for the second round.

objets.nom: Albanian guerilla forces linked to the KLA attack Yugoslav forces within the Ground Safety Zone between…
objets.notes: Albanian guerilla forces linked to the KLA attack Yugoslav forces within the Ground Safety Zone between Serbia proper and Kosovo. The conflict went on for several weeks spreading into Serbia's municipalities of Preševo, Bujanovac and Medveđa before the resistance is finally suppressed. Guerilla fighters take refuge in the Republic of Macedonia…

objets.nom: During the Prague (Czech Republic) NATO summit, Slovenia is invited to start talks in order to join the…
objets.notes: During the Prague (Czech Republic) NATO summit, Slovenia is invited to start talks in order to join the alliance, together with six other countries (Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia, Romania, and Bulgaria.

objets.nom: The European Commission announces that Slovenia, together with nine other countries (Cyprus, the Czech…
objets.notes: The European Commission announces that Slovenia, together with nine other countries (Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, and Slovakia), has met the criteria to join the European Union, which would see its membership expand from 15 member states to 25.

objets.nom: Slovenia enters the European Union along with Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia,…
objets.notes: Slovenia enters the European Union along with Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland and Slovakia. The Slovenian tolar becomes part of the European Exchange Rate Mechanism, in preparation for eventual adoption of the euro.

objets.nom: Croatian presidential election, 2005
objets.notes: Mesić, running as an independent, and Jadranka Kosor of the HDZ qualified for the second round.

objets.nom: Croatian presidential election, 2009–10
objets.notes: Ivo Josipović of the SDP and the independent Milan Bandić qualified for the second round.

objets.nom: Croatian parliamentary election, 2015
objets.notes: The Patriotic Coalition won a plurality of seats in the Sabor, with Croatia is Growing coalition coming second and MOST third.

objets.nom: Croatian presidential election, 2014–15
objets.notes: Kolinda Grabar-Kitarović was voted to be the president of Croatia with 50,74% of the vote, becoming Croatia's first female president.

objets.nom: Croatian parliamentary election, 2016
objets.notes: The HDZ-led coalition won a plurality of seats in the Sabor. Andrej Plenković confirmed as the prime minister.

objets.nom: Iron Age settlements emerge in Wales, two of the earliest being Castell Odo, a small hillfort near the…
objets.notes: Iron Age settlements emerge in Wales, two of the earliest being Castell Odo, a small hillfort near the tip of the Llŷn Peninsula and Lodge Wood Camp, above the later Roman fort at Caerleon.

objets.nom: Roman General Julius Caesar invades Great Britain for the first time, gaining a beachhead on the coast…
objets.notes: Roman General Julius Caesar invades Great Britain for the first time, gaining a beachhead on the coast of Kent.

objets.nom: Roman general Julius Caesar invades for the first time, gaining a beachhead on the coast of Kent.
Caesar invades a second time
objets.notes: Caesar invades a second time. These two invasions are known as Caesar's invasions of Britain.

objets.nom: Adoption par la Grande-Bretagne du calendrier grégorien ; le lendemain passe directement au 14 septembre.
objets.fr: Adoption par la Grande-Bretagne du calendrier grégorien ; le lendemain passe directement au 14 septembre.

objets.nom: Après avoir remporté les élections, le travailliste Tony Blair assume le poste de premier ministre
objets.fr: Après avoir remporté les élections, le travailliste Tony Blair assume le poste de premier ministre
objets.notes: Après avoir remporté les élections, le travailliste Tony Blair assume le poste de premier ministre. Il inaugure une politique connue sous le nom de «blairisme».

objets.nom: Gibraltar est pris par les flottes anglais et hollandaises combinées sous le commandement de l'amiral…
objets.fr: Gibraltar est pris par les flottes anglais et hollandaises combinées sous le commandement de l'amiral…
objets.notes: Gibraltar est pris par les flottes anglais et hollandaises combinées sous le commandement de l'amiral George Rooke.

objets.nom: Reign of Cuno, an influential king of southern England before the Roman occupation; son of Tasciovanus
Création du Commonwealth, régi par le statut de Westminster.
objets.fr: Création du Commonwealth, régi par le statut de Westminster.

objets.nom: Le roi George I meurt et son fils George II lui succède en tant que roi.
objets.fr: Le roi George I meurt et son fils George II lui succède en tant que roi.

objets.nom: La bataille de Culloden met une fin effective au soulèvement jacobite.
objets.fr: La bataille de Culloden met une fin effective au soulèvement jacobite.

objets.nom: Le roi Guillaume III meurt et sa belle-sœur Anne lui succède en tant que reine.
objets.fr: Le roi Guillaume III meurt et sa belle-sœur Anne lui succède en tant que reine.

objets.nom: Bataille de Prestonpans.
objets.fr: Bataille de Prestonpans.

objets.nom: Guerre de l'oreille de Jenkins - Le premier ministre Robert Walpole déclare la guerre contre l'Espagne.
objets.fr: Guerre de l'oreille de Jenkins - Le premier ministre Robert Walpole déclare la guerre contre l'Espagne.

objets.nom: Earliest reliably-dated "modern human" burial with artefacts, first discovered in the 1820s on the Gower…
objets.notes: Earliest reliably-dated "modern human" burial with artefacts, first discovered in the 1820s on the Gower in Swansea. After the Red Lady of Paviland bones were recalibrated in 2009, the (male) Homo sapiens bones were determined to be from 33,000 years ago.

objets.nom: The earliest farming communities become established in Wales, marking the beginning of the Neolithic period
objets.notes: The earliest farming communities become established in Wales, marking the beginning of the Neolithic period. Megalithic tombs still survive from this period, such as the Pentre Ifan Dolmen in Pembrokeshire.

objets.nom: Aulus Plautius leads an army of forty thousand to invade Great Britain
objets.notes: Aulus Plautius leads an army of forty thousand to invade Great Britain. Emperor Claudius makes Britain a part of the Roman Empire. This is known as the Roman conquest of Britain.

objets.nom: Aulus Plautius leads an army of forty thousand to invade Great Britain; Emperor Claudius makes it a part…
objets.notes: Aulus Plautius leads an army of forty thousand to invade Great Britain; Emperor Claudius makes it a part of the Roman Empire

objets.nom: London settled by the Romans, known as Londinium
Caratacus, a defeated chieftain from east England, encourages the Silures and Ordovices to attack Roman…
objets.notes: Caratacus, a defeated chieftain from east England, encourages the Silures and Ordovices to attack Roman territories, ultimately unsuccessfully; he is betrayed by the Brigantes and taken to Rome as a prisoner
