objets.nom: The Silures have been defeated; Romans establish Venta Silurum, a market town in the Roman province of…
objets.notes: The Silures have been defeated; Romans establish Venta Silurum, a market town in the Roman province of Britannia; the modern village of Caerwent in Monmouthshire is built around the Roman ruins; Roman fortress at Caerleon is established for the Legio II Augusta

objets.nom: Romans defeat Caledonians at the Battle of Mons Graupius.
Emperor Hadrian orders a 73-mile (117 km) wall built to mark the Northern Roman Empire's province on the…
objets.notes: Emperor Hadrian orders a 73-mile (117 km) wall built to mark the Northern Roman Empire's province on the British Isle. Hadrian's Wall, as it comes to be known, is intended to keep the Caledonians, Picts, and other tribes at bay.

objets.nom: Emperor Hadrian orders a wall to be built to mark Roman territory of Britain in the north.
According to Ptolemy, Wales was populated by five indistinct peoples, mostly of Celtic origin:…
objets.notes: According to Ptolemy, Wales was populated by five indistinct peoples, mostly of Celtic origin: Ordovices, Silures, Demetae, Deceangli and Gangani

objets.nom: Romans withdraw south to Trimontium and Hadrian's Wall.
Britain is divided into two parts – Britannia Superior and Britannia Inferior.
Governor Lucius Alfenus Senecio repairs Hadrian's Wall and appeals for help from the Emperor against the…
objets.notes: Governor Lucius Alfenus Senecio repairs Hadrian's Wall and appeals for help from the Emperor against the northern tribes.

objets.nom: Emperor Septimius Severus and his son Caracalla take personal command of the army in Britain.
Severus and Caracalla lead an expedition against the Caledonii, and build forts at Cramond and the Tay…
objets.notes: Severus and Caracalla lead an expedition against the Caledonii, and build forts at Cramond and the Tay estuary.

objets.nom: Britain is divided into two provinces, Britannia Inferior and Britannia Superior
objets.notes: Britain is divided into two provinces, Britannia Inferior and Britannia Superior. This is likely due to the Roman emperor at the time, Caracalla.

objets.nom: Britain divided into two provinces, Britannia Superior and Britannia Inferior, with administrative…
objets.notes: Britain divided into two provinces, Britannia Superior and Britannia Inferior, with administrative centres at London and York respectively

objets.nom: Saxons raid south-east coast; forts built at Reculver and Branodunum (Brancaster).
Many thousands of acres of modern-day Lincolnshire are inundated by a great flood.
Rebel leader Latinus Postumus proclaims Britain as part of his "Empire of the Gauls".
Imperial edict lifts restrictions on British wine production
objets.notes: Imperial edict lifts restrictions on British wine production. General Victorinus puts down revolt, and settles Burgundian and Vandal prisoners in Britain.

objets.nom: Marcus Aurelius Mausaeus Carausius, a Roman military commander at the time, usurps power during the…
objets.notes: Marcus Aurelius Mausaeus Carausius, a Roman military commander at the time, usurps power during the Carausian Revolt.

objets.nom: Finance minister Allectus murders Carausius and seizes power; employs Frankish mercenaries.
Julius Constantius defeats Britons near Silchester, killing Allectus; prevents retreating Franks from…
objets.notes: Julius Constantius defeats Britons near Silchester, killing Allectus; prevents retreating Franks from sacking London

objets.nom: Re-building of forts near Hadrian's Wall begins
objets.notes: Re-building of forts near Hadrian's Wall begins. Constantius returns to Gaul. First mention on record of the Picts attacking from the north in Eumenius' Panegyrici Latini.

objets.nom: The term Pict is first recorded in describing the federated tribes invaded by Constantius Chlorus.
The Great Conspiracy begins, starting a year-long period of disorder and war in Britain.
Irish, Scots and Saxon invaders begin to fill the vacuum left by Magnus Maximus and his garrison
Traditional date at which Saint Ninian establishes a Christian mission at Whithorn.
Roman garrison withdrawn from Britain, followed by the emergence of Welsh kingdoms, principally Gwynedd…
objets.notes: Roman garrison withdrawn from Britain, followed by the emergence of Welsh kingdoms, principally Gwynedd (north), Demetia (south, subsequently Dyfed) and Powys (east)

objets.nom: The Angles begin their invasion of England and establish tribal kingdoms on the east coast.
Cunedda Wledig (possibly the grandson of a Roman or Romano-Briton with military rank on the border with…
objets.notes: Cunedda Wledig (possibly the grandson of a Roman or Romano-Briton with military rank on the border with Scotland) comes "from the north" and founds Gwynedd by driving out the Irish settlers

objets.nom: Votadini peoples form the kingdom of Gododdin in the region north of the River Tweed.
Tydfil, later Saint Tydfil—a daughter of Brychan, king of Brycheiniog (later Brecknockshire)—is murdered…
objets.notes: Tydfil, later Saint Tydfil—a daughter of Brychan, king of Brycheiniog (later Brecknockshire)—is murdered at Merthyr

objets.nom: The supposed time of the legendary King Arthur, of Welsh parentage and crowned at Caerleon, referred to…
objets.notes: The supposed time of the legendary King Arthur, of Welsh parentage and crowned at Caerleon, referred to by early writers such as Nennius, Geoffrey of Monmouth and many others, but considered by more modern historians as a combination of "monkish legends and chivalrous fiction"

objets.nom: The time of Dewi ap Sanctus (grandson of Ceredig, founder of Ceredigion), who later became Saint David,…
objets.notes: The time of Dewi ap Sanctus (grandson of Ceredig, founder of Ceredigion), who later became Saint David, patron saint of Wales

objets.nom: Angles capture the Northumbrian fortress at Bamburgh and found the kingdom of Bernicia.
Death of Maelgwn Gwynedd, king of Gwynedd, known for funding the foundation of Christian churches…
objets.notes: Death of Maelgwn Gwynedd, king of Gwynedd, known for funding the foundation of Christian churches throughout Wales; Maelgwn may have died of the bubonic plague, a pandemic that spread across Europe and beyond in the early 540s, mostly via trade routes

objets.nom: Saint Columba founds a monastery at Iona and begins his mission to the northern Picts.
Áedán mac Gabráin begins reign over the Gaelic kingdom of Dál Riata.
Riderch I of Alt Clut rules region later known as the kingdom of Strathclyde.
Christianisation of the Kingdom of Kent and its leader King Æthelberht by Saint Augustine.
The terms Cymry (Welsh people) and Cymru (Wales), as opposed to other Celtic peoples and regions,…
objets.notes: The terms Cymry (Welsh people) and Cymru (Wales), as opposed to other Celtic peoples and regions, already in use as self-identifiers

objets.nom: Æthelfrith unites Bernicia and Deira to form the kingdom of Northumbria.
Battle of Chester between Anglo-Saxons and native Britons
King Æthelberht of Kent dies and is succeeded by his son Eadbald of Kent.
Welsh/Mercian alliance between King Cadwallon of Gwynedd and Penda of Mercia defeats army of King Edwin…
objets.notes: Welsh/Mercian alliance between King Cadwallon of Gwynedd and Penda of Mercia defeats army of King Edwin of Northumbria at the Battle of Cefn Digoll (or "Battle of the Long Mynd") at Long Mountain near Welshpool

objets.nom: Northumbrians capture Edinburgh from Gododdin.
Trumwine Bishop of Abercorn.
Bruide mac Bili, King of Fortriu, campaigns against Orkney.
Pictish King Bruide mac Bili defeats Ecgfrith of Northumbria at the Battle of Dun Nechtain, halting the…
objets.notes: Pictish King Bruide mac Bili defeats Ecgfrith of Northumbria at the Battle of Dun Nechtain, halting the northern expansion of Northumbria.

objets.nom: Bruide mac Der-Ilei among the signatories of the Cáin Adomnáin.
At the height of its powers, Mercia expands westwards to the Dee, Wye, and Severn rivers, at the expense…
objets.notes: At the height of its powers, Mercia expands westwards to the Dee, Wye, and Severn rivers, at the expense of the Welsh kingdom of Powys; forced back into the upland regions, the Welsh launch a series of raids throughout the late 7th and early 8th centuries, in a bid to regain the rich farming territory of the lowlands.

objets.nom: Nechtan mac Der-Ilei expels Ionan clergy from Pictland and adopts Roman usages with the aid of Bishop…
objets.notes: Nechtan mac Der-Ilei expels Ionan clergy from Pictland and adopts Roman usages with the aid of Bishop Curetán; masons sent by Abbot Ceolfrid of Monkwearmouth-Jarrow Priory help build stone churches at Restenneth, Rosemarkie and elsewhere in eastern Scotland.

objets.nom: Reign of Cuthred, King of Wessex.
St Andrews founded by this time, death of Abbot Túathalán.
Offa's Dyke is built along the Wales–England border to mark the boundary between Anglian Mercia and the…
objets.notes: Offa's Dyke is built along the Wales–England border to mark the boundary between Anglian Mercia and the Welsh kingdom of Powys; however, radiocarbon dating of samples taken from excavations in 2014 reveal that it may have been constructed much earlier than this, and over an extended time period

objets.nom: Battle takes place in Fortriu between Ciniod and Áed Find; result unknown.
The Welsh church adopts the Catholic method of calculating Easter through the efforts of bishop Elfodd
Viking raid on a monastery in Lindisfarne, often taken as the beginning of the Viking age.
Battle at Rhuddlan Marsh, between the Saxons and Welsh; there is confusion between possible battles at…
objets.notes: Battle at Rhuddlan Marsh, between the Saxons and Welsh; there is confusion between possible battles at Rhuddlan Marsh (Denbighshire) in 795 and Rhuddlan (Flintshire) in 796

objets.nom: Nennius, a 9th-century Welsh monk, is thought to have written Historia Brittonum, a history of the…
objets.notes: Nennius, a 9th-century Welsh monk, is thought to have written Historia Brittonum, a history of the Celtic Britons, although some experts argue that the work was written anonymously

objets.nom: Abbot Diarmait, abbot of Iona, goes to Alba with relics of St Columba.
Eóganan mac Óengusa and his brother Bran killed in battle with Vikings, end of dominance of Fortriu.
Alfred the Great, the future king of Wessex (r
objets.notes: Alfred the Great, the future king of Wessex (r. 871-899), is born to Aethelwulf of Wessex and Osburh.

objets.nom: Death of Kenneth mac Alpin, King of the Picts; "union of Picts and Scots" traditionally dated from his reign.
Alt Clut—Dumbarton Rock — captured by the Norse-Gael or Viking leaders Amlaíb Conung and Ímar after a…
objets.notes: Alt Clut—Dumbarton Rock — captured by the Norse-Gael or Viking leaders Amlaíb Conung and Ímar after a six-month of siege.

objets.nom: Kenneth mac Alpin's son Áed killed; Giric becomes king.
When Rhodri the Great dies fighting the Saxons on Anglesey, his three eldest sons become regional…
objets.notes: When Rhodri the Great dies fighting the Saxons on Anglesey, his three eldest sons become regional rulers: Cadell in Seisyllwg (mainly Ceredigion), Anarawd in Gwynedd and Merfyn in Powys.

objets.nom: Merfyn ap Rhodri was slain by Vikings
objets.notes: Merfyn ap Rhodri was slain by Vikings. Hywel ap Cadell (grandson of Rhodri the Great) marries Elen, daughter of Llywarch ap Hyfaidd, the late king of Dyfed, thus inheriting the kingdom

objets.nom: Sweyn Forkbeard, the future king of England (r
objets.notes: Sweyn Forkbeard, the future king of England (r. 1013-1014), is born in Denmark to Harald Bluetooth and either Tove or Gunhild.

objets.nom: Earl Byrhtnoth and his thegns lead the English against a Viking invasion in the Battle of Maldon in Essex.
Vikings sack St David's in Pembrokeshire, and murder the bishop, Morgeneu
Cnut the Great is crowned king of England in London.
Llywelyn ap Seisyll defeats the pretender Rhain ("the Irishman"), who claimed to be a son of Maredudd ab…
objets.notes: Llywelyn ap Seisyll defeats the pretender Rhain ("the Irishman"), who claimed to be a son of Maredudd ab Owain, at Abergwili and takes control of the south

objets.nom: Malcolm II of Scotland dies at Glamis
objets.notes: Malcolm II of Scotland dies at Glamis. He is succeeded as king of Scotland by his grandson Duncan I the Diseased of Scotland.

objets.nom: Cnut dies
objets.notes: Cnut dies. He is succeeded as king of England, Denmark and Norway by his son Harthacnut.

objets.nom: Duncan the Diseased is killed in action at Elgin, Moray attempting to suppress a rebellion by Macbeth,…
objets.notes: Duncan the Diseased is killed in action at Elgin, Moray attempting to suppress a rebellion by Macbeth, King of Scotland, Mormaer of Moray, who replaces him as king of Scotland.

objets.nom: Harold Harefoot dies at Oxford
objets.notes: Harold Harefoot dies at Oxford. Harthacnut, his brother, succeeds him as king of England.

objets.nom: Harthacnut dies, probably due to a stroke after excessive drinking at a wedding in Lambeth
objets.notes: Harthacnut dies, probably due to a stroke after excessive drinking at a wedding in Lambeth. He is succeeded as king of England by his brother Edward the Confessor.

objets.nom: Battle of Lumphanan
objets.notes: Macbeth is killed in battle at Lumphanan by Duncan the Diseased's son Malcolm III of Scotland. He is succeeded as king of Scotland by his stepson Lulach.

objets.nom: After defeating Mac Bethad and Lulach, Máel Coluim III is proclaimed king.
Lulach is assassinated by Malcolm III, who succeeds him as king of Kingdom of Scotland.
Battle of Fulford
objets.notes: English forces are defeated by Norse invaders in northeastern England.

objets.nom: Battle of Hastings
objets.notes: Harold Godwinson is killed in battle against the forces of William the Conqueror at Battle, East Sussex, causing the collapse of his army.

objets.nom: Battle of Stamford Bridge
objets.notes: the remaining Norse under Harald Hardrada are defeated by the bulk of England's army under the command of its king.

objets.nom: Edward the Confessor dies, probably after a series of strokes
objets.notes: Edward the Confessor dies, probably after a series of strokes. He is succeeded as king of England by his brother-in-law Harold Godwinson.

objets.nom: Norman conquest of England
objets.notes: William the Conqueror, duke of Normandy, lands with an army at Pevensey.

objets.nom: William the Conqueror is crowned king of England at Westminster Abbey.
Gwent is invaded by William FitzOsbern, 1st Earl of Hereford and his followers, and becomes the first of…
objets.notes: Gwent is invaded by William FitzOsbern, 1st Earl of Hereford and his followers, and becomes the first of the Welsh kingdoms to be overrun following the Norman conquest of England the previous year

objets.nom: William the Conqueror dies at Rouen
objets.notes: William the Conqueror dies at Rouen. He is succeeded by one son, Robert Curthose, as duke of Normandy and by another, William II of England, as king of England.

objets.nom: Battle of Alnwick (1093)
objets.notes: Malcolm III and his eldest son are ambushed and killed at Alnwick by an army of knights led by Robert de Mowbray, earl of Northumbria.

objets.nom: | Shortly after capturing Anglesey from the Welsh, the Normans are defeated at the Battle of Anglesey…
objets.notes: | Shortly after capturing Anglesey from the Welsh, the Normans are defeated at the Battle of Anglesey Sound and forced to retreat, paving the way for the return of the exiled Gruffudd ap Cynan

objets.nom: The White Tower of London is completed.
William II is killed by an arrow through the lung while hunting in the New Forest
objets.notes: William II is killed by an arrow through the lung while hunting in the New Forest. He is succeeded by his brother Henry I of England.

objets.nom: Period of violent power struggles for regional control between the English crown, under the new King…
objets.notes: Period of violent power struggles for regional control between the English crown, under the new King Henry I, and Welsh leaders such as Iorwerth ap Bleddyn, Prince of Powys, and his brothers Cadwgan and Maredudd

objets.nom: Normans move into south and north Wales; peace is agreed between King Henry I and Gruffudd ap Cynan of…
objets.notes: Normans move into south and north Wales; peace is agreed between King Henry I and Gruffudd ap Cynan of Gwynedd; Owain ap Cadwgan is knighted by King Henry I for his service in Normandy

objets.nom: Stephen, King of England is crowned king of England at Westminster Abbey.
| Owain ap Gruffudd, allied with Gruffydd ap Rhys of Deheubarth, inflicts a crushing defeat on the…
objets.notes: | Owain ap Gruffudd, allied with Gruffydd ap Rhys of Deheubarth, inflicts a crushing defeat on the Normans at the Battle of Crug Mawr and annexes Ceredigion

objets.nom: Gruffudd ap Cynan, king of Gynedd, dies
objets.notes: Gruffudd ap Cynan, king of Gynedd, dies. He is succeeded by his son Owain Gwynedd.

objets.nom: The Anarchy
objets.notes: Stephen enters Normandy in an attempt to conquer it from Empress Matilda, his rival for the succession in Normandy and England.

objets.nom: Stephen dies of a stomach disease
objets.notes: Stephen dies of a stomach disease. He is succeeded as king of England by Henry II of England, grandson of Henry I.

objets.nom: Following the death of Madog ap Maredudd, the kingdom of Powys is split into two parts: Maelor, the…
objets.notes: Following the death of Madog ap Maredudd, the kingdom of Powys is split into two parts: Maelor, the northern portion, is later renamed Powys Fadog; and Cyfeiliog, in the south, becomes Powys Wenwynwyn

objets.nom: Henry II issues the Constitutions of Clarendon, which provided that members of the Catholic Church…
objets.notes: Henry II issues the Constitutions of Clarendon, which provided that members of the Catholic Church accused of serious crimes would be tried and sentenced in secular courts.

objets.nom: Somerled is defeated by Malcolm IV in the Battle of Renfrew.
The Constitutions of Clarendon, a set of laws which governed the trial of members of the Catholic Church…
objets.notes: The Constitutions of Clarendon, a set of laws which governed the trial of members of the Catholic Church in England, are issued.

objets.nom: Death of Owain Gwynedd throws the kingdom of Gwynedd into disarray; within weeks, his nominated heir…
objets.notes: Death of Owain Gwynedd throws the kingdom of Gwynedd into disarray; within weeks, his nominated heir Hywel is dead, and his illegitimate son Dafydd usurps the rule of Gwynedd, but he fails to maintain his father's hold on south Wales, which falls into the hands of Rhys ap Gruffydd

objets.nom: Thomas Becket, archbishop of Canterbury, is murdered in Canterbury Cathedral by followers of Henry II.
Thomas Becket, the Archbishop of Canterbury, is assassinated.
William I signs the Treaty of Falaise in which he swears allegiance to Henry II of England.
Gerald of Wales accompanies the Archbishop of Canterbury on a journey through Wales to recruit…
objets.notes: Gerald of Wales accompanies the Archbishop of Canterbury on a journey through Wales to recruit volunteers for the Third Crusade; Owain Cyfeiliog, Prince of Powys Wenwynwyn refuses to support the visit and is consequently excommunicated

objets.nom: Henry II dies of illness at Château de Chinon
objets.notes: Henry II dies of illness at Château de Chinon. He is succeeded as king of England by his son Richard I of England.

objets.nom: Crusades
objets.notes: King Richard I is captured by Austrian Duke Leopold V, Duke of Austria while returning from the Holy Land.

objets.nom: Richard is captured near Vienna on the orders of Leopold V, Duke of Austria, duke of Austria, while…
objets.notes: Richard is captured near Vienna on the orders of Leopold V, Duke of Austria, duke of Austria, while returning from the Crusades.

objets.nom: Battle of Aberconwy
objets.notes: Llywelyn the Great defeats his uncle Dafydd ab Owain Gwynedd, one of two princes of Kingdom of Gwynedd, in battle.

objets.nom: Richard is released following the payment of fifty tons of silver to Austria.
Richard dies of a crossbow wound sustained two weeks earlier during a siege of Château de Châlus-Chabrol
objets.notes: Richard dies of a crossbow wound sustained two weeks earlier during a siege of Château de Châlus-Chabrol. He was succeeded as king of England by his brother John, King of England.

objets.nom: King John is excommunicated from the Catholic Church by Pope Innocent III.
The pope Pope Innocent III excommunicates John.
John agrees to Magna Carta, granting political rights including the right to a fair trial to his barons.
John dies of illness
objets.notes: John dies of illness. He is succeeded as king of England by his son Henry III of England.

objets.nom: Henry III and Alexander II of Scotland sign the Treaty of York, under which the latter renounced his…
objets.notes: Henry III and Alexander II of Scotland sign the Treaty of York, under which the latter renounced his claims on English territory in Northumberland, Cumberland and Westmorland.

objets.nom: The Treaty of York is signed, fixing the border between Scotland and England.
Death of Llywelyn ab Iorwerth, prince of Wales; Dafydd ap Llywelyn succeeds to the throne of Gwynedd.
Death of Dafydd ap Llywelyn; Llywelyn ap Gruffudd succeeds to the throne of Gwynedd (he does not claim…
objets.notes: Death of Dafydd ap Llywelyn; Llywelyn ap Gruffudd succeeds to the throne of Gwynedd (he does not claim the title of prince of Wales until 1258).

objets.nom: Death of Alexander II, king of Scots; Alexander III succeeds to the throne of Scotland.
Battle of Largs, an inconclusive battle, is fought between Haakon IV of Norway and the Scots.
Battle of Lewes
objets.notes: Rebel English barons led by Simon de Montfort, 6th Earl of Leicester defeat King Henry III.

objets.nom: Simon de Montfort leads rebel English barons to defeat Henry III at the Battle of Lewes.
Norway cedes the Hebrides and Isle of Man to Scotland in the Treaty of Perth.
Henry III of England recognises the authority of Llywelyn ap Gruffudd in Wales.
Henry recognises the authority of Llywelyn ap Gruffudd in Gwynedd.
Death of Henry III, Edward I succeeds to the English throne.
Death of Llywelyn ap Gruffudd, prince of Wales; Dafydd ap Gruffudd succeeds to the throne of Gwynedd.
Margaret, Maid of Norway dies in Orkney.
Edward I of England intervenes in Scottish affairs and grants the Scottish throne to John Balliol.
Andrew de Moravia and William Wallace lead the Scots to victory over England at Stirling Bridge.
Battle of Stirling Bridge
objets.notes: The Scots, led by William Wallace, defeats the English.

objets.nom: Battle of Bannockburn
objets.notes: Scotland wins a decisive victory over England.

objets.nom: Robert the Bruce defeats the English at Bannockburn.
| Llywelyn Bren launches a surprise attack on Caerphilly Castle in a revolt against English rule in…
objets.notes: | Llywelyn Bren launches a surprise attack on Caerphilly Castle in a revolt against English rule in Wales; he lays siege to the castle for six weeks and surrenders unconditionally to King Edward II's forces on 18 March

objets.nom: | Newport, Cardiff and Caerphilly are seized by the Marcher Lord Roger Mortimer in an intense eight-day…
objets.notes: | Newport, Cardiff and Caerphilly are seized by the Marcher Lord Roger Mortimer in an intense eight-day campaign in the Despenser War against King Edward II of England

objets.nom: The Treaty of Edinburgh–Northampton, under which England recognises Scottish independence, is signed.
Treaty of Northampton
objets.notes: Treaty of Northampton. England recognises Scottish independence.

objets.nom: Battle of Poitiers
objets.notes: Second of the three major battles of the Hundred Years' War takes place near Poitiers, France.

objets.nom: Robert II becomes first Stewart king.
The Anglo-Portuguese Treaty of 1373 is signed, forming an alliance between England and Portugal; it…
objets.notes: The Anglo-Portuguese Treaty of 1373 is signed, forming an alliance between England and Portugal; it remains an active treaty, most recently invoked in the Falklands War (see 1982)

objets.nom: Peasants' Revolt
objets.notes: a major uprising across large parts of England led by Wat Tyler; it is also called Wat Tyler's Rebellion or the Great Rising.

objets.nom: English defeat Scots in the Battle of Nesbit Moor and the Battle of Humbleton Hill.
Battle of Shrewsbury
objets.notes: fought between the Lancastrian King, Henry IV, and a rebel army led by Henry "Harry Hotspur" Percy from Northumberland.

objets.nom: Battle of Agincourt
objets.notes: a major English victory in the Hundred Years' War on Saint Crispin's Day, near modern-day Azincourt, in northern France.

objets.nom: The first large-scale eisteddfod is held at Carmarthen: Dafydd ab Edmwnd wins the silver chair for his poetry.
The start of the Wars of the Roses, a civil war for control of the throne of England between the House…
objets.notes: The start of the Wars of the Roses, a civil war for control of the throne of England between the House of York in Yorkshire and House of Lancaster in Lancashire.

objets.nom: | Following defeat at the Battle of Northampton, the Queen of England, Margaret of Anjou, escapes to…
objets.notes: | Following defeat at the Battle of Northampton, the Queen of England, Margaret of Anjou, escapes to Harlech Castle with her son Edward, Prince of Wales.

objets.nom: Denmark cedes Orkney and Shetland from Norway to Scotland.
| The Battle of Tewkesbury ends Lancastrian hopes of regaining the ascendance over the House of York in…
objets.notes: | The Battle of Tewkesbury ends Lancastrian hopes of regaining the ascendance over the House of York in the Wars of the Roses; King Edward IV is victorious, and Edward of Westminster becomes the only Prince of Wales ever to die in battle.

objets.nom: Battle of Bosworth Field (Battle of Bosworth): the last significant battle of the Wars of the Roses, the…
objets.notes: Battle of Bosworth Field (Battle of Bosworth): the last significant battle of the Wars of the Roses, the civil war between the Houses of Lancaster and York. Richard III, the last Plantagenet king was killed, succeeded by Henry VII.

objets.nom: The Battle of Bosworth Field ends the Yorkist reign of Richard III and ushers in Tudor reign, with the…
objets.notes: The Battle of Bosworth Field ends the Yorkist reign of Richard III and ushers in Tudor reign, with the reign of Henry VII.

objets.nom: Battle of Stoke, the decisive engagement in a failed attempt by leading Yorkists to unseat Henry VII of…
objets.notes: Battle of Stoke, the decisive engagement in a failed attempt by leading Yorkists to unseat Henry VII of England in favour of the pretender Lambert Simnel.

objets.nom: The Battle of Stoke is fought between Henry VII and Lambert Simnel a Yorkist claimant to the throne
objets.notes: The Battle of Stoke is fought between Henry VII and Lambert Simnel a Yorkist claimant to the throne. It is the last battle of the Wars of the Roses.

objets.notes: Treaty of Berlin was signed in the aftermath of the Russo-Turkish War. The Ottomans were forced to cede Adjara to the expanding Russian Empire.

objets.nom: Democratic Republic of Georgia established.
Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic disestablished.
Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic established.
Democratic Republic of Georgia annexed by the Bolshevik forces of the Soviet Union, following an…
objets.notes: Democratic Republic of Georgia annexed by the Bolshevik forces of the Soviet Union, following an invasion which begin 14 days earlier on the 11th.

objets.nom: A wave of demonstrations were held in Tbilisi to protest adopting a new constitution of the Soviet…
objets.notes: A wave of demonstrations were held in Tbilisi to protest adopting a new constitution of the Soviet Georgia, no longer declaring Georgian to be the sole state language. Protests resulted in retaining the previous status of the Georgian language.

objets.nom: Georgia declares independence from the Soviet Union, finalized on 25 December the same year.
Soviet forces disperse demonstrations in Tbilisi, leaving 21 civilians killed.
Zviad Gamsakhurdia elected as the first President of Georgia.
Georgian Civil War takes place.
South Ossetia War.
Zviad Gamsakhurdia overthrowed by the military junta.
Eduard Shevardnadze elected as the President of Georgia.
War in Abkhazia.
Battle of Lechfeld (955)
objets.notes: An East Frankish army under king Otto I, Holy Roman Emperor trapped a Hungarian army behind the Lech and wiped it out, saving the city of Augsburg and extending East Frankish territory eastward.

objets.nom: Coup of Kaiserswerth
objets.notes: Anno II, archbishop of Cologne, kidnapped the young Henry IV, Holy Roman Emperor, then King of the Romans, and demanded that his mother and regent Agnes of Poitou hand over the Imperial Regalia to his coconspirators.

objets.nom: Saxon Rebellion
objets.notes: The Saxon nobility, at the head of a large army, came to the Imperial Palace of Goslar to protest the frequent stays of Henry IV, Holy Roman Emperor, king of Germany, on their territory and his promotion of local ministeriales. The king fled.

objets.nom: Battle of Langensalza (1075)
objets.notes: Henry IV, Holy Roman Emperor, king of Kingdom of Germany, and a number of his vassals, including Ernest the Brave, destroyed a Saxon army composed largely of peasant draftees near what is now Bad Langensalza. Ernest the Brave was killed. He was succeeded by his son Leopold II the Fair, Margrave of Austria.

objets.nom: Investiture Controversy
objets.notes: The pope Pope Gregory VII composed the Dictatus papae, declaring that his office was granted by God, and that he had the right to depose emperors, as well as the sole authority to appoint and transfer bishops.

objets.nom: 1138 Imperial election
objets.notes: Conrad III of Germany was elected King of the Romans at Koblenz, defeating Henry X, Duke of Bavaria, duke of Bavaria, Saxony and Spoleto and margrave of Tuscany.

objets.nom: Siege of Jerusalem (1187)
objets.notes: The city of Jerusalem fell to an Ayyubid siege. The capital of the Kingdom of Jerusalem was moved to Tyre, Lebanon.

objets.nom: Third Crusade
objets.notes: The pope Pope Gregory VIII issued the audita tremendi calling for a crusade to reconquer Jerusalem from the Ayyubid dynasty.

objets.nom: Siege of Acre (1189–1191)
objets.notes: Guy of Lusignan, jure uxoris king of Jerusalem, laid siege to the Ayyubid city of Acre, Israel.

objets.nom: Crusade of 1197
objets.notes: Frederick the Catholic left Austria on a crusade organized by Henry VI, Holy Roman Emperor, emperor of the Holy Roman Empire, to reconquer Jerusalem for the Kingdom of Jerusalem and convince the pope Pope Celestine III to support his claim to Sicily.

objets.nom: Albigensian Crusade
objets.notes: The pope Pope Innocent III called for a crusade against Catharism, a gnostic heresy prevalent in Languedoc, and the sympathetic count of Toulouse, Raymond VI, Count of Toulouse.

objets.nom: Fifth Crusade
objets.notes: Leopold the Glorious left Vienna to take part in another crusade to reconquer Jerusalem from the Ayyubid dynasty.

objets.nom: Siege of Damietta (1218–1219)
objets.notes: Crusader forces, including Austrian and Styrian forces, landed near the fortress of the Ayyubid city of Damietta.

objets.nom: Battle of Mohi
objets.notes: Austrian forces defeated a small Golden Horde raiding party near Muhi, then withdrew. Hungarian and Templar forces remained in the theater.

objets.nom: Battle of the Leitha River
objets.notes: The Kingdom of Hungary defeated an Austrian invasion near the banks of the Leitha. Frederick the Quarrelsome was killed. His sister Margaret of Austria, Queen of Bohemia and his niece Gertrude of Austria both claimed the succession in Austria and Styria.

objets.nom: Battle of Kressenbrunn
objets.notes: Austrian and Bohemian forces repulsed a Hungarian attack over the Morava near modern Engelhartstetten. Many Hungarian soldiers drowned in the river.

objets.nom: 1273 Imperial election
objets.notes: Rudolf I of Habsburg of Germany, count of Habsburg, was elected King of the Romans in Frankfurt, defeating Ottokar the Iron and Golden King, who refused to recognize his election.

objets.nom: Battle on the Marchfeld
objets.notes: A Holy Roman Empire and Hungarian army decisively defeated a Bohemian, Głogów and Lower Bavarian force near Dürnkrut, Austria and Jedenspeigen. Ottokar the Iron and Golden King was killed.

objets.nom: 1292 Imperial election
objets.notes: Adolf, King of the Romans, count of Nassau, was elected King of the Romans at Frankfurt, denying the wishes of Rudolf I of Germany to see his son Albert of Habsburg elected.

objets.nom: Battle of Göllheim
objets.notes: Albert of Habsburg personally killed Adolf, King of the Romans, King of the Romans in battle at Göllheim.

objets.nom: Battle of Lucka
objets.notes: Frederick I, Margrave of Meissen defeated the forces of the Holy Roman Empire at Lucka, preserving the rule of the House of Wettin over Thuringia.

objets.nom: Battle of Gammelsdorf
objets.notes: The forces of Louis IV, Holy Roman Emperor, duke of Upper Bavaria, defeated those of Frederick the Fair at Gammelsdorf. Frederick the Fair was forced to renounce the tutelage of the children of the late Stephen I, Duke of Bavaria, duke of Lower Bavaria.

objets.nom: Imperial election, October 19, 1314
objets.notes: Four electors of the Holy Roman Empire selected Frederick the Fair as King of the Romans at Frankfurt.

objets.nom: Imperial election, October 20, 1314
objets.notes: Five electors of the Holy Roman Empire selected Louis IV, Holy Roman Emperor, duke of Upper Bavaria, as King of the Romans at Frankfurt in opposition to Frederick the Fair.

objets.nom: Battle of Mühldorf
objets.notes: The forces of Louis IV, Holy Roman Emperor, duke of Upper Bavaria and a claimant to the title King of the Romans, defeated those of his rival Frederick the Fair in battle at Ampfing. Frederick the Fair was captured.

objets.nom: Battle of Sempach
objets.notes: A Swiss force decisively defeated an invasion by Leopold the Just at Sempach. Leopold was killed, along with a number of his vassals. He was succeeded by his young sons William the Courteous, Duke of Austria and Leopold IV the Fat, Duke of Austria, with his brother Albert with the Braid acting as regent.

objets.nom: Appenzell Wars
objets.notes: A popular uprising took place in Appenzell against the rule of the prince-abbot of the Abbey of Saint Gall, an ally of the Habsburgs.

objets.nom: Hussite Wars
objets.notes: A Hussite procession led by the priest Jan Želivský threw seven government officials, including the burgomaster, from the New Town Hall in Prague, killing them.

objets.nom: Battle of Domažlice
objets.notes: A Holy Roman Empire force, including some troops led by Albert the Magnanimous, was driven from its siege positions at Domažlice and wiped out in the nearby Bohemian Forest.

objets.nom: Transylvanian peasant revolt
objets.notes: A peasant revolt broke out in eastern Hungary following a demand by the local bishop György Lépes that the locals pay several years' overdue tithe in a single lump sum in the new currency.

objets.nom: Battle of Hermannstadt
objets.notes: A Hungarian force was defeated by a numerically superior Ottoman force near Sântimbru, Alba and force to withdraw. One of the Hungarian commanders, the bishop György Lépes, was captured and beheaded.

objets.nom: Battle of Nish (1443)
objets.notes: Hungarian, Polish and Serbian forces captured the Ottoman city of Niš.

objets.nom: Battle of St. Jakob an der Sihl
objets.notes: A Swiss army forced imperial and Zürich forces to abandon a defensive position on the Sihlfeld outside of Zürich.

objets.nom: Battle of Zlatitsa
objets.notes: The Hungarian, Polish and Serbian armies were defeated near modern Zlatitsa, in a pass of the Balkan Mountains, halting their advance into Ottoman territory.

objets.nom: Crusade of Varna
objets.notes: The pope Pope Eugene IV called for a crusade to expel the Ottoman Empire from the Balkans.

objets.nom: Battle of Kunovica
objets.notes: An Ottoman army pursuing Hungarian, Polish and Serbian forces after their retreat from Zlatitsa were ambushed and defeated in the shadow of Suva Planina.

objets.nom: Battle of Varna
objets.notes: The Ottoman Empire decisively defeated an inferior Polish-Hungarian-Wallachian force at Varna. Władysław III of Poland, king of Poland and claimant against Ladislaus the Posthumous to the throne of Hungary, was killed.

objets.nom: Battle of Kosovo (1448)
objets.notes: An allied force of Hungarians, Poles, Wallachians and Moldavians met a numerically superior Ottoman force on Kosovo field, near modern Kosovo Polje.

objets.nom: Battle of Kruševac
objets.notes: While Ottoman forces mobilized further north for an invasion of Serbia, Serbian and Hungarian forces surprised and defeated a smaller contingent at Kruševac.

objets.nom: Bohemian–Hungarian War (1468–1478)
objets.notes: Matthias Corvinus, the king of Hungary, invaded Bohemia on the pretext of restoring it to Catholicism.

objets.nom: Cologne Diocesan Feud
objets.notes: The Landstände of the Electorate of Cologne declared the archbishop, Ruprecht of the Palatinate, deposed and elevated Hermann IV of Hesse in his stead as diocesan administrator.

objets.nom: Siege of Neuss
objets.notes: Burgundian forces laid siege to the free imperial city of Neuss as part of an invasion of Cologne in support of the deposed archbishop Ruprecht of the Palatinate.

objets.nom: Austrian–Hungarian War (1477–1488)
objets.notes: Hungary invaded Austria as punishment for the latter's diplomatic support of Hussite Bohemia in the Bohemian–Hungarian War.

objets.nom: Battle of Nancy
objets.notes: The Burgundian army was surrounded and wiped out by Swiss and Lorrain forces while besieging the Lorrain capital Nancy, now Nancy, France. Charles the Bold, the duke of Burgundy, was killed.

objets.nom: Battle of Guinegate (1479)
objets.notes: Burgundian forces defeated a smaller French army at Enguinegatte, defending Maximilian's claim against that of the French king Louis XI of France.

objets.nom: Battle of Frastanz
objets.notes: Swiss troops flanked a Swabian Letzi in the Montafon and drove out their forces.

objets.nom: Swabian War
objets.notes: Imperial and Swabian League forces occupied the Val Müstair, a strategically important pass in the Three Leagues.

objets.nom: War of the League of Cambrai
objets.notes: Maximilian invaded Venice with the aim of reconquering the Romagna for the Papal States.

objets.nom: Battle of La Motta (1513)
objets.notes: An Aragonese and Holy Roman Empire force decisively defeated a Venetian attack at Schio.

objets.nom: Battle of the Spurs
objets.notes: French forces attempting to break an English and Holy Roman Empire siege of Thérouanne were met by the besiegers at modern Enguinegatte and routed with heavy casualties.

objets.nom: First Congress of Vienna
objets.notes: Philip the Handsome's younger son Ferdinand I, Holy Roman Emperor married Anne of Bohemia and Hungary, the eldest child of Vladislaus II of Hungary, king of Hungary as well as king of Bohemia and Croatia. Philip's daughter Mary of Hungary married Vladislaus's other child, his son Louis II of Hungary.

objets.nom: Battle of Noáin
objets.notes: The bulk of the army dedicated to Navarrese independence under Henry II of Navarre was defeated by a vastly superior Castilian-Aragonese force.

objets.nom: Diet of Worms
objets.notes: An Imperial Diet of the Holy Roman Empire convened at Worms, Germany to address the writings of Martin Luther.

objets.nom: Battle of Bicocca
objets.notes: A French force of Swiss mercenaries advancing under heavy artillery fire failed to dislodge Holy Roman Empire forces from Bicocca in Milan.

objets.nom: Italian campaign of 1524–25
objets.notes: The French king Francis I of France crossed the Alps into Northern Italy at the head of army forty thousand strong.

objets.nom: Siege of Fuenterrabía (1523–1524)
objets.notes: Castilian and Aragonese forces laid siege to Hondarribia, where remained forces loyal to Henry II of Navarre and to the independence of Navarre.

objets.nom: Battle of Pavia
objets.notes: After a precipitate attack, a French force was surrounded and destroyed by Holy Roman Empire artillery at Visconti Park. The French king Francis I of France was captured.

objets.nom: Battle of Mohács
objets.notes: A Hungarian army met an Ottoman invasion at Mohács. After breaking the Hungarian left flank, the Ottoman army surrounded and destroyed the Hungarian and killed Louis II of Hungary, the king of Hungary and king of Bohemia.

objets.nom: Diet of Speyer (1526)
objets.notes: An Imperial Diet of the Holy Roman Empire convened at Speyer to address the rise of Lutheranism.

objets.nom: Battle of Sződfalva
objets.notes: The Serb commander Jovan Nenad was defeated and killed by a Hungarian army of John Zápolya.

objets.nom: Battle of Szőlős
objets.notes: The Serb commander Jovan Nenad defeated an army loyal to John Zápolya, the claimant against Ferdinand to the throne of Hungary, near Seleuș.

objets.nom: Election in Cetin
objets.notes: The Croatian nobility unanimously elected Ferdinand king at Cetin Castle.

objets.nom: Sack of Rome (1527)
objets.notes: After the failure of the Holy Roman Empire to pay them, the Landsknechte mutinied, sacked Rome and forced the pope Pope Clement VII to fortify himself inside the Castel Sant'Angelo.

objets.nom: Battle of Szina
objets.notes: Ferdinand's forces decisively defeated the army of John Zápolya, his rival in the struggle for the Hungarian succession. Zápolya was forced to flee into Poland.

objets.nom: Siege of Naples (1528)
objets.notes: French and allied forces laid siege by land and sea to Naples, capital of the Aragonese kingdom of Naples.

objets.nom: Battle of Landriano
objets.notes: A Spanish force destroyed the French army in Italy at Landriano.

objets.nom: Diet of Speyer (1529)
objets.notes: An Imperial Diet of the Holy Roman Empire was convened at Speyer to address Ottoman gains in Europe and the rise of Lutheranism. Ferdinand, on behalf of his brother Charles, the Holy Roman Emperor, called for the reinstatement of the ban on Martin Luther and his followers and condemned the religious innovations that had taken place in the Imperial…

objets.nom: Protestation at Speyer
objets.notes: Six princes of the Holy Roman Empire and the representatives of fourteen free imperial cities issued a letter to the Imperial Diet declaring their refusal to accept its authority in spiritual matters.

objets.nom: Siege of Florence (1529–30)
objets.notes: Spanish, Holy Roman Empire and papal forces made camp outside of Florence.

objets.nom: Siege of Vienna
objets.notes: Some hundred thousand Ottoman soldiers led by the sultan Suleiman the Magnificent laid siege to the Austrian capital Vienna.

objets.nom: Suleiman I's campaign of 1529
objets.notes: The Ottoman Empire invaded Hungary in support of John Zápolya's claim to the throne against Ferdinand.

objets.nom: 1531 Imperial election
objets.notes: Ferdinand was elected King of the Romans. The prince-electors agreed to elect Charles's preferred candidate, his young son Philip II of Spain, to succeed Ferdinand.

objets.nom: Siege of Güns
objets.notes: Ottoman forces laid siege to Kőszeg, a Hungarian town loyal to Ferdinand, on the border of Austria.

objets.nom: Battle of Guruslău
objets.notes: A force of Hungarians, Wallachians and Cossacks defeated the rebel Transylvanian prince Sigismund Báthory on the plain of the Guruslău River.

objets.nom: Bocskai uprising
objets.notes: The Hungarian nobleman Stephen Bocskai launched a revolt against Habsburg dominion over Hungary.

objets.nom: Long Turkish War
objets.notes: The Peace of Zsitvatorok was signed in what is now Radvaň nad Dunajom, ending a long conflict between the Ottoman Empire and the Holy Roman Empire. The obligations of the Hungarian nobility to their Ottoman suzerains were reduced.

objets.nom: Battle of Luzzara
objets.notes: An Austrian force under the general Prince Eugene of Savoy crossed the Po at Luzzara but failed to dislodge the French from their position despite heavy casualties on both sides.

objets.nom: War of the Second Coalition
objets.notes: France and Francis II, Holy Roman Emperor, the latter acting as emperor of the Holy Roman Empire and as king of Hungary, Bohemia and Croatia and archduke of Austria, signed the Treaty of Lunéville, ending their conflict. France made territorial gains, including the extension of its border with the Holy Roman Empire east to the Rhine.

objets.nom: 1901 Hungarian parliamentary election
objets.notes: Voting began in elections to the Hungarian Diet. Voting ended on 9 October, with the liberal Liberal Party won a supermajority of seats.

objets.nom: Knittelfeld Putsch
objets.notes: An agreement between Jörg Haider, Landeshauptmann of Carinthia and an elder statesman of the Freedom Party of Austria (FPÖ), and Susanne Riess, the party chair, was symbolically torn up at a party meeting at Knittelfeld.

objets.notes: Henry the Blind, Count of Namur and of Luxembourg, being childless, names his nephew, Baldwin V, Count of Hainaut, already heir to all his allodial possessions, as heir equally to all his feudal possessions, "with sod and twig", retaining usufruct during his own lifetime.

objets.notes: Peace treaty between Henry I, Duke of Brabant and Baldwin V, Count of Hainaut, ending twelve years of conflict between the Duchy of Brabant and the County of Hainaut.

objets.notes: Baldwin VI, Count of Hainaut, donates all his possessions in the village of Horrues to the collegiate church of Soignies to endow a Lady chapel and a chantry.

objets.notes: decisive French victory against the forces of Ferdinand, Count of Flanders, Henry I, Duke of Brabant, and Otto IV, Holy Roman Emperor. Count of Flanders carried captive to Paris.

objets.notes: Guy of Saint-Pol and his brother, Hugo of Saint-Pol, stand surety for a loan of 3693 pounds borrowed from citizens of Arras by Daniel, Lord of Béthune: an early example of the use of French rather than Latin in legal documents.

objets.notes: Ferdinand, Count of Flanders and Joan, Countess of Flanders release inhabitants of the Brugse Vrije from the feudal relief of "best beast".

objets.notes: Guy de Thourout does homage to Guy, Count of Flanders for lands in Wervik, Reninge and Rollegem. He also held land in Menen and Rekkem, a manor in Varsenare, and owned a number of houses within the city of Ypres.

objets.nom: Aldermen of Nieuwpoort accept the mediation of Guy, Count of Flanders in their dispute with the abbeys…
objets.notes: Aldermen of Nieuwpoort accept the mediation of Guy, Count of Flanders in their dispute with the abbeys of Duinen and Bourbourg concerning a dyke built near the town.

objets.notes: John II, Duke of Brabant, recognises that Affligem Abbey by immemorial custom has the right to appoint a panel of seven aldermen for the village of Hekelgem.

objets.nom: Guy, Count of Flanders and Marquis of Namur transfers government of Namur to John of Namur, his eldest…
objets.notes: Guy, Count of Flanders and Marquis of Namur transfers government of Namur to John of Namur, his eldest son by Isabelle of Luxembourg, breaking the personal union of Namur with the County of Flanders (which would pass to Robert, Guy's son by Matilda of Béthune).

objets.nom: Battle of the Golden Spurs
objets.notes: Flemish forces defeat knights of Philip IV of France near Kortrijk

objets.notes: Henry of Luxembourg died in Buonconvento while besieging Siena, reputedly of poison put in the chalice during mass.

objets.notes: Rebellion of the commoners in maritime Flanders, sparked by Louis I, Count of Flanders, ceding Sluis to John I, Marquis of Namur.

objets.notes: Pope John XXII provides a dispensation for the marriage of Philippa of Hainault and Edward III of England. The marriage itself took place by proxy in Valenciennes in October.

objets.notes: Christening of the future Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor, in Ghent, with Margaret of York, Margaret of Austria, Charles, Prince of Chimay, and John, Lord of Bergen op Zoom as godparents.

objets.notes: churches and monasteries vandalised and plundered in many parts of the Habsburg Netherlands.
